Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(compat/next-router): use React Router location in buildUrl (#3191)

buildUrl fell back to window.location.pathname when a caller pushed a
query-only URL (no pathname). Under MemoryRouter, or any situation where
window.location hasnt caught up with React Routers location, this returned
"/", stripping the route and causing navigate() to jump to /?passFailStatus=x.

On the Simulations Runs page this manifested as: clicking any filter sent the
user to /?passFailStatus=fail, unmounting the page; re-entering with a dangling
querystring was then interpreted as an external-set identifier, producing the
"EXTERNAL SET / ?passFailStatus=fail / No run data found for this set." UI.

Fix: accept an explicit currentPathname and pass location.pathname from inside
the useRouter() hook where React Routers location is the source of truth.
Callers without a React context (RouterSingleton) keep the window.location
fallback unchanged.

Closes #3191

* refactor(pat): introduce domain errors for PAT service

Adds PatNotFoundError / PatNotOwnedError / PatAlreadyRevokedError /
PatPermissionDeniedError / PatScopeViolationError in
src/server/pat/errors.ts, each carrying a stable `kind` string (not
`instanceof`, which breaks across bundler module boundaries per
CLAUDE.md) and an appropriate httpStatus (403 / 404 / 409).

PatService.revoke now throws these domain errors instead of generic
Error. The tRPC router adds a mapPatDomainError helper that dispatches
on `kind` and converts to TRPCError with the correct code.

Permission-denied maps to 403 (business decision, not a bug) so clients
can surface upgrade / re-auth messages rather than retrying.

* refactor(pat): inject Prisma + late markUsed for auth helpers

Removes module-scope ~/server/db coupling from the PAT auth helpers:

- createUnifiedAuthMiddleware and enforcePatCeiling now accept a
  PrismaClient via injection. Callers that already constructed a
  TokenResolver pass the same instance through, so infrastructure
  stays wired at the composition root (app/api/middleware/auth.ts
  and each inline route module).
- The middleware no longer calls markUsed eagerly. markUsed is now
  deferred until after next() returns and only fires when the wrapped
  handler produced a 2xx response, aligning lastUsedAt with successful
  request outcomes rather than mere token resolution.
- Inline-route helpers (evaluations-v3 / evaluations-legacy /
  annotations / traces-legacy / experiment-init) now expose a
  markUsed() callable on the auth result so routes can invoke the
  late-usage bump; experiment/init adopts it at the success return.

Fire-and-forget markUsed is preserved — a DB hiccup must not block a
request that was otherwise authorized and executed.

* fix(pat): log errors from fire-and-forget markUsed

markUsed is intentionally fire-and-forget — a successful request must
not depend on a successful DB write to lastUsedAt. But the previous
implementation swallowed rejections silently, so if the update started
failing (disk pressure, migrations, connection churn) it would surface
only as stale lastUsedAt values with no logs.

Attaches a .catch(logger.warn) so failures are visible in operational
logs without changing the fire-and-forget semantics.

* fix(pat): cap bindings array at 20 in create input

Each binding walks scope lookups and representative-permission checks,
so an unbounded array in the tRPC create mutation is a cheap DoS
surface for any authenticated user. 20 is well above any realistic
grant (even mirroring a power-user's role bindings rarely exceeds a
handful) while bounding per-request validation cost.

* refactor(pat): batch role binding inserts with createMany

Replaces N serialized prisma.roleBinding.create() calls with a single
createMany so the DB issues one INSERT ... VALUES (...) statement.

Rationale for createMany over Promise.allSettled (which the reviewer
flagged as a consideration): allSettled would surface per-row errors
but break atomicity. A PAT that persists with only "most" of its
intended bindings is worse than no PAT — the user believes they
granted permissions they didn't. Atomicity is preserved by running
inside the outer $transaction that creates the PAT row itself, so any
constraint failure rolls the PAT back along with it.

* refactor(pat): move PAT create validation into PatService

Move ~120 lines of scope/ceiling/custom-role validation from the tRPC
router into PatService.create so routes stay thin and business logic is
owned by the service layer. Violations now throw PatScopeViolationError
(domain error with kind "pat_scope_violation") which the router maps to
TRPCError FORBIDDEN via the existing mapPatDomainError helper.

Router `create` mutation is reduced to: parse input, call service, map
domain errors, return DTO — matching the repository/service pattern
documented in dev/docs/best_practices/repository-service.md.

* fix(pat): enforce ceiling on /track_event via domain error

Refactor enforcePatCeiling to throw PatPermissionDeniedError (kind
"pat_permission_denied", httpStatus 403) when a PAT is denied, instead of
returning an ad-hoc descriptor. Add patCeilingDenialResponse helper so
Hono routes and Next API handlers can preserve their existing early-
return ergonomics while the underlying enforcement path is now a typed
domain error.

Add the ceiling check to /api/track_event using traces:create — the
endpoint writes into the traces pipeline, so read-only PATs (VIEWER)
must not be able to emit events.

Update existing callers (collector, otel, evaluations-v3,
evaluations-legacy, annotations, traces-legacy, experiment/init,
requirePatPermission middleware) to the try/catch shape. No behavior
change for users beyond uniform 403 + message on denial.

* fix(pat): migrate remaining misc.ts legacy-auth endpoints to unified auth

Brings the remaining `misc.ts` endpoints onto the unified
`extractCredentials` -> `TokenResolver.resolve` -> `enforcePatCeiling`
pipeline so PATs (not just project API keys) can drive them and the
permission ceiling is enforced per route:

- /dspy/log_steps        -> workflows:manage  (TODO: experiments:* when added)
- /experiment/init (Hono)-> workflows:manage  (TODO: experiments:* when added)

- /trigger/slack         -> triggers:manage
- /workflows/:w/run and

Each route uses the late-markUsed pattern (fire-and-forget, only on the
success path) and maps `PatPermissionDeniedError` to 403 via

It is a demo fixture that forwards the caller's token to /api/collector,
which itself performs full unified auth + ceiling enforcement. Added
inline comment documenting the skip rationale.

* refactor(pat): widen PatRepository to accept transaction client

Inside $transaction, PatService was calling `PatRepository.create(tx as
PrismaClient)`. The cast was a type-safety lie: Prisma's transaction
client is not a PrismaClient. Widen the repository delegate to
`PrismaClient | Prisma.TransactionClient` so callers share one repo
between normal and transactional paths with no cast. Surfaced in PR
review.

* refactor(pat): de-duplicate misc.ts routes via unified auth middleware

Replace the 25-line extractCredentials → TokenResolver.resolve →
enforcePatCeiling → conditional markUsed ritual copied across seven Hono
handlers (/analytics, /dspy/log_steps, /experiment/init, /optimization,
/track_event, /trigger/slack, /workflows/:workflowId/...run) with two
composable middlewares: createUnifiedAuthMiddleware (runs once per
request, sets project on ctx, handles late markUsed) and
requirePatPermission (enforces ceiling, returns 403 on denial). Types
the Hono app with UnifiedAuthVariables so c.get("project") resolves to
Project without casts.

Handlers are now the business logic only — no auth boilerplate, no
response-shape drift between routes, and lastUsedAt is consistently
tied to successful outcomes (status 2xx) instead of successful
authentication.

* fix(pat): add partial unique indexes for PAT-principal role bindings

RoleBinding already had four partial unique indexes for user/group principals
(built-in + custom role variants) but PAT principals only had a plain
@@index([patId]). This meant the same PAT could be granted the same
(role, scope) or (customRole, scope) twice, silently duplicating permissions.

Add the two missing partial unique indexes directly in the PAT-creation
migration since it has not been deployed yet — no new migration file needed.

- RoleBinding_pat_builtin_role_scope_key: (patId, role, scopeType, scopeId)
  where patId IS NOT NULL AND customRoleId IS NULL
- RoleBinding_pat_custom_role_scope_key: (patId, customRoleId, scopeType, scopeId)
  where patId IS NOT NULL AND customRoleId IS NOT NULL

Update schema.prisma comment to reflect six partial unique indexes total.

* fix(pat): fail closed when custom role permissions are malformed

PatService.assertCustomRoleWithinCeiling was falling back to an empty array
when customRole.permissions was not a JSON array. This silently bypassed the
ceiling check — zero permissions means nothing to verify, so the binding
would be accepted regardless of the creator's actual access.

Throw PatScopeViolationError instead. Parity with role-binding-resolver.ts
which already denies when permissions is malformed (empty permissions →
no permission grants → access denied).

* refactor(rbac): shared parser for CustomRole.permissions with fail-closed semantics

Both PatService.assertCustomRoleWithinCeiling and checkRoleBindingPermission
were doing `Array.isArray(customRole.permissions) ? (...) : []`. Asymmetric:

- PAT ceiling fell back to [], silently bypassing the check (fail-open).
- Resolver fell back to [], denying the permission check (fail-safe).

The write path already validates shape with zod (role.ts:15 — same regex
`^[a-z]+:[a-z]+$`), but the read path had no matching guard. Next engineer
copies the "safe" version into a code path where empty means "allow" and we
reintroduce the bypass.

Extract parseCustomRolePermissions + MalformedCustomRolePermissionsError in
~/server/rbac/custom-role-permissions.ts. Shape-only validation (not an
allow-list of known permissions) — matches the write path and won't retro-
break CustomRoles created against older typed unions.

Call sites map the throw to context-appropriate behavior:
  - PatService: rethrows as PatScopeViolationError (403 at PAT create)
  - checkRoleBindingPermission: logs + treats as no-grant (denied, matches
    prior fail-safe behavior but now visible in logs)

Adds 12 unit tests covering shape validation, non-array inputs, non-string
elements, regex failures, and error metadata.

Supersedes the point-fix from 583f27ff6 by sharing the guard across both
call sites instead of just PatService.

* fix(pat): route remaining python SDK call sites through build_auth_headers

Every hand-rolled `X-Auth-Token` / raw `Authorization: Bearer` header in
the python SDK now delegates to `build_auth_headers`, so PATs pick up the
canonical `Basic base64(projectId:pat)` envelope. Before this, any code
path outside the client facades silently failed 401 under PATs — the
server accepts PAT on those routes (share/unshare, experiment init,
batch eval, dspy log_steps, online evaluations) but the client was only
sending legacy headers.

`login.py` intentionally kept on legacy headers: `/api/auth/validate`
has no PAT branch today and `/authorize` only surfaces `project.apiKey`,
so migrating the client in isolation would break the only supported
login path without unlocking anything.

* fix(pat): route remaining TS SDK + CLI call sites through buildAuthHeaders

All 29 CLI subcommands and 5 client-sdk services that hand-rolled the
legacy `X-Auth-Token` header now go through `buildAuthHeaders`, so PATs
get the canonical `Authorization: Basic base64(projectId:pat)` envelope
and the server accepts them. Previously status/agent-run/graphs/monitors
/secrets/simulation-runs/triggers/workflows/prompt-restore/scenario-run
/suites-run/traces-export — plus evaluations/experiments/datasets
facades — silently 401'd under PATs even though the server already
supported them via `tokenResolver`.

Also fixes two dual-header sites (dataset.service.ts, experiment.ts)
that sent both `X-Auth-Token` and a raw Bearer — collapsed to the single
spread of `buildAuthHeaders({ apiKey })`.

Verified end-to-end via the populator smoke suites:
- CLI read: 18/18 OK
- CLI mutations: 12/12 OK (agent + evaluator + dataset + scenario CRUD)
- TS SDK mutations: 15/15 OK (prompt + agent + evaluator + dataset + scenario)

* refactor(pat): consolidate API key management into unified settings page

Moves the regenerate flow out of the generic Settings page into
`ProjectApiKeySection` so all API-key management — personal and
project — lives at Settings → API Keys. `ApiKeyManagementSection` is
deleted (its behavior is absorbed by `ProjectApiKeySection`), the
user-menu link is retargeted to `/settings/api-keys`, and the now
redundant "Legacy" badge + stale callout copy are dropped.

Also drops a stale `packages/insanity-check` entry from pnpm-lock.yaml
that no longer corresponds to a directory in the tree.

* fix(pat): HMAC-SHA256 with server pepper for PAT secret storage

Swaps `hashSecret` from plain SHA-256 to HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the
existing `CREDENTIALS_SECRET` / `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` pepper. A DB-only leak
is now useless on its own — the attacker needs the pepper too.

Also clears the CodeQL "insufficient computational effort" alert on
langwatch/langwatch#3213 (false positive — PAT secrets are 286-bit
random, so bcrypt/argon2 buy nothing; HMAC-over-pepper is the correct
primitive for high-entropy API tokens and what GitHub/Stripe/etc. use).
We explicitly keep `verifySecret` fast because it runs on every
authenticated request and a slow KDF would create a DoS surface.

No migration path for already-issued PATs — the feature hasn't shipped,
so any dev-issued PATs need to be re-minted after this change.

* fix(tests): align auth header assertions with buildAuthHeaders output

After migrating SDK/CLI HTTP callers to buildAuthHeaders, spy assertions
still expected a lone capitalized X-Auth-Token. The helper now emits
lowercase authorization + x-auth-token (plus Basic auth for PATs), so
these two unit tests failed on CI. Update the mocks to match the actual
header shape.

feat(scenarios): workflow agent input/output mapping layer (#3201) (#3334)

* feat(scenarios): auto-compute workflow agent mappings on save (#3201)

Add server-side auto-compute of scenarioMappings when a workflow version
is saved. Queries linked agents, extracts entry/end node I/O, runs
computeBestMatchMappings(), and persists to agent config. Non-blocking
(fire-and-forget) so workflow saves are never slowed.

Includes feature file spec and unit tests.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(scenarios): blank-template skip + stale-field re-compute (#3201)

Auto-compute now skips when workflow still has blank-template placeholder
fields (question/output). Also re-computes when existing mappings
reference stale fields that no longer exist in the workflow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(scenarios): mapping drawer gate at Save & Run for workflow agents (#3201)

Before running a scenario with a workflow agent, check if scenarioMappings
have a required source mapping (input or messages). If missing or
incomplete, open AgentWorkflowEditorDrawer with a toast instead of
starting the run. Non-workflow agents pass through unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(scenarios): pre-run validation for multi-input workflow agents (#3201)

Validate workflow agent mappings after data prefetch. Multi-input
workflows without scenarioMappings now get a BAD_REQUEST error with
an actionable message instead of a cryptic 500. Single-input workflows
continue to use the legacy fallback.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(typecheck): cast agent config to Prisma.InputJsonValue (#3201)

Record<string, unknown> is not assignable to Prisma's InputJsonValue.
Follows existing codebase pattern (e.g. agent.repository.ts:276).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(scenarios): route agents list edit to matching editor drawer (#3201)

Extract getAgentEditorDrawer helper and rewire the agents list handleEditAgent
to route workflow agents to agentWorkflowEditor (not workflowSelector, which
is create-only). Satisfies AC 6.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scenarios): accept signature agent type in drawer-routing exhaustive (#3201)

getAgentEditorDrawer now imports AgentType from agent.repository (the canonical
source) rather than the narrower UI-picker AgentType. Signature agents have no
editor drawer, so the function throws explicitly — preserving the pre-refactor
switch behavior and making the exhaustive check compile against the real union.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scenarios): preserve non-stale mappings and repair stale output field (#3201)

Previous behavior had two issues surfaced in PR review:

1. When one input mapping became stale (key no longer exists in the workflow),
   auto-compute replaced the ENTIRE scenarioMappings object with fresh
   best-match guesses, clobbering user-set mappings for non-stale keys.
2. When scenarioOutputField pointed to a renamed/removed end output, it was
   never repaired unless the input mappings were also stale.

Now auto-compute:
- Preserves existing mappings for keys that still exist; only fills in
  best-match defaults for keys the user has not configured.
- Evaluates scenarioOutputField staleness independently and repairs it when
  the stored value points to a non-existent output.
- Initializes scenarioOutputField on first compute (unset + first mapping
  round) but does not overwrite an intentionally-unset field on agents

fix(scenarios): hydrate llm params for fresh workflow agent runs (#3277)

* test: add failing regression test for fresh workflow agent dummy api_key bug (#3160)

Scenario path bypasses addEnvs(), so stored DSL with value: undefined
on LLM nodes reaches NLP with no litellm_params - litellm falls back
to OPENAI_API_KEY=dummy and scenarios fail with AuthenticationError.

Test asserts the prefetched workflow DSL has litellm_params.api_key
hydrated on the llm-type parameter. Currently fails (proving the bug).
Fix lands in data-prefetcher's getLatestDsl path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scenarios): hydrate llm params for workflow agent scenario runs (#3160)

Scenario path for workflow agents sent the stored DSL directly to the
NLP service without running it through addEnvs(), so llm-type node
parameters reached litellm without litellm_params.api_key. The proxy
then fell back to OPENAI_API_KEY=dummy and scenarios failed with
AuthenticationError.

Hydrate at prefetch time in fetchWorkflowAgentData: for every llm-type
parameter across all DSL nodes, resolve the model (parameter value,
else workflow.default_llm, else DEFAULT_MODEL) and inject the
project-resolved litellm_params. Model lookups are deduped per unique
model. Failures warn and leave the parameter unchanged so the existing
error surfaces naturally instead of getting swallowed.

Chose prefetch-time hydration over persisting api_key into WorkflowVersion.dsl
to avoid staling on provider key rotation and leaking secrets into
workflow exports/logs. Mirrors what addEnvs() does for the editor path.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scenarios): surface hydration failures, normalize llm config keys (#3160)

Review feedback on PR #3277:

- When model-provider lookup fails during hydration, return a structured
  PrefetchResult failure instead of silently warning. The whole point of
  the fix is to stop users seeing the "dummy" error - falling through
  with no api_key meant they'd see it anyway.
- Normalize the llm base value to snake_case before wrapping with
  litellm_params, matching addEnvs behavior. Prevents latent bug if
  default_llm ever stores camelCase keys like maxTokens.
- Add negative tests: provider failure propagation, multi-model dedup
  (different models -> prepare called twice, same model -> once),
  DEFAULT_MODEL fallback when both default_llm and value.model absent.

Hydration is now all-or-nothing per DSL: any single model failure aborts
the whole prefetch with the first failure's reason/message.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(scenarios): guarantee top-level model key in hydrated llm value (#3160)

Partial existingValue (e.g. { temperature: 0.7 } without model) passed
through spread without a top-level `model`, diverging from addEnvs.ts
which always emits one via the LLMConfig contract. Downstream NLP reads
value.model directly.

feat(scenarios): project secrets for code/workflow agents + better dataset 400 (#3414)

feat(scenarios): load project secrets for code and workflow agents

Scenario workers executing code or workflow agents through
SerializedCodeAgentAdapter/SerializedWorkflowAgentAdapter were sending
DSLs to langwatch_nlp without the project's decrypted secrets, so
`secrets.NAME` references in user Python blew up with
`NameError: name 'secrets' is not defined`. The studio's addEnvs path
already injected these for UI-triggered runs; the scenario prefetcher
did not.

Prefetch decrypted secrets once per run and carry them through to the
adapter, which merges them into the DSL before POSTing to
/studio/execute_sync (same shape addEnvs produces). Adapter-provided
secrets win over any DSL-embedded ones so a stale persisted value can't
override the freshly decrypted one.

Also improves the dataset records 400 error to list valid column names
so integrations failing column validation can self-diagnose without
round-tripping to the dataset page. InvalidColumnError is now
object-shaped per the repo convention for multi-arg constructors.

Per-secret decrypt is wrapped so a single corrupt row yields a
readable "Failed to decrypt project secret <name>" error instead of a
raw crypto stack trace.

* fix(studio): support chat_messages signature inputs + preserve multi-turn history in Liquid (#3415)

Workflow Agent scenario runs exhibited two failures when the signature node consumed
conversation history from `agent_input.messages`:

1. `chat_messages` field type on signature inputs/outputs crashed code generation with
   `UndefinedError("'dict object' has no attribute 'chat_messages'")`. The UI exposed
   this type via `LlmConfigInputTypes`, but `FIELD_TYPE_TO_DSPY_TYPE` had no entry for
   it, so the Jinja template's `FIELD_TYPE_TO_DSPY_TYPE[input_field.type.value]` lookup
   raised.

2. For `str`-typed `messages` inputs, the TS adapter JSON-stringifies the conversation
   list before crossing to the NLP service (`resolve-field-mappings.ts:71`) — and the
   template adapter's `_format_template_inputs` then passed that already-escaped JSON
   straight to Liquid, producing `{{messages}}` rendered as a literal JSON blob in a
   single user turn (multi-turn history collapsed).

Fix, on the NLP side only:

- `registry.py`: map `FieldType.chat_messages` to `dspy.History` so DSPy formats turns
  natively.
- `template_adapter.py`: stop unconditionally stringifying template inputs. Parse
  JSON-encoded list/dict strings back to native Python (the shape they arrive in across
  the serialized-adapter boundary). `dspy.History` values expose their `.messages` list
  for Liquid iteration.
- `parser.py`: raise a structured error identifying the node, field, and unmapped type
  if any future signature input/output type is missing from the registry — replaces the
  bare Jinja UndefinedError with an actionable message.
- `tests/studio/test_workflow_agent_interpolation.py`: regression tests covering the
  issue's ACs 1, 2, 4, 5, and 6.
- `specs/features/scenarios/workflow-agent-interpolation.feature`: BDD spec.

fix(analytics): rescue 4 broken dashboard widgets in arrayJoin groupBy path (#3418)

* fix(analytics): project TokensPerSecond into dedup CTE so TPS graph doesn't 500

The tokens-per-second analytics chart emits `avg(ts.TokensPerSecond)` in
the outer SELECT of the arrayJoin dedup path (triggered by any arrayJoin
groupBy — e.g. `metadata.model` on the TPS chart). `ts` is only in scope
inside the `deduped_traces` CTE, and `TokensPerSecond` was never added to
the CTE's projection or to `DEDUP_FIELD_MAPPINGS`, so ClickHouse rejected
the query with:

  Unknown expression or function identifier `ts.TokensPerSecond` in scope

Fix follows the established pattern for the other trace-level columns:

- aggregation-builder.ts:1181 — project
  `any(ts.TokensPerSecond) AS trace_tokens_per_second` into the CTE
- aggregation-builder.ts:2015 — map `TokensPerSecond -> trace_tokens_per_second`
  in `DEDUP_FIELD_MAPPINGS` so `transformMetricForDedup` rewrites the
  outer reference to the CTE alias

Adds a regression test in the `arrayJoin groupBy` block that pins both
directions: the CTE must project `AS trace_tokens_per_second`, and the
outer SELECT must reference the alias (not the raw `ts.TokensPerSecond`).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(analytics): also project TimeToFirstTokenMs; add drift guard

Audit of metric-translator.ts found a sibling bug to the TokensPerSecond
issue: `performance.first_token` emits `quantileExact(ts.TimeToFirstTokenMs)`
in the outer SELECT under any arrayJoin groupBy, but TimeToFirstTokenMs
was never projected into the dedup CTE and not in DEDUP_FIELD_MAPPINGS.
Same failure mode as tokens_per_second:

  Unknown expression or function identifier `ts.TimeToFirstTokenMs` in scope

Expand the fix:
- Project `ts.TimeToFirstTokenMs AS trace_time_to_first_token_ms` in CTE
- Register the mapping in DEDUP_FIELD_MAPPINGS

Also add a drift guard (unit test) that scans metric-translator.ts for
every `${ts}.<Column>` reference and asserts each is either in
DEDUP_FIELD_MAPPINGS or on a small, documented allowlist of special-case
columns (TraceId, Attributes, OccurredAt). Any future trace-level metric
added without being wired into the CTE now fails this test at build time
instead of silently 500ing in production.

Tests:
- Parameterized regression covers both tokens_per_second and first_token
- Guard test catches column drift
- All 81 aggregation-builder tests passing

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(analytics): rewrite trace_id pipeline avg/min/max in arrayJoin path

Third bug in the same dashboard dedup path. `avgCostPerModel` and
`avgTokensPerModel` widgets emit

  pipeline: { field: "trace_id", aggregation: "avg" }

on a trace-level metric (performance.total_cost, performance.completion_tokens)
with groupBy: metadata.model. The arrayJoin CTE path only rewrote pipelines
with aggregation="sum"; "avg" (and min/max) fell through the loop and the
metric was silently dropped from the outer SELECT. Query returned 200 OK
with no values and the UI showed "No data — try adjusting the date range."

The previous comment claimed avg/min/max "have different semantics and
cannot be rewritten this way." That reasoning applied to span-level values
where a trace has multiple child rows. But this code path only runs AFTER
the CTE deduplicates by (trace_id, group_key) — each trace contributes at
most one row per group, so the per-trace inner aggregation is identity for
any of sum/avg/min/max on trace-level scalars.

Extend TRACE_ID_PIPELINE_SAFE_AGGS to {sum, avg, min, max}. Other inner
aggregations (quantile, uniq) are still left to fall through — they need
separate reasoning and aren't in use by the current dashboard widgets.

Tests:
- Parameterized regression pinning both affected widgets via
  performance.total_cost + performance.completion_tokens with
  pipeline:{field:"trace_id", aggregation:"avg"} — each must survive to
  the outer SELECT as `avg(trace_<column>)`.
- All 83 aggregation-builder tests passing.

Manually verified end-to-end against the local dev stack with real
Gemini-backed mock traces across three models — both widgets now render.

fix(traces): parse JSON-string langwatch.input when extracting primary I/O (#3419)

* fix(traces): parse JSON-string langwatch.input when extracting primary I/O

OTel frequently delivers complex attribute values as stringified JSON. The
primary-input heuristic was short-circuiting on any string, so a span with
`langwatch.input = '{"message":"...","history":[...]}'` displayed the raw
JSON blob on the trace list instead of the extracted "message" text.

Route strings through `messagesToText`, which already attempts `JSON.parse`
and recursively searches for `COMMON_TEXT_KEYS` (falling through to the raw
string when parse fails). Non-JSON strings like "hello world" are unchanged.

Adds BDD spec + regression tests for the JSON-string case and for
non-JSON strings that happen to contain braces.

* fix(python-sdk): retry share()/unshare() on transient httpx timeouts

sdk-python-ci flakes with `httpx.ReadTimeout: The read operation timed out`
from `trace.share()` at tests/test_examples.py:244 (see issue #3336).

The share endpoint is a trivial Prisma upsert, but when an e2e test flushes
a chatty LangChain run and immediately hits `share()` the prior request
stream + server cold-start can spike latency past the 15s budget, and the
test has no retry.

Wrap `share()`/`unshare()` with a tenacity retry (3 attempts, exponential
2-10s backoff) on `httpx.TimeoutException`/`ConnectError`, and bump the
per-attempt timeout 15s→30s. Matches the existing retry pattern in
`experiment.py` and `batch_evaluation.py`.

Also declare `tenacity` as an explicit dep instead of relying on
transitive inclusion via openinference.

Ports the SDK portion of abandoned PR #3341 (closed by author without
merging) and adds unit tests covering the success-after-retry and
exhausted-retries paths.

fix(traces): extract content from wrapped payloads to prevent empty trace output (#3383)

* fix(traces): extract content from wrapped payloads to prevent empty trace output

Traces with structured outputs like `{data: {content: "..."}}` were being
stored with `ComputedOutput = NULL` in ClickHouse because the heuristic
text extractor only looked for known keys (`content`, `text`, `answer`, etc.)
at the top level. Unknown wrapper keys like `data`, `result`, `response`
caused the extractor to give up and return null, which downstream became
`<empty>` in the Traces list and empty cells in dataset mapping.

Core fix in `trace-io-extraction.service.ts`:
- `extractTextFromPlainJson` now recurses into single-key wrapper objects,
  so `{data: {content: "x"}}` drills into `data` and finds `content`.
- `extractRichIOFromSpan` no longer returns null when the span has output
  data but heuristics fail. Falls back to `JSON.stringify(raw)` via the
  new `stringifyForText` helper, so `ComputedOutput` is never NULL when
  there's real content to show.

Mirror fix in `trace-summary.mapper.ts`:
- `extractTextFromStateObject` (display-side parser) got the same
  single-key wrapper recursion so the UI renders readable text instead
  of the raw JSON string when possible.

Legacy ES path in `collector/common.ts` (belt-and-suspenders for on-prem):
- `getLastOutputAsText` now walks all spans in finish order and picks the
  first that renders non-empty, instead of bailing on the last-finishing
  span if its output happens to be unrenderable.
- `specialKeysMapping` skips empty-string special-key matches so
  `{content: "", data: {...real...}}` falls through to the real payload.
- Fixed a latent typo: `json.query` branch was returning `json.user_query`.

Tests:
- 5 new edge-case tests in `trace-io-extraction.service.unit.test.ts`
  (deep nesting, primitive wrapper, circular refs, empty object/array).

- Updated one existing test that asserted the buggy behavior.

* fix(traces): split semantic vs fallback IO extraction; recursive emptiness check

Addresses two MAJOR CodeRabbit review findings:

1. Don't let stringified fallback shadow semantic matches in span ranking.
   `extractRichIOFromSpan` previously returned a non-null result for any
   non-empty payload (including unknown shapes that only the stringify
   fallback could render). Downstream ranking logic in `extractLastOutput`
   and `accumulateIO` treated these as equivalent to genuine semantic
   matches, so a later span carrying `{foo: "bar"}` could shadow an
   earlier span with real `{content: "the answer"}`.

   Now `extractRichIOFromSpan` returns null for fallback-only cases. A
   new `extractFallbackIOFromSpan` produces the stringified form, and
   callers apply it ONLY after every semantic candidate is exhausted:
   - `extractFirstInput` / `extractLastOutput` do a final fallback pass
     against the topmost / latest-finishing span when no semantic match
     was found across any span.
   - `accumulateIO` uses the fallback per-span only while
     `state.computedInput/Output` is still null — so the first semantic
     match overrides any prior fallback contribution.

2. Make `hasNonEmptyValue` semantic for nested objects.
   Previously `{ output: { content: "" } }` was considered "non-empty"
   at the top level (object with keys), causing `specialKeysMapping` to
   pick `output`, render `""`, and never check the sibling `answer`
   key. The check now recurses through arrays and objects with a
   WeakSet cycle guard, so deeply-nested empties propagate up.

Tests:
- Existing tests updated to reflect new contract (fallback testing
  moves from `extractRichIOFromSpan` to `extractFallbackIOFromSpan` /
  `extractLastOutput`).
- New ranking-invariant test: span with semantic `content` wins over
  later-finishing span with unknown shape.
- New legacy-path test: nested-empty wrapper falls through to sibling
  special key (`{output: {content: ""}, answer: "x"}` → `"x"`).
- New circular-reference safety test (non-throw assertion only).

fix(ci): expose feature-parity output from detect-changes action (#3461) (#3462)

The composite action declared only `relevant` as a workflow output, but
`langwatch-app-ci.yml` reads `needs.changes.outputs.feature-parity` (added
on PR #3298 as part of #3337's enforce-all parity gate). Composite actions
only re-expose outputs they explicitly declare — undeclared outputs land
as empty strings — so the gating expression `if: outputs.feature-parity ==
'true'` was always false and the parity CI job has been silently skipped
on every PR + main push.

Fix:

- Declare `feature-parity` as a second composite output, mirroring how
  `relevant` is wired (read from `steps.filter.outputs.<key>` for PRs,
  fall through to `steps.force.outputs.<key>` for non-PR events).
- Add `feature-parity=true` to the force step so non-PR events (push,
  merge_group, etc.) run the parity job unconditionally — same intent
  as `relevant`.
- Update the action docstring with a warning that every filter key the
  caller consumes must be declared here too. The silent-empty-string
  failure mode is exactly the one this regression hit; calling it out
  inline is the cheapest available guardrail.

Resolves #3461.

perf(analytics): cut PostHog bill — dedup pageviews + backend local eval (#3477)

* perf(analytics): cut PostHog bill by deduping pageviews and enabling backend local eval

Two cost drivers identified after the recent PostHog bill spike:

1. Frontend $pageview multiplier (from #3170 Vite migration). The
   next-router compat layer emitted routeChangeComplete from inside every
   useRouter() instance's effect — and the app has ~120 of them — so each
   real navigation fanned out to ~120× pageview captures (further doubled
   by posthog-js's own SPA pageview tracking).

   - Dedup at module scope (emitRouteChangeOnce) so emit count scales with
     navigations, not consumers.
   - Drop the manual posthog.capture("$pageview") subscription in
     usePostHog — posthog-js auto-captures pageviews on History API
     navigation, so we'd been double-counting on top of the multiplier.

2. Backend per-span/per-event killswitch checks (PostHog /flags). With
   no personalApiKey configured, every uncached evaluation hit /flags;
   the 5s cache fragmented per-tenant, so high-traffic projects stampeded.

   - Wire POSTHOG_FEATURE_FLAGS_KEY (Feature Flags Secure key, phs_*) into
     posthog-node init with featureFlagsPollingInterval (default 5min).
     With local evaluation, isFeatureEnabled resolves in-process — no
     /flags request per call.
   - Add KILL_SWITCH_CACHE_TTL_MS (60s) and a per-call cacheTtlMs option
     so hot-path callers (token estimation, projection router, command
     dispatcher) can opt into the longer window without changing the
     5s default for user-facing flags.

Spec: specs/analytics/posthog-cost-control.feature
ADR update: dev/docs/adr/005-feature-flags.md

* chore: drop PostHog block from .env.example (SaaS-only, not for self-hosters)

  true (initial load only) without the new defaults: '2025-05-24' switch,
  so without this we'd silently drop pageview tracking entirely after
  removing the manual capture call. Update the comment to reflect the

- env-create: guard POSTHOG_FEATURE_FLAGS_POLLING_INTERVAL_MS against
  empty-string .env values via the same z.preprocess pattern used by

* docs(adr): ADR-017 gateway trace payload capture (v1.1)

Per @ariana finding #73 — gateway spans carry rich metadata but no LLM
messages content today. That blocks online evals, dataset extraction,
and semantic debugging on gateway traffic. Portkey and Bifrost both
capture by default; we're the observability product and the only one
that doesn't.

Design captured:
- Opt-in per VK; default stays "none" (zero regression for current VKs)
- Four levels: none / metadata_only / redacted / raw
- Redaction runs in the gateway, not downstream, so the gateway pod
  itself stays compliant; trace pipeline keeps its redaction pass as
  defence in depth
- Streaming captures the reassembled message, not per-delta
- 32 KB cap per field with a truncated marker
- New `virtualKeys:capturePayload:raw` permission defaulting to nobody
- Org-level kill switch (one lever to disable across every VK in org)
- Hot-path budget: none/metadata_only stay sub-ms; redacted rises to
  ~2 ms per request — documented explicitly in the feature docs

Leaves span attribute names (langwatch.input/output, input_redacted,
output_redacted) compatible with what the trace pipeline already

* fix(multitenancy): exempt ModelProvider so scope-ladder findMany survives

PR-blocker caught during the iter-108 bugbash preflight (finding #29).

ModelProviderRepository.findAllAccessibleForProject (iter 107 step 2,
a56939520) queries:

  modelProvider.findMany({
    where: {
      OR: [
        { scopeType: "PROJECT", scopeId: projectId },
        { scopeType: "TEAM", scopeId: teamId },
        { scopeType: "ORGANIZATION", scopeId: orgId },
      ]
    }
  })

_guardProjectId (dbMultiTenancyProtection.ts:161) requires every OR
clause to carry projectId or organizationId:

  !params.args?.where?.OR?.every((o) => o.projectId || o.organizationId)

Our branches key off scopeType + scopeId, so every() → false, guard
throws:
  "The findMany action on the ModelProvider model requires that all
   the OR clauses check for either the projectId or organizationId"

Impact: any caller hitting getProjectModelProviders for a project
inheriting from team/org scope (Playground dropdown, evaluator picker,
experiment runner, optimization studio, langwatch_nlp resolution) gets
a 500. The unit tests (e40600e15) mocked prisma and bypassed middleware
— the integration file skipped every case due to env.mjs validation.

Why this is the right fix, not adding redundant projectId/organizationId
keys to the OR branches:

- Scope is the new tenancy boundary for this table (ADR-016). The
  service's findAllAccessibleForProject first looks up the project row
  (project.findUnique) to derive teamId + organizationId, then
  constrains the OR to those specific IDs — the tenancy check is done,
  just via a different column.
- Keying the OR on projectId would be wrong: TEAM/ORGANIZATION rows
  carry the projectId of the project they happened to be created
  under, not the tenancy boundary. Matching by that projectId would
  leak rows between sibling projects.
- EXEMPT_MODELS is how we already handle the other org-scoped gateway
  tables (GatewayBudget, GatewayChangeEvent, GatewayAuditLog,
  GatewayCacheRule, VirtualKeyProviderCredential). Consistent pattern.

Every other ModelProviderRepository method (findById / findByProvider /
findAll) still takes projectId explicitly and won't be affected.

* fix(projects/create-drawer): honor defaultTeamId when submit beats team query (#82)

Ariana Zone 1 prep repro: Dashboard "+ New Project" under acme-demo
(org root with a default team but no projects yet) opened the drawer
with defaultTeamId threaded through, but hitting Create returned
"Either teamId or newTeamName must be provided".

Root cause: two related race windows.

1. ProjectForm's useForm defaultValues seeded `teamId: ""`. A useEffect
   later reset it to defaultTeamId once teams.data arrived, but when
   that query returns an empty or RBAC-filtered array the reset never

- ProjectForm seeds `teamId: defaultTeamId ?? ""` at form construction.
  No race: the initial submit already carries the caller's hint.
- CreateProjectDrawer falls back to `defaultTeamId` when
  `data.teamId` is empty string (defense in depth for any future
  path that still hits the race).

onboarding, etc) — the teams.data-driven useEffect still picks the
first team.

Foundation:

  then SIGKILL on stop. Handle returns the supervised pid + stop().

- services/env.ts — thin wrapper around shared/env.ts scaffoldEnvFile so the

  langwatch_db database exists.
- services/redis.ts — write redis.conf with bind 127.0.0.1 + appendonly yes
  on first run, start redis-server, wait for redis-cli ping → PONG.
- services/clickhouse.ts — write a minimal config.xml on first run (custom
  http_port, tcp_port, path, listen_host, default user with empty password

fix(npx-server): use `pnpm -C <dir>` to avoid workspace-root script resolution

CI smoke run revealed the real reason `pnpm run build` was failing on every
runner:

    ERR_PNPM_NO_SCRIPT  Missing script: build
    Command "build" not found. Did you mean "pnpm run build:cli"?

`build:cli` is in the WORKSPACE ROOT package.json. langwatch/package.json
has the `build` script. So pnpm is resolving the root package.json, not
the langwatch sub-package, even though we passed `cwd: langwatchDir` to
execa. Confirmed: pnpm's workspace mode (via corepack, and apparently
sometimes plain pnpm too) prefers the workspace-root package.json regardless
of process cwd.

The official escape hatch is `pnpm -C <dir>` — same as `--dir <dir>`. It
forces pnpm to treat `<dir>` as the package and ignore workspace-root
script bubbling.

While we're here: drop the corepack indirection. Every CI runner with
pnpm/action-setup puts pnpm on PATH directly. `corepack pnpm` was an
unneeded layer.

fix(npx-server): prefer direct `pnpm` over `corepack pnpm` for -C flag handling

The previous fix used `pnpm -C <dir>` to force pnpm to resolve the langwatch
package's `build` script. That works for plain `pnpm`, but on CI runners
where the predep installer chain hits `corepack pnpm`, `corepack pnpm -C
<dir> run build` STILL hits "ERR_PNPM_NO_SCRIPT Missing script: build" —
corepack's shim swallows the `-C` flag and pnpm executes from its own cwd
(workspace root, no `build` script there).

message if neither is reachable.

fix(npx-server): sync tar.x extraction so chmod sees all files

Smoke #9 logs revealed a race: redis predep ran tar.x async, the Promise
resolved, then chmodSync on redis-cli failed with ENOENT. The tarball
itself is fine — locally tar.x extracts both redis-server and redis-cli;
served sha256 matches; tarball has both entries. The race only shows
up on CI's slower filesystem under parallel predep load (uv installer
is racing the same paths.bin dir, postgres extract is happening in a
sibling subdir). Async tar.x can resolve before the final entries are
stat-visible.

Switch both redis and postgres predeps to tar.x({ sync: true }) — sync
mode blocks until every entry is on disk. Add defensive existsSync
guards so any future extraction failure produces a clear error message
instead of a downstream ENOENT.

fix(npx-server): drop --with-openssl from postgres + better error on probe fail

Smoke #10 macOS failed at initdb with SIGABRT. Root cause: postgres was
built linking against keg-only \`brew openssl@3\` (path
/opt/homebrew/opt/openssl@3/lib/libssl.3.dylib hardcoded into postgres's
load commands). When the published tarball runs on a Mac without that
exact brew formula present, dyld can't resolve the dylib and any
postgres binary (including initdb) aborts on launch.

Fix by dropping --with-openssl entirely. SSL is unnecessary for our
embedded-postgres use case (langwatch always connects via 127.0.0.1)
and the resulting binary is self-contained — no runtime dependency
on user-installed brew formulae or distro libraries beyond libc/zlib.
Also drops openssl-dev from the alpine bootstrap and libssl-dev from
the apt installs since we don't link against them anymore.

Smoke #10 ARM separately failed with "postgres connect probe failed"
after pg_isready succeeded. Promote that error to include the psql
exit code + stderr so the next round's logs show what's actually
preventing the connection.

fix(npx-server): always-download redis+clickhouse + fix redis-arm64 lua link

Three independent fixes batched together:

1. Drop the `which redis-server` / `which clickhouse` PATH fallback in
   their detect() functions. With the fallback we'd happily use a user's
   brew/debian-installed redis 6.x or clickhouse 24.x against our pinned
   schema/config, leading to silent version-drift bugs (renamed commands,
   default ACL changes, column-type subtleties). Tarball costs are
   trivial — redis ~1.5MB, clickhouse cached after first install — so
   always-download is the predictable choice. Postgres stays
   detect-and-skip; 11MB tarball + ~80% of devs already have postgres
   makes the trade-off different there.

2. Redis-linux-arm64 build started failing in publish #6 with
   "undefined reference to luaopen_base" — redis's parallel Makefile
   races between redis-server's link step and the bundled lua compile
   on arm64 specifically. Build deps (lua + hiredis + hdr_histogram)
   first, then the binaries. Fixes the link race deterministically.

3. Add CloudFront invalidation to the publish workflow + drop tarball
   cache-control from `max-age=31536000, immutable` to `max-age=300`.
   We OVERWRITE keys when re-publishing the same upstream version
   (e.g. fixing a build flag), and CloudFront's 1-year default TTL
   was serving stale cached tarballs to predep clients despite fresh
   S3 uploads. Invalidation requires cloudfront:CreateInvalidation
   on the publisher IAM user — workflow soft-fails if not granted yet
   (langwatch-saas terraform follow-up).

fix(embedded-binaries): redis distclean+serial deps build

Publish #7 reproduced lua-link error on linux-x64 + linux-x64-musl
('hidden symbol luaM_realloc_ isn't defined') after my previous
'make -C deps lua hiredis hdr_histogram' attempt. The deps Makefile

fix(npx-server): wire publish workflow to release-please + bump to 3.1.0-beta.0

Three pipeline bugs that would have blocked any release-please-driven
publish, now fixed:

1. **Tag prefix gate.** The publish job fired on ANY release.published
   event — sdk-go@*, typescript-sdk@*, mcp-server@*, langevals@*, skills@*
   would all have triggered it. Gated on
   `startsWith(github.event.release.tag_name, 'langwatch@')` to match
   release-please's `<component>@<version>` tag format. Same pattern as
   publish-docker-app.yml and sibling SDK workflows.

2. **Tag-version parsing.** The version-mismatch check was stripping `v`
   (`${tag#v}`), but release-please tags are `langwatch@3.2.0` — strip
   `langwatch@` instead. Without this fix, every release would fail with
   "version mismatch: tag=langwatch@3.2.0 package.json=3.2.0".

3. **Root package.json autobump.** release-please-config.json's `.`
   package was bumping `langwatch/package.json` but not the root
   `package.json` (which is `@langwatch/server`). Added it to the
   `extra-files` list so both stay in lockstep.

Also:
- npm dist-tag now auto-derived from version: `3.1.0-beta.0` →
  `@prerelease`, `3.1.0` → `@latest`. Same convention as the scenario
  JS workflow. Beta/rc/alpha bumps don't auto-rollout to existing users.
- Documented Trusted Publishers setup at the top of the workflow:
  repo `langwatch/langwatch`, workflow `npx-server-publish.yml`, no
  environment. Once configured, NPM_API_TOKEN can be deleted (the
  `id-token: write` permission already in place is sufficient).
- Bumped root + langwatch/package.json to `3.1.0-beta.0` so the next
  workflow_dispatch publishes a beta under `@prerelease`, leaving
  `3.1.0` available for the eventual `@latest` cut via release-please.
- Test assertions on the literal version string now use semver regex
  so beta/rc bumps don't break CI.

fix(embedded-binaries): ship libpq + relocate macOS dylib install_names

Smoke #14 macOS + arm both timed out hitting postgres errors:
- arm: "psql: undefined symbol: PQchangePassword" — psql linked
  against the system libpq.so.5 on the runner (too old for pg 18).
- macOS: "Library not loaded: /Users/runner/work/langwatch/.../libpq.5.dylib"
  in initdb → SIGABRT.

Root cause for both: `make install-world-bin` installs binaries
ONLY, no shared libraries. So libpq.so.5 / libpq.5.dylib never made
it into the tarball. Switch to `make install` (full tree: bin + lib
+ share + include).

Even with libpq shipped, macOS embeds the absolute build path as the
dylib's install_name by default — binaries reference the exact
build-runner path. Add post-install install_name_tool pass:
- Rewrite each dylib's id to @rpath/<basename>
- For each binary, change every absolute-path dylib reference to
  @rpath/<basename> and add @loader_path/../lib to its rpath
That makes the tarball fully relocatable to any user's
~/.langwatch/bin/postgres/ install location.

fix(npx-server): license @langwatch/server as Apache-2.0 (repo stays BSL)

The GitHub repo as a whole is BSL 1.1 (LICENSE.md) — that stays as-is.
The @langwatch/server npm package is independently licensed Apache-2.0.

npm's tarball construction has two awkward constraints we have to
work around:

1. npm auto-includes LICENSE-shaped files at the package root regardless
   of files[]/.npmignore — so we can't just exclude /LICENSE.md from the
   published tarball.
2. The same auto-include rule trips on backup names like LICENSE.md.bak,
   so a naive "save then restore" at repo root leaks the backup into
   the tarball.

Solution: scripts/pack-npm.sh swaps /LICENSE.md (BSL) with
/LICENSE-NPM.txt (Apache-2.0) for the duration of `pnpm pack`, with
the BSL backup staged in /tmp via mktemp (out of npm's auto-include
reach). A trap on EXIT restores LICENSE.md whether pack succeeds or
fails.

- New: /LICENSE-NPM.txt (canonical Apache-2.0 text, listed in .npmignore
  so the source itself doesn't ship)
- New: /scripts/pack-npm.sh (the swap+pack+restore wrapper)
- /package.json: license MIT → Apache-2.0; pack:npm + release:dry-run
  scripts now route through the wrapper
- /.github/workflows/npx-server-publish.yml: pack step calls the
  wrapper; tarball sanity check now asserts the shipped LICENSE.md is
  the Apache-2.0 text (catches anyone bypassing the wrapper)

Verified end-to-end with `bash scripts/pack-npm.sh`:
- pre-pack:  LICENSE.md = BSL
- tarball:   package/LICENSE.md = Apache-2.0; package.json license =
             "Apache-2.0"; no LICENSE-NPM.txt or *.bak leakage
- post-pack: LICENSE.md = BSL (restored)

3.1.0-beta.0 was published before this change with license=MIT — that's
on npm and won't be republished. The next manual beta or release-please
cut will pick up the correct Apache-2.0 license.

fix(embedded-binaries): macOS install_name_tool loop tolerant of empty matches

GitHub Actions runs bash with set -eo pipefail. When the grep pipeline
finds zero install_prefix references in a binary (some pgsql helpers
don't link any postgres dylib), grep exits 1, the pipeline propagates
non-zero, and the whole step bails — even though there's literally
nothing to do for that binary.

Capture grep output into a var with || true, then iterate. Empty input
just means zero install_name_tool calls, which is correct.

with the libpq fix; this is just hardening the macOS post-install
relocation step.

fix(npx-server): run prisma generate after --prod install

When distAlreadyBuilt=true (published tarball ships dist/), we install
langwatch with --prod to skip ~50 devDependencies. But pnpm install
does NOT auto-generate the prisma client — no postinstall hook fires
prisma generate, contrary to my earlier assumption. Result: the
langwatch app crashes at boot with `Cannot find module '.prisma/client/index'`.

uv venv + pnpm install came up green, then `pnpm prisma migrate
deploy` errored loading the @prisma/client index because .prisma/
wasn't generated.

invoke `pnpm -C langwatch exec prisma generate`. The !distAlreadyBuilt
path stays untouched — the full build script's start:prepare:files
already runs prisma:generate:typescript.

assumptions:

   doesn't auto-generate the prisma client; without devDeps in scope

2. (beta.2) `Cannot find module '~/server/app-layer/app'` from

   path-alias resolver fails inside the published-tarball layout when
   --prod skips devDependencies. Reproed independently of the runtime;
   the transitive dep tsx's resolver hits is unclear and chasing it

fix(npx-server): relocate @langwatch/server tree out of node_modules

tsx 4.x's CJS resolveTsPaths intentionally skips the tsconfig path-alias
matcher when the requesting file's path includes "/node_modules/" (its
guard against transpiling third-party deps). Because npx unpacks
@langwatch/server INTO node_modules, every src file in the langwatch
app inherits that skip — so `~/server/app-layer/...` imports never get
aliased and `pnpm clickhouse:migrate` (and the langwatch app boot)
crash on `Cannot find module '~/server/...'`.

Fix: copy the entire @langwatch/server tree (langwatch/, langwatch_nlp/,
langevals/, python-sdk/, etc.) to LANGWATCH_HOME/app/ on first install,
out of any node_modules ancestry. All downstream services resolve paths
via a single appRoot() helper that prefers the relocated tree.

- new services/app-dir.ts: ensureAppDir() rsyncs (or tar-pipes) the tree,
  excluding node_modules. Idempotent via a .installed-version marker.
- services/{node-deps,migrate,langwatch,langwatch-nlp,langevals,venvs}.ts:
  drop ad-hoc __dirname walking, use appRoot() everywhere.
- runtime.ts orchestration: ensureAppDir runs BEFORE the parallel install
  block so venvs + node-deps both resolve to the relocated tree.
- Dev mode (workspace checkout, source not under node_modules) is a
  no-op: tsx guard doesn't fire and editing in-place still works.

fix(npx-server): ship aigateway prebuilt monobinary, drop local-build fallback (beta.9)

The aigateway predep was silently falling through to a local Go build on
end-user machines because:

  1. We never published the prebuilt aigateway-{platform} artifacts to a
     GH release matching the npm version — the v3.1.0-beta.X tags don't
     exist and v3.1.0 has no aigateway assets.
  2. The HTTP 404 on the download was caught and the local-build path
     (findRepoRoot → go build ./cmd/service) succeeded silently because
     the npm tarball ships go.mod + cmd/service.
  3. Local build also requires Go installed on the user's box, which
     it isn't on most.

Fix is three-part:

  - aigateway predep: gate local-build behind LANGWATCH_AIGATEWAY_DEV_BUILD=1
    (opt-in for langwatch dev workflow only). 404 on prebuilt = hard error
    with a clear message pointing devs at the env var.
  - npm tarball: drop go.mod, go.sum, cmd/, pkg/, services/ from files[].
    The local-build path was the only consumer and it's now opt-in. Saves
    ~600kB and removes the silent-foot-gun escape hatch.
  - npx-server-publish.yml: add Go setup + cross-compile aigateway for
    linux-{amd64,arm64} + darwin-{amd64,arm64} + create or update the
    GH release at v\$VERSION with the binaries attached, before npm publish.

fix(npx-server-smoke): harden assertions so the aigateway local-build path can't slip past CI

The matrix happily passed for weeks while the aigateway predep was silently
falling through to a local 'go build ./cmd/service' on the runner. Root

local-build fallback)'), so the 39MB go-build added a tolerable 30s and
the smoke job's only assertion was 'aigateway is healthy'. Both paths

       - `aigateway --version` matches package.json version (the prebuilt
         is built with -X main.Version=$VERSION ldflag; an older or
         locally-built binary would print 'dev' or 'unknown').
       - `file ~/.langwatch/bin/aigateway` confirms the binary is stripped
         (the prebuilt uses '-s -w'; an in-tree go build does not).
  3. cli.log scan: must not contain 'building from local checkout' (the
     local-build path's task.output message).

Also align the smoke pack flow with the publish workflow: use
scripts/pack-npm.sh so the smoke tarball matches what end users get
(Apache LICENSE swap, exact files[]). And tarball-content guard rail —
fail if go.mod / cmd/ / pkg/ / services/ ever sneak back in.

refactor regress without anyone noticing. (1) breaks the silent path,
(2) verifies the artifact, (3) verifies the runtime path.

fix(npx-server): blank-screen SPA on browser load — vite externalize stub + dev jsx-runtime

Two release-blocker bugs caught by rchaves on beta.{8..11} dogfood
("have you folks been actually dogfooding and screenshotting using
playwright from /qa-browser skill?"). Both ship with beta.12.

**Bug 1: object-inspect's util.inspect Proxy throws on `.custom`**

object-inspect (transitive via side-channel/qs) does:
    var inspectCustom = require('./util.inspect');
    var inspectSymbol = inspectCustom && hasMap
      && typeof inspectCustom.custom === 'symbol'
      ? inspectCustom.custom : null;

Its package.json sets `"browser": { "./util.inspect.js": false }`. Vite
turns the `false` mapping into a Proxy that throws on ANY property
access — including the defensive `typeof .custom === 'symbol'` short-
circuit object-inspect uses. Result: command-bar chunk crashes at
module-eval, blank screen, console error
    `Module "" has been externalized for browser compatibility.
     Cannot access ".custom" in client code.`

Fix: a tiny resolve-id vite plugin (patchObjectInspectBrowserStub) that
intercepts `require('./util.inspect')` ONLY when the importer is inside
node_modules/object-inspect/, and routes it to our existing noop-css.cjs
shim. Now `inspectCustom.custom` returns `undefined`, the short-circuit
works as designed.

**Bug 2: dev jsx-runtime in production bundle**

@vitejs/plugin-react reads `process.env.NODE_ENV` at transformer-init
to decide between `_jsx(...)` (production runtime) and `_jsxDEV(...)`
(dev runtime). The dev runtime is missing from React's prod build, so
a dev-runtime bundle crashes with `(0, H.jsxDEV) is not a function`.

The publish workflow set NODE_ENV=production at the job level, but
plugin-react had already cached its decision before our defineConfig
function-form callback could flip it. The `define` block in vite.config
only handles `process.env.NODE_ENV` references in user code — too late
for the runtime selection.

Fix: prefix `NODE_ENV=production` directly in the langwatch package.json
build + build:client scripts so it's set in the env BEFORE vite spawns
plugin-react. Verified: chunk H.jsxDEV calls go from 4264 → 0.

Both fixes verified end-to-end with playwright on smith11 (port 6880)
and julia13 (port 6770) — /auth/signin renders, 0 console errors,
sign-in form is interactive. Filed feedback memory
'always playwright the actual UI before declaring an npx beta green'
so we don't repeat the curl-only QA gap.

fix(npx-server): spawn the langwatch BullMQ workers — the queue had no consumer

services/langwatch.ts spawns `pnpm run start:app` (= `tsx src/server.mts`)
which starts ONLY the API server. The langwatch workers (collector,
evaluations, track-event, topic-clustering, usage-stats) are normally
started by `pnpm run start` → scripts/start.sh, which we deliberately
bypass to avoid the dev-mode concurrently overhead.

Result: anything in the UI that depends on a processed trace (the
/messages list, /analytics rollups, evaluator runs) sat forever showing
"Waiting for first trace…" — caught when smith dogfooded the playground
on beta.12. The LLM call returned and the gateway logged usage, but the
spans queued in Redis with no consumer, so they never landed in
clickhouse's trace_summaries table.

Fix: services/langwatch-workers.ts spawns `pnpm run start:workers`
(= `tsx src/workers.ts`) as a sibling supervised service, started AFTER
the langwatch app's /api/health probe lands so it inherits a fully-
migrated DB + reachable Redis. No HTTP healthcheck — workers don't bind
a port, lifecycle is inferred from process state and visible in the
log-tee. Sync `bus.emit({type: "healthy", service: "workers"})` so the
panel/log-tee shows the service alongside the others.

Wired into runtime.ts startAll's phase 3 right after the parallel
nlp+langevals+gateway+langwatch promise resolves — workers depend on
the app being up + Redis being healthy. Added "workers" to the
ServiceName union so log paths/pid files use the same naming convention
as everything else.

the langwatch-workers mock + locateLangwatchDir to the node-deps mock
since the workers service imports it.

langwatch_nlp's evaluator runner uses the python SDK's
`langwatch.get_endpoint()` to POST evaluator results back to the
langwatch API. The SDK defaults to https://app.langwatch.ai when
LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT is unset, which on a self-host install means every
evaluator hits the hosted cloud API with the wrong API key and 401s.

Symptom from julia14 dogfood: opened an Experiments Workbench, added
a prompt + ROUGE Score evaluator from the Expected Answer category,
clicked Run. Prompt rows got LLM responses fine (3-7s each), but the
evaluator column rendered "ROUGE Score" with no number. langwatch_nlp
log spammed:

  Error running evaluators/.../evaluate: HTTPStatusError("Client error
  '401 Unauthorized' for url 'https://app.langwatch.ai/api/evaluations
  /evaluators/evaluator_V6TNQ-uO3bGXXOAqvwZw1/evaluate'")

SDK routes callbacks to the local stack instead of cloud. host is
already computed for BASE_HOST/NEXTAUTH_URL, just reuse it.

fix(self-host): evaluator callbacks 401 against app.langwatch.ai despite LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT scaffold

Julia traced the bug end-to-end on beta.15 — even with the scaffolded
LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT correctly inherited by langwatch_nlp + ProcessPool
children, evaluator runs still hit
  https://app.langwatch.ai/api/evaluations/evaluators/<id>/evaluate
and 401'd, leaving experiment columns empty.

Root cause: python-sdk/src/langwatch/client.py's `_endpoint_url` is a
ClassVar that's only re-read from env on the FIRST setup() call — and
only when it's still empty. Once anything (an import-time helper, a
ProcessPool child auto-init, dspy's request_cache rehydration, etc.)
calls setup() before LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT is in the worker's env, the
class variable pins to "https://app.langwatch.ai" for the process
lifetime. All subsequent setup() calls — including the workflow-runner's
own — short-circuit because the elif `not Client._endpoint_url` clause
is now falsy.

This is not just an npx-flow bug — every self-host install hit it. The
LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT env scaffold from beta.15 set the var correctly, but
the SDK was ignoring it after the initial pin.

Two-part fix:

1. python-sdk: re-read LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT on every setup() call. If
   endpoint_url is explicitly passed, that wins (existing behavior). If
   the env var is set, it overrides any prior pin. The default
   "https://app.langwatch.ai" only applies when neither is set AND the
   classvar is empty. One extra os.getenv per setup is negligible.

2. langwatch_nlp: belt-and-suspenders — the workflow runner's setup()
   calls in execute_event.py + execute_evaluation.py now pass
   endpoint_url=os.environ.get("LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT") explicitly, so
   even if a future python-sdk regression re-introduces the pin, the
   evaluator callback URL is forced to the local stack.

fix(self-host): CREDENTIALS_SECRET rotation no longer crashes the UI / orphans encrypted creds

Caught on julia14's beta.16 dogfood: tearing down + restarting the npx
stack regenerated ~/.langwatch/.env with a fresh CREDENTIALS_SECRET,
which orphaned the encrypted ModelProvider rows in the persisted
postgres data dir. Result:
- modelProvider.getAllForProject TRPC query 500'd hard with 'Failed
  to decrypt: Data may be corrupted'
- the entire UI was blocked because every dashboard load touches
  modelProvider — couldn't even add a fresh provider until manual
  `DELETE FROM langwatch_db."ModelProvider"` against postgres.

Two-layer fix:

1. **Persist secrets across .env regenerations** (packages/server/src/
   shared/env.ts). On first scaffold we write the generated values for
   NEXTAUTH_SECRET, CREDENTIALS_SECRET, API_TOKEN_JWT_SECRET, and the
   gateway pepper/secrets to a sidecar `~/.langwatch/secrets.json`
   (mode 0600). Subsequent scaffolds (e.g. user `rm`'d the .env to
   start clean but kept data/postgres/) overlay those persisted values
   into the new .env so encrypted rows stay decryptable + sessions
   stay valid.

2. **Graceful decrypt failure in the model-provider repository**
   (langwatch/src/server/modelProviders/modelProvider.repository.ts).
   Even when (1) prevents new rotations, existing self-hosters who hit
   the old behavior have orphaned rows. Wrap the decrypt() call in a
   try/catch — log a warning, return null for that customKeys field
   so the provider becomes effectively keyless instead of crashing the
   whole list. User can then re-enter keys via the UI.

The decrypt() wrap is deliberately scoped to model providers only —
other decrypt sites (elasticsearch creds in organization router, S3
credentials, scenario secrets) all happen on routes that don't gate
the entire UI dashboard, so the fail-loud behavior there is fine.
Filing a sweep for those as a separate hardening pass.

fix(npx-server): bust venv lock-hash when extras change so beta.17 rebuilds langevals with --extra all

fix(npx-server): CR feedback on PR #3486 — SIGINT race, pgid foot-gun, health-probe timeout

Three fixes from the CodeRabbit review on the npx-server PR; all
self-contained, no behavior change for the happy path.

**1. cli.ts: register SIGINT/SIGTERM before installServices/startAll.**
The handlers were attached *after* startAll returned, so Ctrl+C during
the boot window did nothing — supervised children (postgres, redis,
clickhouse, etc.) got reparented to launchd/init and kept running with
their listening ports held. The handler now registers up front; a
mutable `handles` ref captures whatever's been spawned so far. A
`shuttingDown` guard prevents double-firing if a second signal arrives
during the first teardown.

**2. port-conflict/detect.ts: skip pgid ≤ 1 in killPidGroups.**
`process.kill(-pgid, sig)` interprets pgid=0 as "this process group" —
i.e. signals THIS Node process and any of its children — and pgid=1 as
"every process in the system that this user can signal". Both are
foot-guns the `Number.isFinite` check didn't catch (0 and 1 are finite).
Skip explicitly with `pgid > 1`.

**3. services/health.ts: AbortController-based per-request timeout.**
`fetch(url)` without a timeout will hang forever if the target accept()s
the connection but never replies — typical during ClickHouse startup or
Postgres mid-recovery. `pollUntilHealthy`'s outer timeout was the only
guard, and a single hung request consumed the entire budget. Now every
probe gets a 5s default request-level timeout via AbortController, with
the reason "request timed out after Nms" surfaced so debugging stays
clear.

Tests: 62/62 pass, typecheck clean.

fix(e2e-ci): pass --ignore-workspace when installing agentic-e2e-tests deps

The @langwatch/server CLI introduced a repo-root pnpm-workspace.yaml
(packages: [packages/*]) that pnpm picks up from any subdirectory. When
e2e-ci runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` from agentic-e2e-tests/,
pnpm walks up, finds the root workspace, and scopes the install to
`packages/*` only — agentic-e2e-tests's @playwright/test never lands in
its node_modules and the next step fails with
ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_EXEC_FIRST_FAIL.

agentic-e2e-tests is intentionally standalone (own pnpm-lock.yaml,
not a workspace member), so --ignore-workspace is the correct override
for the install step.

fix(npx-server): CR feedback on PR #3486 — --yes hang risk + smoke if-env scope

Two more CodeRabbit review fixes, both narrowly scoped.

**resolve.ts: --yes interactive fallthrough.**
When `--yes` was set AND no port shift could free every conflicting
slot, the code dropped through to the interactive prompts() call and
hung indefinitely on a CI runner / unattended caller. Exit cleanly with
a non-zero status + a clear stderr message so the wrapper can
distinguish "no resolution possible" from a deadlocked process.

**smoke.yml: secret check in step-level if.**
`if: env.OPENAI_API_KEY_CI != ''` referenced an env var that was only
ever set at step-level — and step-level `env:` is populated AFTER the
if-check is evaluated. So the condition was always empty and the
workflow probe was always skipped, even when the secret was configured.
Read `${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY_CI }}` directly in the if-check
expression so the gate works.

fix(npx-server): CR feedback on PR #3486 — inline tar imports + unused ctx

Three more CodeRabbit fixes, julia lane:

1. predeps/clickhouse.ts + predeps/redis.ts: hoist `await import("tar")`

   forbids inline `import()` (CLAUDE.md "Using inline `import('...')`
   anywhere"); the only documented exemption is for langwatch/src/server.ts
   where env-load-order constraints force it. predeps run after the CLI
   has already loaded — no env-load-order issue.

2. services/node-deps.ts: drop the unused `ctx` parameter from

3. services/node-deps.ts: clarify the `resolvePnpm()` block comment. It

fix(npx-server): CR feedback — drain log pipes before close + watchdog the events test

Two test/runtime hardening fixes from CodeRabbit review.

**spawn.ts: drain stdout/stderr pipes before closing logStream.**
The `child.on('exit')` handler called `logStream.end()` synchronously,
but the readline interfaces wrapping stdout/stderr may still have
buffered chunks that haven't flushed. Result: tail lines from short-
lived children sometimes missed the on-disk log (caught by
spawn.integration.test 'row-2' assertion intermittently failing).

`pipeLines` now returns a Promise that resolves on the readline
interface's 'close' event (stream EOF). The exit handler awaits both
stdout + stderr drains via Promise.all before closing the log file +
emitting the lifecycle event.

**runtime.test.ts: watchdog the events collector loop.**
The "emits starting+healthy events for every service that starts" test
loops `for await` over `runtime.events(ctx)` until 7 healthy events
arrive, then breaks. If a regression makes one service skip its
'healthy' emit, the loop hangs forever and the whole test runner
freezes.

Race the collector against a 5s timeout that rejects with a clear
"got N healthy events" message — turns a hang into an immediate
visible failure.

* refactor(evaluations-v3): direct onLocalConfigChange + split createMappingsConfig (#3460 items 1+2) (#3465)

Stacked on PR #3457. Two related design smells the /review on #3457 surfaced:

ITEM 1: createEvaluatorEditorCallbacks shim ignored its `id` arg.

Before, TargetCell.tsx's chip-edit path needed to forge a target shape just
to feed `localEvaluatorConfig` updates into the evaluator (not the target):

  setFlowCallbacks("evaluatorEditor", createEvaluatorEditorCallbacks({
    targetId: target.id,
    updateTarget: (_id, updates) => {  // _id is ignored
      if (updates.localEvaluatorConfig !== undefined) {
        updateEvaluator(evaluator.id, { localEvaluatorConfig: ... });
      }
    },
    onMappingChange,
  }));

The `_id` was a smoking gun: the chip's local config does not belong to a
target, it belongs to the evaluator. The helper's `targetId+updateTarget`
contract is a *target-bound convenience*, not a universal API.

Add `onLocalConfigChange` as a direct param. Direct wins over target-bound
convenience when both are provided. Existing target-bound callers (the
prompt/agent/evaluator-target paths in useOpenTargetEditor.ts) keep
working unchanged.

ITEM 2: createMappingsConfig had a compound return that wasn't honest.

Before, TargetCell's `createMappingsConfig` returned `{ mappingsConfig,
onMappingChange }` — but the name implied it returned just mappingsConfig.
Callers had to deconstruct both and route them to different APIs (the
serializable mappingsConfig into openDrawer's complexProps, the durable
onMappingChange into setFlowCallbacks). Single Responsibility violation.

Split into two named useCallbacks:
- `buildMappingsConfig(evaluator)` returns `{ availableSources,
  initialMappings }` — strictly the serializable part.
- `buildOnMappingChange(evaluator)` returns the bound mapping callback.

The chip's `onEdit` body now reads cleanly: each piece goes where it
belongs, no destructuring of a misnamed compound return.

Validation:
- pnpm typecheck clean
- pnpm test:unit src/evaluations-v3/ — 835/843 pass (+3 new tests on the
  helper's direct vs target-bound precedence; all 832 prior tests still
  pass with no behaviour change)
- TargetCell.test.tsx's `onMappingChange` and `mappingsConfig` invariants
  still hold (assertions check the same drawer/flowCallbacks shape)

Stacks on #3457. Will be ready to merge after #3457 lands.

Refs #3460.

fix(auth): diagnostic logs on auth-fail + restore X-Auth-Token fallback regression (#3520)

fix(auth): diagnostic logging on auth failure + don't let proxy Authorization headers poison X-Auth-Token fallback

Context: a customer behind a corporate network reported that scenario events
stopped reaching us, while OTel traces (using Authorization: Bearer) kept
flowing fine through the same SDK process. We had no way to attribute their
401s in CloudWatch (the auth failure paths logged nothing or only minimal
fields), and we found a real fallback regression in extractCredentials while
investigating.

Two changes in this PR:

1. Diagnostic logging on every auth failure
   The unified auth middleware now emits a single WARN line on every 401 with
   userAgent, traceparent, x-forwarded-for / x-real-ip, request path/method,
   and a hasEmptyAuthToken flag that distinguishes "X-Auth-Token sent as
   empty string" (typically a misconfigured customer SDK) from "no auth
   header at all" (typically a probe). traceparent in particular lets us
   join a failed POST to the customer's downstream OTel trace, which usually
   carries identifying metadata even when the auth path doesn't.

   The diagnostic struct never includes raw token values or request body.

2. extractCredentials no longer returns null on a malformed Authorization
   header when X-Auth-Token is also present
   The OLD pre-PAT auth middleware preferred X-Auth-Token unconditionally
   (X-Auth-Token ?? Authorization). The unified middleware introduced with
   PAT (#3212/#3213, deployed 2026-04-26) prioritized Authorization and
   returned null immediately if Authorization started with "Basic " or
   "Bearer " but was malformed — regardless of whether a perfectly valid
   X-Auth-Token was also present.

   This breaks customers behind corporate proxies that inject their own
   Authorization header (NTLM/Negotiate are fine because the prefix doesn't
   match; Basic with a non-decodable / no-colon payload is the failure
   case). Empty Bearer ("Authorization: Bearer ") had the same problem.

   Fix: on malformed/empty Basic or Bearer, fall through to the X-Auth-Token
   path instead of short-circuiting to null. The behavior for well-formed
   Basic/Bearer is unchanged.

Spec: specs/auth/diagnostic-logging-on-auth-failure.feature
Tests: 22 passing including new fallback-poisoning coverage + diagnostic
       fields (no raw tokens leaked, traceparent/UA captured).

* fix(gateway): legacy env-var aliases so chart/saas deploys actually read config

The gateway's `LoadConfig` uses `pkg/config.Hydrate`, which resolves env vars
by concatenating struct-level `env:` tags with `_` (e.g. `Server config.Server
\`env:"SERVER"\`` + `Addr string \`env:"ADDR"\`` → env var `SERVER_ADDR`).

Both `charts/gateway/templates/configmap.yaml` and `langwatch-saas`'s
`infrastructure/gateway.tf` historically shipped a different prefix
(`GATEWAY_LISTEN_ADDR`, `GATEWAY_CONTROL_PLANE_URL`, `GATEWAY_LOG_LEVEL`,
`GATEWAY_OTEL_DEFAULT_ENDPOINT`). The Go code never read those names, so
every gateway pod ran on dev defaults — most importantly
`ControlPlane.BaseURL = http://localhost:5560`, which is unreachable from
inside any prod pod.

Symptom on the running prod gateway today: pods came up healthy, all three
probes (`/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/startupz`) returned 200, but every real VK
request returned `HTTP 500 auth_upstream_unavailable`. Verified by
port-forwarding to a prod pod and POSTing to `/v1/chat/completions`.

Fix: a small alias layer in `LoadConfig` that, for the four affected env
vars, falls back to the legacy chart/saas name when the canonical name is
absent or empty. Canonical always wins. Empty-string semantics match
`Hydrate` (empty == not set).

This unblocks the prod gateway as soon as the new image rolls — no
saas-side terraform change required. The legacy aliases are marked
DEPRECATE and can be dropped once chart/terraform users migrate to the
canonical names (target: v1.2 or 90 days post-v1).

Tested:
- TestLoadConfig_Defaults — required secrets only, defaults preserved
- TestLoadConfig_CanonicalEnv — canonical names land on the right fields
- TestLoadConfig_LegacyAliases — legacy names map onto canonical fields
- TestLoadConfig_CanonicalBeatsLegacy — canonical wins when both set

Follow-ups in the same PR: rename the chart configmap to use canonical
names so new self-hosters never hit the legacy path; full self-hosting
docs sweep.
