* fix(gateway-chart): align configmap + deployment env vars with code reality

The chart's `templates/configmap.yaml` shipped ~25 `GATEWAY_*` env vars and
the deployment template injected three more secret-bearing ones, but the
Go gateway (services/aigateway/) reads almost none of them. The few that
DO matter were named with the wrong prefix.

Truth checked against `services/aigateway/config.go` + `pkg/config/{server,otel}.go`:
the Hydrate library walks parent/child `env:"…"` tags and joins them
with `_`. Resolved canonical names are e.g. `SERVER_ADDR`,
`LW_GATEWAY_BASE_URL`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `OTEL_OTLP_ENDPOINT` — not
`GATEWAY_LISTEN_ADDR`, `GATEWAY_CONTROL_PLANE_URL`, etc.

Result of the mismatch: the chart-deployed gateway pod ignored every
`GATEWAY_*` env var and ran on dev defaults, including
`ControlPlane.BaseURL = http://localhost:5560`. The pod passed
`/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/startupz`, but every real VK request returned
`HTTP 500 auth_upstream_unavailable` because the auth resolver couldn't
reach the control plane. Verified live on prod by port-forwarding to a
gateway pod and POSTing to `/v1/chat/completions`.

This commit:

- **configmap.yaml**: kept only the env vars the gateway actually reads,
  renamed to canonical names: `SERVER_ADDR`, `LOG_LEVEL`,
  `LW_GATEWAY_BASE_URL`, `OTEL_OTLP_ENDPOINT`,
  `SERVER_MAX_REQUEST_BODY_BYTES`. The other ~25 dropped — they were
  silently ignored before, dropping them avoids misleading operators
  into thinking they're tuning behavior. Forward-compat for v1.1 lives
  in values.yaml; wiring it at the env-var layer is a v1.1 task.

- **deployment.yaml**: dropped the secret-bearing env blocks that the
  gateway code never read (`GATEWAY_REDIS_URL` — no Redis client in the
  gateway, auth cache is in-process LRU; `GATEWAY_ADMIN_AUTH_TOKEN` —
  no admin/pprof listener; `GATEWAY_OTEL_DEFAULT_AUTH_TOKEN` — no OTel
  auth-token field on the config struct). Replaced with an inline
  comment documenting why each was removed and pointing OTel-auth
  customers at `OTEL_OTLP_HEADERS` (the actual mechanism).

The matching code-side change in `services/aigateway/config.go`
(commit 92d489a50) adds a backward-compat alias layer so the
existing langwatch-saas terraform deployment — which still ships the
`GATEWAY_*` legacy names directly — keeps working until the next
saas-side rename. New self-hosters using this chart get the
canonical names from day one.

feat(scenarios): http agent url template interpolation (lw#3389) (#3390)

* feat(scenarios): HTTP agent URL template interpolation (lw#3389)

Step 1 of #3385. Renders `config.url` through Liquid with the same
template context as `bodyTemplate`, so HTTP agents can build URLs like
`/conversations/{{threadId}}/messages` dynamically.

- Shared `http-template-engine.ts` with two Liquid instances
  (urlLiquid + bodyLiquid) configured identically, so workflow HTTP
  nodes and scenario HTTP agents render via one pipeline.
- URL values from `{{ expr }}` are URL-encoded by default via Liquid's
  `outputEscape` hook — applied AFTER filter chains — so interpolated
  data can't break URL structure. Literal path segments (`/chat/`) are
  preserved verbatim.
- `| raw` filter escape hatch: `{{x | raw}}` marks a reference as safe,
  skipping URL-encoding for that reference only. Registered with
  `raw: true` so liquidjs skips outputEscape natively.
- Body interpolation is NOT URL-encoded — bodyTemplate behavior preserved.
- Non-serialized adapter's regex body-templating replaced with Liquid to
  match the serialized adapter — single render pipeline across both.
- SSRF validation runs against the RESOLVED URL: render happens before
  ssrfSafeFetch, so interpolated `localhost` / `127.0.0.1` / AWS metadata
  IPs still hit the existing SSRF rejection path.
- `TemplateRenderError` surfaces malformed Liquid with `field: "url" | "bodyTemplate"`.

Tests: 37 cases for the DB-backed adapter + 32 for the serialized
adapter. Covers URL interpolation, default encoding, `| raw` escape
hatch, conditional branches, SSRF regression for private IPs, and
malformed-template error typing.

Note: replaces the string-replace body-template path in the DB-backed
adapter — body templates that referenced undefined variables previously
left `{{foo}}` literal in the output. With Liquid, undefined variables
render as empty string (matching the serialized adapter's existing
behavior). Production agents always supply user messages, so the common
path is byte-identical.

Out of scope (stays in #3385 phase 2): response captures, per-run
capturedValues state, `{{captured.*}}` namespace, JSONPath capture
extraction.

Refs: #3389, #3385

* fix(npx-server): use `pnpm -C <dir>` to avoid workspace-root script resolution

CI smoke run revealed the real reason `pnpm run build` was failing on every
runner:

    ERR_PNPM_NO_SCRIPT  Missing script: build
    Command "build" not found. Did you mean "pnpm run build:cli"?

`build:cli` is in the WORKSPACE ROOT package.json. langwatch/package.json
has the `build` script. So pnpm is resolving the root package.json, not
the langwatch sub-package, even though we passed `cwd: langwatchDir` to
execa. Confirmed: pnpm's workspace mode (via corepack, and apparently
sometimes plain pnpm too) prefers the workspace-root package.json regardless
of process cwd.

The official escape hatch is `pnpm -C <dir>` — same as `--dir <dir>`. It
forces pnpm to treat `<dir>` as the package and ignore workspace-root
script bubbling.

While we're here: drop the corepack indirection. Every CI runner with
pnpm/action-setup puts pnpm on PATH directly. `corepack pnpm` was an
unneeded layer.

stat-visible.

exact brew formula present, dyld can't resolve the dylib and any
postgres binary (including initdb) aborts on launch.

embedded-postgres use case (langwatch always connects via 127.0.0.1)
and the resulting binary is self-contained — no runtime dependency
on user-installed brew formulae or distro libraries beyond libc/zlib.
Also drops openssl-dev from the alpine bootstrap and libssl-dev from
the apt installs since we don't link against them anymore.

after pg_isready succeeded. Promote that error to include the psql
exit code + stderr so the next round's logs show what's actually
preventing the connection.

   brew/debian-installed redis 6.x or clickhouse 24.x against our pinned
   schema/config, leading to silent version-drift bugs (renamed commands,
   default ACL changes, column-type subtleties). Tarball costs are
   trivial — redis ~1.5MB, clickhouse cached after first install — so
   always-download is the predictable choice. Postgres stays
   detect-and-skip; 11MB tarball + ~80% of devs already have postgres
   makes the trade-off different there.

   "undefined reference to luaopen_base" — redis's parallel Makefile
   races between redis-server's link step and the bundled lua compile
   on arm64 specifically. Build deps (lua + hiredis + hdr_histogram)
   first, then the binaries. Fixes the link race deterministically.

   cache-control from `max-age=31536000, immutable` to `max-age=300`.
   We OVERWRITE keys when re-publishing the same upstream version
   (e.g. fixing a build flag), and CloudFront's 1-year default TTL
   was serving stale cached tarballs to predep clients despite fresh
   S3 uploads. Invalidation requires cloudfront:CreateInvalidation

* fix(npx-server): license @langwatch/server as Apache-2.0 (repo stays BSL)

The GitHub repo as a whole is BSL 1.1 (LICENSE.md) — that stays as-is.
The @langwatch/server npm package is independently licensed Apache-2.0.

npm's tarball construction has two awkward constraints we have to
work around:

1. npm auto-includes LICENSE-shaped files at the package root regardless
   of files[]/.npmignore — so we can't just exclude /LICENSE.md from the
   published tarball.
2. The same auto-include rule trips on backup names like LICENSE.md.bak,
   so a naive "save then restore" at repo root leaks the backup into
   the tarball.

/LICENSE-NPM.txt (Apache-2.0) for the duration of `pnpm pack`, with
the BSL backup staged in /tmp via mktemp (out of npm's auto-include
reach). A trap on EXIT restores LICENSE.md whether pack succeeds or
fails.

  so the source itself doesn't ship)
- New: /scripts/pack-npm.sh (the swap+pack+restore wrapper)
- /package.json: license MIT → Apache-2.0; pack:npm + release:dry-run
  scripts now route through the wrapper
- /.github/workflows/npx-server-publish.yml: pack step calls the
  wrapper; tarball sanity check now asserts the shipped LICENSE.md is
  the Apache-2.0 text (catches anyone bypassing the wrapper)

- tarball:   package/LICENSE.md = Apache-2.0; package.json license =

- post-pack: LICENSE.md = BSL (restored)

  drop ad-hoc __dirname walking, use appRoot() everywhere.
- runtime.ts orchestration: ensureAppDir runs BEFORE the parallel install
  block so venvs + node-deps both resolve to the relocated tree.

* fix(otel): emit projectId + customerTraceIds on every /api/otel/v1 error

Customer reports of "we sent traces but they didn't arrive" are nearly
impossible to triage today because every OTLP error path returns silently:
401s log nothing, the 429 plan-limit branch returns without logging the
project, and body-parse failures don't include the customer's trace_id.
This came up live during a customer investigation — we couldn't tell
whether the 429 spikes on /api/otel/v1/traces belonged to that tenant
because the access log has no projectId, no IP, and no body context.

Bring /api/otel/v1/{traces,logs,metrics} up to the same diagnostic shape
the unified-auth middleware emits for /api/scenario-events (PR #3520):

- Auth failures (no creds, invalid token, DB error, PAT-permission-denied)
  now emit a WARN with the standard auth-diagnostic fingerprint
  (path, method, userAgent, traceparent, forwardedFor, hasEmptyAuthToken,
  tokenType, hasProjectId) so on-call can attribute a 401 without asking
  the customer to reproduce.
- Plan-limit 429 now logs "Project has reached plan limit" with projectId,
  count, planName, maxMessagesPerMonth — matching collector.ts's existing
  shape so existing CloudWatch queries cover both paths.
- /traces additionally peeks the OTLP body for customer trace_ids and
  emits them on the 429 log and the parse-failure log, so a customer who
  reports "I sent trace_id X but it didn't show up" can be matched
  directly to the rejection record. Peek is best-effort: empty/malformed
  bodies just yield customerTraceIds: [], the projectId is still logged.
- Body-read failure on /traces now also returns a logged 400 instead of
  bubbling an unhandled exception.

The same projectId-on-429 log is added to the generic
blockTraceUsageExceededMiddleware so any other Hono route protected by it
benefits without needing to opt in.

* fix(nlpgo): honor edge handle renames between nodes (outputs.X → inputs.Y)

Studio workflows commonly use edges like
  sourceHandle="outputs.question"
  targetHandle="inputs.user_query"

The previous resolveInputs implementation merged ALL upstream outputs
under their source-side names — so the downstream node never saw its
declared input "user_query", and any workflow that renamed values
across edges silently produced empty inputs.

Now the engine indexes edges by target node id at run-state init
time, parses the "outputs."/"inputs." prefixes, and binds each
upstream output under the target node's input name. Falls back to
the legacy "merge by source name" behavior when handles are missing
or stripped, so workflows authored without explicit prefixes still
work.

* test(nlpgo): SSE round-trip + cancel + header tests for legacy proxypass

The /studio/* reverse-proxy through proxypass was specced with
FlushInterval=-1 to forward SSE chunks unbuffered, but no test
actually streamed bytes through it to verify. rchaves flagged this
explicitly: nlpgo as front-door means uvicorn's SSE has to traverse
proxypass with no buffering, no header drift, and proper cancel
propagation — and we'd never proven any of it.

- SSE_StreamsChunksUnbuffered: emits 4 SSE frames separated by 80ms
  gaps, asserts each frame arrives at the client byte-equivalent and
  that the first→last gap is >150ms (proving the proxy is not
  buffering until upstream completes). Flipping FlushInterval to 0
  makes this test fail with all chunks delivered as one blob.

- PreservesUpstreamHeaders: Content-Type, Cache-Control, and arbitrary
  X-Custom-Upstream survive the round-trip; the proxy adds its own
  X-LangWatch-NLPGO-Proxy=1 hint for log correlation.

- ClientCancelPropagatesUpstream: when the client cancels its request
  context mid-stream, the upstream's request context fires within 3s,
  so an in-flight Studio run on uvicorn knows to stop wasting CPU.

- UpstreamUnreachable_Returns502: when the child is down, the proxy
  returns a clean 502 with a friendly message instead of a connection
  error or hang.

- ForwardsMethodAndPath: every legacy method/path that the TS app
  actually sends (POST /studio/execute_sync, GET /health, POST
  /topics/batch_clustering, POST /proxy/v1/chat/completions) reaches
  uvicorn with byte-equivalent body, exact path, exact method.

fix(langwatch_nlp): code node accepts class with __call__ or forward (FF=off back-compat) (#3543)

* fix(langwatch_nlp): legacy Code node accepts class with __call__ / forward (back-compat for FF=off)

PR #3483 shipped a new Studio default Code template:

    class Code:
        def __call__(self, input: str):
            return {"output": "Hello world!"}

The Go runtime's runner.py was updated to resolve four shapes
(dspy.Module / __call__ / forward / top-level execute), but the
Python parser only matched `class X(dspy.Module):`. Customers still
on the legacy Python NLP service (FF=off — release_nlp_go_engine_
enabled override missing for their project) got:

    Could not find a class that inherits from dspy.Module for component Code

This is a real regression for unflipped customers: the new template
is now the default in Studio, so any Code block they drag in errors
out before flipping the FF rolls them onto the Go path.

**Fix**: extracted `_resolve_code_class_name(code, node_name, kind)`
in studio/parser.py. Resolution order mirrors the Go runner:

  1. `class X(dspy.Module):` — preferred (legacy default).
  2. `class X:` matching the node's normalized class name —
     disambiguates when the user defines helpers alongside the entry.
  3. First `class X:` declaration in the file.
  4. No class found → ValueError listing supported shapes.

Method-shape (__call__ vs forward vs neither) isn't inspected at
parse time — the chosen class is materialized downstream and the
caller uses Python's normal `instance(**inputs)` protocol, which
dispatches to __call__ if defined and would TypeError at call time
on a class with neither (clearer than failing at parse).

Loosened materialized_component_class's return type from
`Type[dspy.Module]` to `Type[Any]` to match.

**Tests**: TestCodeNodeClassResolutionShapes pins all four cases —
__call__-only, forward-only, dspy.Module back-compat, and the
helper-classes-above-the-entry disambiguation. Existing
test_parse_code (dspy.Module subclass) still passes — back-compat
anchor.

Same fix applies to the agent-code sub-handler (agent_type=code path),
also ported.

* docs(parser): clarify Go-runtime parity gap + pin multi-line base list

Two non-blocking nits from sarah's review of #3543:

**1. Docstring overclaim**: `_resolve_code_class_name` said its
resolution order "matches the Go runtime" — true for class-based
shapes, but the Go runner ALSO accepts a top-level ``def execute()``
callable that this parser doesn't. The parser is a class-name
extractor (the result is later passed to ``getattr(module, name)``);
a top-level function has no class name to extract. Updated the
docstring to call out the gap explicitly so future readers don't
hunt for parity that was never intended.

**2. Multi-line base list edge case**: Sarah flagged the regex
might not match
    class X(
        dspy.Module,
        SomeMixin,
    ):
Verified empirically: ``[^)]*`` is a negated character class which
includes newlines (unlike ``.`` without re.DOTALL), so the multi-line
case resolves correctly. Added a comment on the regex documenting
this contract, plus a regression test
``test_class_with_multi_line_base_list_resolves`` that locks in
the behavior — exercises the fallback path (the dspy fast-path
intentionally doesn't match multi-base classes, but the fallback
with node-name disambiguation picks the right class).

* fix(parser,execute): address CodeRabbit review on PR #3543

Three CodeRabbit findings, all valid:

**1. Major — class discovery via AST, not regex (parser.py)**
The previous `_CLASS_DECL_RE.findall(code)` ran on raw source so a
`class Fake:` inside a docstring or comment could be picked up,
later failing at `getattr(module, 'Fake')` with a confusing
AttributeError instead of a clean ValueError. Replaced both regex
paths (`_DSPY_MODULE_SUBCLASS_RE` + `_CLASS_DECL_RE`) with AST-based
discovery — `ast.parse(code)` then iterate `tree.body` for
`ast.ClassDef`. Side benefits:

  - The dspy.Module fast-path now matches multi-base classes
    (`class X(dspy.Module, SomeMixin):`) too, since AST inspection
    looks at all `cls.bases`. The old regex was strict-single-base.
  - SyntaxError in user code returns an empty candidate list, so
    the user still gets the "no class definition" message — the
    actual syntax error is reported by black later in the pipeline
    with a nicer location.
  - Top-level only (no nested-class candidates), matching the
    practical regex behavior the existing test suite locked in.

Added regression test `test_class_in_comment_or_docstring_is_not_picked`.

**2. Major — forward fallback in execute_component.py**
The parser accepts `class X: def forward(...)` (no `__call__`, no
`dspy.Module`), but `execute_component.py` did
`await dspy.asyncify(instance)(**inputs)` — a plain class with only
`forward` isn't directly callable, so this would TypeError. Mirrors
the priority-3 path in the Go runner
(`services/nlpgo/.../codeblock/runner.py`): try `instance(...)`
first, fall back to `instance.forward(...)`, raise a typed error
when neither exists. dspy.Module subclasses always have `__call__`
inherited from the base class, so they hit the fast path with no
behavior change.

**3. Minor — Ruff RUF059 cleanup (test_parse.py)**
Two test cases unpacked `code, class_name, _` but only used
`class_name`. Replaced unused `code` with `_`.

* fix(execute): callable() guard catches non-callable forward attribute

CodeRabbit minor on PR #3543: the previous `if invoke_target is None`
check missed the case where `forward` exists on the class but isn't
callable (e.g. `forward = "string"` set as a class attribute, or
shadowed by a non-method). That non-callable would slip past the None
check and reach `dspy.asyncify(non_callable)(...)`, surfacing
asyncify's generic 'object is not callable' instead of our typed
message naming the class.

Switched to `not callable(invoke_target)` which covers both legs —
`callable(None)` is False so the missing-attribute case is still
handled, AND any non-callable forward attribute now raises here with
the same operator-visible message. Slightly clearer error text too:
'has no callable entrypoint' + the suggested fix.

* fix(nlpgo): isNlpGoEnabled auto-resolves organizationId from project

PostHog FF rules that target the `organization_id` person property
(org-level rollouts) wouldn't match because every call site of
`isNlpGoEnabled` passed only `projectId` — `organizationId` was
optional and nobody supplied it. rchaves enabled the FF org-level
in PostHog and saw it not propagating to projects under that org.

Fix: when `organizationId` isn't supplied, look it up from the
project via `resolveOrganizationId` (10-min TTL cache, returns
undefined for orphan projects). Caller signature unchanged so all
existing call sites get the org context for free; explicit
`organizationId` overrides the lookup when callers do supply it.

Same diagnosis as why the user couldn't enable the FF locally
despite an org-level toggle — the post_event / workflows.ts /
topicClustering.ts call sites all pass only projectId, so PostHog
saw an empty organization_id property and the org-level rule
didn't fire.

* fix(nlpgo): preserve undeclared output keys + emit started_at on duration

Two FF=on dogfood bugs from rchaves on PR #3543:

**Bug 3 — undeclared output keys silently dropped**

User code returning `{"output": ..., "dspy": ...}` with only "output"
declared on the node lost the "dspy" key in the OUTPUTS panel. Legacy
Python NLP path returned ALL keys; the new runner filtered to the
declared list. Caught by rchaves's customer-debug-style return that
inspected dspy alongside the real output.

Fix in services/nlpgo/.../codeblock/runner.py: validate declared keys
are present (still required — they're wired to downstream nodes), but
copy the FULL result dict to outputs instead of just the declared
subset. Flipped the existing `TestCodeBlock_ExtraOutputDropped` to
`TestCodeBlock_ExtraOutputKeysPreserved` since that test was pinning
the wrong behavior.

**Bug 4 — per-component duration line went blank**

Studio's ExecutionOutputPanel.tsx gates the "<duration>ms · Full Trace"
line on `hasTiming = timestamps.started_at && timestamps.finished_at`.
The Go emitter only set `finished_at` so the gate failed silently
("·  Full Trace" with no duration). Caught by rchaves comparing
new-vs-old execution panel side-by-side.

Fix in services/nlpgo/.../engine/stream.go: derive `started_at` from
`finished_at - DurationMS` when emitting the component_state_change
finished event. No NodeState struct change — the wall-clock skew
between running and finished events is microseconds, and the UI only
uses the diff. Pinned by `TestStateEvent_TimestampsHaveBothStartedAndFinished`

* fix(nlpgo): execute_component feeds manual inputs to target node

Studio's "Run with manual input" flow types values into a node's
input panel and clicks Execute. The frontend
(useComponentExecution.ts:124-136) sends an execute_component event
with `{node_id, inputs}` — inputs are the user-typed values for THAT
node, not for the workflow's Entry node.

Pre-fix, nlpgo's decoder ignored `node_id` entirely, and the engine
treated `req.Inputs` as Entry-node outputs that flow downstream via
edges. A fresh-dragged Code node with no `Entry → Code` wiring (or
where Studio just opened the manual-input panel directly) received
an empty input map. The Python runner then raised:

  Code.__call__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'input'

…and the Studio UI silently re-rendered with the input field blank,
which looked like the user's typed value vanished on click.

Mirrors langwatch_nlp/studio/app.py's `payload.node_id` semantics.

**Plumbing**:
  - app.WorkflowRequest gains `NodeID string`
  - handlers.go decoder reads `node_id` from the inner payload
  - cmd/engine_adapter passes NodeID through to engine.ExecuteRequest
  - engine.ExecuteRequest gains `NodeID string`
  - runState gets `manualInputsTarget` + `manualInputs`
  - Engine.Execute populates them when req.NodeID is set + Inputs are
    non-empty
  - resolveInputs short-circuits for the target node (returns a copy
    of manualInputs, skips edge resolution)
  - runEntry stops consuming `req.Inputs` when NodeID is set —
    otherwise Entry would swallow the per-node typing on its way to
    a target deeper in the graph

**Regression tests** (services/nlpgo/app/engine/manual_inputs_test.go):
  - TestResolveInputs_ManualInputsForTargetNode — happy path
  - TestResolveInputs_ManualInputsScopedToTarget — non-target nodes
    still get edge-based resolution (multi-node runs unaffected)
  - TestResolveInputs_ManualInputsReturnsCopy — caller mutation
    doesn't leak back into runState

fix(nlpgo): bind HTTP listener before uvicorn-child to escape Lambda 10s init ceiling (#3559)

* fix(nlpgo): bind HTTP listener before uvicorn-child to escape Lambda init ceiling

services/nlpgo/serve.go registered services in this order:
  1. Closer("otel")        — no-op start
  2. Worker("uvicorn-child") — Manager.Start synchronously polls /health
  3. ListenServer("http")    — binds $PORT

pkg/lifecycle/group.go starts services sequentially via svc.Start(ctx),
so the HTTP listener didn't bind $PORT until uvicorn-child.Manager.Start
returned (~12-18s — dominated by litellm + langwatch_nlp imports).

On AWS Lambda the init phase has a hard 10s ceiling. CloudWatch
INIT_REPORT lines from the prod incident at 18:13 UTC after deploying
langwatch-saas#473 showed every cold start hitting "Init Duration:
9999.10ms Phase: init Status: timeout". Failed inits retried, the
retry storm pinned account-level ConcurrentExecutions to the 1000 cap,
and AWS bubbled TooManyRequestsException as "Rate Exceeded." through
InvokeWithResponseStreamCommand to the Studio toast.

Fix:
  1. Reorder lifecycle registration so ListenServer("http") comes
     before Worker("uvicorn-child"). The listener binds in milliseconds
     and Lambda init completes well under the 10s ceiling.
  2. Wrap the Worker startFn body in a goroutine so Manager.Start
     runs in the background. The lifecycle group's synchronous
     Service.Start returns instantly and the next service starts.

/go/* paths are immune to child not-ready (the Go engine handles
is_alive, execute_*, etc. without touching the proxy). /studio/*
fall-through to uvicorn proxy returns the existing typed 502 ("child
upstream unavailable") on connection refused while the child is still
warming up — short-lived window, AWS SDK's default 3-attempt backoff
handles it.

Add serve_test.go::TestServe_ListenerBindsBeforeBlockingChild — pins
the contract by registering a Worker that would block forever and
asserting the listener binds within 100ms. Verified the test catches
the regression: swapping ordering back AND removing the goroutine wrap
fails the deadline assertion.

* fix(studio-lambda): bump LambdaClient maxAttempts from 3 to 6

The AWS SDK default of 3 retry attempts for retryable errors
(TooManyRequestsException etc.) was insufficient for the
ConcurrentExecutions saturation window observed at 18:13 UTC on
2026-04-28. With per-project Lambdas all hitting cold-start init
timeouts simultaneously, AWS returns "Rate Exceeded." for ~30-60s
across the saturation peak — long enough that 3 retries with
exponential backoff land entirely inside the bad window and the
error surfaces to Studio as a toast.

The companion serve.go reorder (9cea81a00) makes init complete in
milliseconds so this scenario shouldn't recur, but bumping the
attempt count is a cheap defense-in-depth against future cold-start
regressions: if a slow Lambda push ever holds slots open for
seconds again, 6 attempts × ~9s of backoff (~50s total) will ride
out the burst transparently instead of erroring.

Test asserts the override is wired through to the AWS SDK config
so a future refactor of the client constructor doesn't silently
revert to the SDK default.

* test(studio-lambda): wrap maxAttempts test in given/when BDD nesting

CodeRabbit flagged the new createLambdaClient test in PR #3559 for
missing the repo's mandated describe('given X') / describe('when Y')
nesting (CLAUDE.md test convention). The flat describe('createLambdaClient')
shape doesn't satisfy that even though the surrounding test file uses
the older flat shape; we follow the convention on new code.

* fix(nlpgo): extract buildServices helper so tests pin Serve's wiring

Address CodeRabbit comment on services/nlpgo/serve_test.go:76 — the
prior shape rebuilt the lifecycle.Group with hardcoded ordering in the
test, so a regression that swapped Worker("uvicorn-child") and
ListenServer("http") inside Serve would still pass.

Extract the lifecycle service slice into buildServices(deps, srv) and
have Serve call g.Add(buildServices(...)...). The tests now call
buildServices directly:

- TestBuildServices_RegistersListenerBeforeUvicornChild — fails if
  someone reorders Worker before ListenServer in serve.go.
- TestBuildServices_UvicornChildWorkerDoesNotBlockStart — fails if
  someone removes the `go func()` wrap and the worker startFn returns
  to blocking on Manager.Start.
- TestServe_ListenerBindsBeforeBlockingChild — runtime sibling that
  drives the lifecycle.Group end-to-end with the same buildServices
  output and asserts the listener binds within Lambda's 10s init
  budget.

Validated on lw-dev via aws lambda invoke against an arm64 image built
from this branch + AWS_LWA_READINESS_CHECK_PATH=/healthz env override:

  Init Duration: 416.60ms  (was: 9999ms TIMEOUT)
  Wall-clock cold-start invoke: 1057ms
  /go/studio/execute is_alive returns 200 SSE end-to-end

The env var override is required alongside this fix — Lambda Web
Adapter's default readiness probe path / falls through to the
not-yet-ready uvicorn proxy and fails the init regardless of how fast
the listener binds. Saas-side companion PR adds the env var.

* fix(nlpgo): make blocking-child regression tests deterministically protective

Address two CodeRabbit comments on serve_test.go:

1. (Major) Disabled=true on the test child made
   TestBuildServices_UvicornChildWorkerDoesNotBlockStart non-protective —
   Manager.Start returns immediately when Disabled, so a regression that
   dropped the `go func()` wrap and called Start synchronously would
   still pass the 100ms deadline.

   Replace with a deliberately blocking child: spawn a `sleep 3600`
   subprocess and point HealthURL at a closed port (127.0.0.1:1) with
   StartTimeout=5s. Manager.waitHealthy now polls until the test deadline
   trips; the goroutine wrap is the only thing that lets the worker's
   Service.Start return within 100ms. Verified the test fails as
   expected when the wrap is removed (output: "Lambda init regression:
   uvicorn-child worker.Start did not return within 100ms").

   Skipped on Windows since `sleep` isn't a POSIX binary there; the
   protected platforms (Linux on CI, macOS for local dev) get the full
   contract.

2. (Minor) TestServe_ListenerBindsBeforeBlockingChild ignored the err
   from runDone after cancel, so an unexpected lifecycle.Run error
   could pass silently. Now asserts err is either nil or wraps
   context.Canceled (the two values lifecycle.Run produces on graceful
   teardown). Bumped the graceful window to 5s and the wait-for-runDone
   timeout to 7s — Manager.Stop on a real `sleep` child can take longer
   than the previous 1s/2s budgets.

t.Cleanup(child.Stop) ensures the spawned sleep is reaped after each
test, no leaked processes.

fix(studio-lambda): bump per-project Lambda MemorySize 1024 → 2048 MB (#3565)

Mid-request Max Memory Used hit 805/1024 MB on lw-dev TEST H
(2026-04-28) when the bundled image runs nlpgo + uvicorn + litellm
together. With ~80% RSS pressure, Python's multiprocessing.fork()
cannot clone the parent's memory pages and the uvicorn worker pool
crashes (Thread-1 _fill_pool_continuously traceback). The crash
cascades to /studio/* 502s as the proxy can't reach a now-dead
upstream.

2048 MB doubles the headroom AND doubles allocated CPU (Lambda
scales CPU proportionally to memory; 0.58 vCPU at 1024 → 1.17
vCPU at 2048), so cold-start init also gets faster.

Only affects newly-created project Lambdas. Existing 26 lambdas
need the one-shot migration:

  for fn in $(aws --profile lw-prod lambda list-functions \
      --query 'Functions[?starts_with(FunctionName, `langwatch_nlp-project_`)].FunctionName' \
      --output text); do
    aws --profile lw-prod lambda update-function-configuration \
      --function-name "$fn" --memory-size 2048
  done

Migration is reversible (swap 2048 back to 1024). Cost framing:
per-project Lambdas are mostly idle; 2× memory billing during
brief Studio sessions is bounded.

fix(nlpgo): cold-start wait + 503 retry + Recover-middleware ErrAbortHandler (#3566)

* fix(nlpgo): proxypass waits for upstream during cold-start, returns 503 not 502

Symptom: PR langwatch-saas#476 deployed the lifecycle reorder + LWA env
var fix to prod. Studio FF=off (legacy) workflow runs immediately
surfaced "Failed run workflow: 502 child upstream unavailable". Reverted
via langwatch-saas#477.

Root cause: the lifecycle reorder in PR #3559 made nlpgo's HTTP listener
bind $PORT before the uvicorn child finishes warming (~12-18s of
litellm + langwatch_nlp imports). On cold-start, /go/* paths are
self-contained and work immediately, but /studio/* paths fall through
nlpgo's chi NotFound handler into the proxypass — which dialed
127.0.0.1:5561 against a not-yet-listening child, got connection-
refused, and returned 502 from the ErrorHandler. The lw-dev validation
covered the FF-on /go/studio/execute is_alive heartbeat (handled in
nlpgo, no proxy hit) but missed the FF-off /studio/* path entirely.

Fix: wrap proxypass with a wait-with-deadline preamble. On every
request we TCP-probe the upstream host. If reachable, hand off to the
reverse proxy (existing happy path). If not, poll every 100ms up to
ColdStartWait (default 5s). After the deadline, return 503 with
Retry-After:1.

503 + Retry-After is the right SLA signal: it tells the caller the
upstream is transiently unavailable and to retry shortly. The
LambdaClient on the langwatch-app side already has maxAttempts:6 (also
from PR #3559), so a transient cold-start storm rides through
transparently instead of toasting the user.

The 502 ErrorHandler is preserved for actual upstream errors (5xx
mid-stream, write-error, etc.) that occur AFTER the dial succeeded.
The wrapper only widens the no-route window — happy path and steady-
state behavior are unchanged.

Tests:

- TestReverseProxy_UpstreamUnreachable_Returns503AfterWait — permanent
  unreachable upstream returns 503 + Retry-After:1 (was 502 pre-fix).
- TestReverseProxy_UpstreamReachableMidWaitProxiesThrough — pins the
  cold-start happy path: when upstream becomes reachable inside the
  wait window, the request flows through to the upstream instead of
  503'ing.
- All existing proxypass tests still pass.

Defaults are conservative (5s wait, 100ms probe interval, 200ms probe
timeout) so the cold-start window is invisible to callers without
introducing risk on permanently-failed upstreams.

* fix(nlpgo): bump proxypass ColdStartWait default 5s → 15s for real cold-start

Local docker boot of the saas Lambda runtime image showed the uvicorn
child becoming reachable at ~14s after nlpgo's listener binds (litellm
+ langwatch_nlp.main imports dominate). The previous 5s default was
not enough to absorb the cold-start window — every /studio/execute
request landing in that window 503'd, and even with the LambdaClient
maxAttempts:6 retry, all 6 attempts could land before the child was
ready.

Bumping to 15s gives the proxy room to wait through the full child
warmup window in a single request, so callers see one ~14s delay
instead of 6 retries × 5s = 30s of accumulated waiting.

Lambda function timeout is 900s, so 15s is well within budget.

* fix(nlpgo): bump proxypass ColdStartWait default 15s → 25s

Local docker boot of saas Lambda runtime image showed:
- nlpgo HTTP listener binds at ~3s after container start
- uvicorn child reachable at ~22s after container start
  (litellm + langwatch_nlp.main imports dominate)

15s default absorbed late-window requests but not the very first
/studio/* request that lands shortly after the listener binds. The
SDK retry path (maxAttempts:6) would catch it, but that's a worse
UX than waiting 25s in a single request and getting 200.

25s gives ~3s headroom over the observed cold-start in a stress-
free local build; production Lambda is typically faster but this
keeps the default conservative.

* fix(nlpgo): bump uvicorn-child StartTimeout 30s → 120s for Lambda CPU

lw-dev real-Lambda invoke of /studio/execute revealed CloudWatch:

    [error] uvicorn_child_exited error: "uvicornchild: exited unexpectedly:
            signal: killed"
    [error] uvicorn_child_start_failed error: "uvicornchild: not healthy
            within 30s: context deadline exceeded"

Manager.Start spawns the python child, then waitHealthy polls /health
with a StartTimeout deadline. Default was 30s — fine on dev hardware,
too tight on AWS Lambda 1024MB (~1 vCPU, plus possible freeze/thaw
during init). litellm + langwatch_nlp.main imports take longer than
30s, so Manager kills the still-importing child via SIGKILL. Then the
proxy waits 25s against a now-dead upstream and returns 503.

Bump default to 120s. 4× headroom over observed 30s, well under
Lambda's 900s function timeout. Once the child is healthy this knob
is off the hot path — it's a one-time cold-start budget.

* fix(nlpgo): bump proxypass ColdStartWait default 25s → 90s for Lambda CPU

lw-dev real-Lambda probe shows >50s of cumulative active wall-clock
spent on uvicorn child imports before 127.0.0.1:5561 binds. Lambda
1024MB (~1 vCPU) is meaningfully slower than local docker (M-series
CPU showed ~22s). 25s wait was insufficient — proxy gave up before
the child could even progress past the joblib import warning.

90s gives generous headroom for Lambda Python imports while still
fitting under the AWS SDK's 5-minute streaming-invoke deadline.

This is paired with a Dockerfile preload step (saas-side change) that
warms .pyc bytecode + litellm initializers at docker BUILD time, so
the Lambda cold-start no longer pays the full import cost.

* fix(httpmiddleware): re-panic http.ErrAbortHandler without writing 500

Recover middleware previously caught EVERY panic, wrote a 500 response,
then re-panicked. That's the right contract for unexpected panics, but
http.ErrAbortHandler is a sentinel — net/http's serve loop catches it
specifically to "abort this request, do not write further output, and
tear the connection down." Most commonly produced by
httputil.ReverseProxy when the upstream connection EOFs mid-body.

Writing a 500 on the abort path puts the response writer into an
indeterminate state:

  - The Go server logs "superfluous response.WriteHeader call"
    because WriteHeader was already called by the proxy when it
    started streaming the upstream response.
  - On AWS Lambda the Rust-based Lambda Web Adapter sees the
    inconsistent wire shape, panics with
    "unexpected EOF during chunk size line", and the whole container
    is SIGKILL'd as Extension.Crash.

Observed live in lw-dev probes against the saas Lambda runtime image
on 2026-04-28: a /studio/execute proxy through to a uvicorn child
that crashed mid-stream produced ErrAbortHandler → wrote a 500 →
LWA extension SIGKILL → Lambda billed 49s/Extension.Crash.

Fix: detect ErrAbortHandler before touching the response writer and
re-panic immediately. net/http handles it per its documented contract
(close the connection silently). Generic panics still get the 500 +
re-panic path.

Tests:

  TestRecover_GenericPanicReturns500AndRePanics — historical contract
    preserved: a generic panic still gets a 500 written and is
    re-panicked.

  TestRecover_ErrAbortHandlerIsRePanickedWithoutWritingResponse — the
    new contract: ErrAbortHandler re-panics with the response writer
    untouched. ResponseRecorder defaults to 200 (i.e. WriteHeader was
    never called) and the body is empty.

* fix(studio-lambda): bump per-project Lambda MemorySize 1024 → 2048 MB (#3565)

Mid-request Max Memory Used hit 805/1024 MB on lw-dev TEST H
(2026-04-28) when the bundled image runs nlpgo + uvicorn + litellm
together. With ~80% RSS pressure, Python's multiprocessing.fork()
cannot clone the parent's memory pages and the uvicorn worker pool
crashes (Thread-1 _fill_pool_continuously traceback). The crash
cascades to /studio/* 502s as the proxy can't reach a now-dead
upstream.

2048 MB doubles the headroom AND doubles allocated CPU (Lambda
scales CPU proportionally to memory; 0.58 vCPU at 1024 → 1.17
vCPU at 2048), so cold-start init also gets faster.

Only affects newly-created project Lambdas. Existing 26 lambdas
need the one-shot migration:

  for fn in $(aws --profile lw-prod lambda list-functions \
      --query 'Functions[?starts_with(FunctionName, `langwatch_nlp-project_`)].FunctionName' \
      --output text); do
    aws --profile lw-prod lambda update-function-configuration \
      --function-name "$fn" --memory-size 2048
  done

Migration is reversible (swap 2048 back to 1024). Cost framing:
per-project Lambdas are mostly idle; 2× memory billing during
brief Studio sessions is bounded.

* fix(proxypass): clamp negative probe knobs + dial scheme-default port (CR)

Two CodeRabbit follow-ups on the cold-start preamble:

1. ColdStartProbeInterval / ColdStartProbeTimeout only defaulted when
   exactly zero, so a negative value (deliberate or accidental) survived
   into the retry loop. time.After(-1s) fires instantly and the loop
   would CPU-spin during outages; net.DialTimeout with a negative
   timeout returns immediately on every probe. Unlike ColdStartWait,
   neither knob has a documented "negative disables" sentinel — both
   now clamp to the default. New regression test
   TestReverseProxy_NegativeProbeKnobsFallBackToDefaults pins the
   functional outcome.

2. waitForUpstream took target.Host directly, which omits the default
   port when the URL has none (http://example.com -> "example.com",
   no ":80"). net.DialTimeout requires "host:port", so every probe
   would have failed with "missing port in address" and the cold-start
   wait silently 503'd through the full window. Added probeAddress(u)
   which resolves the scheme-default (80 / 443) before joining;
   non-http(s) schemes without an explicit port now surface as a loud
   error from New() instead of a runtime probe failure. Production
   currently always uses http://127.0.0.1:5561 so this never triggered,
   but the helper keeps the contract honest. Direct unit tests in a
   new internal-package proxy_internal_test.go cover ipv4 / hostname /
   ipv6 / explicit-port / bare / unsupported-scheme cases.

* fix(npx-server): inject LD_LIBRARY_PATH so bundled postgres can find libpq.so.5

The embeds.langwatch.ai postgres tarballs ship with a leaked RUNPATH
pointing at the GitHub Actions runner's build prefix
(/home/runner/work/...). On any other host, ld.so can't find libpq.so.5
and every postgres binary (initdb, postgres, pg_ctl, psql, createdb,
pg_isready) exits 127.

Repro on bare Ubuntu 24.04 LTS amd64 (sure-oak via boxd.sh):
  npx @langwatch/server
  ✗ /home/boxd/.langwatch/bin/postgres/bin/initdb exit 127

ldd showed libpq.so.5 "not found"; readelf -d showed RUNPATH pointing
at the build host. The lib IS bundled in ~/.langwatch/bin/postgres/lib/.

Why CI/dev missed it: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runners + Homebrew-on-
mac dev boxes have system libpq.so.5 in /usr/lib (or /opt/homebrew/lib),
so ld.so default search path masks the RUNPATH leak. Bare Ubuntu without
postgresql apt packages — like sure-oak — has neither.

Fix:
1. Inject LD_LIBRARY_PATH (DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH on darwin) pointing at
   LANGWATCH_HOME/bin/postgres/lib for every postgres-binary execa +
   the supervised postgres process. No-op when sibling lib dir absent.
2. Add LANGWATCH_FORCE_BUNDLED_POSTGRES=1 env flag so devs can dogfood
   the bundled-tarball path locally even when system postgres is on PATH.

Long-term: rebuild embeds tarball with --with-rpath '\$ORIGIN/../lib'
or patchelf post-extract — tracked separately. Bare-distro CI smoke
(alpine/distroless) also tracked separately as the proper regression
guard.

* fix(npx-server): bundle pnpm as a predep + strip macOS postgres binaries with -S

Two bare-metal failure modes uncovered while dogfooding @langwatch/server
3.1.0-beta.20 on a fresh Linux box (sure-oak via boxd) and via
LANGWATCH_FORCE_BUNDLED_POSTGRES on macOS:

1) **Bare Linux (nvm-installed node, no pnpm on PATH)**: the langwatch
   app's `prisma:migrate` + `clickhouse:migrate` scripts wrap their
   work in `sh -c '… pnpm prisma migrate deploy …'`. The OUTER call
   (commit 6bb3f4679) routed through `corepack pnpm`, but the INNER
   `pnpm` inside the sh subshell resolves via PATH — and corepack
   doesn't put pnpm on PATH for child processes. Result: `sh: 1: pnpm:
   not found` and the install bombs after postgres is up.

   Fix: install pnpm as a real predep (parity with uv) — downloads the
   pinned v10.24.0 standalone binary into `~/.langwatch/bin/pnpm`.
   `resolvePnpm()` now prefers the bundled binary, and every supervised
   invocation prepends `ctx.paths.bin` to PATH so any nested `pnpm`
   call resolves to the same binary. No corepack runtime dependency.

2) **macOS bundled postgres** (`LANGWATCH_FORCE_BUNDLED_POSTGRES=1`):
   initdb fails post-bootstrap with
     dlopen: Symbol not found: _CurrentMemoryContext
     Expected in: …/postgres/bin/postgres
   when loading dict_snowball.dylib. Default BSD `strip` (macOS) removes
   ALL symbols, including the globals that postgres modules dlopen
   against at runtime. Switch the embedded-binaries-publish.yml step to
   `strip -S` (debug-only), which is portable across GNU + BSD strip
   and preserves global symbols on both.

Verification: cold install on sure-oak (Linux x64, no pnpm/postgres
pre-installed) reaches all phases healthy — pnpm 10.24.0 in
`~/.langwatch/bin/pnpm`, postgres + redis + clickhouse + aigateway +
langwatch + langwatch_nlp + langevals + workers all green, /api/health
returns 204.

* fix(npx-server): print ASCII banner outside pino + first-run setup signpost

Two UX fixes for the npx flow:

**Banner mangling under pino's prod transport.** Under `pnpm dev`, pino
uses pino-pretty which unescapes `\n` in `msg`, so the ASCII art logged
at server-listen time renders as multi-line art. Under
`npx @langwatch/server`, the langwatch app runs with NODE_ENV=production
and pino emits raw JSON — the ASCII art comes out as a single mangled
line:

  | langwatch  {"level":"INFO",...,"msg":"\n\n██╗   ...\n"}

Bypass pino entirely for the banner: `process.stdout.write(asciiArt)`
goes to stdout cleanly regardless of transport. Metadata
(hostname/port/fullUrl/mode) still goes through the structured logger
for downstream aggregators.

**First-run setup signpost.** Cold install on a fresh box pulls the
178MB clickhouse tarball, ~36MB goose binary, builds a uv venv,
installs ~50 langwatch deps via pnpm — easily 3-5 min on home
broadband. Warm runs hit cached predeps and finish in <30s. Print a
short signpost up front when both `paths.bin` and
`paths.installManifest` are absent (the gate-pair that says "nothing
installed yet"), so the wait isn't silent.

binary, dropping the heaviest dependency in the npx flow:

dspy, litellm, big transitive tree) and added ~150MB to ~/.langwatch.

* fix(npx-server): keep workers alive (disable 15-min self-exit timer) + bump 3.1.0-beta.24 (TEMP)

**Bug**: subsequent traces (after the first ~15 min) silently fail to
reach the UI. nlpgo emits OTel spans → /api/otel/v1/traces returns 200
→ collector job staged in Redis → never consumed → traces.getById 404
→ "Full Trace" stays on skeleton loaders.

**Root cause**: langwatch's worker process self-exits cleanly every 15
min as a memory-leak safety pattern (langwatch/src/workers.ts:22 calls
`worker.start(void 0, 15 * 60 * 1000)`). In helm/docker, an external
supervisor (k8s/restart-policy=always) re-spawns the process
immediately. In our npx flow, supervise() in spawn.ts emits a
`stopped` event but doesn't restart — so all queues that depend on the
worker silently stop draining at T+15m.

**Fix (this commit)**:
- langwatch/src/workers.ts: read `LANGWATCH_WORKERS_MAX_RUNTIME_MS`
  env var; default stays 15min for helm/docker back-compat.
- packages/server/src/services/langwatch-workers.ts: set
  `LANGWATCH_WORKERS_MAX_RUNTIME_MS=0` in the supervised env block —
  npx local has no external supervisor.

A broader fix (supervise() restart-on-exit with backoff) is the right
long-term direction and is filed as a follow-up — out of scope for
#3539.

guards so the dispatched workflow can build + publish from this PR

fix(studio): strip LWA RESPONSE_STREAM prelude before forwarding SSE chunks (#3568)

Lambda Web Adapter in RESPONSE_STREAM mode emits each Lambda response as
`<JSON prelude with statusCode + headers>\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00<body>`.
AWS often delivers the prelude AND the first body bytes inside a single
PayloadChunk, so when invokeLambda forwards chunks raw to a downstream
SSE parser the parser splits on `\n\n`, sees the first segment start
with the prelude `{` instead of `data: `, and silently drops it.

For the Go control path (services/nlpgo/adapters/httpapi/handlers.go
emitStudioControlEvent) the dropped frame IS `is_alive_response` because
that handler writes both `is_alive_response` and `done` synchronously
before flushing — so the entire response (prelude + both events) lands
in one PayloadChunk and only the trailing `done` survives. Studio's
heartbeat hook (usePostEvent.tsx:226) never flips socketStatus to
"connected", the workflow page stays "Connecting…", and after
fetchSSE's 20s timeout fires Studio logs `name: "Timeout"` (errors.ts
FetchSSETimeoutError). The Python /studio/execute path is not affected
in steady state because uvicorn flushes per SSE event, so the prelude
only contaminates the cosmetic `debug` first frame and `is_alive_response`
arrives in its own later PayloadChunk where startsWith("data: ")
matches cleanly.

Buffer chunks until the 8-zero separator is seen (handles the rare case
where AWS splits the prelude across multiple PayloadChunks), parse the
JSON prelude for statusCode, and enqueue only the post-separator body
bytes. Reproduced live on rchaves's project_MZZOfbwLOfoiXeg9KnbqF
Lambda 2026-04-29 — hex-dump of /go/studio/execute is_alive response
showed prelude+both events glued in a single chunk.

Tests in lwa-prelude.test.ts cover findLWAPreludeSeparator (boundary,
partial-prelude, false-positive avoidance), concatBytes (identity +
order), and three end-to-end strip-loop shapes: prelude+body in one
chunk (the prod failure mode), prelude split across chunks, and
prelude alone in chunk 1 with body in chunk 2 (legacy uvicorn shape).

fix(evaluations): skip custom evaluators with no DSL so /api/evaluations/*/evaluate stops 500-ing (#3579)

Symptom: GET /api/health/evaluations returned 500 with body "Failed to run
sample evaluation: Internal Server Error". Reproduced live on prod via
`curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-lw-…' https://app.langwatch.ai/api/health/evaluations`.

Stack trace from prod pod logs:
  SyntaxError: "undefined" is not valid JSON
      at JSON.parse (<anonymous>)
      at evaluations-legacy.ts:572:16
      at Array.map
      at getEvaluatorIncludingCustom (evaluations-legacy.ts:570:41)
      at handleEvaluatorCall (evaluations-legacy.ts:692:6)

Root cause: getEvaluatorIncludingCustom does
    JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(evaluator.versions[0]?.dsl))
on every custom evaluator the project has. When `dsl` is undefined (a
draft custom evaluator that hasn't been saved with a DSL yet, or one
whose `versions` row is missing), `JSON.stringify(undefined)` returns
the literal string "undefined" and `JSON.parse("undefined")` throws.
The throw propagates up through handleEvaluatorCall, past the route's
try/catch (which only covers schema validation, not the resolver path),
and Hono's default 500 handler returns plain text "Internal Server
Error" — which the health-check's wrapper then surfaces as
"Failed to run sample evaluation: Internal Server Error".

Side-effect blast radius: ANY POST /api/evaluations/:evaluator/evaluate
call (or :evaluator/:subpath/evaluate) by ANY project that has a custom
evaluator with no DSL. Status-page health-check happened to be the
canary. Production's per-trace PII redaction path
(workers/collector/piiCheck.ts) hits the Lambda directly and bypasses
this resolver, which is why real user PII detection kept working.

Fix: replace the .map over custom evaluators with a for-loop that
skips entries with no DSL. Same shape result for the happy path.

* fix(langwatch_nlp): resolve __call__ entrypoint in wrapped() for Code nodes

LangWatchWorkflowModule.wrapped() assumed the module class always had a
forward() method. Classes using only __call__() (the new default Code
template from PR #3543) raised AttributeError("type object 'WrappedModule'
has no attribute 'forward'").

Resolution order now mirrors execute_component.py and the Go runner:
forward() first, fall back to __call__(), raise TypeError if neither.
Uses MRO __dict__ inspection to avoid false-positive on type.__call__.

with_autoparsing and with_reporting both assume a forward method exists.
For __call__-only classes, assign forward = __call__ on the WrappedModule
subclass before the patching chain runs, so all three layers
(autoparsing, reporting, metadata) work through the same forward path.

* fix(langwatch_nlp): wire __call__ through forward for non-dspy.Module classes

For plain classes, instance() calls __call__ directly, bypassing the
forward patching chain (autoparsing, reporting, metadata). After the
chain wraps forward, rewire __call__ to delegate to forward so all
layers are always hit. dspy.Module subclasses already have this
delegation built in.

fix(pat): use scope-aware representative permissions in ceiling check

The PAT ceiling check used scope-agnostic representative permissions —
MEMBER mapped to `project:create` regardless of scope. At org scope,
MEMBER only has `organization:view`, so the check always failed,
blocking every MEMBER user from creating PATs.

Map each role to a permission it actually holds at the given scope:
- ADMIN: `organization:manage` (org) / `project:manage` (team/project)
- MEMBER: `organization:view` (org) / `project:update` (team/project)
- VIEWER: `project:view` (all scopes)

Also adds RoleBindings to the test fixture (ceiling checks use
RoleBindings, not TeamUser) and tests for MEMBER PAT creation.

feat(auth): in-app change password for Auth0 users on /settings/authentication (#3478)

* feat(auth): in-app change password for Auth0-authenticated users

Adds a Change Password section to /settings/authentication for tenants
running on NEXTAUTH_PROVIDER=auth0. The form takes new + confirm and
applies the change directly via Auth0 Management API
(PATCH /api/v2/users/{id}). Uses dedicated AUTH0_MGMT_CLIENT_ID/SECRET
env vars (a separate Machine-to-Machine app), since the user-login app
is typically a Single Page Application and cannot use the
client_credentials grant. Falls back to AUTH0_CLIENT_ID/SECRET for
tenants where the login app is a Regular Web App with Client
Credentials enabled.

Identity is proven by the authenticated app session (current password
not re-verified — modern Auth0 tenants don't expose the Resource Owner
Password Grant). Existing 5/15min per-user rate limit applies. Email
provider flow is unchanged.

* refactor(auth): move Change Password into a dialog, link from Linked Sign-in Methods

Per UX feedback on PR #3478 — having the form always visible on /settings/authentication
felt cluttered. Now:

- Auth0 mode: a "Change Password" link sits next to the Email/Password (via auth0)
  identity in the Linked Sign-in Methods list. Hidden for social-only auth0 users
  (google-oauth2, etc) — they have no password we can update.
- Email mode: a dedicated section with just a button (no inline form).
- Both modes open the same ChangePasswordDialog. Submit -> success toast +
  dialog auto-closes; error -> stays open with error toast.
- Reopening the dialog clears any leftover values.

* fix(auth): address CodeRabbit findings on Auth0 change-password

- Filter Auth0 account lookup to database-connection identities only
  (`providerAccountId` starting with `auth0|`). Without this, a user
  who linked a social identity via Auth0 (google-oauth2|..., github|...)
  could have findFirst return that row and the Management API PATCH
  would fail with the wrong connection name. Frontend already hides
  the entry point for social-only users; this makes the backend match.
- Revoke other BetterAuth app sessions after a successful Auth0
  password change. The Auth0 OIDC session is managed by the IdP, but
  the LangWatch app session is a local DB row independent of Auth0
  and should be invalidated on password rotation so a stolen token
  can't outlive it. Mirrors the email/credential path's behavior with
  the same impersonation safeguard.
- Derive the dialog's form-values type from the Zod schema via
  z.infer instead of duplicating it as a hand-written interface.

* fix(auth): omit currentPassword from mutation payload in Auth0 mode

Per CodeRabbit — when the dialog hides the Current Password field
(Auth0 mode), don't send an empty string for it either. Build the
payload conditionally so the server-side schema is free to tighten
to z.string().min(1).optional() in the future without breaking the
Auth0 flow.

* perf(auth0): cache Management API token + tighten frontend test assertion

Two more CodeRabbit findings:

- Cache the Management API token in passwordService.ts. Auth0 returns
  expires_in (typically 24h for M2M) — cache keyed on mgmtClientId with
  a 60s safety window so successive password changes don't each pay a
  token-issuance round-trip and don't burn the tenant's rate budget.
  Defensive: skip caching if expires_in is missing.
- Tighten the Auth0-mode test in authentication.integration.test.tsx
  to exact-match the mutation payload and explicitly assert no
  currentPassword key. The previous objectContaining would have passed
  even if currentPassword silently leaked.

* perf(auth): memoize ChangePasswordDialog zod resolver

Per CodeRabbit nitpick — `buildSchema()` returns a fresh `ZodEffects`
on every render. Wrap in `useMemo` keyed on `requireCurrentPassword`
so RHF gets a stable resolver reference.

* fix(auth0): match insufficient_scope on errorCode, not HTTP 403 alone

Per CodeRabbit — Auth0's Management API attaches an explicit `errorCode`
on 403s. Matching on HTTP status alone would mis-label unrelated 403s
(blocked user, MFA-required) as missing-scope and surface bad
remediation advice. Now we trigger the insufficient_scope branch only
when `errorCode === "insufficient_scope"`. Other 403s fall through to
the generic Auth0ApiError code=unknown. Test added for that path.

* fix(auth0): timeout + transport-error normalization, scenario bindings, more UI tests

- Wrap Auth0 fetch calls in AbortSignal.timeout(10s) and a fetchAuth0
  helper that converts transport errors (DNS, connection refused,
  AbortError from the timeout) into Auth0ApiError. Without this, a
  hanging upstream would hold the tRPC mutation hostage and a network
  error would leak as raw Error, breaking the caller's
  `instanceof Auth0ApiError` check (CodeRabbit critical).
- Bind every @integration scenario in the feature file to a real test
  via @scenario JSDoc annotations (PR #3298 parity check). Three
  server-side-only scenarios (M2M fallback, rate-limit branch,
  email-mode session-revocation) tagged @unimplemented as tracked
  gaps rather than added in this PR's scope.
- Add three new UI tests previously implied but not exercised:
  server error keeps dialog open with toast, Cancel closes without
  submitting, reopening clears stale form values.
- Add a transport-error test that points the fetch at a closed port
  and asserts Auth0ApiError comes back.

* test(auth0): rename describe block to '200 OK' to match handler stub

Per CodeRabbit nitpick — the handler returns 200, not 204. Pure
documentation fix, no behavior change.

* fix(dev): align BASE_HOST + NEXTAUTH_URL to PORT in pnpm dev

When the port-conflict detector picks a non-default slot (e.g. PORT=5580
because another worktree already owns 5560), BASE_HOST and NEXTAUTH_URL
in .env still pointed at 5560 — so BetterAuth's trustedOrigins rejected
the actual listening port with 403 INVALID_ORIGIN, and the OAuth
sign-in/social call (which uses NEXTAUTH_URL to build the redirect_uri)
died before reaching Auth0.

Now scripts/start.sh, dev-only, exports BASE_HOST and NEXTAUTH_URL as
http://localhost:$PORT whenever PORT is set. Production is untouched
(no PORT-derived URL, NEXTAUTH_URL there is the real public domain).

* feat(auth0): re-verify current password before changing it

Previously the Auth0 path trusted the authenticated session as proof of
identity and skipped current-password verification. That left a real
threat — a stolen session can lock the actual owner out by rotating the
password. This adds it back, using Auth0 Resource Owner Password Grant
on the Management M2M client (which has a client secret).

Server flow:
  1. ROPG verify against /oauth/token with the user's email + typed
     current password and the M2M creds. 200 → ok; 403 invalid_grant →
     UNAUTHORIZED "Current password is incorrect".
  2. On verified, fetch the Management API token (still cached) and
     PATCH /api/v2/users/{id} with the new password. Same insufficient_scope
     handling as before.

Required Auth0 setup (PR description has the full checklist):
  • Management M2M app → Advanced Settings → Grant Types → enable Password
  • Tenant Settings → API Authorization Settings → Default Directory =
    "Username-Password-Authentication"

Both modes (auth0 and email/credential) now require a non-empty
currentPassword in the schema. The dialog always asks for it.

* fix(auth0): surface tenant password-policy errors verbatim

When Auth0's tenant password policy rejects the new password,
Auth0 returns 400 Bad Request with
\`message: "PasswordStrengthError: Password is too weak"\` (and
similar for PasswordHistoryError, PasswordDictionaryError,
PasswordNoUserInfoError). The previous catch-all mapped this to
"Could not update password with Auth0. Please try again later." —
hiding the actionable reason from the user.

Now we recognize these prefixes, strip the type-tag, and propagate
the message as a typed Auth0ApiError code=weak_password. The tRPC
mutation maps it to BAD_REQUEST so the dialog's error toast shows
the real Auth0 message verbatim. Two new test cases cover
PasswordStrengthError and PasswordHistoryError.

* feat(dev): tsx watch the API + workers in pnpm dev

Vite already HMRs the frontend. The API (tsx src/server.mts) and
workers (tsx src/workers.ts) ran without a watcher, so backend edits
required a manual `pnpm dev` restart — easy to forget when iterating
on tRPC or queue handlers and a frequent source of "why isn't my fix
showing up" confusion.

Adds two new scripts (`start:app:watch`, `start:workers:watch`)
that run tsx with `--watch --clear-screen=false`, and start.sh now
prefers them when NODE_ENV=development. Production behavior is
unchanged (single-shot tsx, no watcher overhead).

revert(dev): drop tsx watch from pnpm dev — restart manually for now (#3597)

* fix(dev): scope tsx watch to the API only (workers stay heavy)

Workers boot heavy state — BullMQ connections, model registries,
the scenarios runtime — so restarting them on every backend save
is wasteful and disruptive. Revert workers to plain tsx in dev.

The API alone keeps tsx watch (boot is ~3-6s, ~150-250MB; reload
peaks at ~2x memory during overlap then settles back). Vite stays
on its own concurrently process — it is not affected by the API
reload. Production behavior is unchanged for both processes.

* revert(dev): drop tsx watch from pnpm dev — restart manually for now

The auto-watch caused too many full-API restarts under fast saves
(BullMQ/Prisma/ClickHouse pool churn, briefly 2x memory) without
a great escape valve. The right fix is lazy reload-on-request via
@hono/vite-dev-server (Vite SSR), but that needs the API to move
inside the Vite process and ship its own PR. Until then, plain tsx
both for the API and workers, manual `pnpm dev` restart when you
want to pick up backend changes.

fix(charts): `helm dep update` so release-please rp branches don't fail CI (#3601)

fix(charts): use `helm dependency update` so release-please rp branches don't fail CI

`helm dependency build` is strict: it cross-checks Chart.lock against the
on-disk Chart.yaml versions and errors if they differ. release-please
bumps the local file:// gateway sub-chart's `version` field via
extra-files on every langwatch release (in lockstep with the umbrella
chart) but cannot recompute the sha256 digest in Chart.lock. Result:
every release-please PR fails all 11 `template (*)` jobs with
`can't get a valid version for dependency langwatch-gateway`,
gating the whole 3.x release.

`helm dependency update .` regenerates Chart.lock from the current
on-disk Chart.yaml and writes a fresh digest. Equivalent in practice to
`build` here because the only registry-based dep (prometheus) is
hard-pinned at 25.27.0 in Chart.yaml. Local `helm dependency build`
on a freshly cloned repo still works between releases; CI just self-
heals the lock-vs-Chart.yaml drift introduced by release-please.

Also adds `charts/gateway/**` to the workflow's path filters so
gateway-only edits trigger the chart CI (currently they don't, even
though the umbrella depends on the gateway sub-chart).

Verified locally: simulated the rp-branch state by bumping
charts/gateway/Chart.yaml to 3.2.0; `dependency build` fails with the
exact CI error, `dependency update` succeeds, `helm template` renders.

fix(rbac): restore project creation for team members (#3585)

fix(rbac): restore project creation for team members (#3581)

The RBAC migration in #724 changed the project creation permission
check from team-level TEAM_CREATE_NEW_PROJECTS to org-level
organization:manage, accidentally requiring org ADMIN to create
projects. This broke project creation for all non-org-admin users.

Two changes restore the pre-migration behavior:
- Add project:create to MEMBER team permissions (was only on ADMIN)
- Change project.ts check from organization:manage to project:create

RoleBindings at the target team scope, so users without a binding
for that team are denied. Org ADMINs bypass via the org-scoped
ADMIN shortcut.

fix(nlpgo): trace parity — execute_component span + langwatch.input/output JSON + scope-to-single-node + LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT fallback (#3569)

* feat(nlpgo): execute_component span + langwatch.input/output JSON for Studio trace parity

The previous span shape was a single nlpgo.node.<type> span with no
input/output attributes, so the Studio Trace Details drawer fell back
to output_source="inferred" and rendered a near-empty span tree
(rchaves regression callout 2026-04-28).

Match Python langwatch_nlp's optional_langwatch_trace shape:
  - span name:           "execute_component" (was "nlpgo.node.<type>")
  - langwatch.span.type: "component"
  - langwatch.input:     JSON-encoded inputs map
  - langwatch.output:    JSON-encoded outputs map (omitted on error)

Setting langwatch.input/output flips Studio's output_source from
"inferred" → "explicit" so the actual values render in the drawer.

No truncation: agents can return huge outputs and operators want full
content. Python SDK default truncated at 5000 chars/string; we keep
the full payload on the Go path. Downstream limits (OTLP body size,
ClickHouse storage) cap at the wire if needed.

engine.go and stream.go reorder endNodeSpan to run after ns.Outputs
is set, so the success-branch output is captured.

Tests:
  - tracing_test.go covers helper-level shape (name, attrs, JSON I/O,
    error path no-output, 200KB no-truncation, no-attrs absence)
  - tracing_e2e_test.go runs Engine.Execute end-to-end and asserts
    the span tree contains execute_component spans with JSON I/O
    flowing across edges; error path stamps input but not output.

Spec: specs/nlp-go/tracing-parity.feature documents the matrix
covering code/signature/http/evaluator/agent_workflow + execute_flow
+ evaluation batch_run. M1+M2 implemented in this commit; M3+ (per-
implementation child spans, gateway context propagation) follow.

* fix(nlpgo): execute_component scope to single node + LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT fallback for evaluator base URL

Two prod regressions surfaced 2026-04-29 by rchaves once the cold-start
+ post-event lanes landed and Studio actually got responses through:

1. **execute_component runs the WHOLE flow.** Trace showed
   entry+code+end+evaluator spans even when the user only clicked Execute
   on the Code component. Engine walked plan.Layers regardless of
   req.NodeID. Python's execute_component.py instantiates and invokes
   one materialized component, never the DAG; bring Go to parity.

   Fix in Engine.Execute and ExecuteStream: when req.NodeID is set,
   dispatch only that node via runLayer/runLayerStream with a
   single-element layer list. Validates the target exists in the
   workflow up-front so a typo returns a synchronous error instead of
   a silent no-op. Tests in execute_component_scope_test.go pin both
   the sync and stream paths with a 4-node workflow and assert no
   sibling nodes get dispatched.

2. **Evaluator: "LangWatchBaseURL is required to call the evaluator API"**
   on every dispatch. Cause: the resolver only read the explicit
   `NLPGO_ENGINE_LANGWATCH_BASE_URL` env, but prod terraform sets just
   `LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT` (the universal LangWatch URL the rest of the
   pipeline already uses — see configureNLPGoOTel in deps.go). So
   cfg.Engine.LangWatchBaseURL was empty in every prod Lambda.

   Fix in cmd/root.go: extract resolveLangWatchBaseURL helper that
   prefers the explicit cfg field (so dev / docker-compose can still
   point evaluator callbacks at host.docker.internal:5560 without
   touching the universal endpoint) and falls back to LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT
   otherwise. Trailing slash trimmed on the fallback to match the
   shape evaluatorblock.runEvaluator concatenates with. Test in
   root_test.go pins all 5 resolution paths (explicit-wins, fallback,
   slash-trim, neither-set, explicit-preserved) with an injected
   getenv so process env stays clean.

* feat(nlpgo): emit LLM child span around gateway dispatch (M3 step 1 — Python parity for the LLM row in Studio's trace tree)

Studio's Trace Details drawer compared a successful single-component scenario between Python langwatch_nlp (FF=off) and Go nlpgo (FF=on) and surfaced a gap rchaves flagged 2026-04-29:

  Python                                        Go
  ------                                        --
  COMPONENT execute_component (4.1s)            SPAN   nlpgo.studio.execute_stream (3.6s)
   └ MODULE  Llmcall.forward (3.9s)             └ COMPONENT execute_component (3.5s)
     └ MODULE PredictWithMetadata (3.6s)        ✕ no LLM span
       └ LLM openai/gpt-5.2 (24 toks $0.00018)

The Go side had ZERO evidence of the LLM call — no model name, no token count, no cost, no provider. Operators debugging a workflow couldn't tell which model ran or how much it cost.

This commit lands the LLM-row span — the bottom-most node in Python's tree — by wrapping the dispatcher call in `runSignature` with an OTel child span carrying the Python-parity attribute set:

| attr                                | source                                   |
|-------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| span name                           | "<provider>/<model>" (e.g. "openai/gpt-5-mini") |
| span kind                           | Client                                   |
| langwatch.span.type                 | "llm"  (Studio's drawer groups by this)  |
| gen_ai.system                       | provider                                 |
| gen_ai.request.model                | model                                    |
| gen_ai.usage.input_tokens           | resp.Usage.PromptTokens                  |
| gen_ai.usage.output_tokens          | resp.Usage.CompletionTokens              |
| gen_ai.usage.reasoning_tokens       | resp.Usage.ReasoningTokens (omitted if 0)|
| langwatch.cost                      | resp.Cost                                |
| langwatch.duration_ms               | resp.DurationMS                          |
| langwatch.input                     | JSON-encoded request messages            |
| langwatch.output                    | JSON-encoded assistant message           |

Reserved-attr alignment (langwatch.span.type=llm + langwatch.input/output) is what flips Studio's `output_source` from "inferred" to "explicit" so the drawer renders the actual messages instead of best-guess JSON. The standard `gen_ai.*` set is what powers the model/token/cost columns.

Span lives BETWEEN the existing execute_component span (its parent) and the gateway HTTP exchange, so the Studio tree shows execute_component → openai/gpt-5-mini and rolls up tokens correctly. The execute_component duration still covers all child time including this span.

Per spec/tracing-parity.feature §"Per-implementation child span names match the Python entrypoint" §"signature node creates a child span Signature.predict and a grandchild gateway.chat.completions". * fix(nlpgo): treat entry_selection "first"/"last"/"random"/"all" as selection MODES (Python parity)

  if entry_selection == "first": return entries[:1]
  if entry_selection == "last":  return entries[-1:]
  if entry_selection == "random": return [random.choice(entries)]
  return entries  # "all" default

nlpgo's dataset.SelectByEntry instead routed every string through the byString column-name fallback, returning `string_selection_lookup_not_provided` whenever runEntry called it (runEntry passes byString=nil because column-name interpretation is workflow-specific, not engine-level).

- Evaluation run (small dataset)
- Single-item trace from inside an evaluation run

"all" maps to row 0: SelectByEntry's contract is "give me one row". The SSE batch path iterates rows above this layer; sync execute_component falls back to row 0 the same way Python's execute_sync does when no per-row index is set.

* fix(nlpgo): surface upstream LLM provider error message verbatim instead of a bare 'gateway returned non-2xx status'

rchaves dogfood 2026-04-29 saw a 429 in the Studio Trace Details drawer rendered as just `gateway returned non-2xx status 429` — no signal whether the gateway is broken, the API key is invalid, the model is throttled, the prompt is malformed, or the account is out of credits. Turned out to be "out of OpenAI credits" but the error gave the user zero clue.

`GatewayHTTPError.Error()` was throwing away the response body — only formatting the status code. The body always carried OpenAI's standard `{"error":{"message":...}}` envelope (or LiteLLM's top-level `{"message":...}` passthrough variant) with the actual reason: "You exceeded your current quota...", "Rate limit reached for gpt-5-mini", "Incorrect API key provided".

The provider's text is the most useful thing we have; wrapping it would just bury the actionable signal under our own framing. Mirror the LiteLLM behavior the Python path used to expose: pass-through.

Falls back to the historical `gateway returned non-2xx status %d` shape when the body is missing, not JSON, or doesn't carry a recognizable error envelope (raw 5xx HTML from a misbehaving LB, future passthrough endpoints, empty 504s) — preserves a useful signal there too.

The dispatcher + dispatcheradapter chain already passes the body through unchanged (services/nlpgo/adapters/dispatcheradapter/adapter.go:96-100, services/aigateway/dispatcher/dispatcher.go) — no upstream-gateway change needed for this fix. The body was on the floor inside `GatewayHTTPError.Error()` only.

fix(release): chart-release + npx-server tag stripping for langwatch@3.2.0 (#3604)

fix(release): chart-release pipeline + npx-server tag stripping for langwatch@3.2.0

Three independent failures gating the langwatch@v3.2.0 release. Audit and
fixes below.

## release-langwatch-chart (failed)

`helm dependency build charts/langwatch` failed with
`can't get a valid version for dependency langwatch-gateway`.

Root cause: release-please bumps charts/gateway/Chart.yaml `$.version` to
3.2.0 in lockstep with the umbrella, but cannot recompute the sha256 digest
in charts/langwatch/Chart.lock. Helm 3.12's `dependency build` hashes both
the Chart.yaml deps AND the Chart.lock resolved versions together — so the
freshly-bumped sub-chart version invalidates the digest.

PR #3601 papered over the symptom in the template-CI workflow by switching
to `helm dependency update`, which always rewrites the lock. That defeats
the purpose of the lock — and the same band-aid wasn't applied to
release-langwatch-chart.yml, hence today's failure.

Proper fix: keep `dependency build` (strict) everywhere AND have
release-please's PR ship a regenerated Chart.lock. New
release-please-chart-lock-sync.yml watches release-please umbrella PRs,
runs `helm dependency update`, and pushes the refreshed lock back to the
PR branch with a PAT so the chart CI re-runs against the correct state.

This commit:
- reverts langwatch-chart.yml back to `helm dependency build` (PR #3601's
  workaround is no longer needed)
- regenerates charts/langwatch/Chart.lock now so main is consistent
  (gateway 0.1.0 → 3.2.0 + fresh digest) and the next chart-release
  workflow run can succeed for the existing langwatch@v3.2.0 tag
- adds .github/workflows/release-please-chart-lock-sync.yml so future
  release-please PRs self-heal the lock

## npx-server-publish (failed)

Step `Resolve and verify versions` aborted with
`✗ version mismatch: tag=langwatch@v3.2.0 (parsed=v3.2.0) package.json=3.2.0`.

The bash strip was `${tag#langwatch@}` — leaves the leading `v`. All other
component-tag workflows (publish-docker-app, sdk-go-cd, sdk-python-cd,
sdk-javascript-cd, mcp-javascript-cd, publish-docker-clickhouse-serverless)
correctly strip `@v`. Aligning npx-server-publish with the rest.

## Re-running the failed v3.2.0 jobs

After this PR merges, both can be retried via workflow_dispatch:
- `release-langwatch-chart` (dispatch from main) — picks up the new lock
  and publishes langwatch-3.2.0.tgz to gh-pages
- `npx-server-publish` (dispatch from main) — reads version from
  package.json (3.2.0), creates the v3.2.0 GH release with aigateway
  monobinaries, publishes @langwatch/server@3.2.0 to npm @latest

publish-docker-app already succeeded for v3.2.0; the multi-arch manifests
for langwatch / langwatch_nlp / langevals / ai-gateway @ 3.2.0 + latest are
on Docker Hub.
