fix(nlpgo): inline saved datasets + parallelize eval + sklearn-parity train/test split (3.2.0 prod fix) (#3607)

* fix(nlpgo): inline saved datasets in Studio + parallelize eval iteration + sklearn-parity train/test split

Three fixes from the rchaves 2026-04-30 callout that surfaced after
shipping 3.2.0 to prod (a customer hit 'entry node has no inline
dataset (remote datasets not yet supported on Go path)' on a saved-
dataset Evaluate run):

**S1 — Saved (database) datasets work on Go path again.**
Studio's loadDatasets() forwarded saved datasets as dataset_id-only
when entry_selection was 'all', relying on Python's SDK to fetch via
langwatch.dataset.get_dataset(id). The Go engine has no equivalent
fetch port, so any execute_evaluation against a saved dataset blew
up. Now loadDatasets() always inlines server-side via getFullDataset
— both engines see the same uniform shape, Python's path is unchanged
semantically (it took the inline branch already when given inline
data). New unit test pins: inlining on execute_evaluation/full,
inline preservation when already inline, dataset-stripping on
execute_component.

Go engine's defensive guard rewritten to point operators at the
TS-side helper instead of saying 'remote datasets not supported'.

**S2.1 — Eval rows now run in parallel (10 workers, Python parity).**
DSPy Evaluate uses num_threads=10. Pre-fix Go iterated sequentially,
~10x slower for medium-size datasets. Worker pool capped at
min(10, total).

**S2.2 — train/test split shuffle parity with sklearn.**
Python passes shuffle=(seed >= 0), random_state=seed. Pre-fix
splitTrainTest ignored the seed and took an in-order slice. Now
Fisher-Yates with seeded RNG when seed >= 0, in-order fallback
otherwise. Also honors explicit testSize (was discarded as
_ = testSize) so users get the count they asked for, not the full
complement.

* fix(nlpgo): route `type: "custom"` nodes through agentblock.WorkflowRunner

Saved sub-workflow drops in Studio's NodeSelectionPanel emit nodes with
`type: "custom"` and typed `data.workflow_id` / `data.version_id`
(NodeSelectionPanel.tsx:168). Pre-fix the planner blanket-rejected
this kind as "retired" with a misleading replace-the-node hint, even
though the executor (agentblock.WorkflowRunner) was already wired and
tested for `agent_type: workflow` — same wire shape, same auth header,
same do_not_trace=true contract Python's CustomNode.forward emits.

Customer impact: any saved workflow (4+ instances observed in real
data) carrying a `type: "custom"` node would fail the planner stage
on the FF-on path with no diagnosable surface beyond "retired kind".
Fix routes ComponentCustom through a new runCustom executor that
reads the typed Component fields (with defensive fallback to legacy
parameters[] shapes) and invokes the same WorkflowRunner.

Tests:
- planner_test.go::TestPlan_AcceptsCustomKind — pins planner accepts
  the kind (replaces the prior TestPlan_RejectsRetiredKindCustom)
- dsl_patterns_test.go::TestPattern016_CustomNodeKindRoutesToWorkflowRunner
  — end-to-end via /go/studio/execute_sync: typed workflow_id +
  version_id reach /api/workflows/<id>/<v>/run, body carries upstream
  inputs verbatim + do_not_trace=true, wrapper response unwraps to the
  declared output, all nodes succeed
- dsl_patterns_test.go::TestPattern010_CustomNodeMissingWorkflowIDFailsActionably
  — repurposed: pins the typed-error boundary when data.workflow_id
  is empty (Type="custom_missing_workflow_id", Message names the field)

Closes the S2.3 lane from the 2026-04-30 parity sweep.

* fix(nlpgo): wire /v1beta passthrough through dispatcher.Passthrough

Pre-fix, /go/proxy/v1beta/* (Gemini-native generateContent +
streamGenerateContent, called by gemini-cli + Google's GenAI SDK
directly) returned a typed 501 passthrough_not_implemented. The
playground proxy classified the path as RequestTypePassthrough but
short-circuited rather than constructing the dispatcher's
PassthroughRequest, which needed HTTP-shape fields (method, raw query,
forwarded headers) that DispatcherShim didn't carry.

This commit plumbs the passthrough end-to-end:

- adapters/httpapi/playground_proxy.go:
  - playgroundProxyRequest: HTTPMethod/HTTPRawQuery/HTTPHeaders fields
    (only populated when Type=passthrough)
  - DispatcherShim: Passthrough + PassthroughStream methods +
    PassthroughDispatchRequest type
  - shimAdapter routes Type=passthrough to shim.Passthrough/Stream
  - filterPassthroughHeaders helper strips x-litellm-* (already in
    Credential), Authorization/X-Auth-Token (never expected from a
    /v1beta caller in our deployment shape), hop-by-hop, Host,
    Content-Length
  - classifyPath fix: was trimming "/v1" prefix even from "/v1beta",
    leaving "beta/models/..." which broke Gemini's generateContent
    adapter. Now strips "/v1beta" / "/v1" explicitly.

  domain.PassthroughRequest{Method,Path,RawQuery,Headers,Stream}.

- adapters/httpapi/playground_proxy_test.go: replaces the prior
  TestPlaygroundProxy_PassthroughPathReturns500_NotImplemented
  with TestPlaygroundProxy_PassthroughForwardsHTTPShapeToDispatcher.

  (3) HTTPMethod/HTTPPath/HTTPRawQuery captured (4) caller's Accept
  is forwarded but x-litellm-* + Authorization stripped

* fix(nlpgo): honor do_not_trace + workflow.enable_tracing=false

A1 audit from the 2026-04-30 parity sweep found two unhonored trace-
suppression knobs that Python respects but Go ignored:

1. envelope-level event.do_not_trace — set by sub-workflow callers
   (Python's CustomNode.forward / Go's agentblock.WorkflowRunner) on
   /api/workflows/<id>/run bodies. Python's execute_flow.py:53
   wraps the run in optional_langwatch_trace(do_not_trace=True) so the
   inner trace doesn't double-count against the parent's span. Go was
   emitting the inner trace anyway → duplicate spans in LangWatch trace
   UI for any agent_type=workflow / type:custom dispatch.

2. workflow.enable_tracing=false — customer opt-out per workflow. The
   typed field already existed on dsl.Workflow.EnableTracing but no
   code path consulted it. Python defaults true and uses
   `not workflow.enable_tracing or event.do_not_trace` to decide
   suppression.

Fix:
- adapters/httpapi/handlers.go: decode envelope-level do_not_trace +
  peek workflow.enable_tracing; OR them into req.DoNotTrace
- app/app.go: + DoNotTrace bool field on WorkflowRequest
- adapters/httpapi/tracing.go: startStudioSpan returns the no-op
  span-from-context when DoNotTrace is set, mirroring Python's
  optional_langwatch_trace(do_not_trace=True). All engine descendants
  use the no-op parent so they stay silent too.

Tests (handlers_do_not_trace_test.go):
- TestDecodeStudioClientEvent_DoNotTrace_FromEnvelope —
  event.do_not_trace=true → req.DoNotTrace=true
- TestDecodeStudioClientEvent_DoNotTrace_FromEnableTracingFalse —
  workflow.enable_tracing=false → req.DoNotTrace=true
- TestDecodeStudioClientEvent_DoNotTrace_DefaultsFalse — happy path:
  neither set → DoNotTrace=false (engine emits as usual)
- TestPeekWorkflowEnableTracing — defaults true on missing/malformed
  so a malformed workflow doesn't accidentally suppress all
  observability before the engine even runs

* fix(nlpgo): passthrough stream-action detection + Connection-nominated header denylist

Two CodeRabbit findings on PR #3607's S2.5 commit:

(3) /v1beta passthrough stream detection — Gemini-native streaming
endpoints (`:streamGenerateContent`, `:streamRawPredict`) signal
streaming via the URL action suffix on `:`, NOT via OpenAI's
`"stream": true` body flag. peekBodyMetadata only sees the body
flag, so streamGenerateContent calls (gemini-cli + Google GenAI SDK)
fell through to handleSync and discarded SSE deltas. Fix: new
`isPassthroughStreamPath` helper recognizes the known stream actions
and promotes isStream when the action matches. Falls back to
non-stream for unknown actions so a typo on the inbound URL
surfaces as a regular sync 4xx instead of an opened SSE stream that
never closes.

(4) Connection-nominated header denylist — RFC 7230 §6.1 lets the
`Connection` header name additional hop-by-hop tokens
(e.g. `Connection: Foo, Bar` makes Foo/Bar hop-by-hop too).
filterPassthroughHeaders dropped Connection itself but still
forwarded the headers it nominated. Fix: parse the Connection token
list before copying headers and add each token to the per-call skip
set.

Tests:
- TestPlaygroundProxy_PassthroughStreamPathDetectsActionSuffix —
  6 cases covering sync/stream actions and missing/unknown suffixes
- TestFilterPassthroughHeaders_StripsConnectionNominatedHeaders —
  pin the dynamic skip set: `Connection: X-Hop-By-Hop, Trailer-Test`
  blocks both upstream while Accept + X-LangWatch-Trace-Id pass through

Both findings filed by CodeRabbit on review of `094c844b2`. No
behavioral change for the OpenAI/Anthropic-shape paths.

* fix(nlpgo): full Liquid templates in LLM Call instructions + race fixes from CodeRabbit

**S2.4 — Liquid loops/ifs/filters work in LLM Call instructions.**
Pre-fix nlpgo's template renderer was a partial Liquid subset: only
`{{ var }}` interpolation with dotted paths and array indexing. Any
`{% for %}`, `{% if %}`, or pipe-filter usage left the literal tag in
the rendered output, confusing the LLM and breaking parity with
Python (`langwatch_nlp/.../template_adapter.py` uses python-liquid).

New `template.RenderFull` routes through `github.com/osteele/liquid`
when the template uses Liquid-extended syntax, falling back to the
existing `template.Render` for pure `{{ var }}` templates so the
HTTP-block JSON-escape semantics (the existing template_test.go pins)
stay intact.

`coerceForLiquid` mirrors langwatch_nlp's `_coerce_for_liquid`:
strings that arrived through the TS↔NLP wire as JSON-stringified
arrays/objects are parsed back into native Go containers so
`{% for m in messages %}` works on a chat-history value.

LLM Call's `composeSystemPrompt` (engine.go:1187) now uses RenderFull;
HTTP block keeps using Render. Five new test cases pin the contract:
loop iteration, if/else branching, pipe filters, JSON-string coerce,
parse-error fault tolerance.

**CodeRabbit critical (#1) — data race on progress counter.**
`evaluationReporter.recordEntry` writes `progress` under a mutex; the
worker pool was reading `reporter.progress` directly across
goroutines (a race per Go memory model). New `progressCount()` helper
reads under the same mutex; ExecuteStream's per-row event emission
goes through it.

**CodeRabbit major (#2) — success after cancellation.**
When ctx was canceled mid-iteration the loop emitted an error event
then `break`'d, but execution still reached the unconditional
`workflowSuccessEvent` at the end — producing two terminal states for
one run. Now tracks a `canceled` flag and short-circuits to the done
event after the error. Final batch flush uses a fresh
`context.Background()` when canceled so partial results still post
(operator visibility into how far the eval got before it was killed).

The OpenAI bill on PYTHON_SDK_OPENAI_API_KEY was ~$14/day (gpt-5
output dominating), which made the dashboard label misleading: the
key was shared across sdk-python-ci, langevals-ci, and
langwatch-nlp-ci, so "langwatch-nlp-ci" in the OpenAI breakdown was
actually all three jobs combined.

   - langevals-ci → LANGEVALS_OPENAI_API_KEY (new)
   - langwatch-nlp-ci → LANGWATCH_NLP_OPENAI_API_KEY (new)
   This makes per-workflow spend visible in the OpenAI dashboard and
   limits blast radius if any one key leaks.

2. python-sdk/examples/* hardcoded model="gpt-5" (full, $10/1M output).
   `make test-examples` runs every example end-to-end, so the bill
   compounded across PRs. Switched all 23 example files to
   "gpt-5-mini" per the CLAUDE.md rule. Examples are documentation;
   they don't need flagship-tier reasoning to demonstrate API usage.

The mass gpt-5 → gpt-5-mini rewrite incorrectly touched this assertion.
The example exercises `npx langwatch@latest prompt create` and verifies

typescript-sdk/src/cli/commands/create.ts). The example never makes a

perf(group-queue): score-based dispatch filter to cut Redis CPU under backlog (#3654)

* perf(group-queue): score-based dispatch filter to cut Redis CPU under backlog

Encodes group dispatchability in the ready zset score so dispatch only
walks groups that are actually dispatchable. Replaces ZREVRANGE-then-skip
with a single ZRANGEBYSCORE filter.

Score semantics on readyKey:
- earliest pending job's dispatchAfter when group has eligible jobs
- nowMs + activeTtlSec*1000 while a job is processing (heartbeat refreshes)
- removed when blocked or empty

Migration: legacy entries with score=1 remain dispatchable (1 < nowMs)
and get re-scored on first dispatch/complete. No data loss.

* perf(group-queue): address PR review — active/blocked gates and dispatch pagination

Addresses Copilot and CodeRabbit feedback on PR #3654:

- STAGE_LUA / STAGE_BATCH_LUA: skip ready-score updates while the group is
  processing (active key set) or blocked. Prevents lowering ready below
  activeUntil and re-introducing the dispatch hot-path skips. Active heartbeat
  / completion / unblock paths own the score in those states.
- REFRESH_LUA: only ZADD when the group is already in ready (ZSCORE gate).
  Prevents heartbeat from re-inserting a blocked group that RESTAGE_AND_BLOCK
  removed mid-flight, preserving the "blocked => not in ready" invariant.
- DISPATCH_LUA / DISPATCH_BATCH_LUA: page through ZRANGEBYSCORE up to a
  bounded scan budget so a head full of paused / blocked / legacy-drift
  entries does not starve runnable groups deeper in the zset.

Adds integration coverage:
- stage does not lower ready score while group is active
- stage does not re-add blocked group to ready
- refreshActiveKey does not reinsert a blocked group
- refreshActiveKey pushes ready score to nowMs + activeTtlSec*1000

fix(clickhouse): IN-tuple dedup on hot projection state reads (#3664)

* perf(clickhouse): IN-tuple dedup on hot projection state reads

Two repository methods read the latest version of a projection row from
ReplacingMergeTree tables using `ORDER BY UpdatedAt DESC LIMIT 1`. With
many unmerged versions per key, that pattern forces ClickHouse to read
every version *with the heavy columns* into memory just to sort by
UpdatedAt — a 100×+ read amplification under load.

Switched both to the IN-tuple dedup form: an inner SELECT scans only the
sparse `(key..., UpdatedAt)` tuple to find the latest version, the outer
SELECT then reads the heavy columns for that single row.

- `TraceSummaryClickHouseRepository.getByTraceId` — called per-event
  during the trace-summary projection apply (highest-frequency hot path).
- `EvaluationRunClickHouseRepository.getByEvaluationId` — same pattern,
  lower volume but heavier per-call payload.

Pattern documented in dev/docs/best_practices/clickhouse-queries.md;
this commit aligns the two highest-volume callers with it.

Follow-up sweep PR will cover the remaining ReplacingMergeTree
repositories (experiment_runs, simulation_runs, billable_events, etc.)
with the same anti-pattern.

* fix(clickhouse): qualify UpdatedAt with table alias in IN-tuple dedup

The outer SELECT projects `toUnixTimestamp64Milli(UpdatedAt) AS UpdatedAt`,
shadowing the raw DateTime64 column with a UInt64 alias. Without table
qualification the WHERE-clause `UpdatedAt` in the IN-tuple comparison
could resolve to the projected alias rather than the raw column, leading
to a type-mismatch with the inner subquery's `max(UpdatedAt)`.

Switched both repositories' outer SELECT/WHERE to reference columns via
a `t.` table alias as called out in
dev/docs/best_practices/clickhouse-queries.md.

* perf(ops): split badge counts off the dashboard snapshot query

The global ops badge in the main menu polls every 60s on every page —
which dragged the full dashboard aggregation (pipeline tree, error
normalization, etc.) into every off-route tRPC batch. Because tRPC's
httpBatchLink waits on every procedure in the batch before responding,
one slow getDashboardSnapshot call would stall the page-level queries
batched alongside it.

Split out a getBadgeCounts procedure that returns just the two integers
the badge renders. Off-route the menu polls only this; on-route it
keeps using the full snapshot since the user actually wants the data.

Result is memoized for 5s on the server so concurrent calls (multi-tab,
layout remounts) share a single computation. computedAt timestamp
ships back so callers can tell how stale the value is.

rows only re-render when their own data, lens config, or status flags
change. Inline callbacks are skipped on purpose — they read latest parent
state from a stable closure, so identity churn doesn't affect paint.

useTraceLensColumns: comfortable-density columns are derived from traces
(eval keys, event names, has-error). Previously the memo depended on the
traces array reference itself, so every SSE refresh rebuilt the column
model and forced TanStack Table to rebuild row models, which re-rendered
every row. Now the memo depends on a stable column-shape signature, so
SSE refreshes that don't change shape leave the column model untouched.

* perf(traces-v2): memoize TracesPage subtree boundaries

TracesPage drives 13 hooks at the top — store subscriptions, URL sync,
freshness, presence, debounced filter, etc. Every subscription tick
re-rendered the whole page, cascading through FilterAside, ResultsPane,
and the FilterSidebar's DndContext.

Wraps FilterAside, ResultsPane, and EmptyResultsPane in React.memo so
hook-driven parent re-renders stop at each child boundary; each subtree
only re-renders when its own subscriptions actually fire.

Multi-phase workout numbers (cumulative since previous commits):
- Scroll: +276MB heap → +25MB; 70 long tasks → 6; 443ms max stall → 67ms
- Drawer open: +79MB → +1MB
- Viz tabs 1→5 cycle: was leaking ~130MB/cycle (peak 668MB) → now flat
- Idle 5s: ~2 long tasks → 0

* feat(traces-v2): highlight + filter LangWatch-instrumented spans

Adds a secondary `tracesV2.spanLangwatchSignals` endpoint that scans
SpanAttributes keys and buckets them (prompt, scenario, user, thread,
evaluation, rag, metadata, genai). Both Waterfall and Span List views
overlay badges per row and expose a "Only LangWatch" toggle that prunes
non-instrumented spans (preserving ancestors in the waterfall tree).
Detection runs as a parallel query so the primary span tree fetch stays
on its existing fast path.

* perf(presence): stable selectors + memoized cursor list

Two related fixes that flatten the presence-driven re-render storm.

1. Presence-store selectors (selectPeersOnTrace, selectPeersOnConversation,
   selectPeersMatching) all return a freshly filtered array. Zustand's
   default Object.is comparator misses that, so every cursor tick on any
   peer woke every subscriber — six different presence components, often
   one per row — even when their slice was unchanged. All six call sites
   now subscribe via useShallow so identical-content arrays short-circuit.

2. usePeerCursors returned Array.from(map.values()) on every call,
   handing PeerCursorOverlay a new array reference on every parent render
   regardless of cursor state. Wrapped in useMemo keyed on the Map
   identity so the array stays stable when nothing has changed.

Profile data showed TracePresenceAvatars as the #1 commit-scheduler in
the session (259 of ~338 commits). With the table tree memoized in the
prior commits, those wasted commits short-circuit at the row boundary —
this fix kills them at the source.

* perf: memo PeerCursor, TracePresenceAvatars, CurrentDrawer parse

Three small follow-ups that close the remaining churn paths exposed by the
profile.

PeerCursor: each peer's marker is rendered as a child of PeerCursorOverlay.
Without memo, every cursor tick from any peer re-renders all of them
(parent's cursors array is rebuilt by the prior usePeerCursors fix, but
the children themselves still reconciled). React.memo skips peers whose
own cursor object hasn't changed.

TracePresenceAvatars: takes only primitive props (traceId, max, size) so
default React.memo just works. With useShallow already in place upstream,
this short-circuits avatar instances on rows whose peer set hasn't changed.

CurrentDrawer: re-parsed qs.parse and re-allocated the queryDrawer object
on every render, handing whatever drawer is mounted a fresh props object
each tick — which cascaded a re-render through the drawer subtree even
when nothing drawer-relevant changed. Wrapped the parse in useMemo keyed
on the URL query string so the drawer component sees a stable spread.

* fix(presence): stop broadcasting email + add cross-tenant guard

Drop `email` from `PresenceUser` and the two router payload constructions
(`update`, `cursor`). Email was only used as a fallback display label and
was being fanned out to every project member with `traces:view` — a needless
data-minimization gap in a real-time channel.

Also adds a defensive check in `onPresenceUpdate` that drops any join/update
event whose `session.projectId` doesn't match the subscriber's projectId.
The per-tenant emitter already isolates events; this is belt-and-braces in
case a future broadcast refactor regresses the boundary.

* style(ui): drop backdrop-filter from menu + popover

Tiny/transient/multiplied surfaces (menus, popovers) shouldn't carry
the brand blur — it stacks weirdly when many menus open at once and
muddies the underlying content. Keep blur reserved for Drawer/Dialog.

* style: fg.DEFAULT → fg across onboarding + form inputs

DEFAULT is theme-definition plumbing; consumers should write color="fg"
directly. No visual change.

* perf(hooks): bump client staleTime for feature flags + ops scope to 5min

Both queries fire from many consumers (every drawer open, every layout
mount). Without staleTime, React Query refetched on every observer
mount even though the server already short-circuits with its own
5s cache, so the per-page request volume was doubling for no
freshness gain. Move client-side staleTime to 5min — kill switches
still propagate quickly via the server cache; ops scope doesn't
change mid-session.

* refactor(query-language): split queryParser into focused modules

The 700-line queryParser.ts mixed parsing, AST walking, validation,
mutation helpers, and field metadata into one file — every change
touched everything. Split along the natural seams:

  parse.ts     — AST construction + isEmptyAST
  queries.ts   — query execution + validateAst
  mutations.ts — AST mutation helpers
  walk.ts      — AST traversal
  metadata.ts  — SEARCH_FIELDS + FIELD_VALUES

Test file renamed to match the new shape.

* refactor(foundry): factor traceExecutor into reusable factory

Replace the per-call executeTrace() helper with getFoundryExecutor() —
construct one executor (apiKey + endpoint + projectId + resource
attributes) and reuse it across the loop in ExecutionControls,
FoundryDrawer, and GenerateConversationDialog. Avoids re-initialising
the OTel exporter / setting up the SDK on every send in batch mode.

Also drops the unused PlaygroundDrawer + aiClient/langwatchClient
helpers (superseded by traceExecutor) and adds the OTLP-HTTP exporter
package the new executor needs.

* refactor(traces-v2/searchbar): chip + delete-button as joined siblings

The X used to overlap the right edge of the chip via negative margin
and a 22px right padding well — fragile against sub-pixel rounding,
the chip looked frayed in some browsers, and the X faded out unless
hovered. Restyle as two adjacent inline-flex pieces glued with a
-1px overlap: the token gets only the left half of the border + radius,
the X picks up the right half. whiteSpace:nowrap prevents the editor
from breaking the pair across lines. Variant tints (exclude/scenario)
mirror onto the X via sibling selectors.

Drive-by: tightened editorStyles + filterHighlight; +browser test for
ActiveSearchEditor and unit tests for filterHighlight.

* refactor(traces-v2): migrate FilterSidebar + filterStore to split query-language

Mechanical follow-up to the query-language module split — point each
consumer at its new home (parse/queries/mutations/metadata). No
behaviour change.

* perf(traces-v2/drawer): lazy mount accordions, pin latest turn, chunk markdown

A handful of independent drawer wins:

- AccordionShell gains opt-in `open` prop that defers child mount until
  the section opens at least once. Saves work for sections the operator
  never expands on a given trace.
- ConversationTurnsList pins to the latest turn on mount (both inline and
  virtualized paths) — operators land on what's new, not a wall of
  carried-forward chat history.
- ConversationView's MarkdownView builds chunks instead of one giant
  string, so the virtualizer only renders the chunks on screen.
- annotations queries gain 5min staleTime + no refetchOnWindowFocus
  (TraceHeaderChips, AnnotationsView).
- DrawerHeader drops the redundant `Thread` auto-pin — it just echoed
  Conversation when no explicit thread was set.

* refactor(traces-v2): migrate JsonHighlight + markdown to Chakra CodeBlock

Replace the hand-rolled JSON tokenizer in `TraceDrawer/JsonHighlight`
with Shiki via Chakra's `CodeBlock`, matching the onboarding
JsonHighlight surface. The drawer + onboarding env block now share one
highlighter pipeline (one `useShikiAdapter`, one set of themes).

Hoist the highlighted-line styling to a global rule in `_app.tsx`
(`[data-line][data-highlight]:after` → orange) so every code block in
the app — drawer pinned attributes, onboarding env blocks, future
surfaces — picks up the LangWatch tracing-orange accent without each
caller re-declaring the colour.

Drive-bys in the markdown stack: thinner `RenderedMarkdown`,
deduplicated `shikiAdapter` highlighter cache, broader exports from
markdownView/index.ts.

* refactor(onboarding): polish Claude Code/Desktop screens + endpoint rule

ViaClaudeCodeScreen: clicks anywhere on a prompt row copy the prompt
(matches SkillRow's whole-row affordance), with an animated Check on
success. Drop the dead `glassCard({ highlight })` branch — every card
now uses the same border, hover swaps to orange.emphasized.

ViaClaudeDesktopScreen: same row-as-button pattern; consistent visual
language across the two paths.

ApiIntegrationInfoCard: only render `LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT=` when the
deployment differs from the public cloud default. Cloud users never
need this in `.env`. Routed through the shared `CLOUD_ENDPOINT`
constant so the comparison can't drift.

* feat(traces-v2): empty-state onboarding tour with seeded preview traces

Replace the dual-banner empty state with a single staged journey that
makes a brand-new project feel like a populated, interactive product
the moment they land on /traces. See `prd-024-empty-state-tour.md`
for the full design.

Stages (driven by `onboardingStageStore` + `onboardingJourneyConfig`):
  density       — hero centred, table populated with seeded preview traces
  postArrival   — two arrival traces appear at the top of the table
  drawerOverview — drawer auto-opens with rich seeded content; glow ring
  facetsReveal  — sidebar reveals with matching glow
  outro         — exit cleanly; per-project dismissal persists

Preview traces (`samplePreviewTraces.ts`) feed the table and drawer
without hitting tRPC — `usePreviewTracesActive` short-circuits
`useTraceListQuery`, and ten read-side hooks (`useTraceHeader`,
`useSpanTree`, `useSpansFull`, `useTraceEvals`, `useTraceEvents`,
`useSpanDetail`, `useSpanLangwatchSignals`, `useTraceSpanTree`,
`useConversationContext`, plus `useOpenTraceDrawer`'s rich seeding)
gate on `isPreviewTraceId` so the synthetic IDs never round-trip to
ClickHouse. The drawer + table render from the same fixture set.

Server-side, `projectMetadata.reactor` skips traces tagged
`langwatch.origin = "sample"` so the seed-sample-data path can't
prematurely flip `firstMessage`/`integrated` and dismiss the journey
before the user has connected their own app.

`EmptyFilterState` now distinguishes "never sent" (intercepted by the
journey via `firstMessage=false`) from "real but empty in this
window" — the latter gets actionable copy + a rewatch link.

`PatIntegrationInfoCard` is reworked to mint a PAT inline and surface
an env block (LANGWATCH_API_KEY + X-Project-Id) with the global
[data-line] orange highlight; `IntegrateDrawer` and `SampleDataBanner`
provide the two onramps. `useEdgeGripAnchor` keeps the hero centred
in the *visible* canvas when the drawer is open.

Drops the old `DemoModeBanner` + `sampleTraceTemplates` + `useSampleData`
trio (replaced by the staged journey).

fix(clickhouse): in-tuple dedup sweep across remaining projection repos (#3665)

* perf(clickhouse): IN-tuple dedup sweep across remaining projection repos

Sweep companion to perf/evaluation-runs-in-tuple-dedup. The same
`ORDER BY <version> DESC LIMIT 1` anti-pattern over ReplacingMergeTree
tables existed in every other projection-state repository. Under load
each call reads every unmerged version of the matching key tuple
*together with all heavy columns* into memory just to sort by the
version column.

Switched all of them to the IN-tuple form documented in
dev/docs/best_practices/clickhouse-queries.md: an inner SELECT on the
sparse `(key..., UpdatedAt)` tuple finds the latest version, an outer
SELECT pulls the heavy columns for that single row.

Repos converted (each was a "load latest projection state" call):
- app-layer/suites/repositories/suite-run.clickhouse.repository.ts
  (`getSuiteRunState`)
- app-layer/dspy-steps/repositories/dspy-step.clickhouse.repository.ts
  (`getStep`)
- evaluations-v3/services/clickhouse-experiment-run.service.ts
  (`getRun` summary block)
- event-sourcing/pipelines/simulation-processing/repositories/
  simulationRunState.clickhouse.repository.ts (`getProjection`)
- event-sourcing/pipelines/experiment-run-processing/repositories/
  experimentRunState.clickhouse.repository.ts (`getProjection`)
- event-sourcing/pipelines/suite-run-processing/repositories/
  suiteRunState.clickhouse.repository.ts (`getProjection`)

Where the SELECT projects `UpdatedAt` via `toUnixTimestamp64Milli(...) AS
UpdatedAt`, the IN-tuple comparison must reference the raw column via a
table alias (`t.UpdatedAt`) — without the alias ClickHouse resolves
`UpdatedAt` to the projected UInt64 alias, breaking the type comparison.
The doc's "Single-Row Lookups" section already calls this out; this PR
applies the same fix consistently.

Doc changes: added an explicit "Anti-Pattern 1" section calling out
`ORDER BY <version> DESC LIMIT 1` (the most common form of the bug),
and a Code Review Checklist at the end so the next reviewer catches it.

Skipped:
- gateway/budget.clickhouse.repository.ts — `ORDER BY OccurredAt DESC`
  there is a legitimate time-ordered ledger range query, not a "load
  latest version" lookup.
- pipelineRegistry.ts:568 lookupExperimentId — selects a single small
  column (ExperimentId), so the read amplification is bounded; not worth
  bundling here.

* fix(clickhouse): qualify UpdatedAt with table alias in suite-run repo

Same alias-shadow class as the hotfix companion: SELECT projects
`toUnixTimestamp64Milli(UpdatedAt) AS UpdatedAt` and the IN-tuple
WHERE referenced bare `UpdatedAt`, which can bind to the projected
UInt64 alias instead of the raw DateTime64 column. Aliased the table
to `t` and qualified all column references in the outer block.

* perf(clickhouse): PREWHERE + partition prune for evaluation_runs lookup

Post-deploy of the IN-tuple hotfix (#3664) confirmed the
trace_summaries.getByTraceId fix worked (5.8MB → 0.05MB per call) but
evaluation_runs.getByEvaluationId stayed at ~5.8MB per call.

Two ClickHouse-specific shapes the IN-tuple alone didn't fix:

1. The plain `WHERE … AND (…) IN (…)` form lets the engine read heavy
   ZSTD(3) columns (Inputs, Details, Error, ErrorDetails) for every
   unmerged version of the matched key range *before* the IN-tuple
   filters. Switched to `PREWHERE` so the IN-tuple is evaluated first
   and heavy columns only get decompressed for the one row that wins
   max(UpdatedAt).

2. `evaluation_runs` is `PARTITION BY toYearWeek(ScheduledAt)`. Without a
   bound on `ScheduledAt`, the engine scans every weekly partition
   (incl. cold storage on S3). Added an optional `scheduledAt` hint —
   when the caller knows when the eval was scheduled, we partition-prune
   to a ±7 day window (covers the typical schedule → run → archive
   lifetime).

API change: `EvaluationRunRepository.getByEvaluationId` and the matching
service method gain an optional third `hints?: GetByEvaluationIdHints`
arg with `{ scheduledAt?, scheduledAtSlackMs? }`. Default behaviour
unchanged when no hints are passed (still PREWHERE, no partition
predicate).

Follow-up: thread `scheduledAt` through `ProjectionStoreContext` so the
projection-apply hot path (the dominant caller of this method) actually
uses the partition predicate. Right now the hot path benefits only from
PREWHERE; the partition prune is available to non-hot callers that have
the value.

Doc/best-practices reference: dev/docs/best_practices/clickhouse-queries.md.

* refactor(evaluations): named-params object for getByEvaluationId

Switch the EvaluationRunRepository contract and EvaluationRunService
method from positional `(tenantId, evaluationId, hints?)` to a single
`GetByEvaluationIdParams` object. Matches the project convention to use
named parameters via object destructuring once a function has more than
one argument, and removes the per-call ambiguity called out by the
CodeRabbit nitpick on #3665.

* fix(clickhouse): include LastEventOccurredAt in evaluation_runs.getByEvaluationId

The SELECT was missing this column, so fromClickHouseRecord fell back to
the `?? 0` branch and every load returned `lastEventOccurredAt: 0`. The
projection executor uses it for out-of-order event detection
(foldProjectionExecutor.ts:36-50); without the real value the
strictly-less-than check never fires and the re-fold path is silently
unreachable for evaluation-run projections.

Alias is camelCase (`lastEventOccurredAt`) to match the
ClickHouseEvaluationRunRecord field and the reader at
fromClickHouseRecord. Pre-existing on main; surfaced by a CodeRabbit
review on the rebase of #3665.

* fix(clickhouse): unify lastEventOccurredAt → LastEventOccurredAt across evaluation_runs and trace_summaries

Migration 00015 left two tables (evaluation_runs, trace_summaries) with a
camelCase `lastEventOccurredAt` column while the other three tables
(simulation_runs, experiment_runs, suite_runs) used PascalCase
`LastEventOccurredAt`. The mismatch caused JSONEachRow readers/writers
that referenced `LastEventOccurredAt` to silently miss the field —
falling through `?? 0` and breaking out-of-order event detection in
foldProjectionExecutor.

00022 renames the column on both tables (metadata-only, no part rewrite
on ReplacingMergeTree). Code is unified to PascalCase for the column
identifier, the projection state key, and the TS domain field on
EvaluationRunData / TraceSummaryData.

fix(ops): wire SSE through tRPC subscription and virtualize dashboard tables (#3708)

* fix(ops): wire up SSE route and virtualize dashboard tables

The /api/ops/sse endpoint was a Pages Router-style handler that the Hono
api-router never picked up, so the dashboard was 404ing on first connect
and falling back to polling. Port it to a Hono route under
src/server/routes/ops-sse.ts and refactor OpsMetricsCollector.addClient
to take a generic SSEStream interface (write/end) so it works against a
ReadableStream as well as Node ServerResponse.

While here, virtualize the long flat tables on the ops dashboard
(GroupsCard, BlockedCard, DlqCard) using @tanstack/react-virtual with the
same padding-row pattern as evaluations-v3's VirtualizedTableBody. Each
table now lives in a fixed-height scroll container with a sticky header
and a 30-row threshold so small tables stay un-virtualized. GroupsCard
no longer caps its rendered list at 100 since virtualization makes the
full set cheap.

* refactor(ops): switch dashboard SSE to a tRPC subscription

Drop the bespoke /api/ops/sse Hono route and the SSE-client tracking on
OpsMetricsCollector in favor of a dashboardStream tRPC subscription. The
collector now exposes an EventEmitter and emits "dashboard" on each
broadcast tick; the subscription procedure yields the current snapshot
and then replays emitter events using events.on(..., { signal }), the
same pattern as traces.onTraceUpdate. Auth + RBAC reuse the existing
opsViewPermission middleware, and the client goes through the existing
sseLink at /api/sse/<path>.

useOpsSSE drops the EventSource wiring and just calls
api.ops.dashboardStream.useSubscription.

* fix(ops): stable row keys for virtualized tables and reset scroll on filter change

Three review-driven fixes on the virtualized ops dashboard tables:

- VirtualizedTableRows now accepts getItemKey and forwards it to
  useVirtualizer. Without this, react-virtual falls back to row index for
  vi.key, so a row that shifts position keeps the previous DOM node and
  leaks state across reorders.
- GroupsCard, BlockedCard and DlqCard supply stable item keys derived
  from the underlying record (queueName + groupId, queueName +
  normalizedMessage). BlockedCard's inner Table.Row also drops its
  index-based key for the same composite.
- GroupsCard resets scrollContainer.scrollTop on filter/search change.

fix(clickhouse): lazy-register backup gauges so only workers report them (#3747)

* fix(clickhouse): lazy-register backup gauges so only workers report them

The clickhouse_backup_* gauges were registered at module load and exported
by every process that imported metrics.ts (including the langwatch app),
but only worker pods actually run startStorageStatsCollection. App pods
emitted them as 0 forever. The "ClickHouse Backup Missing" alert relied
on a `> 0` filter to mask this, which silently degraded into NoData when
worker gauges briefly read 0 (fresh pod start, system.backups query
failing, etc.) — and on May 2 a worker rollout left every gauge at 0 for
~10h, with the rule auto-resolving via noDataState=OK.

Lazy-register the gauges on first successful update so:
- non-worker pods never expose them
- a missing series becomes a meaningful "no worker is reporting" signal
  (pairs with switching the rule to noDataState=Alerting)

Also promote the inner system.backups failure log from debug to warn so
silent failures of that query are visible in prod.

* review: throttle backup-stats warn + assert lazy gauge registration

Address Copilot review feedback on PR #3747:

1. collectStorageStats runs every 15s, so the new warn for failed
   system.backups queries would emit 5,760 identical warnings/day if
   the table is unavailable. Make the log edge-triggered: warn only on
   the failure->success transition (or first failure), debug otherwise.
   Emit info on success->failure->success recovery so we know it
   resolved without needing prod log noise.

2. Add tests asserting:
   - backup gauges are NOT constructed at module import time
   - each backup gauge is constructed only on first set call
   - each backup gauge is constructed at most once across repeated calls
   - the failure-logging state machine: one warn for repeated failures,
     a recovery info message, then warn again on a fresh failure cycle

Tests now spy on the logger via a mocked ~/utils/logger/server, which
also silences spurious WARN/ERROR output from the simulated-failure
test cases.

* fix(test): type mock.calls filter as unknown[][] not fixed-length tuple

vi.Mock.mock.calls is any[][] (variable arity), so destructuring to a
fixed-length tuple like [, msg] tripped tsgo's strict overload check.
Switch to a small countCallsMatching helper that takes a positional
index, which matches the actual any[][] shape.

fix(ui): defer mermaid + emoji-picker imports to prevent prod boot crash (#3751)

A top-level value-import from a heavy library (`mermaid`,
`emoji-picker-react`) defeats a sibling `lazy()` / `dynamic()` wrapper:
Rollup collapses the lib into the parent chunk's eager static graph,
which rewires the lib's internal `__name`/helper plumbing and crashes at
top-level evaluation with "X is not a function".

The recently merged traces-v2 work introduced
`import mermaid from "mermaid"` in `useMermaidRenderer.ts` and a static
skeleton import via `./sequenceView/index.ts`, which together pulled the
entire mermaid graph into the trace-page chunk. `EmojiPickerModal` had
the same latent shape via a static enum import that defeated its own
`dynamic()` wrapper.

- useMermaidRenderer: load mermaid via `await import("mermaid")` inside
  the effect (matches the pre-existing `SequenceDiagram.tsx` pattern).
- VizPlaceholder: import skeletons from their direct files rather than
  the index re-export, so the lazy SequenceView graph stays gated.
- EmojiPickerModal: convert the value-import of `EmojiStyle` /
  `SkinTonePickerLocation` to a `type`-only import with local string
  literals matching the enum values.

Verified with `NODE_ENV=production vite build` — the main `index` chunk
and trace-page chunk no longer statically reference mermaid or
emoji-picker; both libs are reached only via dynamic imports.

fix(traces): move filter row click handler from Checkbox to HStack (#3749) (#3753)

* test(filters): add failing regression test for #3749

Asserts setFilters is called when a filter option is clicked. Fails on

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(traces): use onCheckedChange on filter row checkboxes (#3749)

Chakra v3's Checkbox.Root is backed by Ark/Zag, which surfaces toggle
state through onCheckedChange. The onChange={handler} wiring introduced
in #3528 was silently dropped in production browsers, so clicking any
filter option (origin, model, metadata.*, etc.) on /messages did nothing
and the URL never updated.

Swap onChange→onCheckedChange on the two virtualised Checkbox rows in
ListSelection (the standard option row and the "custom value" row), and
simplify the closure to take no args — onCheckedChange's signature is
({ checked }), not a DOM event, so e.preventDefault/stopPropagation are
no longer needed.

The failing regression test landed in the previous commit is updated to
lock in the post-fix contract: clicking a virtualised option's input
fires setFilters with the toggled value. jsdom is more lenient than the
production browser regarding React's synthetic onChange bubbling, so the
test cannot prove the bug fails without the fix — the production repro
on /messages remains the canonical evidence. The test still guards
against future regressions where the toggle path is broken entirely.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(traces): move filter row click handler from Checkbox to HStack (#3749)

onCheckedChange on the Chakra v3 Checkbox does not fire reliably when the
control sits inside a Popover + virtualizer in the production browser —
clicks on the visible label/control area are intercepted by Ark/Zag's
internal pointer event machinery and never bubble to a callback our code
can observe. The previous attempt to fix #3528 by swapping onChange→
onCheckedChange improved jsdom behaviour but left the production /messages
filters still inert.

Move the click handler from the <Checkbox> onto the wrapping <HStack> row
container so a click anywhere on the row toggles the filter, regardless
of how deep into the Checkbox internals the click landed. The Checkbox
becomes purely visual (controlled `checked` only) — keyboard navigation
already drives toggling through the existing handleSelectByIndex path,
not through the Checkbox itself.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

on the same page used the identical broken pattern (<Checkbox onChange>
inside a Popover). Hoist the click handler to the wrapping <HStack> row
so a click anywhere on the row toggles the column, mirroring the fix

fix(traces-v2): testing-pass polish — formatter, drawer header, sticky sections (#3765)

* fix(traces-v2): bug bash round — drawer, table, and tour polish

Fixes a clutch of UX bugs caught during Traces V2 testing.

Table:
- Empty-on-load. Virtualizer was initialised before its scroll element
  attached and never recovered, so a fresh /traces nav rendered the
  pagination ("Page 1 of 26") with zero rows. Replaced the module-level
  RefObject with a useSyncExternalStore-backed scroll-element store so
  the virtualizer re-renders the moment the box mounts. Added an owned-
  element guard so the cleanup-fire from a layout that just unmounted
  can't clobber the newer layout's already-published element when the
  page swaps between ResultsPane and EmptyResultsPane (e.g. tour
  activation with real data already loaded).

Drawer:
- "Click to interact" now only shows when the preview content actually
  overflows. Tracked via a ResizeObserver on the preview Box; short
  inputs render flat with no scrim or dim opacity.
- Missing OUTPUT no longer hides the section. Renders a dim italic
  "— no output recorded" placeholder so the gap is visible at a glance.
- Sticky-stack accordion section headers. Each trigger pins at
  `stackIndex * 32px`, so collapsed triggers above the open section
  stay at the top of the scroll container as the user scrolls — the
  Notion-style pattern.
- Merged Scenario / Scenario-run pills. The hoisted `scenario.run_id`
  attribute pin is suppressed when the rich ScenarioChip is firing,
  and the chip's label is now "Scenario run" (single source of truth).

Onboarding tour:
- Aurora animation sped up (~50%); curtains cycle in 4.25–6.75s rather
  than 8.5–13.5s so the ribbon reads as something happening *now*.
- Aurora arrival now plays in two beats: ribbon-only first, then rows
  arrive while the ribbon is still on screen. Adds a new
  `auroraLanding` stage between `auroraArrival` and `postArrival`;
  RichRowGlow's ACTIVE_STAGES updated to glow during the landing beat.
- Rich-row glow now spans both rows of the trace's tbody in
  comfortable density (top stroke on tr:first-child, bottom on
  tr:last-child, sides on first/last cell of each row, no middle seam).
  Compact density still works because :first-child === :last-child.
- Outro chapter is now a thin top banner instead of a centred overlay
  panel. Adds heroLayout: "topBanner"; mesh and hero band suppress
  during outro so the live table is fully visible underneath. Single
  CTA + dismiss; the duplicate "Integrate my code" button and the
  orphan "Skip for now" / "Integration overview" footer are suppressed
  during outro so the banner owns the chrome.

* fix(traces-v2): unify I/O preview formatter, header cleanup, density-aware drawer

#1 — input/output preview formatting

Adds `langwatch/src/features/traces-v2/utils/previewFormatter.ts` as the
single source of truth for one-line/short-block I/O previews. The four
preview surfaces (table cell, group preview, conversation context strip,
system prompt banner) had four divergent formatting paths — none of
which handled fenced code blocks, none unwrapped single-key JSON
envelopes, and the nowrap-styled ones silently collapsed `\n` runs into
nothing so multiline content looked like one squashed line.

The new pipeline runs once per call site:

  raw
    → JSON unwrap (chat array | Anthropic typed block | single-key
      envelope from a tight allowlist: question/input/prompt/query/text
      /content/message)
    → markdown noise strip (```lang\n…``` fences keep body, ![](url)
      images become "📷 alt")
    → newline treatment ("glyph": " ↵ ", "space": collapse, "preserve":
      verbatim)
    → trim + hard-cap

Each surface picks the treatment that matches its CSS:
- Table cell / group preview / conversation-context strip → "glyph" so
  the reader can see structure existed without losing the cell to wrap.
- System prompt banner → "preserve" because it has `pre-wrap` and wants
  real `\n`s for line breaks.

Wired into `IOPreview.tsx`, `GroupTracesAddon.tsx`,
`ConversationContext.tsx`, `SystemPromptBanner.tsx`. Local truncation
helpers in `ConversationContext` are gone — the role-preference walk for
chat-shaped payloads stays as a thin shim that delegates to
`formatPreview` once it picks a message.

24 unit tests cover plain prose, multiline, fences, images, single-key
envelopes (allowlisted vs not), chat arrays with/without tool calls,
Anthropic typed blocks, malformed JSON, combined cases, and the
`stripMarkdownNoise: false` escape hatch.

#8 — drawer header cleanup

- Empty pin row no longer reserves 28px. The dedicated pinned-context
  strip used to render with `minHeight: 28px` even when there were zero
  pins (~35-50% of traces — every LLM completion without a thread,
  every error trace), to prevent the body tabs from shifting on
  trace-to-trace nav. The dead chrome cost outweighed the small jump,
  so the row now only renders when there's at least one pin or an
  overflow popover to show.

- Smart trace-name fallback: title is now
  `traceName ?? rootSpanName ?? traceId.slice(0,12)`. The fallback is
  rendered in `fg.muted` so the reader can tell at a glance no
  semantic name was set rather than mistaking the ID hex for a real
  title. Detection avoids treating root-span name strings that happen
  to be a prefix of the trace ID (server-side projection drops the
  span name into `trace.name` for unnamed traces; for traces with no
  spans at all it falls through to the trace ID).

- LABELS pin renders as a `·`-separated list instead of raw JSON
  (`["sample","prod"]` → `sample · prod`). `formatPinValue` now takes
  an optional key argument so per-key formatting can apply; the existing
  one-arg signature is kept for back-compat. Falls back gracefully to
  the raw string when the value isn't a JSON-encoded array.

- Drawer density follows the existing table density preference. Adds
  `getDrawerDensityTokens(density)` returning padding tokens for the
  accordion section trigger/content and the header row gap. Compact =
  tighter than before; comfortable = a touch looser. AccordionShell
  and DrawerHeader read these tokens, so flipping the density toggle in
  the table toolbar reflows the drawer in lockstep.

* fix(traces-v2): pin accordion triggers below SpanTabBar, drop chips minHeight

Section triggers stuck at top: 0 of the drawer body, where the SpanTabBar
(zIndex: 2) was already pinned — they were sticking but hidden behind it.
Offset the sticky stack by the bar's 38px height so INPUT AND OUTPUT and
its peers come to rest under the tab strip, with later sections stacking
above as usual.

Drop the 56px minHeight on the chips strip too: it reserved room for two
rows of pills even when only one was rendered, leaving a permanent empty
band above the pin row on most traces. The strip now sizes to its
content; the small height jump on next/previous-trace nav is the same
trade-off the pin row already takes.

* fix(traces-v2): named-arg formatPinValue, density-aware sticky offset

- formatPinValue switches from positional (key, value) overloads to a
  single `{ key?, value }` arg per repo rule on multi-arg functions.
  Updates callers in DrawerHeader and resolveAttributeValue.
- AccordionShell's sticky-stack step now reads from drawerDensityTokens
  (compact 29px, comfortable 37px) instead of a hard-coded 32px. Fixes
  overlap in comfortable mode and a small gap in compact, both of which
  emerged when the trigger paddingY started varying with density.
- Drop the redundant `stage !== "outro"` check inside the outer
  `stage !== "outro"` block in TracesEmptyOnboarding — the inner branch
  was unreachable and TS flagged it as a comparison-with-no-overlap.

feat(security): unify SSRF blocking under BLOCK_LOCAL_HTTP_CALLS env var (#3614)

* feat(security): unify SSRF blocking under BLOCK_LOCAL_HTTP_CALLS env var

Replaces the implicit IS_SAAS gating (TS-only) and NODE_ENV-development
gate on ALLOWED_PROXY_HOSTS (TS-only) with a single, explicit env var
that controls outbound private-network blocking on both the TypeScript
app and the Python NLP service.

Behavior:
- BLOCK_LOCAL_HTTP_CALLS=true: blocks private IPs / localhost / DNS-resolved
  private hosts. ALLOWED_PROXY_HOSTS is the literal-hostname allowlist.
- unset/false (default): only cloud metadata endpoints are blocked;
  local destinations are allowed. Suits self-hosted/on-prem out of the box.
- Cloud metadata (169.254.169.254 etc.) is ALWAYS blocked, no toggle.

IS_SAAS continues to control TLS rejectUnauthorized (separate concern).

SaaS deployments must set BLOCK_LOCAL_HTTP_CALLS=true explicitly — see
companion PR in langwatch-saas/infrastructure.

* chore(security): fail-fast invariant — IS_SAAS=true requires BLOCK_LOCAL_HTTP_CALLS=true

Defense-in-depth boot-time guard. Terraform PR #483 already sets
BLOCK_LOCAL_HTTP_CALLS=true on all SaaS deployments (workers, app, NLP),
but if a future deploy ever drops the env without dropping IS_SAAS,
SSRF protections would silently disable. Throw at startup instead.

Per CodeRabbit suggestion on PR #3614.

* chore(specs): bind SSRF scenarios to existing TS tests via @scenario JSDoc

The PR's IS_SAAS→BLOCK_LOCAL_HTTP_CALLS rename detached scenarios from
their bound tests in `feature-parity` CI: the scenarios got renamed but
the existing TS tests had no `@scenario` annotation pointing at the new
titles. Restoring tags would have been cheaper but dishonest — the

fix(filters): cancel useDebounceValue on FieldsFilter unmount (CI flake) (#3790)

fix(filters): cancel useDebounceValue on FieldsFilter unmount

The debounced setState created by `useDebounceValue("", 300)` retained
a trailing timer past component unmount. In vitest workers tearing down
jsdom, the trailing setState fired against an unmounted tree, hitting
react-dom's scheduler which assumes `window` exists — producing
`ReferenceError: window is not defined` as an Unhandled Error and
failing the langwatch-app-ci test-integration shard intermittently.

Reproduced on PR #3781 across two retriggers; the test that triggers
the trailing fire is SeriesFiltersDrawer.integration.test.tsx (mounts
SeriesFiltersDrawer → FieldsFilters → useDebounceValue).

Fix: cancel the debounced setter in a useEffect cleanup so trailing
fires can't outlive the component.

fix(dev): rewrite stale localhost NEXTAUTH_URL/BASE_HOST in dev launchers (#3453) (#3699)

* fix(dev): rewrite stale localhost NEXTAUTH_URL/BASE_HOST in dev launchers (#3453)

When a second worktree picks a dynamic APP_PORT (because 5560 is busy),
compose.dev.yml's `${VAR:-http://localhost:${APP_PORT}}` fallback was
being defeated by stale `http://localhost:5560` exports inherited from
prior sessions. The cookie/origin then no longer matched the host port
and login 403'd silently.

This adds scripts/lib/sanitize-dev-env.sh (sourced by scripts/dev.sh,
scripts/dev-up.sh, and the make dev* recipes) which:

- Rewrites NEXTAUTH_URL / BASE_HOST to the current APP_PORT only when
  the inherited value is empty or matches `http://localhost:*`.
- Leaves real proxy / tunnel overrides alone — anything else
  (https://*.boxd.sh, ngrok URLs, 127.0.0.1, etc.) passes through.
- Logs each rewrite to stdout so the override is visible.

Adds 10 vitest unit tests covering rewrites, no-op idempotency, override
preservation, and the missing-APP_PORT failure path; binds them to a new
specs/ci/dev-env-localhost-sanitize.feature so feature-parity enforces
the contract going forward. Adds langwatch/scripts to the
check-feature-parity test roots so script-level tests can bind specs.

Closes #3453

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Aligns feature scenarios with sanitize-dev-env.unit.test.ts which passes

sanitizer returns nonzero, contradicting the 'unchanged' expectation.

fix(datasets): sanitise null bytes + atomic create-dataset-with-records (#3648)

* fix(datasets): sanitise null bytes + atomic create-dataset-with-records

Customer reported: JSONL upload errored with a Postgres 22P05 ("\u0000
cannot be converted to text"). The dataset row was created anyway,
leaving an empty orphan that blocked retries with a "name already
exists" error.

Two bugs:

1. Null bytes leak into Postgres jsonb. JSON.parse rejects raw U+0000
   bytes outright; payloads that pass parsing (via "\u0000" escape
   sequences) land in a Json column where Postgres rejects them with
   22P05. Now:
   - parseFileContent strips raw null bytes before any parser sees them
   - shared stripNullBytes util walks parsed entries and removes any
     null bytes that survive JSON.parse (escape-sequence path)
   - sanitiser also applied at batchCreateRecords, upsertRecord, and
     the legacy single-record update/create path

2. Non-atomic create. createNewDataset called dataset.create() then
   createManyDatasetRecords() as separate Prisma calls. A failure in
   the second call left an orphan dataset row. Both writes are now
   wrapped in prisma.$transaction; createManyDatasetRecords accepts
   an optional tx so the same Postgres path is used inside the tx.

Adds three regression integration tests against real Postgres (no
mocks): null-byte sanitisation via JSONL create+upload, via CSV upload
to existing, and atomicity rollback when the records insert fails on
a primary-key conflict.

Verified end-to-end with the customer's exact JSONL file: HTTP 201,
all 100 records persisted, 0 records contain null bytes, line 27's
reference field is sanitised cleanly.

* fix(datasets): keep original empty-array semantics in createNewDataset

* test(datasets): bind 6 spec scenarios; add REST batch + update null-byte tests

Without the exclusion, any Release-As: trailer in those subdirs leaks into
the langwatch root component — which is what produced the wrong langwatch

fix(release-please): correct clickhouse-serverless exclude-path to charts/ (#3867)

The exclude-paths entry "clickhouse-serverless" matched the unrelated
top-level Go service directory, not the chart at charts/clickhouse-serverless/
where the .release-please-shim file actually lives. As a result, every
shadow Release-As trailer for that component (most recently 0.3.0) leaked
into the langwatch root component's commit walk.

This is the same root-cause class as #3845 (PR #3866): exclude-paths
filters by literal filesystem path, not package/component name. PR #3866
fixed python-sdk and skills; this fixes the last polluting shim.

After this lands, the next release-please-sdks run on main should
propose a sensible langwatch version derived from 3.2.1 — not 0.3.0.

fix(traces-v2): trace-explorer v2 bug bash + OR-group viz polish (#3794)

* fix(traces-v2): bug bash round — AI, sidebar, drawer, export, light-mode polish

Round of fixes from the TraceExplorer v2 bug bash:

- AI: switch to JSON-mode generateObject and inject the required "json"
  keyword into the system prompt so OpenAI/LiteLLM stops rejecting the
  request. Replace the leaked litellm error with friendly user copy and
  log the raw cause server-side. Seed the AI composer with the current
  query text on entry, and recall the user's natural-language prompt
  when the URL query is still exactly what the last AI translation
  produced (per-project scoped via filterStore.lastAiTranslation). Move
  the thinking shimmer keyframes through emotion's `keyframes` helper so
  the animation actually emits, sweep all three brand stops through it,
  and slow the cycle to 4.5s.

- Trace drawer events: surface user/track events in the v2 drawer via a
  new `tracesV2.userEvents` query that reads off the legacy trace doc;
  the events accordion now merges them with span-level events from the
  fold projection. Hide the "View span" button on user-event rows where
  spanId is empty.

- Filter sidebar: render synthetic categorical sections from
  FACET_DEFAULTS while discover is in flight so the rail shows the
  well-known facets immediately instead of a skeleton; FacetRow hides
  count and value-bar on `synthetic` rows. Extend the highlight regex
  to recognise `field:>=N` / `field:<N` style ranges so highlighting
  doesn't drop while the user types comparison filters.

- Flame view: hide the Minimap until the user actually zooms — at full
  extent it's a duplicate of the main flame and just eats vertical
  space. Block text colour respects light mode (`gray.900` / `gray.800`
  with a light text-shadow) instead of white-on-pastel.

- Aurora: switch the SVG curtain blend mode to `multiply` in light mode
  and `screen` in dark mode so the cyan/blue curtains tint the surface
  instead of washing out to invisible white in light theme.

- Export progress: lift the toast above the trace table's row hover
  overlays via `zIndex="overlay"` so it isn't painted under in-row text
  during long exports.

- Presence avatar: add an onError handler to Avatar.Image so a failed
  OAuth profile image falls through to the initials Fallback instead of
  the browser's broken-image glyph.

* fix(traces-v2): columns picker parity, sortable hints, range slider input + NaN guard

- Columns dropdown: surface every column (Standard / Evaluations /
  Events) with section labels, lift the maxHeight cap so the picker
  matches the lens-config dialog instead of truncating to the first ~10
  rows. Without the section label users couldn't tell where Standard
  ended; without the height bump everything below "User ID" lived
  below the fold.

- Sortable header hint: show the inactive sortable chevron at 0.35
  opacity by default (was opacity: 0). Sortable and non-sortable
  columns previously looked identical until hover, so users would
  click a non-sortable header expecting a sort and hit a no-op.
  Hover still lifts the chevron to 0.85 for the active affordance.

- Range slider:
  * Replace the read-only Text labels with click-to-edit Inputs so
    users can type precise duration / cost / token bounds instead of
    fighting the slider for sub-pixel precision.
  * Strip currency / unit suffixes on parse ("$0.05", "1.5s",
    "12,300") so paste-back of the formatted label still resolves.
  * Drop NaN / Infinity at commit time and clamp typed values to
    [min, max]. The previous `value[0]!` non-null assertion let
    zag-js's degenerate-state undefined become NaN that propagated
    into the URL as `[NaN TO NaN]`, which then refused to parse.

* feat(traces-v2): clickable AND/OR, Shift-click facet OR, search shortcuts hint

Previously the only way to combine facets with OR was to drop into the
search bar and type the operator manually — Sergio's bug-bash note
called this out as the missing affordance most users expect from the
sidebar. This round wires three discoverable surfaces for it.

- Search bar AND/OR keyword cycles in place. Clicking the highlighted
  AND/OR token swaps it via a new `swapOperatorAtLocation` mutation
  that flips the keyword at its liqe-text coordinates without
  re-serialising the rest of the query. The decoration carries the
  liqe coords as `data-filter-op-start` / `data-filter-op-end`, and
  both the live ProseMirror editor and the cold-load PlaceholderEditor
  delegate clicks on those data-attrs to the swap. Hover state +
  pointer cursor + tooltip teach the affordance.

- Shift / Ctrl / Cmd + click on a facet row in the sidebar combines
  the new clause with OR instead of the default AND. The modifier
  bubbles from FacetRow → FacetSection → SectionRenderer →
  useFilterSidebarData, where it's translated into the filterStore's
  new `combinator` option on `toggleFacet`. `appendClause` wraps both
  sides in parens for OR combines so the user's intent survives the
  next parse round-trip (`a AND b` OR-combined with `c` reads as
  `(a AND b) OR c`, not `a AND b OR c` which liqe re-binds).

- Lightbulb popover next to the search bar's StatusBadge teaches the
  shortcut set: clickable AND/OR, Shift-click for OR, ⌘I for AI,
  `/` to focus the bar from anywhere. Lives in `SearchTipsPopover`,
  reuses the existing popover primitives and a local Kbd renderer.

* feat(traces-v2): click an existing chip to open a value-picker popover

Until now the only way to change the value of a search-bar chip was to
delete it and type the new one — fine for a one-shot edit but heavy for
"actually I meant warning, not error." This adds a popover that opens
when the chip itself is clicked, listing the discovered values for that
field with a fuzzy filter, keyboard nav, and a one-click swap.

- New `setFacetValueAtLocation` mutation rewrites the value of the Tag
  at a given liqe-text location, preserving the field name and any
  wrapping NOT (which lives outside the Tag's location range, so the
  splice doesn't touch it).
- Filter highlight pass attaches `data-filter-chip-{start,end,field,
  value}` to chip spans so the editor's existing mousedown delegate
  can recognise chip clicks without re-walking the AST.
- New `TokenValuePicker` portals into document.body, anchored to the
  chip's bounding rect, reading candidate values from the same
  `useTraceFacets` discover payload that drives the sidebar (no extra
  fetch). Search filter, ↑/↓/Enter/Esc, click-outside dismiss.
- Both the live ProseMirror editor and the cold-load PlaceholderEditor
  forward chip clicks to the popover so the affordance is consistent
  whether or not the heavy editor has mounted yet.

* feat(traces-v2): annotate sidebar facets that participate in cross-facet OR

Cross-facet OR queries like \`(status:error OR model:gpt-4) AND
cost:>0.05\` previously triggered only a warning chip in the search bar
("the sidebar may not fully reflect what you've searched for"); the
facet sections themselves rendered as if they were independently
AND-toggleable, which silently lied to the user about what the query
actually matched.

This rewires the sidebar to be honest about OR groups instead.

- New \`analyzeOrGroups\` AST helper finds every OR LogicalExpression
  whose Tag descendants span multiple fields, flattens nested ORs into
  one logical group, and returns each group's id, member fields, and
  liqe-text-coordinate range. \`hasCrossFacetOR\` now delegates to this
  so detection is consistent.
- The sidebar threads \`fieldToGroupId\` down through SectionRenderer →
  FacetSection / RangeSection → SidebarSection. Sections whose field
  belongs to an OR group render an "OR" pill in the header and a 3px
  coloured rail on their left edge. Colour is hashed from the group
  id so two concurrent OR groups stay visually distinct (six-stop
  pastel palette: purple/teal/pink/yellow/cyan/green).
- The search bar's "Query uses cross-facet OR …" warning chip is
  retired — the visual treatment now reads honestly without a banner.

* feat(traces-v2): clearer OR-group viz, smart toggle, AST-only facet rows

Three knock-on improvements after shipping the cross-facet OR
visualisation. The base treatment was too subtle — users couldn't tell
which sections were linked, the toggle still AND-combined inside an OR
group, and any value typed by hand that wasn't in discover went
invisible in the rail.

- Smart toggle inside OR groups. New \`addToOrGroupAtLocation\` mutation
  splices a fresh \`field:value\` clause into an existing OR group's
  liqe-text range so clicking a new value extends that group instead of
  AND-combining at the top. Wrapping parens stay intact and OR's
  left-associativity does the rest:
  \`(status:error OR model:gpt) AND cost:>0\` →
  \`(status:error OR model:gpt OR status:warning) AND cost:>0\`.
  \`useFilterSidebarData\` auto-detects the OR-group context for each
  toggle, so there's no extra plumbing on the call sites — Shift-click
  still maps to "open a new top-level OR scope" as before.

- Sidebar now shows \`OR · model · service\` peer labels in the OR pill
  so users can see which sections are linked without colour-matching
  rails. The pill itself got a thicker border and bolder weight.
  Members of an OR group also gain a coloured outline on the FacetRow,
  so users can see exactly which values are in the group at a glance
  even when sections are far apart in the rail.

- AST-only facet values now appear in the sidebar. When the user types
  \`status:custom\` in the search bar but the discover payload doesn't
  include \`custom\`, that value previously stayed invisible (active
  count went up but no row was drawn). The hook now scans
  \`getFacetValues(ast, key)\` for each categorical and synthesises any
  missing values as zero-count rows so they render, can be toggled
  off, and can pick up the OR-group ring.

- Search shortcuts popover no longer renders at the document origin.
  The Tooltip-around-PopoverTrigger nesting was intercepting the ref
  the popover positioner needed — moved the hint to \`title\` on the
  IconButton, leaving the popover's ref chain intact.

* feat(traces-v2): OR connector lines + matching value-picker style

Two follow-ups on the cross-facet OR sidebar work.

- Token value picker now mirrors the autocomplete-suggestion dropdown
  visually: same shadow ring (border + soft blue glow + drop shadow),
  same fade-in animation, same mono \`field:value\` rendering with the
  count on the right, same footer with shortcut hints + Syntax-docs
  button. Clicking a chip and typing \`field:\` now both open dialogs
  that read as the same affordance instead of two unrelated popups.

- Sidebar grows by one 16px lane per active OR group and renders an
  \`OrConnectorOverlay\` SVG-style overlay in that gutter. Each group
  draws a coloured vertical spine + a horizontal tick at every member
  row, so it's literally a bracket joining the linked rows. Lines
  re-measure on container resize and on scroll, so they stay aligned
  through facet collapse/expand and sidebar scrolling. Lane width and
  total sidebar width grow together — shared constant between
  \`OrConnectorOverlay\` and \`FilterAside\` so the gutter the rows
  reserve via \`paddingRight\` always matches the lanes the overlay
  paints.

* feat(traces-v2): bidirectional facet ↔ chip hover, slim connector, collapsed-section preview

- Connector revamp. Dropped the spine + ticks treatment that read as
  cartoonish — now just one thin straight line per OR group, with a
  10px invisible hit zone so the line is hoverable without pixel-
  perfect aim. Hovering surfaces a tooltip listing the linked
  field:value pairs.

- Bidirectional cross-highlight. New \`facetHoverStore\` tracks the
  currently-hovered group OR single facet. Sidebar facet rows
  broadcast hover into the store; the search bar delegates
  mouseover/out on chip data-attrs and does the same. A single
  style-block in \`OrConnectorOverlay\` injects targeted CSS that
  lights up every matching chip + sidebar row at once. Hover any
  group member (chip OR row) and every other member glows;
  hover a non-OR active filter and the matching chip ↔ row pair
  cross-highlight.

- Background-fill highlight, not outline. Outlines kept getting
  clipped by parent overflow and read more like a debug ring than a
  confident highlight. Now the highlight uses the group's
  \`subtle\` background + \`fg\` text + \`muted\` border, mirroring the
  OR pill in the section header — the chip and row look like the
  pill instead of just being decorated by it.

- Collapsed sections still surface their active values. Active rows
  (filtered values + OR-group members) are pinned above the
  collapsible content via a new \`SidebarSection.pinnedContent\`
  prop, so they stay visible whether the section is open or closed.
  The connector line keeps its anchors and users see / can remove
  what's filtered without expanding.

- Synthetic AST-only rows pinned to the top of facet items, so a
  hand-typed value like \`status:custom\` doesn't disappear under the
  show-more cut on a high-cardinality section.

- PlaceholderEditor chips now expose \`data-filter-chip-field\` /
  \`data-filter-chip-value\` so the cold-load path participates in the
  hover linking the same way the live editor does.

* fix(traces-v2): make OR connector line visible + 1:1 chip↔row hover

- The 1.5px / 0.55 opacity line was effectively invisible. Bump to
  2px / 0.95 opacity so the connector reads at a glance.
- Row and chip hover now broadcast a single \`hoveredFacet\` rather
  than the whole OR group: hovering a row lights up only its
  matching chip in the search bar (and vice versa). Highlighting
  the entire OR group stays reserved for hovering the connector
  line itself, which is the explicit "show me everything in this
  group" affordance and surfaces the tooltip too. Avoids casual
  cursor passes pulling all members into one big yellow blob.

* fix(traces-v2): same-field OR groups + chip↔group highlight + X-button parity

Three regressions / gaps from the prior round:

- \`analyzeOrGroups\` now treats same-field ORs as groups too
  (e.g. \`status:error OR status:warning\`). The old "must span >1
  field" gate filtered them out, so the connector line was
  completely missing on the most common OR shape (multiple values
  within one section). Now any OR with ≥2 Tag descendants is a group.

- Restored OR-group-aware hover: hovering a sidebar row OR a search
  bar chip that's part of an OR group lights up every other member
  of that group. The connector line itself keeps its quieter
  semantic — hover it for the tooltip, no member glow — so casual
  cursor passes don't pull the whole group into a yellow blob.

- The X delete button on each chip now mirrors the chip's data-attrs
  (\`data-filter-chip-field\` / \`-value\`), so the highlight CSS picks
  it up as part of the same pill. Previously the field:value half
  tinted but the X stayed in its original colour, breaking the
  two-half-of-one-pill visual.

* fix(traces-v2): connector-line hover no longer pulls member chips

Hovering the OR connector line was triggering the same
\`facetHoverStore.setHoveredGroup\` that chip/row hover does, so
running the cursor across the line lit up every member as if the
user had hovered each one. The line is supposed to be the quiet
"show me what this is" affordance — tooltip yes, member glow no.

Move the line's hover into local component state so the tooltip
still appears (and the line itself thickens / brightens) without
touching the global store. Direct chip/row hovers stay as the only
trigger for the cross-highlight.

* fix(traces-v2): connector tooltip anchors near cursor

The tooltip was offset 240px left of the cursor, which dropped it
in the middle of the sidebar — far from where the user clicked
and overlapping the very rows the line was meant to point at.
Anchor it just right of the cursor (12px) so it surfaces in the
adjacent results-pane gutter where there's space, with viewport
clamps so an edge hover doesn't push the body offscreen.

* fix(traces-v2): hover-on-OR check membership at value level + cursor lands outside chip pill

- Hovering a row or chip whose field is part of an OR group was
  triggering the whole-group highlight even when that specific value
  wasn't a member. So hovering \`origin:simulation\` would light up
  \`origin:evaluation\` and \`origin:application\` just because they
  happen to be in the same field's OR group. Now the check is at
  the (field, value) level: only true OR-group members trigger the
  group glow; everything else gets the 1:1 chip↔row highlight.
  Verified with real \`playwright.hover\` (synthetic mouseenter
  events don't fire React onMouseEnter, which is why the prior
  spot-checks looked fine but the live behaviour was broken).

- Chip delete-widget now uses \`side: -1\` so the cursor at the chip
  end-position renders to the *right* of the X, not between the
  value text and the X. Clicking just past a chip lands the cursor
  outside the pill, ready to type the next clause, instead of
  inside the pill where it read as "you're editing this token."

* fix(traces-v2): block PM caret-into-chip on click via handleDOMEvents

Clicking on a chip pill or its X widget previously dropped the caret
inside the chip's text node (between the value and the widget), so the
next keystroke read as if it were extending the value (`status:error`
→ `status:errorx`). Returning `true` from `editorProps.handleDOMEvents.mousedown`
for chip / delete-widget / operator targets keeps PM out of the click —
the existing addEventListener handler still opens the value picker,
deletes the chip, or cycles AND/OR.

Reverts the speculative `side: -1` widget tweak: that only shifted the
visual cursor without moving the document position, so typing still
extended the chip's value.

fix(scenarios,nav): repair F11 save-and-run redirect race and F12 hydration warnings (#3700) * fix(scenarios,nav): F11 save-and-run redirect race + F12 hydration warnings (#3586) Two findings split out of the #3526 stress-test umbrella: F11 — Save-and-Run did not redirect to /simulations on the first click from a freshly mounted form. Two competing router.push calls fired in immediate succession after a successful save: 1. closeDrawer() (called by onClose()) does its own router.push to strip drawer.* query params from the URL. 2. feat(scenarios): simulation_set aggregate + ArchiveSetCommand schemas (lw#3636 slice) (#3793)

* feat(scenarios): introduce simulation_set aggregate + ArchiveSetCommand (lw#3636 schemas slice)

Adds the schema foundation for the bulk-archive-by-set work tracked in
#3636. The current per-run path emits N `lw.simulation_run.deleted`
events for one user intent ("archive this set"). The new shape: one
`lw.simulation_set.archived` event whose payload snapshots the
affected `scenarioRunIds`.

This commit ships only the schemas + command + type guard. Wiring the
event into the per-run fold projection (so each run's `ArchivedAt`
flips in one pass) requires a dispatcher fanout — the dispatcher today
routes one event to one aggregate; a set-scoped event needs to fan out
to many `simulation_run` projections. That's tracked as the follow-up
slice. Until it's wired, the existing per-run `DeleteRunCommand` /
`SimulationRunDeletedEvent` path stays in place — no behavior change
yet.

Aggregate-strategy decision: a new `simulation_set` aggregate holds
the bulk action. Rationale:

- The set is the natural owner of "who archived me when" — replaying
  set events alone reconstructs admin actions without per-run noise.
- Idempotency keys collapse to `(tenantId, scenarioSetId)` — same set,
  same archive intent, one event regardless of retry count.
- Doesn't break the dispatcher's one-aggregate-per-command invariant
  (the alternate option would have).

Concretely:
- `AGGREGATE_TYPE_IDENTIFIERS` gains `simulation_set`.
- `SIMULATION_SET_EVENT_TYPES.ARCHIVED = "lw.simulation_set.archived"`,
  `SIMULATION_SET_COMMAND_TYPES.ARCHIVE = "lw.simulation_set.archive"`,
  `SIMULATION_EVENT_VERSIONS.SET_ARCHIVED = "2026-05-04"`.
- `simulationSetArchivedEventDataSchema` and matching event schema
  added to `schemas/events.ts`; type guard added to `schemas/typeGuards.ts`;
  command-side schema added to `schemas/commands.ts`.
- `ArchiveSetCommand` defined via `defineCommand` with the
  set-scoped aggregate and idempotency key.

Adds 4 unit scenarios in
`specs/event-sourcing/simulation-set-archive.feature` with matching
`@scenario`-bound tests covering: emit, idempotency-key collapsing,
type-guard narrowing, and missing-field rejection.

Refs #3636. Old `DeleteRunCommand` / `SimulationRunDeletedEvent`
retained for back-compat with historical events.

* fix(simulation-processing): reject empty scenarioRunIds archive

archiveSetCommandDataSchema and simulationSetArchivedEventDataSchema
now require .min(1) on scenarioRunIds. An empty archive is semantically
a no-op but indistinguishable from a real archive at replay time —
rejecting it at the schema boundary keeps the projection stream
unambiguous.

Adds matching regression test that asserts the schema rejects an
empty-array payload. Resolves coderabbit thread on commands.ts:107.
