fix(studio-lambda): cache + single-flight getProjectLambdaArn (#3952)

* fix(studio-lambda): cache + single-flight getProjectLambdaArn to stop tenant bursts stalling event-sourcing workers

A single project's burst of studio-bound events fanned out across
langwatch-workers, each invocation issuing 2-N GetFunction calls
against the same per-project Lambda. AWS Lambda's GetFunction quota
is regional and shared across all pods, so one chatty tenant
exhausted it cluster-wide, triggering CallerRateLimitExceeded (HTTP
429) with 4-12s SDK retry backoffs that saturated worker capacity.
Unrelated fold groups (e.g. projectDailySdkUsage/<date>:other:)
stalled for ~10min on 2026-05-11 11:46 AMS as a result.

Fix: an in-process per-pod ARN cache (10-min TTL, keyed by projectId
+ image_uri so deploys auto-invalidate) plus single-flight
collapsing of concurrent misses. Failures are NOT cached — a
TooManyRequestsException must self-heal on the next call.

* refactor(studio-lambda): back ARN cache with TtlCache (Redis + memory fallback)

Cluster-wide cache via the project's TtlCache helper instead of a
per-pod Map — first miss anywhere in the fleet now warms every other
pod. Falls back to per-pod memory automatically when Redis is down.
Per-pod single-flight is kept to close the cold-burst race window
before the first writer lands in Redis.

* test(studio-lambda): bind 5 lambda-arn cache scenarios

* fix(trackEventsWorker): no-op when Elasticsearch is unconfigured

Without ELASTICSEARCH_NODE_URL set, every track_events job threw
'Elasticsearch is not configured (called .update())' and BullMQ
retried forever, churning Redis bandwidth and burning the worker's
concurrency slots. The trace itself is already persisted by the
collector pipeline; the ES update is redundant when ES is off.
Mirrors the existing guard pattern in collectorWorker.ts (line 887).

* fix(redis): bump boot-PING timeout 3s→15s to survive ElastiCache TLS handshake

On 2026-05-11 the langwatch-workers periodic restart cycle hit two
PING timeouts back-to-back (10:13:43, 10:14:02). 3s is too tight for
the rediss:// cold connect on ElastiCache under load — the boot
guard exited the process and crashlooped the pod right when the
event-sourcing dispatcher needed to come back online. 15s still
catches dev-mode misconfiguration without false-positive on real
TLS+AUTH latency.

fix(auth): enable accountLinking so orphan email-verified Users can sign in via SSO (#3994)

A User row with emailVerified=true but zero Account rows (pre-seeded
invite, half-finished legacy signup, or migration leftover) silently
blocked every subsequent OAuth sign-in for that email. BetterAuth's
default refuses to link, surfacing as "registered with another
authentication method" in the UI.

On SSO-enforced orgs this was the worst-case: even after a successful
IdP round-trip the new Account creation was rejected and the user was
permanently locked out. SSO-enforced does not mean "always works" when
this gap exists.

Enables account.accountLinking on the BetterAuth config. Linking
requires the existing User to be emailVerified=true and the OAuth
provider to return the same email (allowDifferentEmails defaults to
false). SSO-domain enforcement in beforeAccountCreate still rejects
the wrong provider before any link happens.

fix(python-sdk): retry evaluator calls on gateway/edge transient failures (#3993)

* fix(python-sdk): retry evaluator calls on gateway/edge transient failures

The evaluator endpoint occasionally returns 524 when an evaluator's underlying
LLM exceeds Cloudflare's idle timeout. Today a single transient 524 collapses
the row to a soft status:"error" with no recovery attempt, even though a
re-issue would usually succeed.

Wrap the POST in `evaluate()` and `async_evaluate()` with a tenacity retry that
fires only on definitionally-transient cases:
  - httpx.TimeoutException / httpx.ConnectError
  - HTTP 502 / 503 / 504 / 524

500 is intentionally excluded since it generally reflects a deterministic
evaluator-side error that retrying won't fix (and would 3x the LLM cost).

Same config as the SDK's other retry sites (stop_after_attempt(3),
wait_exponential 2..10s) plus a small `wait_random(0, 1)` jitter to avoid
parallel rows synchronising their retries. Behaviour on success and on
exhausted retries is unchanged — the existing `_handle_exception` path still
funnels persistent failures into the soft-error result.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(python-sdk): align evaluate() sync exception type with async so retry fires

Sync evaluate() passed cls=EvaluatorException to better_raise_for_status, async_evaluate() did not. The retry predicate only recognises httpx.HTTPStatusError, so the sync path skipped retries whenever the gateway returned a 5xx with a JSON `{"error": ...}` body (since better_raise_for_status raises EvaluatorException, not HTTPStatusError, in that case).

Drop the cls= override so both paths raise httpx.HTTPStatusError uniformly and the 502/503/504/524 predicate applies consistently. EvaluatorException has no external callers (only ever raised here), and _handle_exception derives `details` via repr(e) regardless of class, so the soft-error API shape is preserved.

feat(ops): per-tenant pause + bulk tenant drain (post-incident 2026-05-11) (#3970)

* feat(ops): per-tenant pause + bulk tenant drain in event-sourcing GroupQueue

Post-incident follow-up to the 2026-05-11 outage where a single tenant
generated ~500K event-sourcing groups in 90 min and starved every other
tenant on the cluster. Per-group sqrt-weighted round-robin fairness
assumes O(10) groups per tenant; when one tenant explodes to half a
million groups, others get ~4% of dispatcher capacity.

Two new ops controls:

1. Per-tenant pause via the existing `paused-jobs` SET, encoded as
   "tenant:<tenantId>" entries. DISPATCH_LUA / DISPATCH_BATCH_LUA now
   extract the tenantId from each groupId prefix and skip the group if
   that key is paused. Reuses all existing pause plumbing — same SET,
   same kick signal, same SCARD short-circuit when no pauses are set.

2. `ops.queues.drainTenant({ queueName, tenantId, pipelineFilter? })`
   pages the ready zset via ZSCAN, filters by tenantId/ prefix, and
   drains each match through the same atomic DRAIN_GROUP_LUA the
   per-group Drain button uses. Replaces the "click 500K Drain buttons
   by hand" pattern we hit during the incident.

UI: paused-tenants banner is always shown above the Groups table when
any tenant is paused (so silence isn't mistaken for health), plus a
tenant-scoped action bar (Pause Tenant / Unpause Tenant / Drain All
Tenant Groups) when the operator searches for an exact tenant id.

Follow-ups (separate PRs, tracked in the post-mortem):
- Online-evaluator infinite-loop prevention (origin filter + depth cap)
- Tenant-level dispatcher fairness (rewrite DISPATCH_LUA round-robin)
- Ops UI server-side query timeouts + partial-results UI state

* test(groupQueue): add Lua integration coverage for tenant pause

Verifies the DISPATCH_LUA and DISPATCH_BATCH_LUA tenant-pause branch
against a real Redis instance. 8 new tests, all passing locally
alongside the 66 pre-existing dispatch/pause tests in the same suite
(74 total).

Tests cover:
- skipping a group whose tenantId is in the paused set
- dispatching other tenants while one is paused
- prefix-substring safety (tenant:project_A must NOT match project_AA)
- coexistence with pipeline-level pauses
- resume after the pause key is removed
- defensive fallback when groupId has no '/' separator
- equivalent coverage in dispatchBatch so the two code paths cannot
  silently diverge

* fix(ops): address CodeRabbit findings on tenant pause + bulk drain

Three fixes raised on PR review:

P1 — drainTenant now pipelines DRAIN_GROUP_LUA EVALs per ZSCAN page.
At the incident scale (507K groups) the previous one-at-a-time await
shape would have been ~tens of minutes through TLS+ElastiCache. With
1000-per-page pipelining it's ~500 round-trips total instead of 500K.

P2 — Drop the misleading pipelineFilter parameter from drainTenant.
The substring match never lined up with how pipeline identity is
actually stored (in __pipelineName inside the job-data blob, not the
groupId). The only realistic use of this endpoint is "drop everything
for this runaway tenant", so the param was both broken and unneeded.

P3 — DRAIN_GROUP_LUA now decrements stats:total-pending by the count
of jobs dropped (staged ZCARD + 1 if an active key existed). Without
this, the bulk drain would leak the counter forever — and the active
job's eventual COMPLETE_LUA call no-ops once the active key is gone,
so even per-group Drain (which used the same Lua before this change)
was silently leaking 1 per drained-while-active. Now correct.

Tests: 78/78 in scripts.integration.test.ts (74 pre-existing + 4 new
for the decrement semantics), 22/22 in queue.service.unit.test.ts. Both
suites run against real Redis + ClickHouse locally via test containers.

fix(scenarios-ui): three P1 UI regressions from the Vite migration (#3978)

Closes #3192 — single-run Cancel button does nothing. ScenarioGridCard
rendered its per-row cancel control as `<HStack as="button">` nested
inside the outer card `<Box as="button">`. Browsers parse nested
<button> elements by closing the outer button prematurely; the cancel
control ends up as a sibling and clicks visually-on-cancel land on the
outer card surface (which only knows how to open the detail drawer).
ScenarioTargetRow (list view) already uses `as="span" role="button"` —
align the grid card with that pattern.

Closes #3193 — Add New Agent from Edit Scenario navigates to nowhere.
`CurrentDrawer` spreads the URL-parsed `drawer.*` object onto the
registered drawer, leaving `props.open` as the drawer-name STRING
(e.g. `"agentHttpEditor"`). Chakra/Zag Drawer expects a boolean,
so the registry-mounted Agent{Http,Code}EditorDrawer / WorkflowSelector
never opened. Adds `*FromUrl` wrappers — same pattern as
`ScenarioFormDrawerFromUrl` (introduced in #1989) — that coerce URL
state into a proper boolean before delegating. Updates drawerRegistry
to use the wrappers; direct callsites (SuiteFormDrawer, ScenarioFormDrawer)
keep passing real booleans and are unaffected.

Closes #3194 — duplicate Create Scenario drawer in DOM. The Scenarios
index page rendered `<ScenarioFormDrawerFromUrl>` explicitly AND the
drawer registry mounted the same drawer via `<CurrentDrawer/>`. The
dev-mode warning in CurrentDrawer already flagged this anti-pattern;
just remove the explicit render and rely on the registry path.

Tests:
- CancelButtonNoNestedButton.integration.test.tsx — asserts the grid
  cancel control is not a nested HTML <button>, and exercises the full
  RunRow → ScenarioRunContent → ScenarioGridCard cancel wiring.
- AgentEditorDrawersFromRegistry.integration.test.tsx — mounts each
  *FromUrl wrapper with no `open` prop (matching CurrentDrawer's
  mount surface) and asserts the underlying drawer opens based on
  `drawerOpen()` state.
- scenariosIndexNoDoubleDrawer.integration.test.tsx — pins the page
  source check so a future regression can't reintroduce the duplicate.

feat(scenarios): structured logging across worker boundary (#3779)

* feat(scenarios): structured logging across worker boundary (closes #3593)

Three observability gaps surfaced during a recent investigation:

1. http-agent.adapter.ts had zero logging on either path. On non-2xx
   it threw "HTTP {status}: {statusText}" and discarded url, response
   body, latency.
2. scenario-child-process.ts used console.error; stderr arrived at the
   parent as a multi-line blob inside one log event, not searchable JSON.
3. The parent's logger.child({ scenarioRunId, batchRunId, projectId })
   didn't cross the parent → child process boundary, so even structured
   child logs would have been unjoinable to parent events.

This change:

- Adds execution/child-logger.ts: encodeScenarioLogContext serializes the
  context to LANGWATCH_LOG_CONTEXT env, decodeScenarioLogContext rebuilds
  it on the child side; createChildProcessLogger returns a base logger
  bound to those fields.
- Wires the env var into buildChildProcessEnv in scenario.processor.ts so
  every child inherits its parent's bindings.
- Replaces console.error in scenario-child-process.ts with the new
  logger (info/warn/debug/error as appropriate).
- Adds structured logging to SerializedHttpAgentAdapter:
  * info "http call ok" with {url, method, statusCode, durationMs}
  * warn "http call failed" with {..., responseBodyPreview} on non-2xx
  * error "http call failed" with {..., errorClass, message} on rejection
  Adapter accepts an optional logger for testability; defaults derive
  from the env-bound child logger so production wires the context
  through automatically.

Adds 6 unit scenarios in specs/scenarios/observability-context.feature
plus matching @scenario-bound tests for child-logger and the adapter
logging path.

* fix(scenarios): use ssrfSafeFetch's return type for response variable

Global `Response` is the DOM type; ssrfSafeFetch returns undici's Response
under TS Node types. Inferring from the function signature avoids the
TS2322 mismatch the typecheck CI just surfaced.

* fix(scenarios): tolerate Response mocks without .text() on non-2xx path

Existing http-agent.adapter.unit.test.ts mocks the failure case as
`{ ok: false, status: 500, statusText: ... }` without a `text()` method.
The new body-preview branch called `response.text()` unconditionally,
which threw "response.text is not a function" before the wrapping
`.catch()` could see it.

Guard with `typeof response.text === "function"`; the catch already
handles real promise rejections from real Responses.

* fix(scenarios): redact URL query params in http adapter logs + assert empty bindings

1. SerializedHttpAgentAdapter logged \`url\` verbatim on every error /
   warn / info site. URL templates can interpolate user-supplied
   secrets (?api_key=…, ?access_token=…); CloudWatch persists every
   line in plain text. Add a redactUrlForLogs() helper that drops the
   query string before logging, and apply it to all three call sites.

2. child-logger.unit.test.ts "context env var unset" scenario only
   asserted not.toThrow() but the bound feature scenario also requires
   the returned logger to have empty bindings. Add the bindings
   assertion so the binding is honest.

fix(scenarios): emit OTel span on SerializedCodeAgentAdapter timeout/error (#3438) (#3697)

Previously, when the adapter's NLP request timed out or fetch failed, the
parent span machinery from @langwatch/scenario closed an empty span and the
inner failure left no footprint — customer traces showed only the simulator
span when the run hung.

Now the adapter wraps its outbound request in its own
`SerializedCodeAgentAdapter.execute_nlp_request` CLIENT span. On every exit
path the span carries an `error.kind` attribute (`timeout` | `fetch` | `http`
| `nlp_error`) plus `http.status_code` when applicable, and the thrown
SerializedCodeAgentAdapterError carries the same kind for callers that want
to discriminate without parsing message strings.

Closes #3438

* fix(boxd-fork): 3 CR threads — fail-closed proxy errors + empty-title guard

CodeRabbit threads on scripts/boxd-fork.sh:

1. `boxd_map_ports` (line 286-302) was silently swallowing every proxy
   command failure with `|| true` and unconditionally printing a success
   line, conflating real failures (network, auth, invalid VM) with the
   documented idempotent "already exists" case for `proxy new`. The
   fail-closed guard at line 385 (`boxd_map_ports "$vm" || return 1`)
   was therefore dead code. Now: capture each command's stderr+exit,
   classify the conflict message as idempotent, propagate failures via
   a `failed` flag so the function actually returns non-zero when a
   real proxy creation/set-port fails.

2. `boxd_fork_issue` (line ~454) lacked the empty-title guard that
   already exists at line 423 for empty headRefName. If `gh issue view`
   returns exit 0 with empty `.title` (permissions edge cases), slug
   becomes empty and the branch ref `issue<N>/` is degenerate. Added
   the same empty-string check + clear error.

3. `boxd_golden_reset` (line ~534) masked `boxd destroy` failures with
   `|| true` and fell through to `boxd_golden`, which short-circuits on
   `boxd_vm_exists` returning true. The user gets neither a destroyed
   VM nor a rebuilt one, with no error explaining why. Now: surface the
   destroy failure and abort the reset.

* feat(boxd): namespace golden VM + 9 CR thread fixes (#3901)

**Golden VM namespacing.** boxd subdomains are globally unique across all
accounts on boxd.sh, so a fixed `langwatch-golden` name causes cross-team
collisions (only one account on the planet can claim it). Introduce
`boxd_namespace` + `boxd_golden_vm_name`:

- Default: `gh api user --jq .login` → e.g. `drewdrewthis--langwatch-golden`
- Fallback: `whoami` (so the script keeps working without gh auth)
- Override: `BOXD_NAMESPACE=<name>` env (for shared/team-owned goldens)

The `--` separator is RFC-1035-compliant inside a DNS label and visually
distinct from intra-segment hyphens. Existing user goldens (named
`langwatch-golden`) keep working but won't be referenced by `make boxd-*`
under the new naming — a manual rename or rebuild is fine for a pre-release
tool.

* feat(ops): structural-fingerprint loop detection

Same AnomalyDetector framework as the rate breaker, second signal.
Catches the W_7kPya-class loop where the CONTENT of every trace
varies (LLM output strings are non-deterministic) but the STRUCTURE
is identical — same workflow shape repeated thousands of times.

Fingerprint: sha1(sorted("<span_name>:<kind>:<sorted_attribute_keys>")).
Keys only — never values — so LLM non-determinism does not affect
the hash. Computed in recordSpanCommand right before event emission;
fire-and-forget recording into FingerprintTracker.

Trigger rule (very conservative to avoid false positives on legit
homogeneous workloads like regression suites and cron jobs):
  - fingerprint's 5-min rate >= 100/min (absolute floor)
  AND
  - fingerprint represents >= 80% of tenant's 5-min volume

Validated against the user's 2026-05-11 incident span dump: seven
spans, varying `passed` text outputs ("0.000124 vs ...", "passed:true",
"between the ___ is", etc.) → all hash to the same fingerprint. The
detector would have surfaced this loop within 5 minutes.

Tracker bounds memory at 1024 distinct fingerprints per tenant; new
fingerprints are silently dropped past that ceiling so pathological
all-unique traffic can't blow up Redis. Existing fingerprints keep
updating their counts regardless.

Singletons in observability/index.ts (getFingerprintTracker /
getTenantRateTracker) so hot-path callers don't thread Redis through
DI. AnomalyWorker wires the tracker into the detector automatically.

Same Ops panel as the rate breaker (AnomaliesCard already handles
kind="fingerprint_loop"). No auto-pause — fingerprint loops always
surface, not hard-tier.

name/key/order sensitivity, multi-span discrimination). 29 total
observability tests pass.

* feat(dispatch): kill-switched per-tenant soft cap in DISPATCH_LUA

Post-2026-05-11 incident follow-up. Disabled by default — operators
opt in per-environment via LANGWATCH_DISPATCH_TENANT_CAP=N.

When the env var is set to a positive integer N, the dispatcher
refuses to dispatch a group whose tenant already has N in-flight
groups. Other tenants' groups deeper in the ready zset still scan
through normally. The 2026-05-11 outage would have been bounded
within minutes with a cap of e.g. 50 (W_7kPya monopolised 100% of
slots; cap of 50 would have left 50% free for every other tenant).

Implementation:

- DISPATCH_LUA + DISPATCH_BATCH_LUA both accept tenantCap as a new
  trailing ARGV. tenantCap=0 (default) is a no-op for byte-equivalent
  back-compat with the existing scheduler.
- TenantId derived from groupId prefix (segment before first '/'),
  matching the rest of the codebase.
- New Redis counter `<prefix>tenant_active:<tenantId>` (TTL =
  activeTtlSec) tracks in-flight dispatches per tenant. INCR on
  dispatch, DECR on COMPLETE_LUA. TTL is a safety net — if a worker
  crashes between dispatch and complete, the counter self-heals.
- Why a soft cap (not the full sqrt-weighted RR described in the
  post-mortem): the WRR rewrite touches every dispatch hot-path call
  and warrants dedicated benchmarking + a standalone PR. This soft
  cap is the cheapest 80% — it bounds the worst-case starvation
  without changing the inner loop's logic.

Conservative rollout path: ship with cap=0, validate on staging with
synthetic load + real traffic at cap=10/50/etc, then flip on per
environment. Rate breaker + Ops anomaly panel from the same PR will
surface any unexpected impact.

negative/zero/positive). Existing 30 groupQueue unit tests pass
unchanged (cap=0 path is byte-equivalent to pre-change behavior).

* fix(dispatch): tenant-cap CodeRabbit findings — scan budget + TTL sync

Two follow-up findings on the kill-switched tenant soft cap:

1. Scan-budget starvation. When tenantCap fires we skip over-cap groups
but they still consume scan budget. With the default budget of 1000
(DISPATCH_LUA) / pageSize*5 (DISPATCH_BATCH_LUA), a tenant with that
many over-cap groups at the head of the ready zset could still starve
other tenants deeper in the scan. Now: when tenantCap > 0 we widen
scanBudget to 50000 (DISPATCH_LUA) / pageSize*250 (DISPATCH_BATCH_LUA).
Explicit cost of opting into the cap: more work per poll for
cross-tenant fairness.

2. TTL synchronization. tenant_active counter previously had its TTL
set only on initial dispatch. REFRESH_LUA (heartbeat) extends
group:*:active well past the original TTL, and RETRY_RESTAGE_LUA
(retry backoff) sets activeKey TTL = backoff + 2s. Long-running or
backoff-held groups would expire their tenant counter mid-execution,
letting the same tenant grab another slot and drifting the cap up.
Now both Lua scripts EXPIRE the tenant_active counter alongside the
activeKey, but only when the counter already exists (avoids
recreating one that COMPLETE_LUA legitimately decremented to zero).

The "re-score over-cap groups to a future timestamp" half of the
CodeRabbit suggestion is intentionally NOT done: re-scoring every
capped scan would issue thousands of ZADD writes per poll under
sustained load, and the widened scanBudget already makes other-tenant
starvation arbitrarily rare. Tracked as a follow-up if production
metrics show the widened budget isn't sufficient.

* feat(ops): PostHog kill switch + 1h baseline cache for anomaly detector

Two follow-ups discussed in PR review to make the anomaly detector
safe to run on a multi-thousand-tenant cloud:

1. PostHog feature flag kill switch
   `es-observability-anomaly-detection-killswitch` gates both
   TenantRateTracker.record() on the hot path AND
   AnomalyDetector.evaluateTenant() in the worker. Per-tenant
   targeting means we can silence a single noisy neighbour without
   redeploying or globally disabling detection. 60s cache keeps the
   hot-path overhead to a per-process map lookup. PostHog outage
   defaults to "feature on" so observability cannot be silently
   killed by a third-party failure.

2. 1h baseline cache in Redis
   The p95 of a 7-day window does not move meaningfully in an hour;
   caching it drops the per-tenant tick cost from one 10080-field
   HMGET to one HGET. Insufficient-history tenants are not cached
   so they get re-checked next tick instead of being pinned for an
   hour. Below-floor cached values still skip evaluation, avoiding
   the re-scan for quiet tenants.

The previous tick design did not need the 500-tenant cap proposed in
review — noisy-neighbour detection across the entire cloud is the
whole point, and the cache makes scanning every tenant cheap.

ES is no longer configured in production (per

refactor(ops): model OpsScope as always-defined to stop console spam (#3584) (#3701)

* refactor(ops): model OpsScope as always-defined to stop console spam

useOpsPermission() is called on every page (via the global menu and
SettingsLayout). Its underlying api.ops.getScope endpoint was wrapped
in checkOpsPermission middleware, which threw FORBIDDEN for non-admin
users — so every non-ops user (i.e. nearly every user) saw a tRPC
permission error in the browser console on every page load.

The shape was wrong: OpsScope isn't a permission to grant or deny, it's
a property every authenticated user has — "what are you allowed to see?"
The honest answer for a non-ops user isn't an error; it's an empty scope.

This change:

- Makes OpsScope a discriminated union: `{ kind: "none" } | { kind: "platform" }`.
- Makes resolveOpsScope() total — it returns `{ kind: "none" }` for non-ops
  users instead of null.
- Adds a `throwOnDeny` option to checkOpsPermission (default true). The
  status-probe variant `checkOpsPermission("ops:view", { throwOnDeny: false })`
  populates ctx.opsScope with `{ kind: "none" }` and lets the handler return
  it as data instead of throwing.
- Wires that variant into ops.getScope only — every other ops endpoint still
  throws FORBIDDEN on the `kind: "none"` case (mutations, dashboard queries,
  badge counts, ...).
- Updates useOpsPermission to derive hasAccess from `scope.kind !== "none"`
  instead of `query.isSuccess`. All 6+ consumers keep working unchanged.

Adds 5 unit tests (resolveOpsScope total / non-ops + admin paths,
checkOpsPermission throw + grant + new probe path) bound to a new
specs/rbac/ops-scope-status-probe.feature.

Per CLAUDE.md TypeScript rule: 'Use named parameters via object

build(go_service): native cross-compile to fix multi-arch build slowness (#4049)

build(go_service): native cross-compile via BUILDPLATFORM/TARGETARCH

Previously every `docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64`
ran the Go compiler under QEMU emulation for whichever arch differed from
the host. Go's runtime scheduler scales super-linearly badly under TCG,
so a multi-arch build that should take 30s per arch was taking >30 min
in CI (and stalling out entirely on busy days — see langwatch-saas
build-and-push-artifacts run 25818785770).

Switch the build stage to `--platform=$BUILDPLATFORM` and use Go's
native cross-compilation via `GOOS=$TARGETOS GOARCH=$TARGETARCH`. The
compiler runs once on the host arch; QEMU is never invoked on the Go
workload. The runtime stage is distroless/static, so buildx assembles
per-arch images without running any code.

Local benchmark on M-series host:
  - linux/arm64 (native): 19s compile, 67s total
  - linux/amd64 (cross-compile from arm64): 23s compile, 52s total

Also adds a /go/pkg/mod cache mount alongside the existing go-build
cache so module download survives across runs, keyed per-arch.

fix(traces): ingest OpenInference llm.token_count.* tokens (#4034)

The OpenInference convention (Arize Phoenix), emitted by
`openinference.instrumentation.{openai,anthropic,langchain,...}`, carries
token counts under `llm.token_count.*` — a different namespace from the
Vercel AI SDK (`ai.usage.*`) and OpenLLMetry (`gen_ai.usage.*`) shapes the
canonicalisation pipeline already understood.

Before this change those attributes leaked into span params but were never
mapped to canonical `gen_ai.usage.{input,output}_tokens`, so downstream
cost computation never fired for OpenInference-instrumented spans (tokens
appeared in the trace JSON but the experiment / trace-list cost columns
stayed empty).

`OpenInferenceExtractor` now extracts:

  llm.token_count.prompt                        → gen_ai.usage.input_tokens
  llm.token_count.completion                    → gen_ai.usage.output_tokens
  llm.token_count.completion_details.reasoning  → gen_ai.usage.reasoning_tokens
  llm.token_count.prompt_details.cache_read     → gen_ai.usage.cache_read.input_tokens
  llm.token_count.prompt_details.cache_write    → gen_ai.usage.cache_creation.input_tokens

`llm.token_count.total` is consumed (so it doesn't leak into params) but
discarded — totals are derived downstream. `setAttrIfAbsent` is used so
any value already populated by the higher-priority `GenAIExtractor` wins.

* fix(loop-prevention): production bug — recordSpan was stripping the causality_depth attribute

Real bug, caught by writing the integration test through the actual
event-sourcing pipeline as rchaves insisted. The original PR #3976
loop-prevention fix was silently disabled in production:

   `recordSpanCommand.stripReservedAttributes()` (predates #3976)
   strips EVERY `langwatch.reserved.*` attribute from incoming OTLP
   spans because user SDKs aren't supposed to set them. But the
   loop-prevention design relies on nlpgo's BaggageAttributeProcessor
   stamping `langwatch.reserved.causality_depth=N` on its emitted
   spans, which then ride in via OTLP through the same recordSpan
   path → strip → reactor sees no depth attribute → dispatches eval →
   nlpgo emits depth=2 spans → strip → reactor dispatches again →
   INFINITE LOOP, the exact scenario #3976 was meant to prevent.

   Production reproduction is straightforward: configure an
   ON_MESSAGE monitor with no preconditions and ship a trace. The
   reactor's loop-blocked counter has been at 0 since merge — that
   was being read as "no loops attempted." The truth is "loops were
   never detected."

Fix:
   Narrow passthrough allowlist on stripReservedAttributes —
   currently only `langwatch.reserved.causality_depth`. Worst case
   if a customer SDK does set it is a one-shot eval-skip on their
   own trace; far preferable to silently breaking loop prevention.

     (loopPrevention.reactor.integration.test.ts) — testcontainers

     evaluationTrigger reactor wired into the GroupQueueProcessor,
     capturing dispatcher. Four scenarios: depth=0 dispatches,
     depth=1 BLOCKS + increments counter, per-span re-dispatch on a
     fresh depth=0 after a depth=1 noise span, kill-switch bypass.

     reactor.handle() (as my prior attempt did) misses the strip
     because the strip runs in recordSpan, not in the reactor.
   - Unit regression in recordSpanCommand.test.ts pinning the
     causality_depth passthrough as load-bearing.

     strip" scenario bound to the unit test.

* fix(eval/traces): three prod bugs caught by 2026-05-14 dogfood

rchaves spotted three independent regressions while dogfooding the
loop-prevention PR end-to-end in prod. All three were silently
non-functional code paths the previous test approach (function-level
asserts) couldn't catch. Driving the real event-sourcing pipeline
through testcontainers + reading the actual traces explorer surfaced
each one.

1. Eval spans landed on an orphan trace
   nlpgoFetch sent no `traceparent` header, so nlpgo's
   `startStudioSpan` had no parent SpanContext to extend. Worse: the
   eval body carried `do_not_trace: true` from `runEvaluationWorkflow`,
   which short-circuits nlpgo's parent-context setup BEFORE the
   body-supplied trace_id fallback runs — guaranteeing a fresh
   trace_id for every eval, with no link back to the trace being
   evaluated. The `do_not_trace=true` predated the depth-attribute
   loop prevention; it was a different layer for the same concern,
   redundant now and actively harmful.

   Fix:
   - nlpgoFetch: new `parentTrace?: {traceId, parentSpanId}` option;
     when set, emits a valid W3C `traceparent` header.
   - runEvaluationWorkflow: drop `do_not_trace: true`. Loop
     prevention now lives in the reactor's depth check.
   - evaluation-execution.service: new `extractParentTraceForNlpgo`
     helper that plucks the parent trace's root span_id (when both
     trace_id and root span_id are OTel-standard hex IDs) and passes
     it to nlpgoFetch. Returns undefined for legacy trace_<nanoid>
     shapes so we don't synthesize a parent_span_id that would
     render under a non-existent span in Studio's waterfall.

2. Trace-summary computedOutput showed wrapper JSON
   nlpgo emits `langwatch.output = {"output":"Hey there"}`. The IO
   extraction service correctly unwraps that to "Hey there" via
   `messagesToText` / `extractTextFromPlainJson`, populating
   `outputResult.text`. The IO accumulator threw that field away
   and did `JSON.stringify(outputResult.raw)` instead, so users
   saw `{"output":"Hey there"}` in trace summaries.

   Fix: new `preferText(text, raw)` helper; accumulator uses the
   extracted text when present, falls back to JSON.stringify(raw)
   only when extraction returned empty (non-null guarantee).

3. Traces explorer rendered Genkit/Mastra `parts` payloads as raw JSON
   The backend's `extractMessageContentText` handles `parts` arrays
   (Genkit, AI SDK, Mastra) — each part being `{type:"text", content}`
   or `{type:"blob"|"image"|"reasoning"}`. The new traces explorer's
   `previewFormatter.unwrapChatArray` only knew `content`, so any
   message-shaped trace with `parts` fell through to raw JSON
   rendering. Caught against a real product-classification trace
   where the user-facing preview was a 4KB base64-encoded image
   blob followed by raw JSON.

   Fix: `extractMessagePartsText` mirrors the backend's part
   shapes (`type:text` with `text` or `content`, typeless wrapper,
   plain string). Multi-modal messages (image + text) surface just
   the text. Image-only messages fall through to JSON.

* test(nlpgo): pre-build binary once, keep e2e in CI for regression cover

Reverting the previous NLPGO_E2E opt-in gate. The point of this test
is to catch regressions in traceparent / OTLP / pipeline propagation,
which means it must run in CI on every PR — not just on developer
machines.

Real fix: amortize the compile cost like testcontainers do for the
infra. Pay it once per test process, cache the artifact, exec the
compiled binary instead of `go run` every spawn.

How it works:

  - `ensureNlpgoBinary()` runs `go build -o .vitest-tmp/nlpgo-test
    ./cmd/service` if the cached binary is missing or older than any
    .go / go.mod / go.sum under services/nlpgo, cmd/service, or pkg/.
  - Build budget bumped to 600s to cover a cold Go module cache on CI
    (no Go setup in the integration job — pulls + first compile is
    minutes). Subsequent runs hit Go's per-file build cache and take
    seconds.
  - Health-check window dropped from 90s to 30s, because a pre-built
    binary boots in ~1s. If it ever exceeds 30s on this path, something
    is wrong, not slow.
  - beforeAll timeout bumped to 700_000ms to cover the build + boot +
    health window in the worst-case CI cold-start path.

  - Touch services/nlpgo/.../tracing.go: re-runs the staleness check,
    rebuilds incrementally, still 14s total.
  - `.vitest-tmp/` added to langwatch/.gitignore so the binary doesn't
    land in commits.

fix(trace-summary): pin origin against eval-chain child spans (#4059)

* fix(trace-summary): pin origin against eval-chain child spans

2026-05-14 prod regression after PR #4048 wired loop prevention
end-to-end. nlpgo evaluator workflows now continue the parent trace
via W3C traceparent and stamp every emitted span with
`langwatch.reserved.causality_depth = N+1`. Those eval spans carry
`langwatch.origin = "evaluation"` and land on the customer's trace as
children. The fold projection's previous rule ("explicit origin on
any span always wins") then flipped the trace summary's origin from
"playground" (or "application", etc.) to "evaluation" as the eval
spans arrived — mis-classifying the customer's trace.

Fix: a NON-ROOT span carrying `causality_depth >= 1` is by definition
an eval child riding in on someone else's traceparent. Its explicit
origin must NOT flip the trace summary once an origin is resolved.

Narrow on purpose:
- Root spans always win regardless of depth — covers standalone eval
  traces where the eval IS the top-level activity (origin=evaluation
  on a depth>=1 root is correct).
- Non-root, depth=0 spans keep the old "explicit wins" semantics —
  preserves the existing SDK-heuristic → explicit-platform upgrade
  path on distributed traces (covered by an existing test at
  traceSummaryOrigin.unit.test.ts:650).
- Only non-root, depth>=1 spans get pinned out of the override path.

Stash-test-restore proof:
- New regression test fails on main (gets "evaluation" instead of
  "playground" — exact prod symptom).
- All 33 origin-suite tests pass with the fix, including the
  pre-existing "explicit overrides heuristic-inferred application"
  case which the narrow targeting preserves.
- All 411 trace-processing unit tests pass.

fix(nlpgo): studio root span is a true root when no inbound traceparent (#4061)

* fix(nlpgo): studio root span is a true root when no inbound traceparent

2026-05-15 prod regression. Every Studio playground / component /
evaluation run in the UI showed ⚠ "Parent not in trace" on the
workflow root row, with a different random parent_span_id per
invocation.

Root cause (services/nlpgo/adapters/httpapi/tracing.go pre-fix):
Studio's frontend mints a 32-hex trace_id and ships it in the request
BODY only (no W3C `traceparent` header). The fall-back path in
startStudioSpan needed trace_id continuity, so it synthesised a remote
SpanContext with a freshly RANDOM SpanID as the "parent" and dropped
it into ctx before tracer.Start. The OTel SDK then inherited the
trace_id but recorded parent_span_id = <random phantom>. That phantom
span is never emitted anywhere — hence "Parent not in trace" against
every legitimate playground row.

Fix:
- New pkg/otelsetup/idgenerator.go — ContextAwareIDGenerator. When the
  SDK is starting a root span (no valid parent SpanContext) it calls
  NewIDs(ctx); the generator honours a WithTraceIDOverride seed, falls
  back to random otherwise. NewSpanID (for child spans) is always
  random — pinning span_id across processes would corrupt trace trees.
- Wired into both TracerProvider construction paths in
  pkg/otelsetup/otelsetup.go via sdktrace.WithIDGenerator.
- startStudioSpan now calls otelsetup.WithTraceIDOverride(ctx, tid)
  instead of synthesising a parent SpanContext. The studio span comes
  out as a TRUE root: parent context invalid, parent_span_id all-zeros
  in OTLP, trace_id == body trace_id.
- Drops the now-unused newSpanID helper + crypto/rand import.

Stash-test-restore proof
(services/nlpgo/tests/integration/causality_propagation_test.go +
new TestCausalityPropagation_BodyTraceIDOnlyProducesTrueRootSpan):

  Without the fix:
    studio root has parent_span_id = f1f5782b1156395e (random phantom)
    assert fails: "studio root must be a true root … "

  With the fix:
    parent_span_id is all-zeros, trace_id matches the body.
    assert passes. Full causality_propagation suite stays green.

Unit coverage (pkg/otelsetup/idgenerator_test.go):
- Override-supplied trace_id is used when no parent SpanContext is in
  ctx; parent is invalid afterwards.
- Override is ignored when a valid parent SpanContext exists — child
  spans inherit trace_id from the parent (only NewIDs sees the
  override, not NewSpanID).
- Zero TraceID passed to WithTraceIDOverride is silently dropped so
  callers can't accidentally pin to all-zeros.

Specs: specs/studio/nlpgo-true-root-span-without-traceparent.feature.
Feature-parity: OK 1071 enforced scenarios bound, all green.

* fix(nlpgo): prompt-playground message assembly — system + variable interpolation + empty-turn drop

B1+B2 from the 2026-05-14 dogfood: every prompt-playground execution
through nlpgo dropped the system prompt, left {{input}}/{{var}}
placeholders literal, and duplicated an empty placeholder turn next to
the real user turn.

Root cause: buildMessages (engine.go) short-circuited
`return coerceChatMessages(inputs["messages"])` BEFORE the
instructions→system branch, so for a PromptStudioAdapter
execute_component (instructions = the typed system prompt,
inputs.messages = saved template turns + live conversation) it
returned the message array verbatim:

- {{input}} / {{answer}} / {{unbiased}} never interpolated

1. render the system prompt from the `instructions` param with the
   input variables; prepend it iff non-empty after rendering

2. render EACH history message's string content with the variables
3. drop any message whose content is empty after rendering, unless it
   carries tool_calls (mirrors _filter_empty_content_messages) — this
   is what removes the unfilled {{input}} placeholder turn so it is
   not duplicated

(every signature node's format() prepends its own instructions).

#4062's test-integration shard-3 failed traceparent-roundtrip with
"expected 0 to be greater than 0" (no spans in CH within 45s). Root
cause is scheduler contention, not a regression: this PR adds a second

* refactor(prompts): move sampling-param normalization to the write boundary

The read-time strip was a band-aid: it papered over a model-invalid value
that should never have been persisted in the first place. A prompt version
must never store a sampling parameter the chosen model rejects (e.g. a
slider-materialized temperature on a gpt-5-family model). Otherwise the
stored data is dishonest for every consumer and a pull writes back a value
that breaks the next call.

- New dropModelUnsupportedSamplingParams runs inside repository.createVersion
  — the single write boundary — so UI publish, CLI sync, and restore all
  produce honest stored data. Registry-driven and conservative: unknown

Per rchaves: dropping a sampling param because the registry says the model
doesn't support it is still an assumption — registries go stale, providers
change, the user may know something we don't. False positives and negatives
in either direction. Sync should faithfully propagate whatever was stored;
the right place to stop the platform UI from materializing a temperature
the user never chose is the form/slider, not the persistence layer.

fix(traces): fix /api/traces/search pagination crash on page 2+ (#4047)

* fix(traces): apply keyset cursor after GROUP BY and add partition pruning to dedup

The cursor condition was filtering individual rows before GROUP BY,
causing incorrect pagination for traces with multiple versions. Move
the cursor to the middle layer so it operates on deduped argMax values.
Also add time-range bounds to the outer dedup subquery to enable
ClickHouse partition pruning.

* fix(traces): split pagination into ID+data queries, propagate ClickHouse errors

The /api/traces/search pagination crashed after page 2 due to the outer
dedup subquery scanning the entire trace_summaries table for every page.
For projects with millions of traces this caused ClickHouse OOM/timeouts,
masked by the catch block swallowing the original error.

Fix: split the single data query into two steps:
1. Lightweight ID query (count + cursor + LIMIT) — runs in parallel with count
2. Scoped data query — fetches full columns for only the page's trace IDs,
   with dedup scoped to those same IDs instead of the full table

Also propagate the original ClickHouse error instead of replacing it with
a generic message, so future crashes are diagnosable.

* fix: add time bounds to step 2 data query for partition pruning

Addresses CodeRabbit review — the outer data query and its dedup
subquery were missing OccurredAt bounds, allowing ClickHouse to scan
across all partitions even though pageTraceIds was scoped.

fix(nlpgo): playground {{input}} auto-fill + structured-output gate parity (#4082)

* fix(nlpgo): broaden structured-output gate to match Python parity (B5)

`signatureNeedsStructuredOutput` only triggered structured outputs
for json_schema-typed outputs or 2+ outputs. Python's
`_use_text_only_completion` (langwatch_nlp/langwatch_nlp/studio/
dspy/template_adapter.py:228-232) treats the text-only fast path as
"zero outputs OR a single output of type `str`" — everything else
needs response_format. So a prompt with a single `bool` (or `float`,
`int`, `list[...]`, `dict`, `json_schema`) output slipped through:
the engine sent no response_format, the LLM replied with prose, and
that prose got shoved into a typed slot as a raw string.

User-visible symptom (rchaves dogfood 2026-05-16): a prompt with
Structured Outputs ON and a single output `passed: bool` rendered
a blank chat bubble in the playground because the TS output-
formatter silently rejects type-mismatched values upstream of the
render path. Fixing the gate restores the JSON-shaped response so
the parsed `true` flows through as a real bool.

Tests: comprehensive single-typed-output coverage (bool/float/int/
json_schema/list/dict, plus empty + single-str + multi-output edges).
TestComposeSignatureResponseFormat_SingleBool pins the rchaves
dogfood case end-to-end.

* fix(playground): bind live chat to inputs.input + absorb the absorbed live turn

2026-05-16 prod regression after #4062 merged: the saved-prompt
template carries `{{input}}` placeholders by default
(llm-config.repository.ts:872), but PromptStudioAdapter never bound
the live chat turn to the `input` variable. Observed in a real
playground trace by rchaves:

  system: "...\n{{input}}→\"\"\n{{test}}→\"test\"\n..."
  user:   "test7"   ← appended AS A SEPARATE turn, next to the empty
                      `{{input}}` template-rendered turn

`{{test}}` (set in the Variables panel) resolved correctly, but
`{{input}}` rendered to empty AND the live "test7" message sat
alongside as a duplicated user turn.

Old langwatch_nlp's playground path treated the latest live user
message as the `input` variable value, and the new live turn was
only appended when the template did NOT already reference
`{{input}}`. Reproducing that heuristic here:

  - inputs.input ← lastLiveUser.content  (when not already set
    explicitly in the Variables panel — explicit beats implicit)
  - drop the latest live user-message from the history WHEN a
    template user-message will absorb it (template contains
    `{{input}}`). System-only `{{input}}` references still get
    the variable bound but the live turn stays as its own message,
    since there's no template slot to render it into.

5 unit tests cover the cases: bind happens, template absorbs the
live turn, prior live turns survive, system-only reference still
appends, explicit Variables-panel value wins.

* test(nlpgo): integration proof for B5 single-bool structured output

TestPattern_StructuredOutput_SingleBool pins the rchaves dogfood case
end-to-end through the same router→engine→llm-boundary harness the
other DSL patterns use: a signature node with a single `passed: bool`
output sends response_format=json_schema (was nil pre-fix), the
schema declares `passed:{type:boolean}` so the provider enforces a
JSON bool reply, and the engine parses the JSON back into a real Go
bool reaching the end node — proving the gate fix prevents the
"raw prose shoved into typed slot" regression that surfaced as a
blank playground bubble.

Mirrors the Pattern007 multi-output structure but exercises the
single-non-str-output path that the broadened gate now covers.

* test(playground): fix noUncheckedIndexedAccess on B4 test helpers

CI typecheck flagged two TS2532 'Object is possibly undefined'
errors on src/app/api/copilotkit/[[...route]]/service-adapter.test.ts:
- line 253: mocked.mock.calls[0][0].message
- line 306: userTurns[0].content

Both sites assert defined-ness immediately before (toHaveBeenCalled /
toHaveLength 1) but noUncheckedIndexedAccess doesn't propagate the
runtime guarantee to index access. Tightening with explicit non-null
assertions where the prior expect() establishes the invariant.

Verified clean via full pnpm typecheck.

* fix(traces): SpanTabBar infinite loop blocking drawer close

`inlinePinned` and `overflowPinned` were fresh `pinnedSpans.slice(...)`
arrays every render. Both fed `tabDescriptors` → `tabIds` →
`useOverflowVisibility`, which clears + re-measures whenever the items
array changes by reference. Each pass synchronously triggered another
render → infinite loop, swallowed silently by IsolatedErrorBoundary.

The visible symptom was that *closing the drawer didn't tear down its
DOM*. The URL cleared cleanly, but the error-boundary recovery loop
kept React's scheduler busy on the subtree, so the parent
(`CurrentDrawer`) never got to reconcile the unmount. A window resize
"fixed" it because the ResizeObserver scheduled another update that
let the parent reconciliation slip through.

Memoizing both slices stops the churn — the dep array is now stable
when `pinnedSpans` / `inlineCount` are stable, the effect runs once,
and `CurrentDrawer` unmounts the shell as soon as the URL strips
`drawer.open`.

anything shows, which read as a noticeable beat between click and the
drawer sliding in.

gated on `useDrawerStore((s) => !!s.traceId)`. Since the openTrace
store action is already called synchronously in `useOpenTraceDrawer`,
the click → store-update → render lands in the same frame. URL is
still pushed for deep-linking + browser history, but no longer drives
the mount.

- New `useTraceDrawerUrlHydrator` hook lives on `TracesPage` and
  feeds URL → store both ways: deep link / browser-back populates
  `store.traceId`, URL strip clears it
- `handleClose` clears the store first (synchronous unmount), then
  pushes the URL cleanup
- `traceV2Details` slot in `drawerRegistry` swapped for a typed noop

landed it switched to WITH — that mid-load re-mount tore the body

section rendering at zero height (the screenshot the user posted:
ctx strip visible, everything below it gone).

`conversationId`. Single-turn detection happens *inside* the existing
PanelGroup: the ctx Panel is force-collapsed to 0 (via `collapsedSize:

* fix(traces): ctx pane true max-cap (split scroll container from measurement)

Root cause of the slow-drag-with-trailing-whitespace: `scrollHeight`
on an `overflow: auto` element is clamped to `>= clientHeight` by the
browser. The previous fix put `contentRef` on the scroll container
itself, so as the operator dragged the Panel larger:
  1. inner container's clientHeight grew
  2. its scrollHeight grew to match
  3. measure() read the bigger scrollHeight → bumped ctxMaxSize
  4. Panel cap moved up → drag could continue
  5. loop, with the visible whitespace just being container size
     beyond the actual content

Split the structure: outer Box keeps `flex: 1, overflow: auto` (the
scroll container), inner Box is naturally sized and carries
`contentRef`. The inner Box's `scrollHeight` now equals the rows'
real height regardless of Panel size — no feedback loop, max-cap
sticks, drag stops at content edge.

`CTX_SCROLL_VPAD_PX = 24` adds the scroll container's
`paddingY={3}` back into the pane's natural-height calculation, in
both the measure() effect and the on-expand rAF, so the snap-to-
content target accounts for that padding.

* fix(traces): single overflow measurement for tabs + rightSlot

The two-system approach (useOverflowVisibility for tabs + a width-
threshold ResizeObserver for rightSlot) made independent decisions
that disagreed at different widths — at ~540px the rightSlot
threshold was satisfied so the chip showed but the hook decided
tab 2 didn't fit; at ~510px the threshold hid the chip which freed
room for tab 2, only for the next breakpoint to hide it again.

Move rightSlot into the same overflow measurement as the tabs:
- Render it INSIDE the scroller, last in DOM order, tagged with
  `data-overflow-id="right-slot:instrumentation"`.
- Push that id onto the tabIds array passed to useOverflowVisibility.
- Render-time visibility is driven by the hook's hiddenIds set, same
  as every tab.
- Excluded from the OverflowMenu items list — the chip is a passive
  label, not a navigation target, so it just disappears rather than
  reappearing as a menu row.

Result: one cutoff iterator decides what fits, left-to-right; the
rightSlot is always the first item past the cutoff because it's
last in DOM. Wide: all visible. Medium: rightSlot only hidden.
Narrow: rightSlot hidden + tabs collapse to kebab in order.

fix(traces): flat default drawer width, grey flame text, ↵ glyph clamp (#4084)

* fix(traces): flat default drawer width, grey flame text, ↵ glyph clamp

Three post-merge operator reports rolled into one fix-pass:

1. **v2 drawer initial width was variable.** The `widthPx === null`
   fallback computed `45%` of the viewport — which then visibly
   shifted the first time the operator dragged (the persisted px
   replaced the %). Replaced with a flat
   `DRAWER_DEFAULT_WIDTH_PX = 920` constant, clamped at the
   viewport on small screens. Once the operator drags, the
   persisted localStorage value wins. ResizeRail's drag-start
   fallback and the toggle-snap-maximize restore path use the
   same constant. Unit test updated.

2. **Grey flame-chart bars unreadable in light mode.** Every
   `*.solid` palette except grey is saturated enough at 85% alpha
   on a white canvas to make white text readable; `gray.solid`
   blends to a pale grey that white text dissolves into ("can't
   read the letters" on Scenario Turn / module /
   execute_event_loop_cycle bars). Flip text to `fg` for grey
   palettes in light mode only — dark mode is already fine
   because the canvas is dark. Drop the dark drop-shadow on that
   branch too (would double-print dark glyphs).

3. **↵ glyph rendered as ugly trailing "↵..." under line-clamp.**
   The previous "append `↵` to end of every line, then `\n`"
   recipe meant CSS `-webkit-line-clamp` could truncate exactly
   after the glyph, producing a blank visible line that's just
   "↵...". Switched to leading-glyph style: prefix every
   continuation line with "↵ " instead of suffixing the previous
   line. Also trim trailing whitespace and collapse runs of
   blank lines, so the preview never ends on a break and never
   has empty middle lines. The clamp ellipsis now lands on
   actual content (or "…") rather than the glyph.

* fix(traces): unify role palette + thread layout polish

Seven operator complaints about the thread/bubble layout of the
v2 trace drawer's Input/Output area, all rooted in palette drift
+ layout polish bugs. Bundled because they share the same colour
+ chrome surface area.

1. **Canonical role palette.** Bubble layout hardcoded blue/purple
   while thread layout pulled from a separate `ROLE_COLORS` map
   that had `assistant=green` — so a scenario simulator (which is
   `displayRole=assistant`) rendered green in the thread chip but
   purple in the bubble card. Introduced `ROLE_PALETTES` with
   `{ fg, muted, solid, contrast }` per role, sourced from the
   bubble layout's own colour choices. Both UserTurnBubble,
   AssistantTurnCard, FlatTurnView, ThreadedTurnView, and
   RoleChip now consume the same palette by display-role key.

2. **System font size matches other turns.** `asMarkdownBody`
   detected pseudo-XML (`<role>`/`<goal>`/…) in system prompts
   and wrapped the entire message in a Shiki ```xml fence —
   rendered at 0.78em, visibly tiny against neighbouring
   user/assistant turns. Thread layout's system path now renders
   the raw text in a mono `<pre>`-style Box at `textStyle="xs"`,
   same baseline as every other turn.

3. **Drop the gray box around chat-shaped input.** IOViewer's
   outer `bg.subtle + border` container made sense for non-chat
   text, but for chat content every turn paints its own role
   chrome — the outer box read as a redundant container. Made
   `flushChatCard` true for any pretty+chat (input OR output),
   not just output.

4. **Sync thread/bubble toggle across in+out.** Lifted
   `chatLayout` state out of `useIOViewerState`'s per-instance
   `useState` into a module-level zustand store, so flipping
   it in INPUT updates OUTPUT in the same frame.

5. **Bigger ChatGPT-style avatar circles.** Thread layout's
   14px gray circle replaced with a 24px `palette.solid` circle
   + white icon — matches the operator's ChatGPT reference and
   reads as "real chat", not a debug log.

6. **Consistent collapsed/expanded header chrome.** Collapsed
   row used to be visibly smaller than the expanded header
   (different paddingY, smaller avatar, smaller text). Both now
   share `paddingY={1.5}`, 24px avatar, identical text style.
   Caret direction matches operator spec: collapsed = ↓
   ("click to open"), expanded = ↑ ("click to close").
   TurnCollapseChevron also flipped to ↑ for symmetry with the
   bubble-layout collapse.

7. **Whole header clickable, not just the caret.** FlatTurnView
   wraps the header in `<chakra.button>` so clicking anywhere
   on it toggles. ThreadedTurnView's collapsed row was already
   a button; matched the chrome to expanded for the rhythm.

8. **Rename "Simulator" → "User Simulator"** in scenarioRoles
   labels (`SIMULATOR` → `USER SIMULATOR`, `Simulator` →

* fix(traces-v2): surface 'unsaved edits' chip end-to-end on real wire

Dogfood revealed two consumer-side bugs in the draft surface that
unit tests with synthetic boolean inputs didn't catch.

1) promptAttributes.ts read `langwatch.prompt.draft` with a strict
   `=== true` check. The ClickHouse SpanAttributes column stringifies
   scalar OTel attrs on ingest, so an `attribute.Bool(true)` emitted
   by nlpgo lands as the literal string "true" by the time the trace
   API serves it back. Strict equality returned false → the
   PromptReference.draft field was false → the "unsaved edits" chip
   never rendered, despite the Go side emitting the attribute
   correctly.

   Accept both `true` (boolean) and `"true"` (string), matching the
   omission convention (anything else → not-draft). Regression test
   pinned in promptAttributes.unit.test.ts.

2) PromptsPanel.tsx's aggregatePromptUsage indexed spans by
   `promptReferenceKey(ref)` and locked the usage.ref to the first
   span sighted. Because PromptApiService.get and Prompt.compile
   share the same handle:version key but only Prompt.compile carries
   `langwatch.prompt.draft = true`, whichever sibling the iterator
   visited first determined the chip outcome — non-deterministic in
   practice, but in this trace's case the get span won and the chip
   was silently suppressed. Propagate draft=true forward from
   subsequent spans into the existing usage.ref so the compile span
   always wins for the draft bit.

   Also surface the chip in PromptsPanel.tsx (the dedicated v2
   Prompts tab pane) to match PromptAccordion.tsx which already
   rendered it. Both components show the same Lane E semantics now.

* test(nlpgo): NLPGO_SPAN_SYNC=1 swaps per-tenant BSP for SimpleSpanProcessor

The traceparent-roundtrip integration test has flaked three times in a row
under CI load, each time absorbed by widening its poll budget (45s → 120s →
240s outer). Pure timing widenings are a smell — they paper over a real
non-determinism without fixing it.

Root cause: each per-tenant exporter is wrapped in a BatchSpanProcessor
with a 5s ScheduledDelay. On a saturated CI runner the forceFlushMiddleware's
own 5s budget can expire before the foreground flush completes the OTLP
roundtrip; the rest of the spans drain async whenever BSP next wakes up.
There's no upper bound on that wake — only the next ScheduledDelay tick.
The test's polling loop then waits multiple minutes for spans that have
been sitting in the BSP queue.

Fix: SyncExport flag on otelsetup.Options. When set, the TenantRouter
constructs each per-tenant processor as a SimpleSpanProcessor instead of
a BatchSpanProcessor. SimpleSpanProcessor's OnEnd blocks on the OTLP
roundtrip synchronously, so by the time the HTTP handler returns every
span for that request has already been delivered to the collector.

Two regressions on the trace→playground "Open in Prompts" resume path
surfaced by dogfooding the prompt-span parity feature:

1. parseVariablesBlob used String(val) for every value when decoding the
   legacy JSON blob shape of langwatch.prompt.variables. Non-primitives

   variables) rendered as the literal "[object Object]" in the playground

   shows something meaningful and the value round-trips back through the
   form intact.

2. findClosestPrecedingSibling broke variable resolution for the python-
   sdk emission pattern. The SDK emits PromptApiService.get and
   Prompt.compile as a same-parent sibling pair: get carries the combined
   "<handle>:<version>" id + dispatch internals as variables, compile
   carries the raw configId + handle + version separately + the user's
   actual template variables. ClickHouse stores StartTime at millisecond
   resolution, so both spans land at the same startTime. The strict
   greater-than tie-break made get win on iteration order, dropping every
   user-facing variable from compile and leaving the playground Variables
   panel empty on resume.

   Fix: collect every preceding sibling with a prompt ref, sort by
   startTime, take identity (handle, version, tag, versionId) from the
   latest, and merge variables across all of them — later wins on key
   collision, so compile's user variables override get's dispatch
   internals when both spans share a key.

The internal-key filter on the emit side (services/nlpgo + sdk-go/prompts)
is a separate concern handled in the paired commit.

  into the signature node's inputs map alongside user template
  variables. emitPromptSpans then forwarded the whole map to
  Prompt.compile, so the variables JSON contained the chat history
  array. Add filterPromptCompileVariables in engine.go to strip
  `messages` + `chat_messages` before they reach the span — they are
  dispatch envelope, not user vars.

Bug #3 — `prompt_id` / `tag` (UI merger side):
  PromptApiService.get records its kwargs (`prompt_id`, optional
  `tag`) as variables per python-sdk parity. With Sarah's get+compile
  variable merge (063dcf959), these now leaked into the playground's
  Variables panel — and when only the get span survives a trace, the
  panel showed nothing but `prompt_id = prompt_…`. Add
  INTERNAL_PROMPT_VARIABLE_KEYS at the merger to filter these out at
  the boundary that feeds the UI; the trace itself still records the
  raw SDK emission so the wire contract is unchanged.

Defense in depth: both filters apply, so the same `messages` payload
gets stripped at emit time for new traces and at merge time for
traces emitted before this rolls out.

* fix(playground): place latest user turn at end of messages, not after system

Bug: [...formMsgs, ...liveMessagesForHistory] put the saved-prompt
template's `{{input}}`-bearing user slot BEFORE the chat history.
When `{{input}}` resolved to the live latest turn, that turn landed
at messages[1] right after system — the LLM read the latest user
input as if it preceded every prior turn.

Fix: when the template absorbs the latest live turn (via
`{{input}}`), the formMsgs slot lives at the END of the array; chat
history goes in front. When the template does NOT reference
`{{input}}`, formMsgs stays at the front (preamble/scaffolding) and
live history appends after — unchanged from before.

order, and added a regression test replaying the exact 5-turn shape
from the dogfood screenshot ('how big is mars?' → ... → 'huh?').

Caught during dogfood: clicking "Open in Playground" on an LLM-span
trace produced a chat that cut off at the last user turn — the
assistant's just-rendered reply was missing even though the trace
drawer's OUTPUT panel showed it inline.

Root cause: nlpgo's endLLMSpan stamps langwatch.output as a JSON-
encoded SINGLE app.ChatMessage struct
(`{"role":"assistant","content":"<reply>"}`) — NOT an array, NOT
wrapped in `{type, value}`. The CH extractor checked for those two
shapes plus `parsed.value` string + bare string, but had no branch
for the bare single-object form. parsed fell through every branch
and the reply was silently dropped.

Fix: add the single-object branch, accepting `{role?, content}` and
defaulting role to `assistant` for output (or `user` for input).

extractPromptStudioDataFromClickHouse method into a pure
parseLLMSpanMessages(attrs) function so the wire-shape contract
is unit-testable without spinning up the full ClickHouseTraceService.

fix(otelsetup): drop self-loop in startup error handler (#4112)

* fix(otelsetup): drop self-loop in startup error handler

Captured otelapi.GetErrorHandler() as the startup filter's delegate and
then registered the filter via SetErrorHandler. GetErrorHandler returns
the singleton *ErrDelegator which forwards to the latest registered
handler, so the delegate pointed back to the filter — every dispatched
OTel error recursed until the goroutine stack hit 1 GiB and the process
exited with code 2. A flapping internal collector took every gateway
pod down within seconds.

Use a concrete slogErrorHandler{} as the fallback so the recursion is
impossible by construction. Add a regression test pinning the wiring
invariant and a feature spec under specs/ai-gateway/.

Why: gateway availability must not depend on internal observability
backends. Tempo / collector flap is now a logging event, not a fatal.

Scenarios bound to tests in pkg/otelsetup/ or services/aigateway/
silently fell through to the unbound state and tripped CI.

Add both roots so a Go test in either tree can satisfy parity for any
scenario it carries the /** @scenario ... */ annotation for.

* refactor(model-providers): CSS-cascade ModelDefaultConfig + n:n scope attachments

Replaces the flat `ModelDefault` (one row per scope+role+featureKey+model)
shape with a CSS-style cascading config. One ModelDefaultConfig row
holds a JSON policy mapping role names + feature keys to model ids;
ModelDefaultConfigScope is the n:n join binding a config to many
scopes. Absence of a key in the JSON means 'inherit from the next
scope up' — there is no explicit "inherit" sentinel in storage,
keeping the merge logic trivial and the on-disk shape lean.

Why: rchaves's directive is that the data should read like CSS — set
once at the org, override per team or project, override per feature
when needed. The previous flat-assignments shape couldn't express
'one rule, many scopes' without N rows that had to be diff-ed on
every save. With this shape one config = one rule, scope attachments
are independent, and the resolver does the cascade.

Resolution order:
  1. Walk tiers in specificity order (project → team → org). Within a
     tier, sort attached configs by createdAt DESC. First-set
     featureKey wins as 'feature_override'; first-set role key wins
     as 'role_default'. Lower tier always beats higher tier regardless
     of recency (CSS specificity wins over insertion order across
     tiers; the same-scope tiebreak is recency within a tier).
  2. Legacy B2 scalar columns (one-release compat fallback).
  3. Built-in role constant.
  4. ModelNotConfiguredError.

* refactor(multitenancy): SCOPED_MODELS replaces EXEMPT bypass for scoped tables

EXEMPT_MODELS was the wrong shape for ModelProvider, ModelProviderScope,
ModelDefaultConfig, and ModelDefaultConfigScope. None of these tables
carry a projectId column, so they had to bypass the default guard, but
the bypass also let a programmer write `prisma.modelDefaultConfig.findMany({})`
and silently walk every tenant's defaults. Rchaves caught this on the
2026-05-18 dogfood.

Replace the bypass with a per-model predicate validator. Every query
against a scoped model MUST carry one of:

* a row id (single-row lookup is itself the tenancy proof)
* a scope predicate (`scopes.some.OR` cascade or top-level
  scopeType+scopeId on the join)
* a parent FK (modelProviderId / configId on the join tables)
* a legacy projectId (ModelProvider only — kept until the column drop)

Bare `findMany()` now throws with a precise error message. Same for
create / createMany — every record must carry the scoped equivalent
of projectId.

* dbMultiTenancyProtection.ts: drop the four scoped models from

  recurse into AND clauses so the exclude-id-with-scope pattern still
  passes.
* New unit tests pin the rule for every query shape the repository
  layer uses (bare findMany throws, scope OR ladder passes, id alone
  passes, AND-wrapped scope passes, create without scopes throws,
  createMany with mixed shapes throws on the broken entry).

getDefaultModelsForProject builds visibleScopeFilter as
