* fix(chart): address CodeRabbit findings + unblock helm-template CI

Three valid review comments on the gateway-auth + preflight work, plus
the related CI break.

1. Name-mismatch fail-fast (CR major). When autogen.enabled is true, the
   chart materialises the Secret named `autogen.secretNames.gatewayAuth`
   while langwatch-app + the gateway pod mount whatever
   `gateway.secrets.existingSecretName` points at. A mismatch silently
   creates one Secret and boots pods against another. _helpers.tpl now
   appends a render-time error when both names are set and differ.

2. ArgoCD annotations corrected (CR major). The earlier draft slapped
   `argocd.argoproj.io/compare-options: IgnoreExtraneous` +
   `sync-options: ServerSideApply=true` on the materialised Secret in
   the belief they would suppress per-sync rotation. They do not:
   IgnoreExtraneous only affects sync-status calculation, ServerSideApply
   only changes the apply mechanism. Neither prevents Argo from
   reconciling the rendered random `data` toward the cluster. Annotations
   are removed; the file's comment block now describes the actual
   ArgoCD-safe paths (skip autogen and use an out-of-band materialiser,
   OR keep autogen and pin /data via `ignoreDifferences` in the
   Application manifest). `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep` is retained
   because that one is real (Helm-side).

3. values.yaml docs reconciled (CR minor). The new autogen block and the
   later `gateway.secrets.existingSecretName` comment said opposite
   things ("the chart materialises this" vs "the chart does NOT
   materialise it"). The existingSecretName comment now describes both
   states — autogen materialises and reuses-via-lookup; otherwise the
   operator brings the Secret out-of-band before `helm install`.

Plus: chart default `gateway.otel.endpoint` flipped from
`http://langwatch-app:5560/api/otel` to `""`. The earlier default
required an auth token to function (the chart's own NOTES + values
comments documented that) but never enforced it — every chart example
in `examples/` inherited the misconfigured default, my new render-time
validation correctly flagged every single one of them, and the CI
`template (scalable-prod)` job went red as a result. Disabling export
by default is the safe shape: operators who want gateway spans
explicitly point at /api/otel + authExistingSecretName (or at their
own collector with whatever auth that needs). The 401 storm that
historically crashed gateway pods (postmortem 2026-05-21 root cause
#6, Bifrost recursion since patched in main) becomes unreachable
through defaults.

Verified:
- helm template against values-local / values-hosted-prod /
  values-scalable-prod all render cleanly (CI's three matrix entries)
- name-mismatch values render with a crisp error pinning both names
- name-match values render successfully

* fix(chart): tighten preflight hook (security context + jsonpath quoting)

Second pass on CodeRabbit feedback for the preflight Job template.

1. Inherit chart-wide pod security + scheduling defaults via the same
   coalesce(.Values.preflight.*, .Values.global.*) pattern langwatch_nlp,
   app, and workers Deployments use. Pod Security Admission strict
   namespaces (or PSP equivalents) would otherwise reject the hook,
   blocking every upgrade with a non-obvious 'pods "..." is forbidden:
   violates PodSecurity ...' error. Same goes for clusters with node
   taints on the langwatch pool: without inheriting the global
   tolerations, the Job would land Unschedulable.

   Added per-hook overrides under .preflight.* (podSecurityContext,
   containerSecurityContext, nodeSelector, tolerations, affinity) for
   operators who need to deviate from the chart-wide defaults.

2. kubectl JSONPath bracket-quoted form. The earlier `{.data.$key}`
   notation works for keys without dots but breaks on shapes like
   `db.password` because the JSONPath parser splits on `.` before the
   shell substitution lands the key name. Changed to `{.data['$key']}`
   which handles dots, dashes, and any other allowed key characters
   uniformly. Verified end-to-end against lw-dev (langwatch-app-secrets
   + langwatch-gateway-auth keys all read correctly).

Re-verified the three CI-matrix example values renders (local /
hosted-prod / scalable-prod) and the lw-dev pass path. Preflight Job
runs to "all required Secret keys present in namespace langwatch" with
the inherited global security context applied (fsGroup=1000,
runAsNonRoot=true, allowPrivilegeEscalation=false, caps dropped).

* fix(test-helpers): stop pre-seeding langwatch-gateway-auth in helm_install

After the chart-managed gateway-auth Secret landed in feat/nlpgo-default-helm,
the kubectl-create in test-helpers.sh started conflicting with helm install:

  Error: rendered manifests contain a resource that already exists.
  Unable to continue with install: Secret "langwatch-gateway-auth" in
  namespace "lw-test" exists and cannot be imported into the current
  release: invalid ownership metadata; label validation error: missing
  key "app.kubernetes.io/managed-by": must be set to "Helm"; ...

The pre-seed was originally needed because the chart only referenced
the Secret (via gateway.secrets.existingSecretName) without materialising
it. The autogen path now materialises it via templates/gateway-auth-secret.yaml
on first install and reuses existing data via lookup on every subsequent
install, so the pre-seed is redundant and actively breaking e2e overlays.

Both values-e2e.yaml and values-e2e-full.yaml ship `autogen.enabled: true`,
so this is the steady-state path for every e2e suite. The namespace pre-
create stays — it used to piggyback on the same kubectl call and is still
needed before `helm install --create-namespace` in some kind cluster
shapes.

* feat(flags): default release_ui_ai_gateway_menu_enabled to on

Mirrors the release_nlp_go_engine_enabled flip on the same PR: the AI
Gateway product surfaces ship default-on, and operators carve out
per-project exceptions via a PostHog rule or operator-store row.

Also widens the pnpm dev startup warning so it fires whenever gateway
secrets are unset, since the menu now renders by default rather than
only under FEATURE_FLAG_FORCE_ENABLE.

* fix(chart): preflight fetches each Secret once and iterates secretKeys

Addresses two CodeRabbit findings on the preflight Job:

1. Efficiency: one kubectl call per Secret (json) + jq-based key checks
   locally, instead of one kubectl call per key. Drops the call count
   from 6 to 2 and gives the 60s activeDeadlineSeconds far more headroom
   on slow API servers. alpine/k8s already ships jq.

2. Single source of truth: range over .Values.secrets.secretKeys
   instead of hardcoding the 4 app-secret key names. Adding a new
   required key to values.yaml (plus deployment + NOTES) now
   propagates into the preflight check automatically.

* fix(chart): always-on gateway-auth Secret + autogen value helper

Matches the clickhouse/redis/postgresql subchart pattern: when
gateway.chartManaged=true the umbrella chart materialises the
LW_GATEWAY_* Secret via lookup-or-rand on every render, regardless
of autogen.enabled. Stock helm install boots the app + gateway
pods end-to-end with no operator-side Secret prep; helm upgrade
reuses existing data via lookup so neither pod rolls.

Adds langwatch.autogenSecretValue helper so every chart-materialised
secret value flows through one primitive (sha256(64-char alphanum)
b64-encoded). gateway-auth-secret.yaml uses it for per-key backfill
(partially-populated Secrets heal in place) and app/secrets.yaml is
retrofitted to the same helper so a future FIPS / N-bit / Vault-
issued change has one update site.

ArgoCD: lookup returns nil under repo-server, so the chart still
re-generates every sync; mitigation is operator-side ignoreDifferences
on /data in the Application spec, documented in the template comment
and NOTES.txt.

Drops the postmortem-era validation that required autogen.enabled or
gateway.secrets.existingSecretName when chartManaged=true (the empty-
existingSecretName check never fired because the chart defaults that
knob). Also drops the gateway.otel.* auth validation: the gateway
subchart deployment intentionally does NOT inject the OTLP auth-token
env var (forward-compat-only knob), so failing on absent values would
tell operators to set knobs that do not authenticate the export. The
mitigation for the Bifrost startupErrorHandler recursion trigger is
the chart default flipped to gateway.otel.endpoint=""; operators who
opt back in plumb the header via gateway.extraEnvs (OTEL_OTLP_HEADERS)
until the subchart wires the knobs natively.

NOTES.txt rewritten to surface the always-on materialisation, the
ArgoCD ignoreDifferences block, the out-of-band materialisation path
+ kubectl annotate/label ownership handoff, and the helm.sh/resource-
policy=keep reinstall hazard.

* docs(self-hosting): add ArgoCD deployment guide

Standalone page covering the one piece of operator-side configuration
the LangWatch chart needs under ArgoCD: an `ignoreDifferences` block
on the chart-materialised `langwatch-gateway-auth` Secret. Without it,
every Argo sync rotates the gateway credentials because the Helm
`lookup` function returns nil from the repo-server (no cluster access)
and the template falls through to fresh randAlphaNum on every render.

Also documents:
- The app-secret vs gateway-secret asymmetry (app supports out-of-band
  via `secrets.existingSecret`, gateway does not because the chart
  enforces name consistency between materialised and mounted Secrets).
- What does not work (`IgnoreExtraneous`, `ServerSideApply` annotations).
- Reinstall hazard and the `helm.sh/resource-policy: keep` ownership
  handoff via `kubectl annotate` / `label`.
- Smoke test recipe for confirming pods do not roll on subsequent syncs.

Registered under the Self-Hosting > Deployment group in docs.json.

* docs(self-hosting): correct ArgoCD ignoreDifferences caveat after dogfood

Verified against a local kind-equivalent minikube + ArgoCD stable: with
the documented ignoreDifferences block on /data, the chart-materialised
gateway-auth Secret's resourceVersion stays constant across a hard
refresh + selfHeal reconcile cycle. Without the block, selfHeal rotates
the Secret on every cycle (resourceVersion bumps).

The earlier draft implied ignoreDifferences would block all forms of
overwrite. The accurate behaviour is auto-only: a manual
argocd app sync still applies the rendered Secret because the sync
operation always pushes the rendered manifest, regardless of drift
detection. Reworded the Warning callout to make that distinction crisp
and added the resourceVersion comparison smoke test as the canonical
sanity check operators can run.

* fix(chart): drop preflight gateway-auth check now that the Secret is always-on

3eb7388d3 changed gateway-auth-secret.yaml to materialise the Secret
unconditionally when gateway.chartManaged=true (lookup-or-rand, matching
the clickhouse / redis / pg subchart pattern). The preflight Job still
checked gateway.secrets.existingSecretName when autogen.enabled=false,
which means:

- chartManaged=true + autogen.enabled=false + Secret not yet present
  (gateway-adoption upgrade, or any of the documented production paths
  in examples/values-hosted-prod.yaml + examples/values-scalable-prod.yaml
  which set autogen.enabled=false): pre-upgrade preflight fails with
  "required Secret keys missing" pointing at LW_GATEWAY_INTERNAL_SECRET +
  LW_GATEWAY_JWT_SECRET, even though gateway-auth-secret.yaml is about
  to materialise both in the same upgrade. The chart was telling the
  operator to do something the chart was about to do for them.

The gateway-auth Secret now joins the autogen app-secret as a chart-owned
resource that the preflight has nothing to verify ahead of time. Preflight
keeps its original scope: only validate operator-provided Secrets
(secrets.existingSecret). argocd.mdx:104 already documented this
intended behavior; code now matches.

* chore(docs): regenerate llms.txt / llms-full.txt for new argocd.mdx

The argocd.mdx deployment guide added in 2f44cc0e0 / 0a911e929 wasn't
folded into the aggregated docs/llms-full.txt and docs/llms.txt index,
so check_generated_files CI (and downstream docs-complete) failed on
this PR. Regenerated via `node docs/llms.txt.cjs`.

* docs(self-hosting): require RespectIgnoreDifferences for ArgoCD; fix stale gateway-auth comments

Addresses review findings on PR #4423:

- ArgoCD ignoreDifferences alone only hides /data from the diff; an
  ordinary sync (repo-server lookup renders nil) still re-applies a
  fresh random pair and rotates the shared app/gateway credentials.
  Add RespectIgnoreDifferences=true to syncOptions everywhere the
  mitigation is documented (argocd.mdx, NOTES.txt, gateway-auth-secret
  template comment), note the first-sync caveat, and extend the smoke
  test to run a real sync instead of only a hard refresh.
- Correct the ArgoCD hook section: ArgoCD auto-maps Helm pre-install /
  pre-upgrade hooks to PreSync, so no explicit annotation is needed.
- Fix stale values.yaml comments: the gateway-auth Secret is
  materialised whenever gateway.chartManaged is true (independent of
  autogen.enabled), and the default name is langwatch-gateway-auth (not
  {{ .Release.Name }}-gateway-auth).
- Regenerate docs/llms-full.txt.

* docs(self-hosting): tighten ArgoCD caveats (plain kubectl apply, Flux, sync-options link)

Second-round review nits on PR #4423:

- The outside-Argo caveat applied only to force/replace applies; broaden

fix(gateway): forward tool_choice in bedrock VPCE intercept ToolConfig (#4436)

* fix(gateway): forward tool_choice in bedrock VPCE intercept ToolConfig

Customer dogfood 2026-05-31 (managed-bedrock skai, us-east-1, VPCE
intercept, us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-*): nlpgo's structured-output
fix (#4431) translates response_format to tools + forced tool_choice
for bedrock+anthropic, but the VPCE intercept's mapBedrockToolConfig
emitted only the tools array and silently dropped tool_choice. The
model was free to ignore the synthetic lw_so_<schema> tool and reply
with text. The engine's prose-fallback then dumped the entire reasoning
into the first declared output field — exactly the failure mode #4431
was supposed to close, except the VPCE intercept never honored the
forced pin so structured outputs still collapsed.

This was masked by the existing bedrock e2e: it ran against the public
bedrock endpoint via bifrost, which DOES forward tool_choice through
its own convertToolConfigFromFiltered. Customers on the public-bedrock
path benefited from #4431; managed-bedrock-VPCE customers did not.

mapBedrockToolChoice maps the OpenAI/bifrost ChatToolChoice union to
the bedrockruntime ToolChoice union:
- string "any" / "required" or struct{type:any|required} -> ToolChoiceMemberAny
- string "auto" or struct{type:auto} -> ToolChoiceMemberAuto
- struct{type:function, function.name:X} -> ToolChoiceMemberTool with SpecificToolChoice{Name:X}
- string "none" or struct{type:custom|allowed_tools|unknown} or empty function name -> nil (bedrock defaults to auto)

mapBedrockToolConfig now sets ToolConfig.ToolChoice = mapBedrockToolChoice(params.ToolChoice).
When no tool_choice is on the inbound request the ToolChoice field stays
nil and bedrock defaults to auto — same observable behavior as before
the fix, just with the forced-pin case actually working.

Coverage:
- Unit: bedrock_vpce_test.go covers the mapBedrockToolChoice mapping
  matrix (nil input, string variants, struct variants, empty function
  name fallback) + the end-to-end mapBedrockToolConfig contract
  (tools + forced choice both forwarded).
- Live: TestBedrockVPCELive_StructuredOutputToolChoice exercises the
  full dispatchBedrockVPCE path with a forced lw_so_* tool against any
  Bedrock-compatible endpoint (build tag live_bedrock_vpce, env-gated
  BVPCE_ENDPOINT + AWS creds). Pre-fix: model returns text content +
  empty tool_calls. Post-fix: model invokes the forced tool + returns
  JSON in arguments.

Verified end to end against the actual customer VPCE
(http://vpce-...:80, us-east-1, us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0,
STS-temporary creds from the managed-bedrock chain): the synthetic
lw_so_ClassifierRelevance tool gets invoked, arguments parse as
{"output": true, "reason": "<paragraph>"}, text content is empty, just
like LiteLLM's behavior on the python path.

bedrock+anthropic-family models, with a contrived e2e
(workflow_llm_bedrock_structured_outputs_test.go) that used a 1-line

feat(ops): /ops/clickhouse/explain endpoint for the optimizer agent (#4434)

* feat(ops): /ops/clickhouse/explain endpoint for the optimizer agent

Lets the clickhouse-optimizer agent self-validate query plans against
the live ClickHouse instance instead of always opening a PR and waiting
for a human to run EXPLAIN locally. Defenses in depth:

  1. API key auth via LANGWATCH_OPS_API_KEY (constant-time compare).
  2. Server-side EXPLAIN wrapper: user query never reaches CH unwrapped.
  3. EXPLAIN type allowlist. ANALYZE is blocked because it executes
     the inner query (load risk on prod).
  4. Forbidden-keyword pre-filter (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/ALTER/DROP/...)
     plus rejection of multi-statement (semicolon) queries.
  5. ClickHouse-side readonly=1 + max_execution_time=5s + max_result_
     bytes=10MB as the backstop if the wrapper or pre-filter is
     somehow bypassed.
  6. Audit log of every accepted request (type + first 200 chars).

Worst-case key leak surface: caller can read query plans and learn
schema/partition structure (schema is already public in this repo); no
data exfiltration possible, no writes.

9 unit tests cover the parser — types, forbidden keywords, word-boundary
correctness, multi-statement rejection, realistic agent shape.

* fix(ops): address reviewer findings on /ops/clickhouse/explain

P1 (langwatch-agent / coderabbit) — SSRF-capable table functions slipped
past the readonly=1 backstop. readonly only blocks WRITES; url(), s3(),
remote(), postgresql(), file(), mysql() and friends are read operations
and would let a leaked key turn prod ClickHouse into an arbitrary
outbound HTTP / S3 / SQL client. Added TABLE_FUNCTION_RE matching the
known-bad list followed by `(` so column refs are not false-rejected,
plus SYSTEM_SCHEMA_RE for system.* introspection. Tests cover 8 of the
worst table functions and a benign `WHERE file = 'x'` case.

P2 — multitenancy invariant. Every CH query in this repo must be
TenantId-scoped; an unscoped EXPLAIN leaks partition stats across
tenants. Added TENANT_PREDICATE_RE requiring `TenantId =` anywhere in
the query body.

P2 — audit log was capturing the first 200 chars of raw SQL, which
includes tenant ids / emails / PII literals from WHERE clauses. New
redactQueryForAudit() strips all string + numeric literals and emits
the SQL shape + a stable 16-char sha256 prefix for correlation. Both
covered by unit tests.

P2 — three typecheck errors:
  - forbidden[1] possibly undefined: nullish-coalesce
  - m[1] possibly undefined: optional chain on the if check
  - CLICKHOUSE_GUARDRAILS values must be strings per ClickHouseSettings

Test count: 9 → 17.

* feat(ops): prefer dedicated langwatch_ops user via CLICKHOUSE_OPS_URL

The reviewer flagged that the regex-based table-function deny-list in
explain.ts is the only line of defense against a leaked LANGWATCH_OPS_API_KEY
being turned into url()/s3()/remote() SSRF. Add the access-layer boundary
itself: when `CLICKHOUSE_OPS_URL` is set, build a dedicated CH client and
use it instead of the shared default-user client.

The saas-side companion change (langwatch-saas #532) provisions a
`langwatch_ops` user whose only grant is `SELECT ON langwatch.*` -- no
SOURCES grant, so CH refuses every table function call at the access-check
layer regardless of what slips past the input filter.

When the env var is unset the endpoint falls back to the shared client
with a one-shot warning log, so dev / pre-migration prod still works and
the regex filter remains the active boundary. The handler logs
`usingFallback` in the audit line so operators can spot fallback usage.

* fix(ops): max_execution_time is Seconds (number), not UInt64 (string)

ClickHouseSettings is finicky: `readonly` and `max_result_bytes` are
`UInt64 = string`, but `max_execution_time` is `Seconds = number`. The
prior reviewer-fix commit stringified all three, which CI tsgo caught.

* fix(ops): close comment/string bypasses + fail closed in prod (P1/P2/P3)

Reviewer round addressing langwatch-agent's review on the explain endpoint.

P1 (fail closed when CLICKHOUSE_OPS_URL is unset, in production)
The previous "warn + fall back to the shared client" path left the regex
deny-list as the only line of defense against a leaked API key. The
deny-list is best-effort (see P2). In production the handler now returns
503 with a clear "CLICKHOUSE_OPS_URL unset in production" message and
never invokes the shared client. Dev / NODE_ENV=test still falls back
with a one-shot warning so local hacking and pre-prod migrations work.

P2 (comment + string-literal bypasses on the regex pass)
The regex deny-list was being matched against the raw query, so
`url/**/('http://x')` evaded the table-function check (the regex sees
no `(` adjacent to `url`) and `WHERE 1=1 /* TenantId = */` satisfied
the tenant predicate without filtering anything. Same problem for
strings: `WHERE name = 'TenantId = something'`. New
`stripCommentsAndStrings()` strips block / line comments and quoted
strings (single + double, escape-aware) once at the top of
buildExplainQuery; every regex pass runs against the normalized text.

decide what runs.

trips the forbidden-keyword regex" false positive is now correctly
accepted.

P3 (guardrails comment did not match what was sent)
The header advertised a 10s execution cap + 1 GB memory cap;
CLICKHOUSE_GUARDRAILS sent 5s and no memory cap. Bumped to match: 10s
execution, 1 GB memory_usage (UInt64 = string per the CH typing).
These now also match the langwatch_ops `readonly_safe` profile in
the saas users.xml so per-query + user-level limits agree.

  (block-comment table function, line-comment table function, comment-
  hidden tenant, string-hidden tenant, comment-split DROP, layered-
  defense fallback, string-internal semicolon / system.* not tripped)
- 4 new handler tests (prod fail-closed, no-key 401, bad-key 401,

* fix(ops): nesting-aware block-comment stripper (P2 follow-up)

Reviewer found a third bypass on top of the previous round: ClickHouse
supports nested block comments, but the previous regex-based stripper
used a non-greedy `/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//` which stops at the FIRST `*/`. So

  WHERE 1 = 1 /* outer /* inner */ TenantId = 'p_fake' */

was normalized to `WHERE 1 = 1   TenantId = '' */`, the tenant-predicate
regex matched, and the executed query ran unscoped.

Replace the block-comment strip with a small state machine that tracks
depth — increments on every `/*`, decrements on every `*/`, and drops
every char while depth > 0. Unbalanced openers consume to EOF (same as
the CH parser, so the regex pass is safe to treat the rest as gone).
Inserts a single space at the closing `*/` so adjacency tricks like
`INS/**/ERT` still collapse to `INS ERT` (no keyword reborn).

Tests: 43/43. Added the exact reviewer repro plus three-level nesting
and unbalanced-opener regressions, all at both the
stripCommentsAndStrings and buildExplainQuery layers.

Note on the broader concern (regex stripping as the tenant boundary):
the dedicated langwatch_ops user is the actual access-layer boundary
against SSRF / cross-schema access, not the regex. For tenant isolation
specifically there is no row policy — operator endpoints intentionally
have cross-tenant read for the EXPLAIN use case (the agent needs to
look at any project's plan stats). The `TenantId =` regex is therefore
a guard-rail to make sure the caller didn't forget to scope the query
they're EXPLAINing, not a security boundary; it remains best-effort
and now correctly catches the nested-comment bypass.

* fix(ops): integrated lexer for normalizer + drop TenantId presence-check

Two changes for the latest reviewer pass:

P2a (string-vs-comment ordering bypass)
The old two-pass normalizer stripped block comments BEFORE string
literals, so a `/*` inside a legitimate SQL string opened a phantom
comment that swallowed live SQL after it. Reviewer repro:

  SELECT * FROM stored_spans WHERE '/*' = 'literal'
    OR SpanId IN (SELECT SpanId FROM url('http://127.0.0.1:9/', CSV))
    /* trailing */

The OLD stripper turned this into ~`SELECT * FROM stored_spans WHERE ''`,
so the table-function deny-list never saw the live `url(...)` call.

Replaced with a single char-by-char lexer that tracks string, line-
comment, and (nested) block-comment state in ClickHouse order — a `/*`
inside a string stays inside the string and a `'` inside a block
comment stays inside the comment. Handles `\'` and `''` escapes. Word
boundaries preserved (strings -> `''`, comments -> ` ` so `INS/**/ERT`
still collapses to `INS ERT`).

P2b (TenantId presence-check)
Dropped. The clickhouse-optimizer agent is an operator that legitimately
runs cross-tenant EXPLAINs to find slow query shapes across the fleet —
the previous "must contain `TenantId =`" check was about to false-reject
half its work. The actual security boundary is the langwatch_ops user
(no SOURCES, scoped SELECT, enforced via the prod fail-closed path),
not the SQL text. Layering a parser-rejection on top would either
false-reject legit CH syntax the agent uses or have to allowlist enough
to be useless as a gate.

Tests: 46/46. Added the P2a regression (live `url(...)` after a
quoted `'/*'` still rejected), the inverse (a `'` inside a block
comment is NOT a string opener), backslash + doubled-quote escape
cases, and a positive cross-tenant query (no TenantId predicate) that
now correctly passes. Removed the now-invalid "rejects unscoped"
assertion.

Drives the /api/ops/clickhouse/explain handler against a real

`.withReuse()` pattern as the existing clickhouseClient integration
test). Unit tests cover the normalizer in isolation; this is what
guarantees a query that survives the input filter actually returns
sensible EXPLAIN output, that the wrapping + per-query CH settings
round-trip, and that real CH errors propagate cleanly.

fix(ops): stop sending client settings when using langwatch_ops (readonly profile) (#4446)

fix(ops): stop sending client settings when using the langwatch_ops user

After #4445 unblocked authentication, every /api/ops/clickhouse/explain
request 502'd from the langwatch_ops path with "Cannot modify
'date_time_input_format' setting in readonly mode". The user runs under
the readonly_safe profile (readonly=1), which forbids any client-side
session-setting modification — even setting a value to what it already
is. So the createClient default of date_time_input_format=best_effort,
and the per-query CLICKHOUSE_GUARDRAILS we attached on top, both fail.

Functionally those settings were redundant on this path anyway: the
readonly_safe profile already pins exec_time/result_bytes/memory caps
server-side, and EXPLAIN never parses datetime input values. So:

  - Drop the date_time_input_format default from getOpsClickHouseClient
  - Only attach CLICKHOUSE_GUARDRAILS per-query when we fell back to the
    default-user client (legacy/dev path where the ops user isn't
    provisioned and the profile isn't enforcing the same caps).

Why the integration test didn't catch it: the testcontainers ClickHouse
runs with the default user under no profile and no readonly enforcement,
so setting overrides are silently accepted. The failure mode only
surfaces against a prod-shaped CH where users.xml pins readonly=1.

fix(ops): expand EXPLAIN INDEXES to the PLAN modifier form ClickHouse accepts (#4448)

`INDEXES` is exposed as a top-level type in our endpoint, but it's not a
top-level EXPLAIN type in ClickHouse — it's a modifier on `EXPLAIN PLAN`
(`EXPLAIN PLAN indexes = 1, actions = 1 SELECT ...`). Sending
`EXPLAIN INDEXES SELECT ...` raises a parser error inside CH and the
handler returns 502, which the clickhouse-optimizer agent hit during
self-validation.

Translate `INDEXES` into the canonical form so callers keep using the
logical name without needing to know that wrinkle. `actions = 1` is
included alongside `indexes = 1` because the two together are what
gives the agent the index-prune / partition-prune visibility it actually
wants from this type — and they're cheap, EXPLAIN never executes the
inner query.

feat(clickhouse): warn on cold-scan queries with no time filter (#4449)

* feat(clickhouse): warn on cold-scan queries with no time filter

Queries against our time-partitioned tables (stored_spans, stored_log_records,
stored_metric_records, event_log, billable_events, governance_ocsf_events) that
filter without any predicate on the partition time column cannot prune
partitions. They scan the whole history including the cold tier on S3, turning a
single call into a burst of S3 GET requests. That is the dominant driver of our
S3 request bill.

Adds a detector (detectColdScan) and wires it into the resilient client's
existing query observability, alongside the slow/too-heavy checks. It emits a
structured warn with coldScan=true and coldScanTable=<name> so the daily query
optimizer agent can grep for it. Detection-only: it never changes a query.

The detector is deliberately conservative: it only flags when the table is
referenced AND none of its time columns appear anywhere in the SQL, so a time
column used for any reason (filter, projection, order by) clears the flag.

* wire detectColdScan into resilient client logSuccess

The first commit added the detector and test but the warn-path wiring did not
land. This adds the import, the extractRawQuery helper, and the cold-scan branch
in logSuccess so a SELECT against a time-partitioned table with no time filter
actually emits the warn (coldScan=true, coldScanTable=<name>).

* fix(clickhouse): require a time predicate (not just a mention) to clear cold-scan flag

A projection or ORDER BY reference to the partition time column does not
enable partition pruning; only a WHERE/PREWHERE comparison does. The prior
detector cleared the flag on any mention, which would miss the real prod
trace-fetch shape (StartTime only in SELECT/ORDER BY, scans 252/252 parts).

* review: assert IN predicate clears the flag and narrow TIME_PARTITIONED_TABLES with as const

Adds the missing IN-predicate assertion to the BETWEEN test (the name promised
both but only BETWEEN was checked), and narrows TIME_PARTITIONED_TABLES via
`as const satisfies` so callers see exact tuple types instead of readonly string[].

perf(clickhouse): optimize trace-list query (-read bytes) (#4433)

* perf(clickhouse): optimize trace-list query (-read bytes, stop full-window payload scan)

findAll read ComputedInput/ComputedOutput and the rest of the heavy trace
columns for every deduped trace in the window before ORDER BY ... LIMIT trimmed
it to one page, and count() OVER () forced that whole deduped set to buffer in
memory. Together that is the dominant read-bytes cost on the main traces list.

Page the matching TraceIds first (key + sort columns only), then read the heavy
columns for that bounded page alone. The page total moves to a separate light
count() that never touches the payload columns. Ordering, dedup (latest version
via max(UpdatedAt)), and offset paging are unchanged.

perf(clickhouse): cap single-trace span-read memory to contain OOM blast radius (#4432)

* perf(clickhouse): optimize single-trace span fetch (stop OOM, -read bytes)

getSpansByTraceId and getNormalizedSpansByTraceId read the full SpanAttributes
/Events/Links payload for every deduped span in a trace before ORDER BY ...
LIMIT trims it down. A trace with far more spans than the read limit (a leaked
or pathological trace_id, the case the row clamp already guards) materializes
all of those payloads and tips this path into MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.

Page the SpanId set first (key columns + StartTime, no payload), then read the
heavy columns for that bounded set only. Results are identical for traces at or
under the limit; the win is on the long traces.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(clickhouse): cap single-trace span-read memory to contain blast radius

Fetching a trace's spans reads the full SpanAttributes Map; ClickHouse reads the
whole values array to return any of it, so a trace with very large per-span
attribute values (big prompts/responses/embeddings) can allocate gigabytes even
at a low span count. Uncapped, those allocations hit the server's total memory
limit, where the OvercommitTracker kills whichever query is allocating, so one
pathological trace degrades unrelated requests across the cluster.

Set an explicit max_memory_usage on the single-trace full-attribute reads
(getSpansByTraceId, getNormalizedSpansByTraceId, getSpanByIds) so such a read
fails on its own (MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) and surfaces as a query error, instead
of pressuring the whole server. The ceiling sits well above any normal trace
(p95 read is single-digit MB) and below the global per-query limit, so it only
trips on the pathological tail. This complements the page-the-SpanId rewrite,
which bounds the heavy-row sort for high-span-count traces.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* perf(clickhouse): drop the no-op SpanId paging, keep the memory cap

Real-tenant EXPLAIN (INDEXES) on the trace the OOM log named showed it holds
~15 spans in a single granule: the OOM is large per-span attribute VALUES, not
span count. The SpanId-paging rewrite therefore gave no granule-level reduction
for real traces (1 granule old and new) and its memory-comparison test was
flaky on CI (paged vs naive within 0.1% when a trace fits one granule).

Revert the paging and keep the single change that actually contains the
observed server-wide OOM: an explicit max_memory_usage on the full-attribute
single-trace reads, so a pathological trace fails its own query instead of
pushing the cluster past its total memory limit. getSpansByTraceId /
getNormalizedSpansByTraceId return to the prod-proven dedup query (now carrying
the cap); the OOM-safety guard and integration test are restored accordingly.

* fix(tokenizer): bound tiktoken remote BPE fetch with a timeout

TiktokenClient.remoteFetch did an UNBOUNDED network fetch (node-fetch-cache then
globalThis.fetch) with no timeout. TIKTOKENS_PATH local encoding files are never
provisioned, so every encode falls through to remoteFetch; in a network-restricted

  the cached-fetch and native-fetch paths. On timeout it aborts (closing the socket)
  and rejects; loadEncoder's existing try/catch turns that into a graceful skip
  (best-effort tokenization), so a network stall fails fast instead of hanging.
- tiktoken.client.unit.test.ts is now fully offline/deterministic (mocks the encoder
  + fetch) and adds a regression test asserting a never-resolving fetch yields
  undefined within the timeout rather than hanging.

fix(nlpgo): expose project secrets as `secrets.NAME` in code blocks (#4465)

The Go engine dropped project secrets on the floor for code nodes:
`runCode` → `codeblock.Request` → runner.py carried only code/inputs/
outputs, and the runner exec'd user code in a bare namespace. So
`secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID` (the syntax the Studio editor
hint suggests) raised `NameError: name 'secrets' is not defined`, and
`os.environ` failed too (secrets live in the DSL, not the subprocess
env). HTTP nodes were unaffected — they use the separate
`{{ secrets.NAME }}` resolver.

The Python executor already injects a `secrets` namespace via
build_secrets_preamble; the Go engine missed parity during the
dspy-rip. This threads `workflow.secrets` (populated upstream by
addEnvs.ts) through the one path that lacked it and injects a
`SimpleNamespace` into the runner's exec globals, so `secrets.NAME` is
real attribute access. Injected as a global rather than a source
preamble so user-code line numbers in tracebacks stay accurate. Left
undefined when no secrets are configured — byte-parity with the
Python preamble's no-op-on-empty behavior.

perf(clickhouse): stop topic-clustering OOM on trace_summaries ComputedInput (#4496)

* perf(clickhouse): stop topic-clustering OOM on trace_summaries ComputedInput

The topic-clustering trace fetch and its sibling counts query both read the
heavy ComputedInput column from trace_summaries and tipped busy tenants into
MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (Code 241, 3.5 GiB per-query limit).

fetchTracesFromClickHouse: the page CTE already selects the exact 2000 trace
keys to return, so the outer ORDER BY only re-ordered that fixed set. But
ORDER BY ... LIMIT forces ClickHouse to buffer a top-N of full rows, retaining
every row's ComputedInput payload at once, which is what blew the memory limit.
Drop the outer ORDER BY so rows stream out (ComputedInput read in small adaptive
blocks and released) and reapply the page ordering in JS over the small result
set. EXPLAIN confirms the Sorting step and the MergingSorted/PartialSorting
pipeline transforms are gone.

fetchCountsFromClickHouse: countIf(length(ComputedInput) > 0) read the heavy
column across the whole 12-month window to produce a number used only in a
debug log line. Drop it; the remaining counts use light columns.

perf(clickhouse): prune trace_summaries read in RAG document and feedback analytics (#4497)

* perf(clickhouse): prune trace_summaries read in RAG document and feedback analytics

The top-documents and feedbacks analytics queries JOIN trace_summaries to
stored_spans and read their payload entirely from the stored_spans ARRAY JOIN
(RAG contexts / Events arrays). trace_summaries is used only for the JOIN keys
and the OccurredAt date filter. Both queries nevertheless fed their deduped
trace_summaries subquery the full TRACE_ANALYTICS_COLUMNS set, including the
wide Attributes map, for every deduped trace across the window.

For busy tenants the top-documents query (uniq(toString(context.document_id)))
hit MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (Code 241, 3.5 GiB per-query limit) reading that map,
and the read also shows up as a cold-scan cost driver.

Prune the deduped subquery to TRACE_IDENTITY_COLUMNS plus any trace_summaries
columns the active filters reference (resolved with a new
extractReferencedTraceColumns, mirroring the existing span / evaluation column
extractors). Unfiltered queries read 4 columns instead of 20; filtered queries
still read exactly the extra columns their WHERE needs, so a TopicId or
Attributes facet filter stays valid.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(clickhouse): tighten column matcher to avoid identifier-suffix collisions

buildColumnPattern matched a column name as a suffix inside a larger
identifier: "Attributes" matched the tail of "SpanAttributes", and the alias
branch "ts." matched the tail of "Events." in "Events.Attributes". Both made
extractReferencedTraceColumns falsely pull the wide trace Attributes map into
the deduped subquery for span-only references, undercutting the prune.

Apply a single left boundary before the whole match (the optional alias
included) so a column only matches as its own token. Add regression coverage.

* fix(test): stop api-keys scope-filter integration test from OOMing CI

The integration shard hung ~3.5h on this file before OOMing the vitest
worker (Timeout terminating forks worker ... api-keys-scope-filter).

Root cause: the useOrganizationTeamProject mock returned a fresh
organization object literal on every call. That new identity busted the
useMemo([organization]) in useAvailableScopes, which gave filterAvailable
a new identity each render, which retriggered the [..., filterAvailable]
effect in useUrlScopeFilter, which called setScopeFilter -> re-render ->
new organization -> ... an infinite render/effect/setState loop. The
tight microtask loop starves the event loop, so vitest's per-test timeout
never even fires; the heap just grows until OOM.

Production is unaffected: useOrganizationTeamProject is backed by
react-query, which returns referentially stable data. Only the mock was
unstable. Fix builds the org/project/team objects once in the factory
closure and returns them by reference, so the memo/effect deps stay
stable. Test now passes in ~3s (14 tests) instead of hanging.

the cold clause. MODIFY TTL replaces the whole expression atomically, so the

* feat(retention): migration default 308 + byteSize() MATERIALIZED columns

"new migrations not yet in production can be fixed before merging"):

* `_retention_days UInt16 DEFAULT 308`
  Intentional behavior change: rows older than 308 days (44 weeks,
  partition-aligned) become TTL-eligible the next merge cycle. New
  inserts and old parts both inherit 308 via the DEFAULT. Migration
  itself stays metadata-only — no scan, no part rewrite (confirmed
  by CH maintainer; see `ch/migration-and-throttling.md`).

* `_size_bytes UInt32 MATERIALIZED byteSize(<heavy_cols>)`
  ClickHouse computes the row's in-memory byte total server-side at
  insert time across the listed payload columns. Per-table expression
  lists every variable-length payload column (Maps, JSON strings,
  Array(String), nested Events.* / Links.* / Messages.*). Old parts
  compute lazily on read; merges drift the value to disk over normal
  operations.

* `SETTINGS alter_sync = 1, mutations_sync = 0` on every ALTER —
  avoids the "one slow replica hangs the migration forever" failure
  that bit us on the previous attempt.

table repositories. MATERIALIZED columns are non-insertable; CH rejects
INSERTs that include the field. Removed:

* fix(retention): escape projectId in tenant-filter needle (CodeQL)

The system.mutations tenant filter built the WHERE-clause needle via raw
JS interpolation `WHERE TenantId = '${projectId}'`. ClickHouse renders
ALTER TABLE commands with escaped single-quotes and backslashes in the
stored `system.mutations.command` text, so an id containing either
character would never match — the concurrent-mutation guard would
silently return empty and let a second ALTER through.

Mirror CH's string-literal escape (`\` → `\\`, `'` → `\'`) when building
the needle. Resolves the CodeQL "incomplete string escaping" finding too.

* feat(retention): persist orphan-sweep cursor and add scheduled tick

1. Cursor persistence: the in-process cursor reset between sweep runs,

* refactor(retention): replace orphan-sweep tick with per-tenant event chain

The 6-hour BullMQ tick I added to catch inactive tenants was the wrong
shape — it iterated every project on a fixed cadence, doing work for
tenants that never needed it and adding global scheduled infrastructure
the codebase already explicitly avoids.

Replaced with a self-perpetuating per-tenant BullMQ chain:
- Stable jobId `orphan-sweep-chain:${tenantId}` gives natural dedup:
  bursty ingest only ever holds one job per tenant in the queue.
- Ingestion reactor seeds the chain (first trace event after a tenant
  becomes active) and then steps out — no more direct sweep calls.
- Worker sweeps, then re-enqueues itself with delay=24h via the
  `completed` listener — must be the listener, NOT the worker function:
  re-enqueueing inside `handle` would race against the still-active
  jobId and BullMQ would dedup the add into a no-op, stalling the chain.
- Archived/hard-deleted projects break the chain (return stopChain: true);
  the listener skips the re-enqueue and the loop ends for that tenant.
- Transient sweep failures DON'T break the chain — the worker swallows
  the sweep error and returns stopChain: false so the next 24h step
  retries. One flaky run can't silence a tenant's cleanup forever.

- dataRetentionOrphanSweepQueue.ts, dataRetentionOrphanSweepWorker.ts

  truth: "Rewriting existing rows to N days." With multi-category
  saves where the resolved values differ, the toast lists each.

* fix(retention): block manual unpin of source=share pins while share is live

`createShare` auto-pins with `source=share` to protect a shared trace
from retention TTL. The UI treated every pin as user-removable, and
`pinnedTrace.unpin` deleted unconditionally — so a user could unpin a
shared trace, retention TTL would delete it on the next merge, and the
public link would silently return expired data.

Defense in depth:

1. `PinnedTraceService.unpin` now refuses to delete a source=share pin
   while the share is still active. Throws `PinnedToActiveShareError`,
   which the tRPC router translates to CONFLICT. The user has to disable
   sharing first; that path runs `autoUnpin` which clears the pin
   cleanly (and preserves any manual pin via the existing branch).

2. The service takes a `hasActiveShareForTrace` predicate so it can ask
   the question without depending on ShareService (which already
   depends on the pinning service for auto(un)pin — direct dep would
   close the cycle). The predicate is wired in `presets.ts` against
   the shared `PrismaShareRepository` instance.

3. `PinButton` and the traces-v2 `TraceOverflowMenu` read the pin's
   `source` and disable the unpin action when `source=share`, with a
   tooltip explaining why. Mirrors the server-side guard so users get
   immediate feedback instead of a surprise CONFLICT toast.

Tests: new pinning-service cases cover share-active rejection and
share-removed success; existing cases re-verified.

* fix(retention): orphan-sweep chain stalled after one step (BullMQ jobId dedup)

The chain queue used `removeOnComplete: { age: 24h }` so completed jobs
stayed resident in Redis for the same window as the chain delay. The
intent was "keep the jobId warm so ingest re-seeds dedup," but BullMQ
treats jobId uniqueness across ALL states — including `completed` — so
the `worker.on("completed")` listener's `seedOrphanSweepChain` call
deduped into a no-op against the still-resident completed job. Chain
died after one step.

Fix:
- `removeOnComplete: true` / `removeOnFail: true` so the terminal-state
  job is removed atomically with completion. The listener's re-enqueue
  then registers cleanly. The 24h dedup property bursty ingest needs is
  still upheld by the DELAYED job holding the jobId between steps.
- Extracted the completed-listener body into `handleChainStepCompleted`
  so the chain's self-perpetuating link is unit-testable without
  standing up a real BullMQ Worker.
- Dropped the `worker.on("failed")` re-enqueue path. It silently
  papered over genuine signal (a job hits permanent failure only after
  exhausting 3 retries — that's something we want to see, not retry
  forever). Permanent failures now log + posthog capture; the chain
  stalls for that tenant until the next ingest re-seeds it — same
  cold-start tolerance we already accepted for tenants that never
  ingest again.
- Tests cover: re-enqueue on stopChain=false, no re-enqueue on
  stopChain=true, defensive undefined-outcome handling, no-op on
  missing tenantId, and seed-failure being swallowed so the BullMQ
  event loop is unaffected.

* docs(retention): drop read-time lazy cleanup scenario from orphan-sweep spec

The chain is the sole orphan-cleanup mechanism — read-time lazy cleanup
was never wired into the annotation list, public share, trigger history
or queue read paths, and we chose not to add it (would touch every
consumer for what becomes a redundant safety net on top of a predictable
24h cadence).

Replace the stale "Read-time lazy cleanup is still the read path's
safety net" scenario with a comment noting the design choice and the
accepted trade-off (briefly visible stale rows between chain steps).
If read-time cleanup ever returns it gets its own feature file.

* refactor(retention): use INDEFINITE_RETENTION_DAYS in orphan-sweep reactor

Replace hardcoded `0` with the named constant from the retention schema.
Makes the intent explicit: skip seeding the orphan-sweep chain only when
retention is the platform-admin INDEFINITE sentinel, not because of any
other 0-valued condition.

* fix(retention): block manual unpin whenever share is live, not just for source=share

The earlier guard only fired when `pin.source === share`. A user who shared
a trace AND then explicitly pinned it (which upserts source from share to
manual) could then unpin: the source check skipped, the row deleted, and
the next CH merge deleted the still-shared trace. The public share link
then silently returns expired data.

Move the guard's predicate from "is this a source=share pin?" to "is
there an active share for this trace?". Promotion paths now stay safe
regardless of source. After unshare, `autoUnpin` already preserves rows
where source=manual, so the user's manual annotation survives cleanly.

Adds a regression test covering the share→manual promotion flow.

* docs(adr): add ADR-022 (retention) + ADR-023 (orphan sweep) + ADR-024 (cold path)

ADR-022 documents the end-to-end retention design: row-level
`_retention_days UInt16` stamped at ingest from a cached PROJECT > TEAM >
ORG > 49-day cascade, ClickHouse-native TTL doing the deletion, idempotent
reconciler on every deploy, server-resolved retroactive endpoint, the
share-aware pinning guard, and the four authorization gates. Calls out
the audit-log wiring (existing tRPC middleware covers every mutation).

ADR-023 covers the orphan-sweep cleanup half: a reactor seeds a
per-tenant self-perpetuating BullMQ chain on first ingest; each step
re-enqueues itself with a 24h delay via the worker's `completed`
listener (no cron, no tick). Documents the load-bearing details
(`removeOnComplete: true`, re-enqueue placement, why `failed` doesn't
re-arm, cursor persistence) and the rejected alternatives.

ADR-024 covers cold-path tiered storage: two independent TTL clauses
(retention DELETE always reconciled, cold MOVE operator opt-in), the
`local_primary` policy with hot SSD + cold S3 volumes, why both ADD
COLUMN and MODIFY TTL are metadata-only on populated clusters (no
avalanche on a 100 TB deploy), the steady-state lifecycle, and how
retroactive shrink crosses the hot/cold boundary.

* docs(retention): correct stale "pins guard against TTL" comments

Pins are UI annotations only — they do not exempt ClickHouse rows from
the retention TTL. The router rejects manual unpin while a share is live
because the share owns its share-created annotation lifecycle, not
because the pin protects data from deletion. Fixes the comment in
TraceOverflowMenu plus the matching wording in schema.prisma, the SQL
migration, and pinnedTrace.service.ts.

* fix(retention): drop ON CLUSTER on Replicated DB; make TTL reconcile idempotent

The TTL reconciler appended `ON CLUSTER <name>` to every ALTER ... MODIFY TTL.
When a cluster is configured the database always uses the Replicated engine
(enforced in goose.ts), which auto-replicates DDL via Keeper. ClickHouse rejects
ON CLUSTER on a table inside a Replicated DB with "It's not initial query.
ON CLUSTER is not allowed for Replicated database (INCORRECT_QUERY)", crashing
clickhouseMigrate on every run against a cluster. Verified against a Replicated
cluster on CH 25.10: removing ON CLUSTER still replicates the ALTER to all nodes.
The CREATE DATABASE ... ON CLUSTER bootstrap is unaffected — that cluster-level
op is allowed; only DDL on tables inside the Replicated DB is not.

Also fix hasRetentionTTL(): it matched the literal "DELETE" keyword, but
ClickHouse normalizes a bare-DateTime TTL to an implicit DELETE and strips the
keyword from engine_full. The permanent false-negative made the reconciler
re-issue ALTER MODIFY TTL for every managed table on every run. Keying on the
`_retention_days` marker makes reconciliation idempotent (verified: re-run goes
from updated 11 -> updated 0, skipped 12).

Add regression tests: no ON CLUSTER when a cluster is configured, and idempotent
skip when retention TTL exists without the DELETE keyword.

* fix(retention): allowlist projectId_traceId compound key

PinnedTrace uses (projectId, traceId) as its compound unique key, so the
repository's upsert/findUnique queries hit a where clause shaped
`{ projectId_traceId: { projectId, traceId } }`. The multitenancy guard
allowlists `projectId_slug`/`projectId_date`/`projectId_modelProviderId_slot`
but not `projectId_traceId`, so every pin attempt and every isPinned
read failed with "requires a 'projectId' or 'projectId.in' in the where
clause". Unit tests didn't catch this because they mock the repository,
keeping the middleware out of the loop.

Add `projectId_traceId` to the allowlist and lock it in with regression
tests on findUnique + upsert.

feat(simulations): cap per-message Content/Rest size in projection (defensive seatbelt) (#4494)

* feat(simulations): cap per-message Content/Rest size in projection (defensive seatbelt)

Adds a 64 KiB per-message cap on Messages.Content and Messages.Rest in
the simulationRunState fold projection (both MessageSnapshot and
TextMessageEnd handlers). Oversized values are replaced with a clearly-
marked truncation placeholder and a structured warn log is emitted with
{scenarioRunId, messageId, messageRole, field, byteLength}.

Motivation:

A scenario voice run recently leaked 90+ MB of base64 audio inline in
ClickHouse Messages.Content because the stored-objects pipeline failed
to externalise the SDK's audio file parts. The list-page query
(`getSuiteRunData`) then slurped the first 6 messages of every scenario
back to the browser, making the simulations page borderline unusable
for that project.

The SDK fix (langwatch/scenario PR #561) and the content-extractor fix
(sibling langwatch PR) together address the root cause for the known
shapes. This patch is the **defensive seatbelt**: any future SDK
regression — a new content-part shape we forgot to teach the extractor
about, a refactor that accidentally re-stringifies array content
upstream of the extractor, an SDK bug that injects raw bytes into a
text field — gets a hard size cap at the persistence layer instead of
turning into a multi-megabyte list response.

Threshold rationale:

64 KiB is generous enough that no normal text turn — including verbose
multi-paragraph assistant replies and long tool-call argument JSON —
is ever truncated. Messages that exceed it are almost always inline
binary media: that's exactly the case we want to fail-fast on.

The structured warn log makes regressions visible in production
(monitoring can alert on count > 0) and the surfaced "[truncated:
... likely inline media that was not externalised to stored-objects]"
marker makes affected rows discoverable retroactively.

Tests (4 new; 26 existing still pass):

- Snapshot path: oversized Content is truncated to the marker
- Snapshot path: normal-sized Content (~24 KiB long reply) passes through unchanged
- Snapshot path: oversized Rest (array-content duplication) is also capped
- TextMessageEnd path: oversized Content is truncated to the marker

* review: named-args + UTF-8-safe fast-path + scenarioRunId fallback

Addresses CodeRabbit + langwatch-agent review on PR #4494.

- capOversizedString: switch to a single destructured params object
  ({ value, maxBytes, field, ctx }) so the four call sites can't transpose
  field/maxBytes by mistake. Repo coding guideline: "Use named parameters
  via object destructuring for functions with multiple arguments".
- Fix UTF-8 fast-path. `value.length <= maxBytes` is unsafe: UTF-8 may
  emit up to 3 bytes per UTF-16 code unit, so a multi-byte string ~3×
  over the byte cap could slip past unmeasured. Replace with the safe
  inverse bound `value.length * 3 <= maxBytes` (length is the only safe
  short-circuit when each char can be up to 3 bytes); the explicit
  `Buffer.byteLength` check still runs for everything that doesn't
  trivially fit. Comment rewritten to match.
- Use `state.ScenarioRunId || event.data.scenarioRunId` in the warning
  context (both MessageSnapshot and TextMessageEnd paths). Both handlers
  explicitly support folds before the run-started event; on that path
  state.ScenarioRunId is still empty while the event itself carries the
  id. Without the fallback, an oversized first-snapshot warn would
  arrive id-less and be useless for locating the affected run.
- Test added for the UTF-8 multi-byte case (30k 4-byte emojis → ~120 KiB
  bytes); ensures the fast-path bug doesn't regress.

fix(stored-objects): externalise AI-SDK file+audio parts (scenario voice audio leak) (#4493)

* fix(stored-objects): externalise AI-SDK file+audio parts (scenario voice audio leak)

The content-extractor visitor recognised the OpenAI Realtime `input_audio`
shape and the AG-UI `audio`+source shape, but had no branch for the
canonical AI-SDK `file` part (`{type:"file", mediaType:"audio/...", data}`)
that the typescript scenario SDK's `createAudioMessage` emits. AI-SDK
`file` parts dropped through to the no-op `unknown` handler, so base64
audio bytes were never externalised to stored-objects — they flowed
straight to ClickHouse `Messages.Content` and back to the simulations
list response (a single voice scenario set returned 90+ MB on
`getSuiteRunData`).

This patch:

- Adds a `file`-shape branch in `visit-content-part.ts` (both sync and
  async dispatchers). Audio mediaTypes (`audio/*`) route to the existing
  `inputAudio` handler with a best-effort format hint and the original
  mimeType preserved. Non-audio file payloads route to the existing
  `binary` handler.
- Teaches `content-extractor.ts:inputAudio` to prefer an explicit
  `mimeType` over the format-to-mime allowlist (so `audio/pcm16` from
  AI-SDK file parts is stored with its actual mime type, not
  `application/octet-stream`).
- Normalises the rewrite output when the inbound was a file-shape part:
  audio file parts rewrite to a clean `{type:"input_audio", input_audio:{
  url, mimeType}}` (matching the canonical externalised shape), non-audio
  file parts rewrite to a clean `{type:"binary", mimeType, id, url}`.
  Without normalisation the rewrite was a chimera of `type:"file"` and
  input_audio / binary fields, which the UI MediaPart would not render
  consistently.

Defence in depth: the matching typescript-sdk patch (langwatch/scenario
PR #561) translates file+audio parts to input_audio before sending and
stops pre-stringifying array content. With both deployed, current SDK
builds hit the `input_audio` branch; older SDK builds and any future
non-scenario caller that ships raw AI-SDK file parts are caught here.

Tests added:
- AI-SDK file+audio → input_audio externalisation, clean rewrite shape.
- AI-SDK file+image → binary externalisation, clean rewrite shape.

* review: normalise mediaType case + drop unbacked @scenario annotations

Addresses CodeRabbit + langwatch-agent review on PR #4493.

- Lowercase the AI-SDK `file` part's mediaType before the `audio/` prefix
  check and before passing into `mediaTypeToAudioFormat`. MIME types are
  case-insensitive per RFC 2045 §5.1; pre-normalisation a part with
  `Audio/WAV` or `audio/WAV` fell through to the `binary` branch and was
  externalised as the wrong canonical shape. `mediaTypeToAudioFormat` is
  also defensively normalised so any future caller is safe.
- New unit test covers the mixed-case path explicitly.
- Drop `@scenario` JSDoc annotations from the two new unit cases. The
  feature-parity check requires a matching scenario under `specs/` and
  these are intentionally unit-only — removing the annotation rather than
  fabricating a spec keeps the parity gate honest.

fix(retention): anchor evaluation_runs TTL on UpdatedAt (non-null, partition-aligned) (#4511)

The TTL reconciler crashed prod app pods at startup with ClickHouse
BAD_TTL_EXPRESSION (code 450):

  TTL expression result column should have Date, Date32, DateTime or
  DateTime64 type, but has Nullable(DateTime)

evaluation_runs.ScheduledAt is Nullable(DateTime64(3)) (so is StartedAt),
and ClickHouse rejects Nullable in TTL expressions. The retention column
must be non-null AND ideally aligned with the partition key so TTL drops
whole partitions at part level instead of running row-level mutations
across still-warm parts.

evaluation_runs is partitioned on toYearWeek(UpdatedAt), and UpdatedAt is
non-null, so it is both the correct industry-standard choice and zero
schema disruption. Every other retention-managed table already anchors on
its partition key; evaluation_runs was the only mismatch.

Tests:
- Unit: lock in evaluation_runs anchor = UpdatedAt

  Nullable(DateTime) anchor, so this class of bug fails CI in future.

feat(workflows/code-editor): light/dark Monaco theme + Python stdlib intellisense + secrets autocomplete + input/output contract (#4519)

* feat(workflows/code-editor): light/dark theme + Python stdlib intellisense + secrets autocomplete

The Optimization Studio Code node already used Monaco, but the editor was hardcoded to Monokai and only had an LLM-driven completion backend (monacopilot). That left the experience flat in light mode and offered no awareness of the things user code actually has in scope at runtime.

This wires Monaco to the app's color mode and adds a Python provider layer that mirrors the sandbox surface: stdlib modules, builtins, the injected `secrets` namespace, plus a small hover/formatter/validator suite so the editor behaves like a real IDE without a server round-trip.

- Themes: drops the hardcoded Monokai. `themes.ts` defines `langwatch-dark` (Monokai) and `langwatch-light` (warm Tomorrow-ish palette) and `useColorMode` picks. Dialog surfaces use `bg`/`fg` tokens instead of `#272822`/white.
- Completion: `secrets.<Tab>` lists project secrets with `str` detail (live via tRPC); `import X` / `from X import Y` resolve to a curated stdlib catalogue (math, json, re, datetime, os, sys, collections, itertools, functools, random, string, base64, hashlib, uuid, textwrap, statistics, decimal, urllib.parse); attribute access on imported names resolves through `import X as Y` aliases; default surface adds builtins + keywords + already-imported modules + the `secrets` variable itself.
- Hover: signatures + JSDoc for builtins and `module.member`.
- Formatter (Shift+Alt+F): expands tabs to 4-space, trims trailing whitespace, collapses 3+ blank lines, normalises top/bottom blanks. Intentionally not Black — server-free hygiene.
- Validator: string-aware bracket balance, unterminated single/triple-quoted strings, mixed tabs+spaces in leading indentation. Markers refresh on every keystroke and clear on dispose.

monacopilot LLM completion is preserved — the two providers complement each other (local for stdlib/secrets, monacopilot for higher-level intent).

* fix(workflows/code-editor): wrong enum name silently broke every completion + add input/output contract

`monaco.languages.CompletionItemInsertTextRules` (plural) doesn't exist at runtime — the namespace exposes `CompletionItemInsertTextRule` (singular). Every call into my completion provider threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'InsertAsSnippet')`, Monaco swallowed it, and the suggest widget silently fell back to word-based completions. So `secrets.<Tab>` and `math.<Tab>` looked like they were never wired up.

Fix: hardcode the numeric flag (`InsertAsSnippet = 4`) and drop the namespace lookup entirely so we don't depend on which version of monaco the CDN loader resolved.

While here, add the node input/output contract the editor was missing:

- `inputs` flow CodePropertiesPanel → CodeBlockEditor → CodeEditorModal → provider. Each declared input shows as a typed variable at the top of the completion list with its declared type (`str`, `int`, …) in the detail column.
- `outputs` do the same, plus: when the cursor is inside a `return {…}` dict, the declared output names are suggested as `"key": $0` snippets, so users discover the contract without leaving the editor.
- Validator gains an output-coverage check: any declared output that never appears as a string-key literal in the source raises a Warning marker. Cheap heuristic (misses dynamic key construction), but covers the common case of "I renamed the output and forgot to update the dict."

PR description references screenshots under .github/pr-media/feat-workflow-monaco-editor/.

* fix(workflows/code-editor): use built-in VS Code themes, free the space key, light/dark preview

Three follow-ups from manual testing:

- Completion `triggerCharacters` included ` `, which popped the suggest widget on every whitespace and — depending on the browser — swallowed the space keystroke entirely. Dropped the space trigger. Period still triggers attribute completion; explicit `Ctrl+Space` still works for the default surface.
- Dropped the custom `langwatch-light` / `langwatch-dark` themes (and the legacy `Monokai.json`) in favour of Monaco's bundled `vs` / `vs-dark`. Users get the exact VS Code look they're expecting, and one fewer place to maintain.
- CodeBlockEditor preview was hardcoded to monokai dark on every theme. Now follows `useColorMode`: `#1E1E1E` + `vsDark` prism theme in dark mode, `#FFFFFF` + `vsLight` + a subtle border in light. RenderCode gains an optional `theme` prop (defaults to monokai, so the dozen existing call sites are unaffected).
- EditAutomationFilterDrawer was the only other consumer of `Monokai.json` — flipped it to `vs-dark`/`vs` the same way so the deletion is safe.

Screenshot of the editor refreshed to the new theme; added a preview-dark capture so the PR shows both surfaces.

* fix(workflows/code-editor): set acceptSuggestionOnCommitCharacter=false so space inserts a space

Dropping space from `triggerCharacters` wasn't enough — Monaco defaults
`acceptSuggestionOnCommitCharacter` to true, so whenever the suggest widget
is open (which is most of the time once the default surface is registered),
typing a non-word punctuation character (including space) commits the
highlighted suggestion and the keystroke is silently swallowed.

Set the option to false on the workflow editor: only Tab / Enter accept a
suggestion now. Space, comma, parens etc. type literally as expected.

* fix(workflows/code-editor): contain key events at the editor root so React Flow's pan-on-space stops eating keystrokes

@xyflow/react registers a global keydown listener that calls preventDefault on `Space` — Space is its pan-activation key. The optimization studio mounts the React Flow canvas behind the editor dialog, so every Space keystroke bubbled out of the editor and got intercepted before the browser could turn it into a `beforeinput`. Result: typing space in the Code node editor silently dropped the keystroke. (Confirmed by patching `KeyboardEvent.prototype.preventDefault` and watching the stack trace point at `@xyflow/react.js downHandler`.)

Fix: attach keydown/keypress/keyup listeners on the editor's root DOM node that call `e.stopPropagation()`. Monaco's own input handling lives deeper (on `.native-edit-context`), so it still gets every key — but nothing escapes to the canvas. React Flow keeps its space-pan behaviour for normal canvas use.

The modal's window-level Cmd/Ctrl+S listener is now unreachable while typing inside the editor, so wire Save through `editor.onKeyDown` too (same `module.fn` shadow pattern that Escape already uses).

Listeners are cleaned up via `editor.onDidDispose`.

* fix(workflows/code-editor): narrow key shield to Space + flag missing Code scaffold

- Cmd+A / Cmd+Z and other shortcuts that Monaco's standalone keybinding service registers above the editor root were being swallowed by the previous blanket `stopPropagation` on every keydown. React Flow only intercepts `Space` (its `panActivationKeyCode`), so narrow the shield to just bare `Space` (no Meta/Ctrl/Alt) and let everything else propagate normally.
- Add Error-level validator markers when the user deletes the required `class Code:` declaration or its `def __call__(self, input: str):` method — the workflow runtime calls `Code().__call__(input)`, so accidental deletion should fail in-editor with a clear message instead of at execution time.

* feat(workflows/code-editor): quick-fix (lightbulb) for missing Code scaffold

The previous commit surfaced an Error marker when the user deleted `class Code:` or its `def __call__`, but the only way to recover was retyping the boilerplate by hand. Wire a CodeActionProvider so Monaco's lightbulb offers a one-click fix:

- "Insert `class Code` scaffold" — appends the full template (`class Code` + `__call__` + a default `return {"output": …}`) at end of buffer.
- "Insert `__call__` method" — inserts just the method on the line after the existing `class Code:` declaration.

Markers now carry stable `code` tags (`langwatch.missing-class-code`, `langwatch.missing-call-method`) so the action provider matches by code rather than by parsing the message. Both actions are marked `isPreferred: true` so Cmd+. picks them automatically. The lightbulb option is set to `"on"` in the editor so the indicator surfaces in the gutter whenever a fix is available.

* feat(workflows/code-editor): hover/signature-help/sticky-scroll/persist-state/DnD-secrets and more quick-fixes

Round of A+ polish on top of the existing Monaco wiring:

- Hover: inputs, outputs and `secrets.NAME` now resolve to typed hover cards (with a callout when a secret name isn't actually configured). `secrets` itself shows the namespace + count.
- Signature help: parameter-hint popup pops on `(` for any callee we know (builtins + every stdlib member). Re-triggers on `,` so multi-arg calls stay informative. Active-parameter index follows the comma count.
- Quick fixes (in addition to the scaffold fix): "Add `\"name\"` to return dict" for the output-coverage warning, and "Normalize indentation to spaces" for the mixed-tabs warning. Markers now carry stable `code` tags (`langwatch.missing-output-key:NAME`, `langwatch.mixed-indent`) so the action provider matches by code.
- Editor options: bracket-pair colorization on, indent + bracket-pair guides on, sticky scroll on (pins `class Code` / `def __call__` while scrolling deep), ruler at column 100 (PEP-8 friendly), smooth scrolling + smooth cursor for parity with VS Code, parameter hints enabled, tabSize: 4 / insertSpaces: true to match the stdlib it targets.
- Cmd/Ctrl+Enter (Notebook muscle memory) and Cmd/Ctrl+S both Save & Close from inside the editor.
- View state persistence: cursor, scroll and folding state are serialised to `localStorage` keyed by node id (`langwatch.monaco.viewstate:code-node:<id>`) on dispose, and restored on the next mount. Reopening the modal drops the user back where they were.
- Drag-and-drop secrets: chips in `SecretsIndicator` are now draggable; dropping one into Monaco inserts `secrets.NAME` at the drop point (translated via `getTargetAtClientPoint`). A `text/plain` payload is also set so dragging into a plain textarea still works.

* feat(workflows/code-editor): type-aware output value placeholders + literal-type-mismatch lint

When the user inserts a declared output key (via completion or the missing-key quick-fix), we now seed the value with a Python literal that matches the declared type instead of always typing `None`:

| Declared type        | Placeholder |
|----------------------|-------------|
| `str`, `image`       | `""`        |
| `float`              | `0.0`       |
| `int`                | `0`         |
| `bool`               | `False`     |
| `list`               | `[]`        |
| `dict`, `json_schema`| `{}`        |
| anything else        | `None`      |

The completion's detail column shows `type  →  literal` so the contract is visible without expanding the suggestion details. The quick-fix title gains the type too (`Add "result" (str) to return dict`).

Add a cheap literal-type-mismatch validator: walk the LAST `return {…}` on the source, parse it into entries (string-aware so commas inside literals don't split), and warn when an obvious literal kind doesn't match what's declared — e.g. `"output": 5` when `output` is declared `str`, or `"flag": "yes"` when `flag` is declared `bool`. Variable references, function calls and anything we can't classify with high signal fall through unchecked to avoid noise. Marker code is `langwatch.output-type-mismatch:<name>`, so future quick-fixes can target it.

* fix(workflows/code-editor): address review comments (any-types, unused import, dotted imports, empty-buffer revalidate)

Address feedback from the PR review pass:

- **Drop `any` annotations on Monaco callbacks** (Copilot). `(code: any)` on `onChange` becomes the natural inference (`string | undefined`) with a `?? ""` so an emptied buffer still propagates state. `editor: any` on `onMount` is replaced with the project-local `MonacoEditorInstance` alias, which now resolves to `monaco-editor`'s real `editor.IStandaloneCodeEditor` instead of the hand-rolled minimal shape. `editor.onKeyDown((e: any) => …)` drops the annotation entirely so the Monaco-provided `IKeyboardEvent` type flows through.
- **Remove unused `PYTHON_STDLIB_MODULES` import** (Copilot + github-code-quality).
- **`scanImports`: preserve dotted module names** (CodeRabbit, ⚠️ major). `import urllib.parse` was previously stored as `parse`, so `urllib.parse.foo` never resolved. Now `import X(.Y)*` binds the full dotted name (or the alias when one is provided), and `from X import …` binds nothing unless aliased.
- **`revalidate()` no longer skips empty buffers** (Copilot). The old applyEdits-no-op trick only fired change events on non-empty buffers, so a fresh node with declared outputs but no code yet got no markers. Expose `revalidate()` directly from the validator so the orchestrator can re-run synchronously without poking the model.

Not addressed in this commit (would expand scope of the PR):

- Splitting `registerPythonProviders.ts` into per-provider modules — file is large but cohesive and the orchestrator is a thin wrapper already; will follow up in a dedicated refactor PR once the feature stabilises.
- Converting all internal helpers to named parameter objects — would touch ~15 call sites and isn't behaviour-affecting; tracking separately.

* fix(workflows/code-editor): hover provider was duplicating the typed prefix

When the cursor sat mid-identifier, the hover provider's `ATTR_ACCESS` regex was being applied to `lineBefore + word.word` — but `lineBefore` already contained the partial prefix up to the cursor, so the result for hovering on `secrets.YEA_BOI` was `secrets.YEA_YEA_BOI` and the hover card showed the wrong name (and the "no secret named …" fallback path always fired).

Fixed by extending the slice to the *end* of the hovered word instead of concatenating, so the regex sees the full attribute expression exactly once. Verified visually in Playwright: hovering on `secrets.YEA_BOI` now shows `secrets.YEA_BOI: str` with the management hint.

Also adds the screenshots captured during the end-to-end pass under `.github/pr-media/feat-workflow-monaco-editor/`:
- 07 — output key completion with type-aware default value
- 08 — dotted-import (`urllib.parse.…`) completion
- 09 — signature help on `math.log(`
- 10 — Quick Fix lightbulb for missing `class Code` scaffold
- 11 — hover on `secrets.YEA_BOI`

* fix(workflows/code-editor): satisfy CI typecheck

- Add monaco-editor as a direct devDependency so `import type` resolves
  in CI (was only present as a peer of @monaco-editor/react)
- Type onChange `value` parameter explicitly as `string | undefined`
- Introduce ValidatorHandle return type so `revalidate()` is part of

- Guard paramListMatch[1] possibly-undefined in signature help

* refactor(workflows/code-editor): replace `any` cast on lightbulb option

Use the proper `editor.ShowLightbulbIconMode` enum type now that
monaco-editor is a direct devDependency. Same runtime value, no `any`.

* refactor(workflows/code-editor): split python providers into per-concern modules

The single 1255-line registerPythonProviders.ts mixed completion, hover,
signature-help, formatter, validator and code-actions in one file — any
tweak risked touching multiple editor behaviours.

Split into per-provider modules under `monaco/python/`:
  shared.ts        — types, regexes, marker codes, helpers (scanImports,

* feat(workflows/code-editor): VS Code-style chrome — file tab + theme-aware status bar + edge-to-edge editor + prominent Save button

The modal used to be a generic Dialog with a `Edit Code` title and a single

fix(nlpgo): resolve `{{ secrets.NAME }}` in HTTP-block url/headers/auth (#4509)

* fix(nlpgo): resolve {{ secrets.NAME }} in HTTP-block url/headers/auth

HTTP blocks copied the bearer token, header values, and URL verbatim
from the DSL, so a `{{ secrets.UPSTREAM_TOKEN }}` reference was sent to
the upstream as a literal string instead of the project secret. Code
blocks already resolved secrets (#4465); HTTP blocks were the remaining
gap — the http-block.feature scenario for it was tagged @unimplemented.

Resolve `{{ secrets.NAME }}` against workflow.secrets (the decrypted map
addEnvs.ts already puts on the DSL — same source #4465 used) at
request-build time, so rotated values are honored. Resolution is applied
to the URL, header values, and auth credential fields only — NOT the body
template, which is rendered into logged execution events and would leak
the plaintext. Unknown names are left verbatim rather than blanked, so a
misconfigured secret is visible instead of silently empty.

Tests: unit coverage for the resolver + an e2e integration test proving
the upstream observes the resolved token while the secret never appears
in the sync response. Un-tagged the now-implemented spec scenario.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(nlpgo): goimports grouping + restore @unimplemented on http-block secret scenario

CI fixes for #4509:
- goimports: split local langwatch imports into their own group in the two
  new test files (matches repo golangci local-prefixes convention).
- feature-parity: restore @unimplemented on the secret scenario. The TS
  parity checker only scans TS test roots and cannot bind Go-side tests
  (documented in the feature file header), so removing the tag made the
  checker report the scenario as unbound. Go coverage is noted in a comment.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(nlpgo): honor Studio's auth_type/auth_token HTTP-block auth params

The Go engine's paramAuth only read a single structured `auth` object,
but the Studio UI and the experiments-v3 builder emit auth as discrete
`auth_type` + `auth_token`/`auth_header`/`auth_value`/`auth_username`/
`auth_password` params (HttpPropertiesPanel.tsx, useAgentPickerFlow.ts,
experiments-v3/workflowBuilder.ts). Nothing ever produced an `auth`
param, so HTTP-block auth was silently dropped on every real UI path —
the engine sent no Authorization header (and thus never resolved the
`{{ secrets.X }}` bearer/api-key/basic credential either).

paramAuth now falls back to the discrete-param shape; resolveAuthSecrets
(from this PR) then substitutes the secret as before. Proven end-to-end:
a Studio HTTP block with bearer `{{ secrets.TOKEN }}` now delivers the
resolved token to the upstream (was: no Authorization header).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(nlpgo): redact resolved secret values from HTTP error messages (P1)

runHTTP returned err.Error() verbatim as the node error message, and Go
transport/build errors embed the full request URL — so a secret
substituted into the URL/query (e.g. `?token={{ secrets.X }}`) could be
reflected into execution events, traces, and logs on request failure.

Scrub resolved secret values from both HTTP error paths (transport +
upstream) via redactSecrets() before constructing the NodeError.
Addresses rogeriochaves's P1 review on #4509.
