fix(ops): populate P50/P99 latency tiles from group-queue durations (#4492)

* fix(ops): populate P50/P99 latency tiles from group-queue durations

The ops dashboard's P50/P99 tiles read `<queue>:completed` ZSET entries
and `<queue>:<jobId>` hash fields (`processedOn`/`finishedOn`) — BullMQ
key conventions that disappeared when the platform migrated to the
in-house GroupQueue. The tiles have been stuck at 0ms / peak 0ms ever
since, because the collector's latency list is always empty.

GroupQueue does not store per-job hashes, so reviving the legacy keys
isn't an option. Instead, after each successful job duration is observed
into the Prometheus histogram, also push the rounded duration into a
capped Redis list `<queue>:gq:stats:latencies-ms` (cap 200, fire-and-
forget so an instrumentation hiccup never bubbles into the worker
pipeline). The collector now LRANGE's this list per queue every 2s and
computes P50/P99 from the union — same percentile math, working source.

Includes integration tests that drive a real GroupQueueProcessor +
Redis end-to-end: list is populated per completion, capped at 200, and
the collector's LRANGE read path produces non-zero percentiles.

* test(ops): scope latency-tile teardown and drive via real collector

Both findings from CodeRabbit on PR #4492:

* afterEach was calling redis.flushall(), which would clobber state from
  other integration suites sharing the same Redis. Switch to SCAN+UNLINK
  over each test queue's namespace (queue names already carry a unique
  hash-tag prefix), plus targeted UNLINK of the two collector-owned keys
  this suite touches.

* The percentile assertion was inlining LRANGE + sort/index math, so a
  future drift in OpsMetricsCollector (key name, filtering, percentile
  formula) would not break the test. Drive the real collector instead:
  stub queueRepo to return the suite's queue name, call discoverQueues()
  and collect() directly, then assert on getDashboardData().

Exposes OpsMetricsCollector as a named class export and lifts collect()
+ discoverQueues() to public so the test seam is honest.

* test(ops): stop unlinking global collector keys in latency-tile teardown

CodeRabbit follow-up on PR #4492: the previous teardown unlinked
ops:known-pipelines and ops:metrics:state, which are process-global
collector caches not namespaced to this suite. A parallel integration
run could erase another suite's collector state.

Drop those unlinks. Both keys are best-effort caches; the only stale
state that survives across runs is peakLatencyP*, and the test asserts
peak >= current — a stale-larger peak still satisfies that, so no
false-pass risk.
chore(main): release skills 0.6.0 (#4508)

fix(ci/skills-publish): skip devDep postinstalls so node-pty doesn't break the workflow (#4546)

The skills-publish workflow has been failing on every push to main since
mid-May because `skills/` pulls `node-pty@^1.0.0` in devDependencies for
the dogfood tests. node-pty@1.1.0 has no prebuilt binary for linux-x64
in this version range, so its postinstall falls back to a node-gyp
rebuild — and `node-gyp` is not on the default `ubuntu-latest` runner,
so install dies with `sh: 1: node-gyp: not found` before sync ever runs.

The publish job only needs to execute `pnpm sync` (a TS transformer over
the SKILL MDX files) and doesn't touch any native binaries, so passing
`--ignore-scripts` to the install lets it skip every postinstall —
including node-pty's rebuild — without changing what gets installed.

Effect: SKILL changes (recent: voice section "how connects to my agent"
clarification, no-runner / no-JSON-DSL nudges, etc.) again propagate
from `langwatch/langwatch` to `langwatch/skills` and tag a new release
on each version bump.

fix(governance): prod blackhole on OTLP ingestion + personal VK without default routing policy (#4533)

* fix(governance): mint personal VK with null routingPolicyId when no default policy exists

Customers with ModelProviders configured at ORG scope but no
isDefault RoutingPolicy saw "No personal virtual key on this
account" on `langwatch login --device`. The mint path used to throw
NoDefaultRoutingPolicyError + the device-flow approval silently
proceeded without minting a VK, so the wrapper bailed at first
gateway call with the wrong error (no providers vs no policy).

The gateway scopeResolver already supported routingPolicyId=null
(falls back to fallbackPriorityGlobal ASC then createdAt ASC on
every scope-cascade-eligible ModelProvider). Refusing to mint when
the runtime would have routed correctly was a mint-time-only
constraint — drop it.

PersonalVirtualKeyService.issue now:
  - When the caller relied on default-resolution AND no default
    policy exists (or the default points at an empty provider
    list), check the personal-team scope cascade for at least
    one eligible ModelProvider. If yes, mint with null policy.
    If no, throw NoEligibleProvidersError (clear "add a provider"
    message → 409).
  - When the caller pinned an explicit policy that turns out to
    be empty, the existing G34 RoutingPolicyHasNoProvidersError
    contract still holds (422).

Removed NoDefaultRoutingPolicyError + the stale "configure
routing policy" CTA on the personal-portal ModelProvider tile —
the new error is self-actionable. Updated specs across personal-keys,
admin-routing-policies, model-provider-tile, tool-catalog-vk-bridge,
and the wrapper-e2e claude scenario.

* fix(otel): classify ik-lw- ingestion keys + actionable 401 on stale bindings

OTLP receiver's classifyTokenType only knew pat-lw-/sk-lw-, so stale
UserIngestionBinding tokens (ik-lw-) showed up as tokenType=unknown
in the failed-auth log. On-call had no way to tell a misconfigured SDK
bearer from a binding that the user later rotated.

The 401 body now also names the surface that issues the token, so the
failure surfaces actionably in the exporter's stderr.

Prod ground truth: rogerio's shell exported an ik-lw- token from a
prior mint that was later replaced (reinstall revives the same row
with a fresh hash). The new row's lastSeenAt was NULL — no spans
ever landed for the personal project.

* fix(otel): stop silently dropping standalone logs and metrics

OTLP LogRecord.trace_id / LogRecord.span_id and metric exemplar
trace context are optional per opentelemetry-proto. Exporters that
emit telemetry outside an active span (Claude Code's
OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER / OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER with no traces exporter
set is the canonical caller) leave them unset.

The receiver previously dropped every such record:
- LogRequestCollectionService gated recordLog on traceId AND spanId
  being non-empty.
- MetricRequestCollectionService.extractSimpleDataPoint returned null
  unless an exemplar with trace context existed, so standalone gauges
  and sums never reached recordMetric.

Result: /api/otel/v1/logs and /v1/metrics returned 200 OK while
nothing landed in ClickHouse. No log line, no metric, no signal —
the receiver counted the drop and moved on.

Both surfaces now store empty TraceId/SpanId when the caller didn't
provide them. Downstream span-correlation queries simply find no
match, which is the correct semantics for context-less telemetry.

Confirmed in prod: a curl against /api/otel/v1/logs with a fresh
ik-lw- bearer + a LogRecord WITHOUT trace context returned 200 and
left zero rows in stored_log_records; the same probe with trace
context landed cleanly.

* fix: address CR round 1 on #4533 + persist exemplar-less histograms

CR thread 1 (service): explicit `routingPolicyId: null` bypassed the
no-provider guard because the gate was keyed on `=== undefined` only.
Collapse "no policy id provided" and "explicit no-policy requested"
into a single `noPolicyRequested` branch so the eligibility check runs
for both shapes; the empty-org case (`routingPolicyId: null` + zero
providers) now throws NoEligibleProvidersError instead of minting a
broken VK.

CR thread 2 (banner copy): "Without a default, personal keys still
mint" overpromised — orgs with zero reachable providers still 409.
Banner now says mint succeeds when at least one provider is reachable
and notes the 409 path.

CR thread 3 (delete-policy warning): the dialog claimed existing VKs
"follow the same fallback on the next request" — actually
routingPolicyId is persisted, so existing VKs keep the deleted policy
id and fail closed until re-bound. Reworded to match the contract.

CR thread 4 (claude.feature scenario): rewrote to assert the swallow
path (login succeeds without `default_personal_vk`, wrapper preflight
surfaces the actionable message) instead of the pre-fix 409.

CR thread 5 (metric histogram path): standalone histograms exported
without exemplars were still dropped. Mirror the gauge/sum graceful
fallback: emit one trace-less row per exemplar-less histogram dp
with the dp's sum (or count) as the scalar value.

Also: sergey's new log/metric unit tests passed `version: null` for an
InstrumentationScope where the IExportLogsServiceRequest type wants
`string | undefined`. Three call sites switched to `undefined`.
Typecheck clean, 161/161 unit tests pass locally.

* fix(traceSummary): skip fold for log/metric events with no trace context

After the receiver-side silent-drop fix (c56eced2d), context-less OTLP
logs and metric data points now reach the event-sourcing pipeline with
empty traceId/spanId. The map projection writes them to
stored_log_records / stored_metric_records correctly, but the
traceSummary fold aggregates by aggregateId=traceId — so every empty-
id event in a tenant folds into a single "" aggregate, producing one
nameless ghost trace_summary entry per tenant that grows unboundedly.

Skip the fold entirely for empty trace/span ids in both
handleTraceLogRecordReceived and handleTraceMetricRecordReceived. The
log/metric rows still land in CH (queryable directly), and the trace
listing stays clean.

Follow-up tracked separately: synthesize a stable traceId from
resource attributes (service.name + service.instance.id) so
standalone logs/metrics surface as named per-service traces.

* fix(claude-code-snippet): recommend OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp + typecheck fix

The three claude_code env-var snippets shown to admins (install drawer +
two governance dashboard pages) recommended only LOGS_EXPORTER and
METRICS_EXPORTER. Without TRACES_EXPORTER, claude-code never emits spans
and every standalone log/metric arrives without trace context, falling
into the fold-skip introduced in c0c2e96f5. Logs/metrics still land in
stored_log_records/stored_metric_records but never surface on /messages.

Add OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp to all three snippets. Claude-code with
this var emits one span per user message, the OpenInference extractor
already maps the carried session.id resource attribute to
gen_ai.conversation.id (unconditional in
openinference.ts handle), and the UI thread-groups messages of the same
session as one conversation. Each message naturally becomes its own
trace.

Also fix a typecheck regression introduced in c0c2e96f5: the metric
event in traceSummaryEmptyIdsSkip.unit.test.ts mistakenly included
piiRedactionLevel, which is only on LogRecordReceivedEvent.data, not
MetricRecordReceivedEvent.data. Strict-object-literal rejected it.

* test(install-drawer): regression-guard claude_code env block contents

Asserts buildEnvSnippet emits CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 + all four
OTEL_*_EXPORTER lines (traces was missing pre-71346729a) + the http/json
protocol + endpoint/bearer interpolation; and that non-claude slugs stay
endpoint+bearer only. Locks the snippet shape so future edits to the
builder can't silently regress it.

Also exports buildEnvSnippet (was private) so the test can reach it
without re-rendering the React drawer.

feat(traces-v2): drive-through audit pass — sidebar, drawer, table, toolbar (#4520)

* chore(traces-v2): remove unused flame and span list view subtrees

These two view modes were never wired into the drawer pane router after
the v2 layout settled on Waterfall + summary/span accordions. Keeping
the dead surface around made every "search for span/flame in drawer"
trip return ~3700 lines of irrelevant code.

Confirmed no remaining imports outside the deleted trees.

* fix(layout): banner radius matches page chrome, restore content flow

Two distinct issues that surfaced together because they both lived in
the dashboard shell:

1. **Banners pushed content off-screen.** `DashboardLayout` rendered
   banners + page body inside a flex column without sizing the body,
   so a page using `height="full"` resolved against the scrollable
   container that already included the banner stack. Showing a banner
   pushed the bottom of the page off the viewport. Wrap the page body
   in a `flex: 1; minHeight: 0; display: flex; flexDirection: column`
   box so banners take their natural height above and the body gets
   `containerHeight - bannerStack`.

2. **Banner corners.** Audit feedback was that the banners' four
   independent rounded corners looked ad-hoc. Drop every corner except
   top-left, which now matches the inner page chrome's
   `borderTopLeftRadius="xl"`. The banner curve continues from the
   chrome's curve; the other three edges run flush.

Also gives `AdminViewingAsBanner` a dismiss-to-mini state with a 24h
per-workspace TTL, so admins can collapse the loud banner during long
debugging sessions without losing the persistent governance signal.

* feat(traces-v2): facet manager popover + per-key visibility store

Adds a dedicated picker — opened from a Settings2 icon in the sidebar
header — for the "which facets are visible" question that previously
had no overview surface. The audit feedback was "I can't tell what I'm
missing": the per-section hover-X to hide and the per-group "+ Add
facet" affordances handled ad-hoc edits but never showed you the full
list of facets the backend knew about.

What's in the popover:
- One checkbox per backend-known facet key, grouped by the FACET_GROUPS
  taxonomy (trace · subjects · span · evaluators · metrics · prompts).
- A Lucide icon per group + per key so each row reads at a glance —
  `model → Cpu`, `cost → DollarSign`, `evaluatorScore → BarChart3`,
  etc. Unknown groups/keys fall back to a generic Filter glyph.
- A `Filter facets…` search input that matches against either the
  human label or the raw key (so power users can grep `selectedPrompt`
  directly).
- Footer with `Reset to defaults` (drops every per-key override and
  returns the sidebar to the density default) and `Done`.

Positioning:
- The popover anchors `bottom-start` so the panel extends INTO the
  trace list area rather than back over the main app menu — at ~280px
  width on a ~260px sidebar, `bottom-end` rendered leftward into the
  navigation chrome.
- Tooltip wraps a host Box that *contains* Popover.Root, not
  Popover.Trigger directly, because both `Tooltip` and `Popover.Trigger`
  use `asChild` ref forwarding and fight over the slot when stacked,
  which left the panel with no measurable anchor (it landed at the
  viewport top-left). Same pattern as CreateLensButton.

State:
- New `facetVisibilityStore` (Zustand, persisted) — per-key
  `explicitlyShown` / `explicitlyHidden` overrides that the sidebar
  reads via `isVisible(key)`. `onResetAll` clears the override map.
- `useFilterSidebarData` exposes the full key list + group resolver to
  the popover via `orderedKeysAll` and `sectionByKey`.

Body uses a hard-clamped pixel height (`BODY_MAX_HEIGHT_PX = 360`) on
the inner scroll Box rather than a `vh`-relative `maxHeight` on
Popover.Content — Chakra's Floating UI positioning measures the
content at its natural height and, if it doesn't fit, flips it to a
position where it overflows the top of the screen. Boxing the
scrollable area to a fixed ceiling stops that.

Also fixes the search input focus ring being clipped by the sidebar's
`overflowX: hidden` (added 2px padding to the input wrapper).

* feat(traces-v2): Summary as default drawer view, all sections expanded, span tab scrolls

Three drawer-defaults changes that together close the audit-feedback
loop on "the drawer feels half-empty / I can't tell what's there":

1. **`viewMode` defaults to `summary`, not `trace`.** Both URL-bootstrap
   paths (`readInitialFromURL` + `loadLastViewMode`) now fall back to
   `summary` when no prior choice exists. Operators landing on a trace
   for the first time should see the top-level summary instead of the
   waterfall, which is what they actually need to decide whether the
   trace is worth investigating. Adds `summary` to the `DrawerViewMode`
   union and the `isViewMode` guard.

2. **All summary accordions open on first paint.** `useAutoOpenSections`
   used to seed `open` with only sections whose content predicate was
   truthy, which made the drawer feel hollow whenever a trace had no
   I/O or attributes — the user couldn't tell whether the section was
   absent or just collapsed. Now seeds with every section key. Empty
   states do the educating: "this trace has no attributes" reads better
   than a silent missing-row.

3. **`SpanDetailPane` scrolls internally.** The pane root now has
   `overflow: hidden` + explicit `height: 100%` so the inner
   `flex: 1; overflow: auto` body owns the available height. Without
   it, the inner scroll container could grow past its parent in
   contexts where the upstream Panel from react-resizable-panels didn't
   strictly clamp child height; the scrollbar then attached to an
   ancestor and the operator read it as "scroll doesn't work in the
   span tab".

While here:
- **Retire `activeTab`** from `DrawerUrlState` + the related
  setters/guards. The SpanTabBar no longer mixes trace-scope tabs
  (Summary/LLM/Prompts) with span-scope tabs; Summary is its own
  DrawerViewMode, LLM/Prompts content is auto-selected by span kind in
  SpanDetailPane. There's no tab choice left for the user to make.
- **Retire `flame` and `spanlist` viz tabs** (matching the removed view
  subtrees) — `isVizTab` returns false for them so legacy URLs fall
  through to the `waterfall` default.
- **Pin spans into the SpanTabBar via URL.** New `pinnedSpanIds` state
  + URL param (`drawer.pinnedSpans=...`), capped at MAX_PINNED_SPANS=8
  so a runaway pin loop can't bloat the URL.
- **Exceptions accordion gets a count badge** matching how Evals/Events
  render theirs — `errorSpans.length` plus `trace.error` when no error
  spans were found.

* fix(traces-v2): unify row colors and propagate column reorder to cells

Two paired bugs that the operator described as one — "the row colors
aren't consistent and the cells don't match the cols" — but came from
two different layers:

1. **Sticky-checkbox column read as a separate strip.** TraceTableShell
   was painting the pinned first column with `bg.panel` while the row
   body left its cells transparent against the parent surface
   (`bg.surface`). In dark mode those resolve to distinct shades, so
   every default row showed three visually-distinct horizontal bands
   (sticky checkbox / row body / IO-preview addon). Switch the default
   sticky-cell paint to `bg.surface` and add hover/selected/error/
   warning variants scoped by the tbody's `data-row-variant` attribute,
   so erroring rows still show their red tint across the whole row
   instead of stopping at the checkbox column.

2. **Headers reordered, cells didn't follow.** TraceLensBody was
   relying on Tanstack's default "columns-array order" for headers but
   Tanstack holds onto an INTERNAL leaf-column cache (built once per
   identity) for cell rendering. Reordering through the viewStore moved
   the headers but kept the cells in their original positions. Surface
   `columnOrder` as explicit Tanstack state — `[SELECT_COLUMN_ID,
   ...lens.columns]` — so leaf order is recomputed on every change and
   headers + cells stay in lockstep.

While here:
- RegistryRow + StatusRow propagate the variant attribute the sticky
  cell rules read.

* feat(traces-v2): add Since and Timestamp time columns + shared hover card

The default trace table had a single TIME column rendering a tiny
relative ("3m") to keep the column narrow. Operators kept asking
follow-up questions the cell couldn't answer ("3m from when in my
timezone?", "is that 3 minutes or 3 months?", "what's the exact wall
clock for this trace?") — so the cell now has two siblings that pick

that gives the rest.

* feat(traces-v2): cluster toolbar controls + inline column reorder + slim time picker

Three coupled toolbar changes — all driven by the same auditor pain

1. **Cluster the toolbar with hairline dividers.** Group the row into

* feat(traces-v2): drawer mode switch reorders, viz strip drops dead tabs, presence lifts to shell

- **ModeSwitch** now exposes three tabs in the order
  `Summary | Trace | Conversation`. Summary leads because it's the
  friendlier default for non-engineering users who just want I/O +
  metadata at a glance; Trace sits middle for the waterfall + span
  detail workflow; Conversation gates on `hasConversation`. Last-used-
  mode persistence (drawerStore) still carries observability-first
  users straight back to where they were. While here, wrap the Kbd
  shortcut chip in a tiny spacer Box — Kbd is closed (no style
  overrides), so without the wrapper the chip ran into the label
  ("SummaryO" instead of "Summary [O]").

- **VizPlaceholder** drops the Flame and Span List tabs (matching the
  removed view subtrees in a prior commit). Flame duplicated what the
  Waterfall tree already showed; Span List added filter chrome but no
  fundamentally new data. Waterfall, Topology, Sequence remain.
  Shortcut numbers stay in the original order so muscle memory is
  preserved.

- **TraceDrawerShell** + **PaneLayout** lift `PeerCursorOverlay` from
  the viz-pane to the drawer-shell scope. Previously cursors vanished
  as soon as a peer hovered out of the viz pane; now they render
  anywhere in the drawer (header, span detail, accordions).

* fix(traces-v2): drawer popovers lazyMount + hover-only annotation row

Two small drawer interaction fixes that shared the same root cause —
"per-row affordances paying full DOM cost up front":

- **AnnotationPopover** (both popovers) and **SpanTabBar** popovers
  gain `lazyMount` + `unmountOnExit`. Each conversation turn renders
  an AnnotationPopover; with 50+ turns the drawer was carrying
  50+ popover DOMs the user never opened. Lazy mount defers
  materialisation; unmount-on-exit drops the popover again on close.
- **TurnAnnotations** hides the annotation chip row at rest (opacity
  0) and reveals it on `_groupHover`, with a force-visible carve-out
  when the popover is actually open. The chip row was visually loud
  at rest and competed with the message body for attention; the
  hover-reveal keeps the affordance discoverable without making it
  the loudest thing in the conversation column.

* feat(traces-v2): RawJsonDialog gains pretty/minify, wrap, search, size readout

The raw-JSON inspector (opened with `\`) used to render a single
pretty-printed JSON dump in a modal — useful as a one-shot escape
hatch but coarse the moment the payload got big or the user wanted
to find a specific key.

Adds, all as small icon-buttons in the dialog header:

- **Pretty / minify toggle** — strings serialize with `JSON.stringify
  (..., pretty ? 2 : 0)`. Defaults to pretty; flipping to minified
  is useful for grabbing the payload into another tool.
- **Wrap toggle** — long string values (chat payloads, base64
  attachments, single-line JSON arrays) no longer disappear off the
  right edge of the dialog. Defaults to wrapped.
- **In-payload search** — case-insensitive substring filter that
  reduces the visible payload to lines containing the query. Finding
  `metadata.tenant` in a 5K-line payload no longer requires scrolling.
  Search resets when switching tabs (trace ↔ spans) so a stale query
  doesn't silently return "empty spans".
- **Byte + line readout** — visible in the header so operators can
  see "this trace dumps 124KB / 5,031 lines" at a glance, which
  matters when traces blow up.

The Copy button still copies the FULL payload (search is for viewing
only — users grabbing the JSON for a bug report want everything).

* feat(traces-v2): waterfall rows pin to span tabs + cost readout + signal chips

- **TreeRow** gains a hover-revealed pin icon — pinning a span adds
  it to the SpanTabBar via the `drawer.pinnedSpans` URL state
  introduced earlier in this branch. Pinned rows show a filled
  `LuPin`; unpinned rows show `LuPinOff` on hover only so the chrome
  doesn't compete with the row content at rest.
- **TreeRow** also picks up a `formatCost` readout on rows that have
  one — the waterfall used to show duration but not cost, even
  though cost is one of the most-asked-for span attributes in
  reviews.
- **GroupRow** + **WaterfallView** propagate the pin state and align
  the new hover affordance with the existing collapse/expand
  toggle so the right-hand action stack reads as one row of
  related controls.

The colored type chip switches from interpolating the palette into
the token string to Chakra v3's `colorPalette` resolution scope —
fixes a class of cases where the chip rendered with the wrong tint
because the palette token didn't exist on the resolved scope.

* feat(traces-v2): query breakdown chips on empty + calmer 'N new' pill

- **QueryBreakdownChips** is a new empty-state companion that breaks
  the active query down into one chip per predicate so a user can
  drop individual pieces without retyping the whole thing. We saw
  users typing junk into the search bar (e.g. `Ω AND status:error`)
  and being unable to figure out *why* results were empty — the
  search bar showed the full string, the sidebar showed a count of
  1 active facet, but the noisy `Ω` was invisible in both. Chips
  walk the AST and render:
   - Fielded tags     → chip × calls `removeFacet(field, value)`
   - Range tags       → chip × calls `removeField(field)` (range
                        removal is whole-field, not per-bound)
   - Free-text tokens → chip × calls `removeFreeText(value)`, with a
                        warning tone for tokens the parser flagged as
                        almost-certainly-junk
- **EmptyFilterState** wires the chip panel underneath the existing
  empty illustration so the affordance is right next to the "no
  results" message.
- **NewTracesScrollUpIndicator** drops the always-on bob+morph orb
  animation in favour of a one-shot arrival bounce. The previous
  "constantly demanding attention" pill on busy projects was loud
  enough that reviewers asked for it to be muted; the new bounce
  signals arrival, then settles. Also flips the chevron to ArrowUp
  to match the rest of the toolbar's iconography.
- **ConversationLensBody** + **GroupLensBody** pick up the matching
  column-order wiring (`columnOrderState` passed as Tanstack state)
  introduced in the trace lens, so headers + cells stay in lockstep
  there too.

* feat(traces-v2): expose per-span cost in the summary endpoint

The summary span row coming back from the ClickHouse repo carried
durationMs, status, model, but no cost — the trace drawer's waterfall
had to derive cost downstream or omit it. Add it as a first-class
field on the way through:

- `SpanSummaryRow.cost: number | null` on the repo type.
- `SUMMARY_SPAN_SELECT` projects `gen_ai.usage.cost` out of the
  attributes Map.
- `mapSpanSummaryRow` parses the Map-typed String to a number,
  collapses empty / NaN to null so the renderer doesn't paint "$NaN".
- `spanTreeNodeSchema.cost: z.number().nullish()` on the tRPC schema —
  `.nullish()` so older clients (or sample fixtures) that don't set
  the field at all stay compatible; readers treat undefined / null
  identically.

The mapper consumer (`mapSpanSummaryToTreeNode` in tracesV2.ts) is
updated separately when the discover SSE changes land.

* feat(traces-v2): SSE-push discover refreshes + canonical window snap

Three coupled changes to the discover (sidebar facet) pipeline,
all aimed at "fresh facet values land in active viewers within a
minute without each viewer paying the ClickHouse cost":

1. **Canonical window snap** (`DISCOVER_WINDOW_PRESETS`). Two users
   looking at "last hour" within seconds of each other were paying
   the full compute twice because their `(from, to)` differed by
   sub-minute drift; even after the 1-min boundary bucket, the
   window SPAN was unique per render. Snap arbitrary windows to the
   nearest preset (1h/6h/24h/7d/30d/all) so every viewer of "the
   last day" on a given tenant hits the same cache slot.

2. **Faster refresh threshold + cross-pod lock.** Drop the
   refresh-after from 2 min → 1 min so active viewers see fresh
   facet values within ~60s of new traces. The heavy ClickHouse
   work is still single-flight (cross-pod `claim` + per-pod
   `discoverRefreshing` Set). New `DISCOVER_REFRESH_LOCK_CACHE`
   holds the leadership lease (60s TTL) separately from the value
   cache (30 min TTL) so a crashed refresher self-recovers fast
   instead of leaving 30 min of stale data.

3. **SSE push on refresh completion.** New `discover_updated`
   broadcast event type wired through `BroadcastService`. After a
   background refresh lands a fresher payload in the shared cache,
   the service fires `discover_updated` to the tenant emitter. New
   tRPC subscription `tracesV2.onDiscoverUpdate` mirrors the shape
   of `onTraceUpdate` so the existing SSE hook handles it without
   changes. The client invalidates its TanStack Query cache and
   refetches; the fresh payload pulls from Redis without recomputing.

Wiring lives in `presets.ts` — module-level `setDiscoverBroadcaster`
keeps the TraceListService constructor lean (null/test presets that
don't want a broadcaster still hydrate the cache successfully).

Also propagates the new `viewMode === "summary"` enum value through
`useTracesV2Presence` — PresenceLocation's shared schema only knows
about pre-redesign modes, so the wire collapses `summary` to `trace`
so peers running older code still see the user as "on the trace".

* feat(traces-v2/query-language): removeImplicitTermFromQuery mutation

Used by the empty-state query breakdown chips when the user wants
to drop a single bare free-text token (e.g. `Ω` they typed by
accident) without clearing the whole query. Walks the AST and
filters out the matching `Tag` whose `field` is `ImplicitField`
and whose value matches; the existing `filterAST` collapses any
orphaned logical parents so we don't leave stray ANDs/ORs behind.
Returns `""` when the result collapses to an empty AST.

* feat(traces-v2): Simplified lens + time-column siblings + conversation sections

- **Simplified built-in lens** — low-density alternative to "All".
  Input / output get their own columns instead of being smashed into
  the composite `trace (summary)` cell + the `io-preview` second-row
  addon. Targeted at non-engineering users who want to scan messages
  without engineering chrome (status code, model, attribute counts,
  duration arc). Deliberately does NOT include the `io-preview` addon
  — the whole point of the lens is that I/O lives in regular table
  columns, not a wrap-prone second row. Engineers who want the dense
  composite stay on All. Named "Simplified" rather than "Basic" —
  "Basic" reads as diminished/insufficient; "Simplified" reads as a
  deliberate choice.
- **Time-column siblings** — `since` (verbose relative) and
  `timestamp` (ISO 8601) join the existing tight `time` in the
  trace-lens capability so the column dropdown surfaces all three
  options under the same Standard section. Matches the new sibling
  cells shipped earlier in this branch.
- **Conversation + group capabilities** — explicit `section: "Standard"`
  on every column. Without it the Columns dropdown rendered an
  "Other" section header on conversation/group lenses (because the
  fallback kicks in for missing sections), which read as
  broken/inconsistent next to the trace lens.

* feat(traces-v2/filterStore): removeFreeText action for query breakdown chips

Wires the `removeImplicitTermFromQuery` mutation through the filter
store as a first-class action. Consumed by `QueryBreakdownChips`
(empty-state) to drop a single accidental free-text token without
clearing the rest of the query.

* feat(traces-v2/formatters): verbose relative + ISO + local timestamp helpers

Backing utilities for the new SINCE / TIMESTAMP cell variants and the
TimeHoverCard:

- `formatVerboseRelative(ts)` — natural-language relative ("3 minutes
  ago", "2 weeks ago"). Used by the SINCE column. Cap at year-grain so
  ancient traces don't render "523 weeks ago".
- `formatISOTimestamp(ts)` — full ISO 8601 in UTC for the TIMESTAMP
  column (copy-paste into log queries).
- `formatLocalTimestamp(ts)` — locale-aware wall clock for the hover
  card alongside the ISO row.

Adds the MS_PER_{SECOND,WEEK,MONTH,YEAR} constants that the new
helpers need, alongside the existing minute/hour/day.

* fix(traces-v2): drawer shortcuts + URL sync follow the view redesign

Catches the keyboard + URL plumbing up to the drawer changes earlier
in this branch (Summary as its own ModeSwitch tab, dead Flame/SpanList
viz tabs retired, span detail no longer carries Trace-scope tabs):

- **traceDrawerShortcutTable** drops the 4/5 shortcuts (Flame/Span
  List), rebinds 2→Topology and 3→Sequence, repurposes `O` to set
  `viewMode = "summary"` (matching the ModeSwitch tab order), and
  retires `L`/`P` (the LLM/Prompts content is auto-selected by span
  kind now — no user-facing toggle to bind to).
- **useDrawerUrlSync** drops `activeTab` from the URL state mirror
  and adds `pinnedSpans` parsing / serialisation. Equality check
  flips to string-compare on the serialised pinned list (one cheap
  `==` instead of a per-element array walk every render).
- **useTraceHeaderChips** small tidy alongside the URL changes —
  pulls the header signal computation off the activeTab path.

* fix(traces-v2): error/new counts follow time range, calmer refresh pulse, comfortable density default

Four small data-plumbing fixes driven by the same audit feedback —
"the badges don't match what's on screen / the page pulses for no
reason / it looks too dense for the people I'm onboarding":

- **useErrorCount** binds to the user's selected `debouncedTimeRange`
  instead of a fixed 24h window mounted at hook start. The previous
  behaviour was a guaranteed contradiction: filter to "last 7 days",
  see 0 errors on the lens-tab badge but 50 in the table.
- **useTraceFreshness** stops firing the top-of-page refresh pulse on
  every SSE `trace_summary_updated` event. For high-throughput
  projects that was a constant flash that didn't correspond to
  anything appearing in the table. The pulse is now reserved for
  (1) user-initiated refresh (via TanStack `isFetching` flips) and
  (2) `useTraceNewCount` watching the visible-window count climb
  above zero just before new rows land.
- **useTraceNewCount** picks up the visible-window pulse logic the
  freshness hook handed off — count > 0 in live mode triggers one
  aurora pulse so the user sees movement when rows are about to
  arrive.
- **densityStore** flips the default for new users from `compact`
  to `comfortable`. Compact (3px row padding, 12px font) reads as
  "engineering ops dashboard" and drove most of the "too dense /
  too busy" feedback from non-developer users. Compact stays a
  one-click toggle. Existing users with an explicit choice in
  localStorage are unaffected — load() only falls back to the
  default when nothing is persisted yet.

* fix(traces-v2): review pass — keyboard a11y on hover-revealed buttons, metadata key validation

Three accessibility + correctness fixes from PR review:

- **SidebarSection hide button** was hover-revealed (`opacity: 0` →
  `_groupHover`) with no keyboard treatment, so sighted keyboard
  users could tab onto an invisible action. Add `_groupFocusWithin`
  to surface the affordance on group focus + `_focusVisible` to paint
  a focus ring when the button itself receives focus.
- **Waterfall TreeRow pin button** had the same hover-only reveal but
  with no `tabIndex` / `pointerEvents` gating. Mark it
  `tabIndex={-1}` + `pointerEvents: none` + `aria-hidden` while
  hidden so keyboard users don't get stranded on an invisible
  control, and add `_focusVisible` for when it's actually visible
  and focused.
- **DrawerHeader `formatMetadataFilterQuery`** was injecting raw
  customer-defined metadata keys straight into the Liqe query string.
  A key containing query syntax (`:`, `(`, etc.) breaks the grammar
  or targets the wrong field. Restrict keys to a safe whitelist
  (`[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+`) and return null otherwise — callers already
  disable `onFilter` on null, so unsafe keys just lose the click-to-
  filter affordance instead of generating a broken query.
- **TraceDrawerShell PeerCursorOverlay anchor** had a redundant
  `trace ?` ternary — the render branch above guarantees `trace` is
  non-null, so the ternary just confused readers (and tripped
  CodeQL's useless-conditional checker).

* fix(traces-v2): query breakdown chips classify comparisons + single-shot bare-term removal

Two correctness fixes around the empty-state breakdown chips:

- **QueryBreakdownChips** was classifying fielded comparison
  predicates (`duration:>1000`, `cost:<5`, etc.) as plain
  `field:value` chips and routing the X to `removeFacet(field,
  value)`. `removeFacet` is value-specific and can't address a
  comparison; the chip just silently no-op'd. Check the operator
  inside the `LiteralExpression` branch — if it's not `:`, render as
  a comparison chip (`field op value`) and route through
  `removeField(fieldName)` (whole-field removal).
- **removeImplicitTermFromQuery** was removing ALL matching bare
  terms in one call (`foo AND foo AND bar` → `bar`), which contradicts
  the "drop just this chip" contract the breakdown UI implies. Add a
  `removed` flag so the AST walk drops only the first matching node;
  subsequent matches pass through. Now `foo AND foo AND bar` collapses
  to `foo AND bar` after one click — matching what the user sees in
  the chip list.

* fix(traces-v2): keep AST-active categorical sections mounted on empty discover

`partitionDescriptors` dropped categorical sections whose `topValues`
was empty regardless of whether the AST had an active filter on the
same field. Result: filter on `status:error`, navigate to a window
with no error traces, the entire Status section disappears from the
sidebar — the user can no longer see or remove the active filter
without dropping back to the search bar.

Thread `activeFieldSet` from `useFilterSidebarData` through to
`partitionDescriptors`. The categorical gate now keeps a section
mounted when (a) it has buckets to show OR (b) the active filter
references the field. Cold tenants stay quiet (no buckets, no active
filter, no section); active-but-empty filters stay visible (no
buckets, but the filter is in the AST, so the section mounts with
just the cleared-filter affordance).

* fix(traces-v2/ColumnsDropdown): reorder uses visible-order index space

The up/down arrows in the "Visible order" strip were resolving move
targets as `columnOrder.indexOf(column.id) ± 1`, but the strip
itself is built from `orderedVisibleColumns` (which filters out
pinned columns). If a pinned column sat between two reorderable
columns, the move targeted the pinned slot instead of the adjacent
visible column — and `reorderColumns` no-op'd against the pinned
slot, so the button did nothing.

Resolve the neighbour from `orderedVisibleColumns[index ± 1]` first,
then map back to the full `columnOrder` index space for the
reorder call. Same pattern for both arrows.

* fix(traces-v2/formatters): clamp future timestamps to 'just now', drop unused MS_PER_SECOND

- `formatVerboseRelative` returned `"in the future"` for negative
  diffs, but real-world clock skew on a busy ingest puts trace
  timestamps a hair ahead of the viewer's clock. The narrow
  `formatRelativeTime` already clamps these to "now"; this match for
  consistency, so the Since column and hover card stop blinking
  "in the future" on freshly arrived traces.
- `MS_PER_SECOND` was added alongside the other MS_PER_* constants
  and never used. CodeQL flagged it; drop it.

* fix(traces-v2/RawJsonDialog): byteSize → charCount (honest unit), await clipboard

Two fixes to the JSON inspector behaviour:

- **Unit honesty.** `byteSize` was computed as `fullPayload.length`,
  which is the JavaScript string length (UTF-16 code units), not a
  byte count under any encoding. The repo elsewhere treats
  `length * 2` as the "bytes" unit, so showing "12KB" alongside
  another component reading "24KB" for the same payload was a recipe
  for confusion. Rename to `charCount`, update the SizeBadge labels
  to "chars", and adjust the helper to use thousand/million
  thresholds (since the unit is character count, not memory bytes).
- **Clipboard.** `CopyButton` set `Copied` immediately after calling
  `navigator.clipboard.writeText` without awaiting the promise.
  On permission-denied (Safari private mode, insecure context),
  users saw the confirmation even when nothing reached the
  clipboard. Await the promise; on rejection stay silent (the surface
  has no error slot, the user can retry, and a toast here would
  compete with the dialog).

* fix(traces-v2/viewStore): reconcile addons in effective lens against live grouping

`getEffectiveLens` was spreading the saved lens config's `addons`
straight into the returned shape, but the live `grouping` can have
been switched to a different RowKind (flat → group, conversation →
flat, etc.) without the saved lens config noticing. Result: a flat
lens like `all-traces` switched to grouping `by-service` kept its
flat-only addons (`io-preview`, `expanded-peek`) attached to a
grouped lens — internally inconsistent even after the column
registry was reconciled in an earlier commit.

Call the existing `reconcileAddons(lens.addons, capability)` helper
against the LIVE grouping's capability so addons the new RowKind
can't mount get dropped. Flat addons survive a flat → flat lens
switch; everything incompatible gets filtered.

* fix(server/traces-v2): discoverCacheKey includes snapped from, test apps reset broadcaster

Two server-side review fixes around the discover cache + SSE bridge:

- **Cache key collision.** `discoverCacheKey` was `[tenantId, label,
  to]`. Two requests for different windows that both classify under
  the same preset label (a 15-minute window and a 1-hour window
  both label "1h") could collide on a single cache slot and serve
  the first-computed payload to both viewers — facets for a window
  they aren't actually looking at. Include the snapped `from`
  alongside `to` so each window-span gets its own slot regardless of
  label collisions.
- **Test broadcaster leak.** `setDiscoverBroadcaster` is module-
  global; `initializeDefaultApp` wires it once with a closure that
  captures the production `BroadcastService`. `createTestApp`
  overwrites the App global but never clears the broadcaster — and
  since `NullTraceListRepository`'s refresh path resolves
  successfully, a test/null app's background refresh could still
  invoke the stale production closure. Call
  `setDiscoverBroadcaster(null)` at the top of `createTestApp` so
  test apps start with no broadcaster wired (tests that want one
  can register their own afterwards).

* fix(traces-v2/FacetSection): enter-to-apply resolves value from label match

Search now matches both `label` and `value`. On Enter, the trimmed query
is resolved against an exact (case-insensitive) match on either field;
the matched item's `value` is submitted. Falls back to the raw typed
value when nothing matches, preserving the one-off filter affordance.

Before: facets where `label !== value` (friendly topic names, IDs with
labels) could submit the typed label as a filter value, applying an
invalid filter while the row visually looked correct.

* fix(traces-v2/useTraceNewCount): scope refresh-pulse baseline to query identity

`prevCountRef` was module-instance-global, so the 0→N transition gate
that fires the aurora refresh pulse compared a count from one context
(project A, "last hour", `errors:true`) against the next count after the
context changed. That fires (or suppresses) the pulse against a stale
baseline.

`prevCountRef` is now `number | null`. It resets to `null` on every
identity change (`project?.id`, time range fields/label, `since`,
`queryText`); the first success in a new context becomes the baseline
without pulsing.

* fix(traces-v2/SectionRenderer): thread onHide into AttributesSection

`AttributesSection` accepts `onHide` and surfaces the header-level hide
affordance, but `SectionRenderer`'s attributes branch never passed it
through, so trace / span / event attribute sections missed the affordance
that `cat` and `range` branches already had.

* fix(traces-v2/VizPlaceholder): show-details icon points toward the stacked pane

The detail-pane reveal toggle used `LuPanelRightOpen` for horizontal
layouts and `LuPanelTopOpen` for the rest. In the non-horizontal layout
the detail pane is stacked below the viz, so the icon was pointing at
the opposite edge. Swapped to `LuPanelBottomOpen` for non-horizontal so
the chevron points toward where the pane will expand.

* fix(server/traces-v2): mark cold-miss discover as pending so sidebar skeleton renders

* chore(traces-v2/formatters): drop dead SPAN_TYPE_BADGE_STYLES export

* fix(traces-v2/facetVisibilityStore): make selectVisibilityFor a pure projection

* fix(traces-v2/hooks): align drawer URL default + polling fallback for cold discover misses

- useDrawerUrlSync: DEFAULTS.mode "trace" -> "summary" so popstate into an
  older drawer URL without `drawer.mode` no longer hydrates the store back
  to Trace mode (drawerStore's mount-time default is Summary).
- useTraceFacets: while `result.pending` is true, poll with 2/4/8/15s
  backoff so the sidebar settles even if the `discover_updated` SSE event
  is missed, delayed, rate-limited, or the subscription isn't connected.
  Backoff resets on every non-pending response and on SSE delivery.

fix(traces-v2): trace drawer drive-through — scroll, span selection, scope, prefetch (#4566)

* fix(traces-v2): summary tab scroll + empty trace tab

PeerCursorOverlay was lifted from the viz pane up to wrap the entire
drawer body so peer cursors render across all three modes. Its outer
Box stayed at `width:100% height:100% position:relative` — without
`min-height: 0` the implicit `min-height: auto` clamped it to its
content size, so the overlay couldn't shrink into the flex slot the
drawer body offered. Two visible regressions:

  - Summary tab: accordion content overflowed `Drawer.Body`'s
    `overflow: hidden` and the bottom (Events, Exceptions) sat past
    the fold, unreachable.
  - Trace tab: `PaneLayout`'s `PanelGroup` resolved its percentages
    against an effectively 0px height, so every pane rendered empty.

Two changes fix both:

  - `PeerCursorOverlay` Box now carries `minHeight={0} minWidth={0}`
    so it shrinks correctly inside any flex parent.
  - The Flex wrapped by the overlay in TraceDrawerShell switched from
    `flex={1}` (inert — the overlay's Box isn't a flex container) to
    `height="100%"` so it reads the overlay's resolved height.

With the chain in place, the inner `<Box flex={1} minHeight={0}
overflow="auto">` finally sees a bounded height and scrolls.

* feat(traces-v2): drawer drive-through — span selection, viz persistence, scope relocation, eager prefetch

Operator drive-through pass on the trace drawer:

  - Preserve span selection across detail-pane collapse/uncollapse.
    `togglePaneCollapsed("spanDetail")` used to null `selectedSpanId`
    on collapse so the next click felt like a fresh detail view —
    feedback was the opposite: hiding the pane and showing it again
    should land on the same span. Selection still clears via the
    explicit `clearSpan` path (X button / keyboard).

  - Persist the last-chosen viz tab (Waterfall / Topology / Sequence)
    the same way `viewMode` is persisted, under
    `langwatch:traces-v2:drawer-last-viz:v1`. Users who prefer
    Topology or Sequence no longer get bounced back to Waterfall on
    every new trace.

  - Move the instrumentation-scope chip out of `SpanTabBar`'s
    rightSlot and into the per-span accordion as a proper
    "Instrumentation Scope" section, gated on `hasScope`. The chip
    was taking tab-row real estate for a piece of metadata that most
    users glance at once and ignore — folding it back into the
    accordion stack keeps the tab bar focused on tab selection.

  - Prefetch `spanTree`, `spanLangwatchSignals`, `traceEvents`, and
    `resourceInfo` at row-click time in `useOpenTraceDrawer`. The
    drawer mount takes a tick; firing the heavy per-trace queries
    in parallel with the route change means the waterfall and span
    accordions render against warm data instead of skeletoning for
    half a second. Preview traces are skipped (the cache is already
    seeded by `buildRichArrivalTraceDetail`).

* chore(trpc): silence presence + subscription logs and traces

The dev log + the tRPC OTel span list were dominated by two flavours
of low-signal calls:

  - `presence.*` heartbeats — peer-cursor + drawer presence pings fire
    every few seconds per open tab.
  - SSE subscription calls — every delivered message emits a `trpc
    call` log line and starts a new span.

The signal-to-noise problem hid real errors and slow paths. Both
middlewares now early-out on these calls when successful:

  - `loggerMiddleware` skips the happy-path log line (errors still
    flow through, so real failures stay visible).
  - `tracerMiddleware` skips span creation entirely.

The silencing is keyed on a small allow-list and a single
`subscription` type check, kept next to each other in trpc.ts so a
future "also silence X" stays a one-line change.

* perf(traces-v2): stop polling per-trace queries when SSE is connected

The per-trace drawer queries (`spanTree`, `spanLangwatchSignals`,
`traceHeader`) were unconditionally polling at `LIVE_REFETCH_MS` for
any trace inside the `isLive` window. `useTraceFreshness` already
subscribes to `traces.onTraceUpdate` and invalidates the relevant
cache keys on every event, so the timed refetches were pure
duplication when SSE was healthy — and the duplicate batched requests
were saturating the browser's 6-connection limit, queueing the heavy
`spanDetail` batch behind them and making the span-detail pane look
like it was loading forever.

Fix:

  - Each of the three hooks now reads `sseConnectionState` from
    `useSseStatusStore` and only enables the live refetchInterval
    when SSE is OFF (`paused` / `disconnected` / `error`). When SSE
    is connected, the cache is kept fresh push-style. Mirrors the
    pattern already used by `useErrorCount` + `useTraceNewCount`.

  - Extended the `onSpanStored` invalidation set in
    `useTraceFreshness` to cover `spanLangwatchSignals`,
    `traceEvents`, and `resourceInfo` — without this the
    "no-poll-when-SSE-up" rule would stale-cache the badges /
    events / scope sections on a recent trace receiving new spans.

`traceHeader` keeps its prompt-pending fallback (`PROMPTS_PENDING
_REFETCH_MS`) regardless of SSE state — the prompt aggregator writes
asynchronously and doesn't broadcast a `trace_updated` event when
only the `lastUsedPromptId` slot fills in, so the SSE invalidation
won't cover that transition.

* Address Copilot review on #4566

- tracerMiddleware: run next() first for silenced calls; only create
  an OTel span when result.ok === false. Failures on presence.* and
  SSE subscriptions stay visible; happy paths still go quiet.
- drawerStore: split setVizTab into a persisting setter (operator
  actions) and a transient setter (programmatic forcing, e.g. the
  preview/onboarding waterfall override). useOpenTraceDrawer's
  preview branch switched to the transient one so it no longer
  clobbers the operator's remembered preference.
- drawerStore: rewrote the now-stale comment in selectSpan to reflect
  the new collapse round-trip (selection preserved; clearSpan is the
  explicit clear path).
- drawerStore.unit.test.ts: added "given a selected span" describe
  block — asserts the selection survives a togglePaneCollapsed
  round-trip and that clearSpan still clears it.
- useOpenTraceDrawer: added occurredAtMs to the resourceInfo prefetch
  so the prefetched cache key matches what useTraceResources reads.

* refactor(trpc): hoist OTel import + dedupe tracer middleware

Pre-existing pattern in `tracerMiddleware` used an inline
`await import("@opentelemetry/api")` (banned by CLAUDE.md —
"never use inline import() — always use top-level import / import
type statements"). My earlier silenced-error commit doubled down
on the violation by adding a second copy, plus duplicated the
4-line error-recording block across both branches.

Cleanup:

  - One top-level `@opentelemetry/api` import.
  - `spanAttributes(path, type)` helper holds the rpc.* attribute
    literal; both call sites share it.
  - `recordSpanError(span, error)` helper holds the
    `recordException` + `setStatus(ERROR)` pair; both branches
    share it.
  - Tracer + spanName are computed once at the top of the
    middleware. The silenced branch is now just "next() first;
    if !result.ok, start a span with the captured `startTime`,
    record the error, end". The normal branch is the existing
    `startActiveSpan` shape, slimmed.

Behaviour is unchanged: silenced routes still get zero spans on
success and a properly-timed error span on failure; normal routes
still get a full `startActiveSpan` wrap.

* style: biome auto-fix on touched files (sort imports, tab indent, jsx wrap)

* refactor(traces-v2): dedupe per-trace prefetch + invalidate inputs

Both the click-time prefetch fan-out in useOpenTraceDrawer and the
SSE-driven invalidation fan-out in useTraceFreshness repeated the
same input object across 4–5 sibling calls. Hoist the shared input
(and prefetch options) into a single binding before the calls and
pass it in; behaviour unchanged, but the per-call payload is no
longer drift-bait if the input shape ever grows another field.

fix(governance): SaaS CLI gateway default points at parked .com host (#4625)

The CLI login bootstrap and personal-VK reveal card each hardcoded
`https://gateway.langwatch.com` as the SaaS fallback gateway URL. Prod
runs IS_SAAS=true with no LW_GATEWAY_PUBLIC_URL / LW_GATEWAY_BASE_URL set,

(already the CLI's own default, the VK usage snippets, and the tests).

the SaaS/local defaults live in a single tested place and can't drift
between call sites again.

* feat(traces): synthesize gen_ai spans from claude_code OTLP log events

Claude Code 2.1.x dropped trace-span emission entirely. Verified by
running real claude code 2.1.162 against a local OTLP catcher with the
full documented env set (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1,
OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=otlp, OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp,
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/json) — ZERO POSTs to /v1/traces,
all telemetry lands in /v1/logs under the scope
com.anthropic.claude_code.events. Binary strings of cli.js confirm
the binary has no OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER read path at all.

Without this synthesizer, Path B claude users would only see metrics
and disconnected log records in stored_log_records; /me/traces would
be empty for them.

The synthesizer pairs user_prompt + api_request log records by
prompt.id (their correlation key within a session) and emits one
gen_ai span per pair:
- gen_ai.system=anthropic, gen_ai.request.model from api_request
- gen_ai.usage.input_tokens / output_tokens
- gen_ai.conversation.id = session.id
- langwatch.input.value = user_prompt.prompt as messages JSON
- langwatch.cost.usd from api_request
- trace_id = sha256(session.id) (groups multi-turn into one trace)
- span_id = sha256(session.id || ":" || prompt.id) (idempotent
  through the stored_spans ReplacingMergeTree on re-ingest)

Known gap (documented honestly in the PR body): Claude Code does
NOT emit the assistant's response text anywhere in the OTel stream
in 2.1.x. Synthesized spans show input + tokens + cost but the
output text field stays empty until anthropic re-adds it.

Also: wrapper-mode + drawer env snippets now set
OTEL_LOG_USER_PROMPTS=1 so the user_prompt event includes the
prompt body attribute the synthesizer reads.

production preset. Tests confirm: span synthesis fires for
claude_code.events scope, does NOT fire for other scopes, and does
NOT fire when recordSpan is omitted (back-compat).

* feat(traces): claude_code OTLP log → trace summary at the right seam

Path B claude code (CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1 + OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER)
emits its cost-bearing api_request events outside any active span, so
the OTLP exporter ships them with empty trace_id / span_id. Two seams
were missing on the event-sourcing pipeline:

1. LogRequestCollectionService now synthesizes stable ids for the
   com.anthropic.claude_code.events scope when the wire ids are empty:
   - trace_id = sha256(session.id) truncated to 32 hex (every turn of
     a session collapses into one /me/traces row)
   - span_id  = sha256(session.id:prompt.id:event.name:event.sequence)
     truncated to 16 hex (each event keeps its own row, idempotent
     through the stored_log_records ReplacingMergeTree on re-ingest)
   Other scopes pass through unchanged; missing session.id leaves
   the ids empty (no inventing).

2. traceSummary.foldProjection's handleTraceLogRecordReceived lifts
   cost/tokens/model off claude_code.api_request log records into the
   canonical langwatch.* attributes the trace UI renders. Anthropic
   cache semantics preserved: cache_creation_tokens (tokens WRITTEN
   to the prompt cache, ≥ 1.25× regular input rate) stays distinct
   from cache_read_tokens (tokens READ from cache, ~0.1× rate). A
   swap would silently mis-bill by ~12×.

Routes that share LogRequestCollectionService:
  - /api/otel/v1/logs (personal Path B today)
  - /api/ingest/otel/:sourceId/v1/logs (governance Path B)
Both gain the synthesis + lift for free since the fix lives in the
shared service.

The legacy otel.logs.ts converter that did the equivalent ES-path

* feat(wrapper): Stage A platform-tool policy gate (allow_vk + allow_otel_direct)

Wires per-tool policy gating into resolveWrapperMode so the wrapper
respects allow_vk / allow_otel_direct flags before falling through
to mode-detect. Stage A ships hardcoded defaults (both true for
claude/codex/gemini/opencode; allowOtelDirect=false for cursor since
its GUI agent panel can't read terminal env). Stage B will swap
resolvePlatformToolPolicy's body for a server round-trip with
per-org overrides without touching any caller.

Gate semantics, both gates symmetric:
  - resolved=gateway + !allowVk + allowOtelDirect -> downgrade to ingestion
  - resolved=ingestion + !allowOtelDirect + allowVk -> fall back to gateway
  - both off -> GovernanceCliError('tool_disabled')

Why the symmetric fall-back instead of throwing: a single disabled
path doesn't mean the user has no usable route, only that one of
two is unavailable. Throwing on a one-sided disable would break
cursor (which has allowOtelDirect=false by design) even though
gateway routing is fully available.

   uses. Without it `--model anthropic/...` fails

* fix(aigateway): preserve native Anthropic SSE shape on /v1/messages streams

DispatchStream routed RequestTypeMessages through ChatCompletionStream,
which translates the upstream stream into OpenAI-shape
BifrostChatResponse chunks (`delta.choices`, `reasoning_details`). The
non-streaming /v1/messages path already worked because it pulls
ExtraFields.RawResponse via rawResponseBytes() when SendBackRawResponse
is set; Bifrost stream chunks don't expose a comparable per-frame
raw-bytes hook, so the chunk path was silently OpenAI-shaping the
response.

Vercel AI SDK's Anthropic provider Zod-validates every chunk against
the Messages event union (`content_block_delta`, `message_start`,
`message_delta`, `content_block_start`, `message_stop`, ...) and
rejected the OpenAI-shape with:

  AI_TypeValidationError: ZodError [No matching discriminator on 'type']

so opencode + any client using @ai-sdk/anthropic saw the request
succeed on the wire (req_id stamped, anthropic provider hit) and then
the response stream collapse mid-flight — the failure mode rchaves
caught dogfooding the opencode Path A wrapper fix.

New `dispatchMessagesStream` raw-forwards the request through
Bifrost's PassthroughStream so the provider adapter
(anthropic.go:2700) speaks /v1/messages directly to api.anthropic.com
with x-api-key + anthropic-version and streams the raw fasthttp body
back chunk-by-chunk. Same shape Gemini's /v1beta passthrough already
uses for its native streamGenerateContent route.

Usage telemetry preserved via parseAnthropicPassthroughUsage:

  - message_start carries `usage.input_tokens` +
    `cache_creation_input_tokens` + `cache_read_input_tokens`
  - message_delta carries `usage.output_tokens` (overwrites as the
    response grows)

The iterator now MERGES per-chunk usage (was: replace) so the
message_start input-side counters survive into the final Usage() when
later message_delta chunks only update completion tokens. Gemini's
existing behaviour is preserved since its usageMetadata always carries
every counter on every emitted chunk.

3 regression tests guard the cache_creation vs cache_read distinction
(silent swap would inflate billed input by ~12×) + the message_delta
output-tokens overwrite + the content_block_delta no-usage no-op.

silence(presidio): drop analyzer recognizer warnings to ERROR (#4643)

Presidio's analyzer logs a WARNING line for every requested entity that
has no recognizer in the active language. Our entity list intentionally
includes language-region specific types (SG_NRIC_FIN, AU_ABN, IN_PAN,
IN_AADHAAR, IN_VOTER, IN_PASSPORT, AU_MEDICARE, AU_TFN, AU_ACN,
AU_VEHICLE_REGISTRATION) that are absent from the English model, so every
single English-language analyze() emitted ~30 WARNING lines about them.

At lambda invocation volumes (warmer pings every minute plus real evals)
the presidio-evaluator-lambda CloudWatch log group was ingesting 13-15
GB/day, with ~$200/month of CloudWatch ingest cost coming almost entirely
from this static-fact noise: the recognizer set is fixed at configuration
time, not per-request, so re-logging the same warnings for every call
provides zero operational signal.

Setting the presidio-analyzer logger to ERROR keeps real failures visible
while dropping the static-config chatter. Application-level signal from
our own code (staged-payload INFO timings, etc.) is unaffected.

fix(evals-v3): coerce non-string evaluator inputs + lock auto-mapping (#4642)

* specs: type coercion + auto-mapping for evaluations-v3

Customer report: workbench live-execute of an evaluator-as-target into
a downstream Exact Match / LLM Answer Match surfaces
  Validation error: Expected string, received boolean at "output"

The fix splits across three layers, deterministic chain:

1. The workbench live-execute (REST) coerces non-string mapped values
   to their string form before validation, matching the python NLP
   autoparse_field_value behavior that the batch + online paths
   already carry. evaluator-as-target.feature gets a regression
   scenario per source type.

2. The nlpgo Studio workflow executor restores the same coercion at
   the evaluator-block dispatch boundary. The Python NLP era hid this
   behind autoparse; the Go migration lost it. Captured in a new
   studio/workflow-evaluator-input-coercion.feature.

3. The langevals exact-match scorer extends its existing float-equality
   short-circuit to a JavaScript-style loose equality so an upstream
   boolean (true) matches a dataset golden label of "1" without false
   negatives. New evaluators/exact-match-loose-equality.feature.

Separately, mapping-auto-inference.feature restricts the
inferEvaluatorMappings heuristic so the "output" identifier ALWAYS
sources from a runner/target output (never the dataset), while
"expected_output" / "input" identifiers ALWAYS source from the
dataset (never the runner). The old behavior would happily map
evaluator.output to dataset.output, producing the very tautology
the user did not want and a confusing default that takes more time
to undo than to write fresh.

* fix(evals-v3): lock auto-mapping per identity, never cross-fall

The evaluator auto-mapping heuristic had a "try the other side as a
fallback" rule that produced confusing defaults: an evaluator's `output`
field would happily map to a same-named dataset column whenever the
runner did not emit one, grading the dataset against itself. The
"expected_output" / "input" identifiers had the mirror trap.

Tighten the rule per the customer's report:

  - identifiers in the output family (output, response, answer, result,
    generated) auto-map ONLY from runner/target outputs
  - identifiers in the input + expected + context families auto-map ONLY
    from dataset columns
  - anything else (score, threshold, label, custom evaluator inputs)
    keeps the original dataset-first / target-fallback dual-try logic
    so the restriction stays narrow

Empty is a recoverable default; a wrong default takes more time to
spot and undo than to write fresh. Regression tests cover each locked
side and the dual-try preservation for the open identifiers.

* fix(evals-v3): coerce non-string evaluator inputs + JS-loose scorer

Customer report: workbench live-execute of an evaluator-as-target into a
downstream Exact Match / LLM Answer Match surfaces

  Validation error: Expected string, received boolean at "output"

The fix lands across three layers, deterministic chain:

1. langwatch REST live-execute (evaluations-legacy.ts) now coerces every
   mapped scalar to its string form via a new coerceEvaluatorScalar
   helper, wired through z.preprocess on input/output/expected_output and
   each conversation turn. Parity with the langwatch_nlp era autoparse
   (true -> "true", 42 -> "42", {...} -> JSON) that the batch + online
   paths already carry via tracesMapping tryAndConvertTo.

2. The nlpgo evaluator-block executor restores the same coercion at the
   Studio workflow boundary, so a bool-emitting node piped into a
   string-input evaluator no longer surfaces a Pydantic rejection from
   the receiving langevals service.

3. The langevals exact_match scorer extends its existing is_float
   short-circuit with a JavaScript-style loose-equality layer. Inputs
   recover their underlying type via json.loads, then the scorer applies
   ECMA 7.2.13 abstract equality across the bool / number / string trio
   (True -> 1, False -> 0, numeric strings cross-coerce). A coerced
   "true" matches a dataset golden of "1" without false negatives, and
   the existing trim / punctuation / case-fold chain still wins for
   genuine free-form text.

- langwatch/src/server/utils/__tests__/coerceEvaluatorScalar.unit.test.ts
  (12 cases: string, null, bool, number, bigint, object, array, NaN/Inf)
- langwatch/src/server/routes/__tests__/evaluator-input-coercion.unit.test.ts
  (9 cases through getEvaluatorDataForParams: bool/number/object/null +
  conversation arrays + custom-evaluator passthrough)
- services/nlpgo/app/engine/blocks/evaluatorblock/coerce_test.go

fix(nlpgo): preserve evaluator result envelope so reasoning survives (#4648)

Customer report: the experiments-v3 workbench evaluator result popover
showed only Status (Passed/Failed) with no reasoning/Details, for both
langevals scorers and LLM-as-judge evaluators.

Root cause: the nlpgo Studio executor (runEvaluator) filtered the
evaluator's output map down to the node's DECLARED output names.
experiments-v3 (workflowBuilder) declares evaluator outputs as exactly
[passed, score, label] and never lists the metadata envelope, so the
filter silently dropped `details` (the reasoning) plus `status` and
`cost`. The legacy Python executor surfaced the full result dict
(end_component_event did `outputs = dict(result)`) and never filtered,
so this was a NLP->Go migration regression.

The same filtered map (ns.Outputs) feeds two consumers, both of which
lost the reasoning:
- the experiments-v3 SSE path: resultMapper reads outputs.details to
  build the evaluator_result event the workbench popover renders.
- the batch eval reporter: evaluation.go reads ns.Outputs["details"].

Fix: in runEvaluator, always surface the EvaluationResultWithMetadata
envelope (status / details / cost) regardless of declarations, and apply
the declared-names filter only to the VALUE outputs (passed / score /
label). Value outputs stay author-controlled (a workflow that wires only
`passed` still gets only `passed`); the reasoning always reaches the
result panel and batch report.

Surfaced by #4642 only in the sense that it unblocked reaching a rendered
downstream meta-eval result (the boolean-output 400 previously made this
path unreachable); #4642 did not write this bug.

Tests: evaluator_envelope_test.go runs entry -> evaluator end-to-end
against a stub langevals server and asserts details survives a
[passed,score,label] declaration, and that undeclared value fields are
still filtered while the envelope is kept. Reverting the fix fails both
(details=nil). Bound to specs/studio/workflow-evaluator-output-envelope.feature.

  on the channel).

  emission + the no-configId negative); add an Origin field to the shared

* fix(traces-v2): dedupe the discover SSE subscription so the drawer stops starving

useTraceFacets opened a tracesV2.onDiscoverUpdate SSE subscription, but it is
consumed by three sidebar components (SearchBar, FilterSidebar,
TokenValuePicker). tRPC subscriptions are not deduplicated across hook
instances the way queries are, so each consumer opened its own EventSource:
three identical onDiscoverUpdate connections. With traces.onTraceUpdate and
presence.onPresenceUpdate that is five persistent SSE connections, and on
HTTP/1.1 (dev) the six-per-origin pool leaves a single free slot, so the burst
of queries fired when a span/drawer opens sits pending behind the held
connections (a devtools resend works because it is a fresh connection).

Hoist the subscription into useTraceFreshness, the page-level coordinator
already mounted once in TracesPage that owns trace-event-to-cache
invalidation. One subscription invalidates the shared discover query, which
refreshes every consumer, so behaviour is unchanged but the connection count
drops from five to three. Reproduced the five-connection state via Playwright
before the fix.

* fix(claude-otlp): one trace per turn, not per session

Claude Code emits its events with no trace context, so the receiver synthesizes
ids. trace_id was sha256(session.id) - constant for the whole session, so every
user turn collapsed onto one ever-growing trace. Key it on the turn instead:
sha256(session.id || ':' || prompt.id). Every event of a single turn (the
user_prompt, the api_request/response model calls its agentic tool-loop drives,
and the tool events) shares one prompt.id, so they stay on one trace, while a
new turn (new prompt.id) starts a new trace. gen_ai.conversation.id = session.id
still groups the turns into one conversation thread. Pre-prompt session-setup
events (no prompt.id) keep falling back to the session-level id.

Validated against a real 2-turn claude-code 2.1.x session captured via an OTLP
intercept: turn 1 ("run three bash commands one at a time") drove 6 api_requests
across a 4-call tool-loop, ALL sharing prompt.id 47fcab35; turn 2 got a distinct
5fc69a28. request_id is per-API-call (8 distinct) and would have shattered turn
1 into 6 traces, so prompt.id is the correct turn key.

* fix(traces-v2): stop the drawer-mode sync from clobbering drawer.open on reopen

refresh lost the drawer. openDrawer's `?drawer.open=traceV2Details&drawer.traceId=…`
push is an async shallow navigation; the store->URL effect fired mid-transition
and wrote drawer.mode off a stale asPath that had no drawer.open/traceId yet,
clobbering them. Gate the sync on drawer.open being present in the URL: the
effect re-fires once the open lands, and updateDrawerParams then reads an asPath
that carries drawer.open + drawer.traceId and preserves them.

* fix(claude-otlp): surface tool calls + drop cross-batch orphan bodies

Three claude-code Path B trace-quality fixes reported while dogfooding a
tool-using turn (`hi` -> `echo "test otlp"` -> `did it work`):

1. Tool calls were invisible. claude emits tool_decision / tool_result as
   separate OTLP log events that stayed on the log path, so the Bash / Edit /
   Read invocations an agent makes never appeared in the waterfall. They are
   now trapped and converted into `tool` spans (one per tool_use_id) via
   convertClaudeCodeToolLogsToSpans. The command lands on
   gen_ai.tool.call.arguments, never langwatch.input, so a parentless tool span
   cannot hijack the trace's headline input.

2. Duplicate / out-of-order model spans. claude logs api_request_body at call
   START and the api_request anchor at call END, so for any call longer than
   the OTLP export interval (every tool-using turn) the body lands in a
   different export batch than its anchor. With no request_id on the body it
   cannot be re-paired, and the old code emitted it as its own input-only span:
   a duplicate of the model call that also sorted before the anchor in the
   waterfall ("output earlier than input"). Orphan bodies are now dropped; the
   turn input is already on the trace via the co-batched user_prompt event, and
   the tool spans show what the call did. Anchor + response co-batch (both at
   call END), so the output stays joined.

3. Mystery empty spans. Utility calls (generate_session_title,
   prompt_suggestion) were named by model, so a turn showed extra
   "claude-opus-4-8" spans carrying no conversation. They are now named by
   query_source so the waterfall reads clearly.

* fix(traces-v2): latch the latest conversational output for claude turns

The trace summary showed input but no output for a claude-code tool-using turn
even though a middle span carried the real reply ("Done - output was test
otlp."). The fold's output accumulation treats a parentless span as the trace
root and lets any root override, so among the many parentless spans a
claude_code turn synthesizes (one per model call) the LAST-FOLDED root won
rather than the latest-finishing one. The real reply sits on a middle call,
with utility calls (prompt_suggestion) finishing after it, so the winner
depended on arrival order.

shouldOverrideOutput now keeps the latest-finishing reply among roots, so the
trace output is deterministic by end time instead of fold order. For a
conventional single-root trace this is a no-op (there is only ever one root); a
root still beats a non-root child that set the output.

* feat(traces-v2): split trace cost into billed vs non-billed (bundled plans)

LangWatch bills per captured event, never per token, but a customer's own
LLM spend depends on how they pay the provider: gateway / virtual-key usage
is billed per token, while a coding assistant on a bundled subscription
(e.g. Claude Max) is not. Today the platform shows the full list-price token
cost everywhere, so a bundled coding session reads as enormous real spend it
mostly is not.

- Admin per-tool flag: coding_assistant tiles get a "Bundled subscription"
  toggle (config.bundledPlan, default true). It only governs the direct-OTLP
  ingest path; gateway usage is always billed and ignores it.
- Receiver stamp: for ingest-key traces the OTLP receiver resolves the tool's
  bundledPlan (cached per org+source) and stamps langwatch.cost.non_billable.
- Trace summary: totalCost stays the grand list-price total; a derived
  nonBilledCost holds the bundled (theoretical) portion, so billed =
  totalCost - nonBilledCost. Surfaced on the v2 header + list item (the list
  CH read projects the marker like langwatch.origin).
- UI: the drawer Cost pill shows the billed amount with a Billed / Non-billed
  / Theoretical-total popover; the traces-list cost cell shows billed with a
  hover breakdown. A bundled session no longer reads as real spend.

Analytics billed/theoretical series is a follow-up on this same marker.

* feat(analytics): add billed vs non-billed (theoretical) cost metrics

Custom analytics now exposes two cost series alongside Total Cost, split on
the receiver-stamped langwatch.cost.non_billable marker:

- Billed Cost: list-price cost minus bundled traces (real per-token spend).
- Non-billed (theoretical) Cost: the bundled-subscription portion.

Both are derived in the trace_summaries aggregation (sumIf-style if() over
the existing TotalCost column + Attributes marker), so no new ClickHouse
column or migration is needed. Total Cost stays the grand list-price total

Delete soft-archived a tile (archivedAt + enabled=false) but adminList

* feat(governance): add 'Add tools to the catalog' as the first setup step

The governance setup checklist skipped the catalog entirely. Add it as the
first step, checked once the org has at least one live catalog tile, so admins

* fix(governance): stamp bundled-cost marker on log-based OTLP ingest

Claude Code (and other coding assistants) emit OTLP *logs*, not spans, so
their traces flow through the /logs receiver path. Only the /traces path
resolved and stamped langwatch.cost.non_billable, so a real claude_code
session's cost was never marked bundled and read as real spend. Resolve
nonBillable on the log path too and pass it to the log provenance stamper.
Proven via a real langwatch claude (Max plan) dogfood: the trace lands with
non_billable=true and the cost splits to the theoretical bucket.

* feat(traces-v2): show 'Bundled' in purple instead of an em-dash for bundled cost

A fully-bundled trace billed nothing, so the cost pill / cell rendered a bare
em-dash that read as missing data. Show 'Bundled' in purple (the drawer pill
via a purple Chip tone, the table CostCell via purple text) so a bundled
coding session is legible at a glance; the popover / hover still breaks down
billed vs theoretical.

* test(governance): cover bundled-cost marker on the OTLP log path

Logs are the path coding assistants (Claude Code) actually use, so guard that
stampIngestKeyProvenanceOnLogRequest carries langwatch.cost.non_billable.

* feat(me): plot billed vs theoretical spend on the /me cost charts

The Spending-over-time and By-tool cards showed a single total (list-price)
series, so a bundled Claude Max session read as real spend. Split each into a
theoretical series (full list price, includes bundled) and a billed series
(actual per-token spend), derived from the langwatch.cost.non_billable marker

rescales to the visible series so a near-zero billed series still reads.

* fix(traces-v2): include current-hour turns in the conversation tab

The conversation-turns query floored its upper time bound to the current

in the current hour then sat after that bound and was excluded, so the
Conversation tab showed "No turns found" while the pager (which queries up
to now) still counted them. Round the bound up to the next hour instead:
the key stays stable within the hour and current-hour turns are covered.

* feat(traces-v2): add Thread layout to the conversation tab

Adds a ChatGPT-style Thread layout as the first (and default) render mode
on the drawer's Conversation tab, alongside Bubbles, Markdown and

column; bubbles keep spanning the pane. ChatTurnRow grows a `layout` prop
that swaps the side bubble for a full-width role row, reusing the same

Also fixes the turn-divider lines stopping short of the edge: the inline
hover actions reserved invisible width in flow, so the rules never reached
the container edge. They now float over one end, out of flow, and the lines
