* feat(traces-v2): reuse the enriched cost breakdown on the list's bundled cell

The trace list's bundled cost cell showed a flat one-line title tooltip
("Bundled plan, not billed per token. Billed —, theoretical $0.63."). Extract
the trace-details cost pill's breakdown into a shared CostBreakdownTooltipContent
and render it from the list cell, so hovering a bundled cost shows the same

* feat(traces-v2): thread turn opens Summary, drop the selected highlight

Clicking a turn in the conversation Thread layout now jumps to that turn's
Summary tab instead of the raw Trace tab, and applies the mode transiently so
peeking at a turn doesn't repoint the user's remembered drawer tab (new
setViewModeTransient + a persistViewMode flag on navigateToTrace). The active
turn also no longer carries a persistent gray background — it reads flat like
the rest of the thread, with only a transient hover cue.

* fix(traces-v2): surface claude utility-call output on the span

Claude Code sends the reply for its utility model calls (prompt_suggestion
autosuggest, generate_session_title) via api_response_body, but the converter
gated that text off the span for non-conversational query sources, so drilling
into a prompt_suggestion span showed no output even though the model returned
one. Attach the reply to every model-call span; the trace-level headline output
stays conversational-only by skipping claude utility spans in the fold
accumulation (the same way tool spans are skipped), so a suggestion or title
never becomes the trace's displayed output.

* feat(traces-v2): show span_id as the first row in span attributes

Inject the span id as a synthetic, always-first row in the span attributes
table so it's one-click copyable. It isn't a real OTel attribute, so it sorts
ahead of the alpha/pin order, is searchable + included in copy-all, and renders
non-pinnable (a synthetic key can't resolve a pinned trace-header value).

* fix(traces-v2): roll up bundled cost per span, not a trace-global boolean

A trace's LLM cost splits into the portion actually billed per token
(gateway / pay-per-token) and the bundled portion covered by a flat
subscription (e.g. Claude Max), which is theoretical. This was derived
all-or-nothing from a single hoisted trace-summary attribute
(langwatch.cost.non_billable), which cannot represent a trace that mixes
billed and bundled spans.

Fold a real per-span NonBilledCost amount instead: each span (and claude
log-record) cost is classified at fold time from the receiver-stamped
marker, a resource-level default a span can override, so a trace rolls up
two real amounts (billed = TotalCost - NonBilledCost). The marker is no
longer hoisted onto the trace attribute map.

All read paths (trace list, drawer router, analytics metric-translator,
/me personalUsage) read the folded amount and fall back to the legacy
boolean for rows folded before the column existed, so nothing reprojects.

Dogfood-verified on a real Claude Max session: NonBilledCost == TotalCost
for the bundled trace and the boolean no longer appears in Attributes.

* fix(me): restore personal usage rollups broken by aggregate-alias collision

The dailyBuckets and breakdownByModel queries aliased the outer cost
aggregate with the same name as the inner per-trace column
(sum(SpentUsd) AS SpentUsd), so the SpentUsd inside
sum(coalesce(SpentUsd, 0) - NonBilledUsd) bound to the outer aggregate and
ClickHouse rejected the query ("aggregate function is found inside another
aggregate function"). The throw rejected the /me Promise.all, collapsing
the whole personal-usage dashboard to an all-zero empty state with an
empty spend chart. Rename the inner column to TraceSpentUsd so the billed
split resolves against the subquery. Adds an integration test that
executes all three rollup queries against ClickHouse.

* fix(me): highlight the personal sidebar Traces and library entries

The personal sidebar hardcoded isActive={false} on Traces, Evaluations,
Datasets, Annotations and Automations, so none of them lit up when you
were on their per-project page. Derive active state from the current path
the same way MainMenu does for project nav.

* fix(me): blue spend palette, zero baseline ticks, and bar tooltips

The /me spend charts now use one blue family (light blue theoretical,
blue billed) instead of purple plus green, render a thin baseline tick on
every day so empty days still read on the timeline, and show a real hover
tooltip with the day plus theoretical and billed amounts on Spending over
time and By tool (replacing the bare title attribute).

* feat(claude-otlp): full-turn converter + truncation-tolerant tool-output recovery

Rework the claude-code log->span converter to fold a whole turn's logs at
once instead of one export batch, so a model call whose request body and
anchor land in different batches keeps both its input and output. Recover
each tool span's output from the next model call's tool_result transcript
block, scanning the real 60KB-truncated request body that does not JSON.parse.
Render a tool-deciding call's tool_use as its span output, and nudge an
incomplete span's StartTime so a later, more complete re-fold wins the
stored_spans max(StartTime) read dedup. Spec + unit tests bound to the new
scenarios; grounded against the real raw OTLP dumps.

* feat(claude-otlp): save claude logs + reactor folds them into a hierarchy of spans

Stop trapping claude_code model/tool/user_prompt logs at ingest. The receiver
now SAVES them to stored_log_records marked with langwatch.claude_code.kind, and
a new claudeCodeSpanSync reactor (tied to the logRecordStorage projection) reads
the whole turn's saved logs and folds them into spans: one root turn span (the
user_prompt, carrying the turn input) with the model and tool calls as children.

This is the event-sourced, ingestion-stateless, idempotent re-architecture: the
receiver holds no cross-batch state, and the reactor re-derives over the full
turn so a model call split across export batches keeps both input and output,
and each tool span recovers its output from the next call's transcript. Token
and cost are unchanged (they ride the derived span; the saved logs add none).
Gated on claude log events so the spans it emits never re-trigger it.

* fix(claude-otlp): fill truncated model-call input from the user prompt

The span-sync reactor now builds promptTextById from the turn's user_prompt
logs and passes it to the converter, so a model call whose request body claude
truncated inline (~60KB, every repl turn) shows the turn's prompt as its input
instead of an empty input. Dogfood-confirmed: model spans had output + cost but
no input because the bodies were 60KB-truncated and no fallback was passed.

* fix(governance): source CLI login summary from the AI tools catalog

The login ceremony listed env-fed project model providers under a 'Your
AI tools are ready' header, conflating two distinct concepts: it surfaced
openai (an unassigned, env-keyed provider) as a 'tool' while the coding
assistants the org actually published (claude, codex, ...) never showed.

cliBootstrap now sources both lists from the org's AI Tools catalog (the
same tiles the /me portal renders): coding_assistant tiles become the AI
tools the member can run via 'langwatch <slug>', and model_provider tiles
become the providers they can issue a virtual key for, each flagged
configured or not. The ceremony renders them as two clearly labelled
sections, and 'try it' only offers tools the org published (falling back
to the built-in wrappers when none are).

* fix(governance): align and lighten the $ prompt in tile command rows

The "$" shell-prompt prefix in the coding-assistant tile command boxes sat
above the command baseline, ran nearly as dark as the command text, and hugged
the box edge. Baseline-align it onto the command's first line, lighten it a
notch, and add a small left indent so it reads as a faint prompt.

* fix(governance): forget a pinned gateway path when it can't serve the org

When the user picks the gateway path at the prompt, the choice is saved to
tool_mode[tool]. If the gateway preflight then fails structurally (no virtual
key, or no provider configured for the org), the saved choice would re-fail on
every run with no way out. Clear the pin on those structural failures so the
next run re-asks and the user can pick direct OTLP instead. A transient
gateway-down failure keeps the pin, since a retry may succeed.

* fix(traces-v2): resolve ingest-key origin + surface cache tokens in the drawer

Two fold/read fixes the claude Path B dogfood surfaced:

- Origin: the ingest-key provenance stamps langwatch.origin onto the RESOURCE
  attributes (so an upstream payload can't forge it per span), but the fold's
  hoistOrigin only read SPAN attributes. Log-derived claude spans carry the
  origin only on the resource, so coding_agent never resolved at fold time and
  the trace decayed to the deferred 'application' fallback. hoistOrigin now
  falls back to the resource-level origin.

- Cache tokens: the trace list/header repository projects a fixed allow-list of
  attribute keys into trace.attributes, and the fold-summed
  langwatch.reserved.cache_read_tokens / cache_creation_tokens / reasoning_tokens
  were not in it, so the drawer header could never render the Cache read/write
  rows. Project those three reserved keys through too.

* feat(traces-v2): keep full claude request/response bodies on spans, expire folded logs

The Claude Code log->span fold kept only the light, readable
gen_ai.input.messages / gen_ai.completion on each model-call span. That
hides where a call's cache_creation / cache_read tokens come from: the
system prompt, every tool and skill schema, and the whole message history
all live in the request body and never reached the span.

Attach the verbatim request and response bodies as
langwatch.claude_code.request_body / response_body (capped at the same
256KB save-time ceiling) alongside the light view, so the full payload is
inspectable in the drawer's Span Attributes panel. A truncated body still
surfaces what we have rather than being dropped; only the readable input
stays clean.

Because the spans now carry every field the raw logs did, those folded
logs are pure duplication. Stamp the claude-kind rows in stored_log_records
with a one-day retention floor (the existing _retention_days DELETE TTL
does the eviction) instead of the platform default. One day clears the
longest single turn the fold re-reads as a set, while day granularity is
the floor of that TTL mechanism.

* fix(governance): keep the last-visited project sticky on the / redirect

The persona home resolver picks the DEFAULT `/` destination for a user
with no history (e.g. /me for a personal-VK persona). On top of that the
client was meant to let the last-visited home stick, but only one
direction was wired: index.tsx forced /me when the implicit
lastVisitedHomeKind was "personal", with no symmetric branch for
"project". So a user whose persona default is /me always bounced back to
/me even after deliberately switching into a project; the project never
stuck.

Add the missing symmetric branch via a pure resolveHomeDestination helper:
with no explicit picker pin, lastVisitedHomeKind === "project" returns to
the last-visited project's home (useOrganizationTeamProject resolves it
from selectedProjectSlug on a slug-less route), while "personal" still
sticks to /me where the governance UI is reachable. An explicit picker pin
always wins. /me stays the default only when there is no project history.

* fix(governance): / redirect lands on the bare project home and keeps /me sticky

Two follow-ups to the last-visited stickiness fix:

1. The project home is the bare /<slug> (pages/[project]/index renders
   HomePage), never /<slug>/messages, which is a legacy surface. Both the

2. /me stopped sticking: useOrganizationTeamProject wrote

* fix(governance): /me 'Spent this month' leads with billed, bundled in the subline

The card's headline was the theoretical list-price total (spentUsd), which
for a coding-assistant user is mostly bundled / non-billed spend (e.g. a

Mirror the 'Spent this month' card on the per-tool breakdown: the headline

perf(clickhouse): fix simulation projection get OOM via scalar latest-version filter (#4555)

getProjection read the latest version of a single simulation run with a
(TenantId, ScenarioRunId, UpdatedAt) IN (max-subquery) tuple predicate.
ClickHouse did not apply that as a PREWHERE on the version, so it
materialized the heavy Messages.* arrays across every version of the run
before discarding the stale ones. Runs with many snapshot versions
exceeded the server memory limit (Code 241, ~9.6 GiB reading
Messages.Content), and the read failed in prod.

Resolve the latest version with a scalar t.UpdatedAt = (SELECT max(...))
subquery instead. The equality is PREWHERE-able, so the light UpdatedAt
column is read first and the heavy columns are materialized for only the
single surviving row. This mirrors the sibling read path
(simulation.clickhouse.repository.ts getScenarioRunData), which already
uses the scalar form for the same reason. The IN-tuple form remains the
right choice for multi-key list reads.

Adds an integration test (real ClickHouse) covering latest-version
selection across many heavy-payload versions and tenant isolation, plus
a structural guard against regressing to the IN-tuple form.

perf(clickhouse): bound storage-metering query memory to stop _size_bytes OOM (#4556)

* perf(clickhouse): bound storage-metering query memory to stop _size_bytes OOM

The storage meter sums _size_bytes, a UInt32 MATERIALIZED byteSize(...)
column over each retention-managed table's payload columns. On parts
written before the column existed, ClickHouse recomputes it lazily on
read by scanning the heavy source columns (Inputs, Details, Messages.*,
EventPayload, ...). Summing across a large tenant reads those payloads
for every row; at the default thread count the parallel per-stream
buffers exceeded the per-query memory limit (Code 241, ~6.6 GiB reading
column Inputs against the 3.5 GiB cap), so the metering read failed.

Cap these cached, background metering queries to max_threads=2. Lower
parallelism keeps the recompute's peak well under the per-query limit so
it succeeds, and shrinks its share of total server memory so it can't
help tip the box into a server-wide OOM. The common case (parts where
_size_bytes is already materialized) reads a tiny UInt32 column and is
unaffected; results are unchanged.

perf(clickhouse): scalar latest-version filter for experiment getRun (#4570)

* perf(clickhouse): scalar latest-version filter for experiment getRun

getRun reads the latest version of a single experiment run with a
(TenantId, ExperimentId, RunId, UpdatedAt) IN (max-subquery) tuple
predicate. ClickHouse does not apply that as a PREWHERE on the version,
so it materializes the heavy columns (Targets and the full row) across
every version of the run before discarding the stale ones. For runs with
many snapshot versions this is the dominant uncovered slow-read shape
(p50 ~1.1s, hundreds/day).

Resolve the latest version with a scalar t.UpdatedAt = (SELECT max(...))
subquery instead. The equality is PREWHERE-able, so the heavy columns are
read for only the single surviving row. This mirrors the sibling
simulation/trace single-aggregate read paths. The IN-tuple form stays the
right choice for the multi-run list reads (listRuns) and for
experiment_run_items.

Adds an integration test (real ClickHouse) covering latest-version
selection across versions, not-found, and tenant isolation, plus a
structural guard against regressing to the IN-tuple form.

* fix(traces): route REST collector + track_event through shared span dedup gate

REST `/api/collector` and `/api/track_event` were dispatching `recordSpan`
directly, bypassing the `SpanDedupService.tryAcquireProcessingLock` short-
circuit that the OTLP collector uses. A client retry storm on a single

both REST paths through it. OTLP's existing `processSpan` now delegates
to the same method, so the dedup gate is the single source of truth and
the two ingestion paths cannot drift again.

* fix(nlpgo): stage oversized Lambda invoke payloads to S3

Workflow and evaluation runs invoke the per-project nlpgo Lambda via the AWS
SDK InvokeFunction operation, whose request Payload is capped at 6 MiB. The
sender (lambdaFetch) inlined the full body, so a large body failed with
'Request must be smaller than 6291456 bytes for the InvokeFunction operation'.

The S3 staging that the langevals HTTP path and the optimization-studio invoke
path already use was never wired into this path, even though the nlpgo engine's
receiver (readStudioRequestBody / staged_payload.go) already fetches a staged
body from the X-Payload-S3-URL header and the S3 bucket/credentials are already
configured. A half-wired migration gap: receiver + env ready, sender not.

- lambdaFetch (ARN branch): when the serialized invoke envelope exceeds the
  staging threshold, offload the body to S3, replace it with an empty body plus
  the X-Payload-S3-URL presigned-GET header, and delete the staged object in a
  finally so a failed invoke still reaps it. The size check is against the
  actual escaped envelope (mirrors the studio path), so a body that only crosses
  the cap after JSON-escaping is still staged.
- Threshold = LANGEVALS_STAGING_THRESHOLD_BYTES with a built-in 5 MiB fallback
  (under the 6 MiB cap) so a deploy with the env unset still stages.
- nlpgoFetch passes projectId through (scopes the S3 client + key; no-op for the
  self-hosted HTTP path).

No infra/env change needed - the bucket, credentials, threshold and the engine
receiver were already in place.

fix(traces): bind recordSpan command to GQ-layer deduplication (#4680)

The recordSpan command was registered without a `deduplication` strategy,
so STAGE_LUA's dedup branch was skipped and every dispatch unconditionally
added a fresh HSET field to the GroupQueue `:data` hash. Re-firing
reactors (claudeCodeSpanSync) and customer retry loops accumulated the
same span identity hundreds or thousands of times in a single trace's
hash — peak observed: ~292k fields, ~3.9 GB on one key.

Register with a deterministic dedup id keyed on
`(tenantId, traceId, spanId)` and a 30s TTL (matches the reactor TTL
precedent from PR #4167 one layer up). STAGE_LUA's squash branch now
fires on identity collision: latest payload wins (`extend: true,
replace: true`), the data hash is bounded by distinct identities.

PR #4677 (REST/OTLP `SpanDedupService` ingestion gate) and this change
are complementary: ingestion catches customer retries before dispatch;
this catches the reactor path inside the worker (past the ingestion

* fix(billing): show real monthly event count on usage page for metered seat plans

The /settings/usage "Events / Month" card showed 0 for seat-based
(GROWTH_SEAT_*) customers even while their events were metered and billed
correctly via Stripe.

Root cause: UsageService.getCurrentMonthCount() short-circuits to "unlimited"
when maxMessagesPerMonth >= UNLIMITED_MESSAGES (seat plans have no monthly
cap). usage-stats mapped that to null and the UI rendered `?? 0`, so the real
billable volume was never queried. Stripe was unaffected — it reports from a
separate billable_events pipeline.

Fix: separate display from enforcement.
- Add UsageService.getCurrentMonthCountForDisplay() that always computes the
  real count (events -> billable_events, traces -> trace_summaries per the
  meter policy), sharing the existing cache.
- getCurrentMonthCount() keeps its short-circuit for limit enforcement
  (checkLimit), so no extra queries on the hot path.
- usage-stats.getUsageStats() now uses the display count.
- UsageIndicator: re-guard the sidebar bar on maxMessagesPerMonth so uncapped
  plans (e.g. self-hosted unlimited license) don't render a meaningless ~0% bar
  now that the count is a real number.

Verified: full typecheck clean; 284 related unit tests pass, incl. a new
regression test (enforcement returns "unlimited" while display returns the real
metered total).

Make the two trace-usage mocks return distinct values and assert

counter. Addresses CodeRabbit review on #4548.

* docs(adr): ADR-021 — differential preview budget, manifest-shaped storage, reserved-namespace rules (#4215)

Three Consequences + two Rules added per Drew's review comment
(https://github.com/langwatch/langwatch/pull/4216#issuecomment-4563042455):

1. Differential preview byte budget — 32 KB for IO attrs, 2 KB default.
   Rationale: trace_summaries.ComputedInput/Output is the search column;
   a 2 KB preview silently truncates ILIKE matches past byte 2048. IO
   attrs get a preview = threshold (32 KB), preserving lossless search
   for sub-threshold values + covering the first 32 KB of offloaded
   ones. Redis fold cache leanness is on a separate knob (toCacheable),
   so raising the CH preview does not reintroduce the Redis clog.

2. One S3 object per span, manifest-shaped, not one per field. A 3-5
   over-threshold-field span costs one PUT instead of 3-5; read
   resolution coalesces N refs from one span into one GET. Per-span
   (not per-trace) because OTLP spans are atomic — one ingest = one
   PUT, idempotent under retry; per-trace would require cross-pod
   locking or LWW data loss.

3. Server-internal namespace must not leak to users. The
   langwatch.reserved.* prefix is server-owned; user-visible
   enumerations of SpanAttributes keys filter it out, and client-
   supplied attributes in that namespace are dropped at the edge
   (defense in depth alongside the project-prefix auth check on
   BlobStore.get).

* docs(adr): ADR-022 — event_log as single source of truth, S3 as transient spool (#4215)

Supersedes ADR-021's edge-permanent-S3 mechanism. Two design facts
implementation surfaced:

1. capOversizedAttributes(256 KB) already exists at the command-worker
   boundary. The unbounded-payload problem is narrower than ADR-021
   framed — it is the edge → command queue leg, where the full OTLP
   request rides through Redis BEFORE the cap fires. Everything
   downstream of the command worker was already bounded.

2. Commands go through a queue. commands.traces.recordSpan(data).send()
   stages the full command payload in Redis (GroupQueueProcessor). The
   event isn't in event_log when .send() returns. To lean the Redis
   pressure point, we must lean before .send() — which the new design
   does at the EDGE via size-check + S3 spool for oversize-only.

Decision (full ADR has the walkthrough):

- COMMAND_INLINE_THRESHOLD = 256 KB. Edge size-check; oversized goes
  to S3 spool transiently with {spoolRef} carried in the command.
- IO_PREVIEW_BYTES = 64 KB. Sized to a standard Claude response —
  covers ~16K tokens, the modal output at common max_tokens settings.
  Search via ILIKE on the preview column stays lossless for the modal
  case.
- Interposition at eventSourcingService.ts:242-251 calls
  leanForProjection(event) between storeEvents and router.dispatch.
  Single hook; all projection types downstream see lean events.
- event_log carries FULL content (ZSTD-compressed). Single durable
  source of truth. Replay-sufficient.
- Replay applies the SAME leanForProjection utility before invoking
  projection handlers — live and replay produce byte-identical
  projection state.
- BlobStore stays as the swap-seam interface. Backend changes: put
  writes transient S3 spool, get reads event_log row by EventId.

What survives from ADR-021: differential preview budget (now 64 KB IO
attrs / 2 KB default), reserved-namespace strip (already at command
worker), facet-enumeration filter, toCacheable for non-IO ephemera.

What is rejected: edge per-field offload to permanent S3, manifest-
shaped storage, sha256-per-field integrity check, project-prefix
auth on BlobStore (cross-tenant now structurally blocked by CH
TenantId WHERE), BlobIntegrityError.

Includes the new dataflow diagram (DOT source + rendered PNG).

fix(spa): make route chunk-load failures recoverable instead of permanent (#4697)

* fix(spa): give the stuck chunk-load error boundary a real escape hatch

The Vite/React-Router SPA lazy-loads each route as its own content-hashed
chunk. When a chunk fetch fails (transient edge race, flaky/proxied network,
an extension or AV blocking the request, or a stale-deploy hash), the
recovery reloaded once then dead-ended: the 10s cooldown blocked every
further reload, freezing the failure into a permanent "Failed to fetch
dynamically imported module" error boundary with no escape. Surfaced via a
customer report on /messages (an empty project) while /traces loaded fine.

- NotFoundOrErrorPage now detects chunk-load errors (isChunkLoadError) and
  shows a "Reload app" button plus an extension/network hint. The button
  records the reload in the cooldown (so the post-reload auto-recovery doesn't
  immediately fire a second reload when the chunk still fails) then reloads —
  a real, repeatable escape for persistent failures. Generic errors and 404s
  are unchanged.
- The existing reloadOnChunkError reload still recovers the stale-deploy case
  (fresh document = fresh hashes).

No same-URL import retry: failed dynamic imports are cached by URL in the
browser module map (HTML spec), so re-importing the same URL returns the
cached rejection with no new request; only a distinct URL (cache-bust /
service worker) would help — deferred. Server build verified healthy (failing
chunk + full closure 200, correct MIME, no-cache HTML, clean 404s); this is
purely client-side fetch resilience.

* fix(static): eliminate TOCTOU race and unhandled stream errors in asset serving

The static file handler used existsSync + createReadStream with no error
handler, creating two failure modes:

1. TOCTOU race: file deleted between check and read (e.g. mid-deploy)
   produced an unhandled stream error that bubbled up as HTTP 500.
2. Any I/O error during streaming had no handler, crashing the response.

A customer reported HTTP 500 on /assets/CopyableInputWithPrefix-*.js,
which cascaded into a "Failed to fetch dynamically imported module" error
on the /messages page (the only page that renders WelcomeLayout → APICard
→ CopyableInputWithPrefix for empty projects).

Fix: open the file descriptor atomically with openSync (single syscall,
no race window), then stream from the fd with an error handler that
returns 500/destroys the connection cleanly. Same treatment for the SPA
index.html fallback stream.

* fix(static): address CodeRabbit review — named params, BDD test nesting, drop jsdom location hack

- Convert tryServeFile, tryServeSpaFallback, pipeWithErrorHandling to
  object-destructured parameters per project convention
- Restructure TOCTOU regression test with given/when BDD nesting
- Remove Object.defineProperty(window, 'location') from not-found test

* test(static): execute the stream-error crash path in serveStaticOrFallback

Addresses the remaining CodeRabbit finding (static-handler.unit.test.ts): the
prior 'TOCTOU' case only deleted the file before the request, exercising the
openSync ENOENT→404 path, not pipeWithErrorHandling's stream-error branch it
claimed to cover. Adds a deterministic test that mocks createReadStream to emit

* fix(rbac): resolve team membership reads via RoleBindings, not legacy TeamUser

Team membership is written only to RoleBinding since the TeamUser->RoleBinding
migration (20260407120000), but several read paths still queried the legacy
TeamUser relation, so any member added after the migration was invisible to them:

- team.getTeamWithMembers: a member added on the team settings page vanished on
  refresh.
- team.getTeamsWithMembers: post-migration members missing from member pickers,
  drawers, and onboarding.
- team.getBySlug: a post-migration member failed the access gate (returned null).
- POST /api/mcp/authorize: the same member got a false 403 "Project not found or
  you don't have access" when authorizing an MCP connection.

All membership reads now go through the service/repository layer (no raw Prisma
in routers/routes):
- New RoleBindingRepository.listTeamScopedUserBindingsByTeamIds (one query for N
  teams, grouped by teamId — no N+1); TeamService gains getTeamWithMembers /
  getTeamsWithMembers / getTeamBySlugForUser sharing one binding->member mapping
  that dedupes to one row per user (highest-privilege wins, since a user may hold
  multiple bindings at one scope), sorted nulls-last to match the prior Prisma
  orderBy.
- MCP authorize fetches the project via ProjectService.getById and authorizes
  with hasProjectPermission(project:view). This is intentionally broader than the
  old direct-team-member check: it also admits org admins and project-scoped
  bindings (the latter were wrongly denied before despite having project access).

Write path: a user can hold a built-in role plus additive custom-role bindings on
one team (RBAC unions them). The settings form shows/edits only the displayed
(highest-privilege) binding, so team.update updates just that binding and
preserves the user's other bindings — deleting them would let a routine autosaved
edit silently revoke custom-role grants. Removing a user from the team still drops
all of their bindings.

Security: the demo project grants project:view to everyone via isDemoProject, so
MCP authorize now rejects the demo project up front — otherwise any authenticated
user could mint an auth code embedding the demo project's API key (the old
TeamUser check happened to block this).

path, the demo-project guard, and the no-binding denial; converts the member-leak
privacy fixtures to TEAM-scoped RoleBindings.

fix(ops): self-heal GroupQueue pending counter drift via ground-truth reconcile (#4684)

* fix(ops): self-heal GroupQueue pending counter drift via ground-truth reconcile

The global `gq:stats:total-pending` counter drifts upward over time: it INCRs
at stage and DECRs at dispatch/complete, but the DECR is lost on ungraceful
worker death, the 6h safety-net `:jobs` TTL reap, and MOVE_TO_DLQ (deletes
`:jobs` without a DECR). The existing reconcile only repairs parked-group /
dynamic-cap state — it never recomputes the pending counter, so drift never
heals. Observed ~12% over-count in production.

Add a low-cadence (60s), single-flighted reconcile that recomputes
`total-pending = Σ ZCARD` over the live group set and writes it back. It runs
off the hot dispatch path, is gated by a dedicated marker key so only one pod
recomputes per window, and surfaces the corrected drift as `pendingDrift` in
the ops dashboard model. The counter is read-only metadata (nothing reads it
for dispatch decisions), so overwriting to ground truth is safe.

The structural DECR-at-dispatch Lua rewrite is deliberately out of scope (higher
risk; the naive version inverts drift via the retry paths) — the reconcile heals
every leak path regardless of cause.

* feat(modelProviders): provider-disabled toast with parent-scope swap

When the cascade resolves a feature to a model whose backing provider
is currently disabled, we used to throw a generic Error with the
disabled-state string baked in. The frontend interceptor had no way
to discriminate it from any other error, so the user saw a generic
red toast pointing at "Settings" with no idea WHICH scope or model
was the problem, or that a parent-scope default was sitting one click
away.

This commit:

- Introduces ModelProviderDisabledError carrying featureKey,
  featureDisplayName, role, resolvedScope, resolvedModel, providerKey,
  and an optional alternate (the cascade-next candidate with its own
  scope / model / providerKey / providerEnabled).
- Adds findAlternateBelowScope() in resolveModelForFeature so the
  utils path can populate the alternate without re-walking the full
  cascade itself.
- Updates getVercelAIModel to throw the typed error instead of the
  generic Error string.
- Adds the typed error to errorFormatterForTesting + domainError
  middleware in trpc.ts so the cause crosses the wire with a stable
  code ("MODEL_PROVIDER_DISABLED").
- Adds extractProviderDisabledInfo +
  markAsHandledByProviderDisabledHandler in trpcError.ts.
- Adds showProviderDisabledToast in MissingModelToast.tsx. When the
  cascade has an alternate AND the disabled scope is "project" (so the
  current user can definitely clear it), the toast's primary CTA reads
  "Use organization default (azure/gpt-4o)" and clicking it calls
  setFeatureOverrideForScope({ scopeType: "PROJECT", scopeId, featureKey,
  model: null }) — which deletes the disabled scope's key for that
  feature, freeing the cascade to fall through to the alternate on
  the next attempt. When the swap isn't safe (different disabled
  scope, no alternate, alternate's provider also disabled), the
  toast falls back to its "Open settings" deep-link variant.
- Wires the interceptor into both the mutationCache and queryCache
  in utils/api.tsx with a providerDisabledSwapHandler that gates the
  one-click swap on permission + alternate availability.

feat(traces): codex/opencode trace fidelity, reasoning effort, and infra-span noise filter (#4669)

* feat(traces): codex/opencode Path B fidelity, reasoning effort, hide cost marker

Audit-driven fixes for coding-agent Path B trace fidelity plus the two
cost/reasoning gaps surfaced while dogfooding:

- codex: stop double-counting tokens. codex emits the turn rollup span
  (session_task.turn) AND a redundant response span (handle_responses)
  carrying the same usage; the fold summed both, inflating token totals ~2x.
  The extractor now flags the redundant span
  (langwatch.reserved.skip_token_accumulation) and the fold skips its
  token/cache accumulation, so the trace total counts the usage once while
  per-span detail is untouched.
- codex: capture reasoning. Lift codex.turn.token_usage.reasoning_output_tokens
  to gen_ai.usage.reasoning_tokens and codex.turn.reasoning_effort to
  gen_ai.request.reasoning_effort.
- opencode: capture tool calls. The Vercel extractor lifts ai.toolCall.
  {name,args,result} to gen_ai.tool.name + langwatch.input/output on tool spans.
- reasoning effort: lift gen_ai.request.reasoning_effort onto the trace
  summary and show it as a pill next to the model in the drawer header, the
  same way models are surfaced.
- bundled cost marker: keep langwatch.cost.non_billable as the internal
  fold-time signal but stop surfacing it in the drawer resources view (it is
  cost-classification plumbing, not user metadata; the billed/bundled split
  shows as real amounts).

Specs in specs/trace-processing/coding-agent-trace-fidelity.feature, bound to
unit + fold tests. gemini reasoning capture and a suspected gemini
input/output double-count are entangled with the shared log-fold path and
need empirical replay verification; tracked as follow-up.

* feat(traces): filter codex/opencode infra spans at ingestion

codex (scope codex_cli_rs) and opencode (scope opencode) export their entire
internal call graph over OTLP: DB queries, file IO, config, auth, websockets,
session init, plugin enumeration. A single "hello" produced 136 spans across 18
trace ids for codex, and 798 spans across 45 trace ids for opencode (including
227 sql.execute spans), with only 2 traces each containing any model/tool
activity. The rest are infra-only fragment traces that bury the AI signal and
bloat storage.

Drop the non-AI spans at ingestion for those two KNOWN tools, keeping only the
turn/model/tool spans (gen_ai / ai semantics). Gated strictly on the
instrumentation scope name, so any OTHER OTLP (customer apps, custom SDKs,
OpenInference, raw OTLP) is never touched. A trace whose spans are all filtered
never gets created, which removes the infra-only fragment traces. Filtered
spans are counted separately (spans.ingestion.filtered) and are not rejections.

Kill-switch: LANGWATCH_DISABLE_CODING_AGENT_SPAN_FILTER=true restores full
fidelity. Specs + unit tests cover the keep/drop sets and the
other-scopes-are-never-touched guarantee.

* feat(analytics): add cache-read/write, reasoning, and total-processed token metrics

Reads the cache/reasoning sums from the trace_summaries Attributes map at

(reasoning is a subset of output, not added). Verified against real traces

* fix(codex): narrow skip-token marker to known duplicate span name

The redundant-usage marker was set on every non-turn codex_cli_rs span
carrying gen_ai.usage, which would silently drop tokens, cost, and cache
from the trace summary if a future codex release emits a model-call span
whose usage is not folded into the session_task.turn rollup. Narrow the
skip to the known duplicate (handle_responses) and keep the llm typing
for any usage-bearing span. An unrecognised usage span now keeps its

* feat(cli): recover codex turn input/output from the rollout transcript

Codex's native OTLP spans (scope codex_cli_rs) carry tokens, model, and
timing but never the prompt or the assistant reply - codex puts no
content on the wire. It DOES persist the full conversation to disk as a
JSONL rollout whose per-turn task_started records the exact OTLP trace_id
codex used for that turn's spans.

After a wrapped 'langwatch codex' Path B session exits, the wrapper reads
the rollout, pairs each turn's user prompt with the assistant's final
message, and POSTs one OTLP span per turn carrying langwatch.input /
langwatch.output on codex's own trace_id. The span joins the existing
token-spans on the same trace, so the trace summary's computed
input/output populate with zero receiver changes. Output is the assistant
reply recovered from the transcript - the only place codex exposes it.

Best-effort and fully swallowed: a coding session never fails on the
post-hoc content harvest.

* fix(cli): cap codex rollout I/O POST so it can't wedge shell on exit

* feat(cli): recover codex full request body (system prompt + tool calls) as chat_messages

The codex rollout parser now reconstructs each turn's full request body as a

results) instead of a flat prompt string. Emitted on langwatch.input as the
structured { type: chat_messages } envelope, the receiver canonicalises it to
gen_ai.input.messages + gen_ai.system_instructions, so a codex trace renders the
same full conversation a claude trace does. Verified end-to-end against a real
rollout: the 11.7KB system prompt lands on gen_ai.system_instructions and the
exec_command tool call renders in the drawer.

* fix(governance): reset project/team context on ?org= switch so /me re-resolves

The org resolver pins org-scoped pages to the previously selected project's org

and selectedTeamId on an actual org change lets the new org take effect; the

* refactor(cli): extract CodexTurnAccumulator from parseCodexRollout

CodeRabbit flagged parseCodexRollout as exceeding the 60-line / complexity-10

* fix(cli): pair id-less codex tool calls to their outputs by FIFO order

A function_call/function_call_output that codex emits without a call_id fell
back to call_${history.length}, which differs between the call (length N) and
its output (length N+1), so the pair would never join. Mint one synthetic id per
id-less call and FIFO-match it on the output instead. Real rollouts always carry
a call_id, so this only changes the previously-broken fallback path (verified
byte-identical across every local rollout).

the layout looked orphaned. Nest each governance personal under its org header
regardless of org count, and render the org header whenever the org has a
personal under it (or the user spans multiple orgs). A lone non-governance org
stays header-free, its context implicit.

usePreviewTracesActive only checked tourActive, while useOnboardingActive

* fix(cli): clear codex synthetic tool-call queue at turn boundaries

pendingToolCallIds queues synthetic ids for id-less function_calls so the
matching id-less function_call_output pairs back to the same id. The queue
was an instance field that persisted across turns: a call left unmatched at
a turn boundary (its output never arrived) would leak its queued id into the
next turn, where the first id-less output would shift it off and mispair to
the previous turn's orphaned call.

Clear the queue in closeTurn() so synthetic fallback ids are valid only
within the turn that minted them. autoToolCallSeq stays monotonic so the
ids themselves remain unique across the session. Adds a regression test
covering the cross-turn case.

* fix(traces): show the system prompt in the span Input panel

The canonicaliser splits the system message out of gen_ai.input.messages
into gen_ai.system_instructions (OTel semconv), so the drawer's Input panel
- which renders gen_ai.input.messages - silently dropped it: a codex/claude
transcript read as if nothing steered the model, even though the prompt was
captured in the raw langwatch.input.value.

Recombine them for display in mapSpanToDetail: when a span's input is a chat
transcript with no system message of its own and it carries system
instructions, prepend them as a leading system message. Done at the display
boundary (not the canonicaliser) so the stored attribute split stays semconv-
correct while Pretty/Text/JSON/Copy all stay consistent. Tolerates both flat-
dotted and nested param shapes.

* fix(traces): show a disabled pin on the span_id attribute row

The synthetic span_id row rendered a blank gap where every other attribute
shows a pin, so the column read as ragged. Render a disabled, extra-faded,
non-interactive pin with a tooltip explaining why it can't be pinned to the
trace header instead - the column now reads consistently top to bottom.

* fix(cli): gate the gateway path on a coding tile + configured credential, not a provider tile

The gateway preflight blocked `langwatch <tool>` with 'No <family> provider
is configured' whenever the org had no model_provider catalog tile - even
with dozens of enabled provider credentials. That tile only gates the /me
one-click mint-your-own-VK surface; the gateway actually routes through the
org's configured credentials. An admin who set up providers at
/settings/model-providers (but never published a provider tile) was wrongly
blocked, and the error pointed back at the page where everything was already
configured.

Surface the configured credential families (gatewayProviders, membership-
scoped via listConfiguredProvidersForUser) on cliBootstrap and gate the
preflight on them instead. Keep the gateway opt-in per tool via the coding-
assistant tile: no tile for the tool means the org hasn't enabled the gateway
for it (block, point at the AI Tools catalog); a published coding tile plus a
configured credential is enough, no provider tile required. Falls back to the
provider tile list on legacy servers that don't send gatewayProviders.

* feat(cli): stream codex turn I/O during the session, not one burst on exit

Codex exposes prompt/reply content only in its append-only rollout JSONL

perf(clickhouse): scope model-cost matching-spans preview to candidate traces (#4734)

perf(clickhouse): scope model-cost sample-span read to candidate traces

The model-cost rule preview's sample-span read (findRecentSpansByModels) filters
stored_spans by 'Model IN', a predicate computed from the SpanAttributes map, so
it decodes that heavy map for every span in the 7-day window just to evaluate
the filter. On a busy project that is a multi-second scan, and it fires on every
(debounced) keystroke that has a match.

Narrow first: pull the recent traces that use one of the matched models from
trace_summaries.Models (a small, deduped, bloom-indexed Array(String) written at
fold time), then constrain the span scan with TraceId IN (candidate set).
stored_spans is ORDER BY (TenantId, TraceId, SpanId), so the TraceId set prunes
via the primary index to those traces' granules before any SpanAttributes map is
decoded. The in-stored_spans selection (light columns, argMax dedup, token-first
ordering, LIMIT BY model) is unchanged, so the sample list is the same.

Trade-off: the sample now depends on trace_summaries being folded for a trace
(seconds of lag), which is acceptable for a best-effort preview. Models is
complete per trace, so a matched model cannot be dropped from the candidate set.

The findModelUsageStats inventory read is intentionally left on stored_spans:
it must catch rare models reliably and cannot be sampled or window-shortened.

fix(api-key): stop misclassifying legacy project keys that contain underscores (#4730)

Legacy project keys are random strings from alphabets that include _ and -.
getTokenType treated any sk-lw- token containing an underscore as a
new-format {lookupId}_{secret} API key, so such legacy keys went down the
ApiKey lookup path, missed, and got a 401 with no fallback.

Classify sk-lw- tokens as API keys only when the body matches the exact
generated shape (16-char lookupId, 48-char alphanumeric secret), and fall
back to the legacy project key lookup when an sk-lw- token misses the
ApiKey lookup, so look-alike legacy keys still authenticate.

fix(event-sourcing): reclaim blobs displaced by GroupQueue dedup squash (#4758)

* fix(event-sourcing): reclaim blobs displaced by GroupQueue dedup squash

A dedup squash overwrites a staged payload in place inside the stage Lua.
Since #4726 moved >32 KiB bodies to standalone `gq:blob:*` keys, the
displaced value's blob was never reclaimed and leaked until its 7-day TTL,
driving Redis toward the noeviction wall under large-span ingestion (the
reactor re-folding `recordSpan`, which is extend+replace per #4680).

The stage scripts now report the displaced value and GroupQueue reclaims its
blob through the existing deleteEnvelopeBlobs path: on replace the old stored
value, otherwise the discarded new value, covering every extend/replace combo.
The reclaim only does a round-trip when a blob actually exists, so inline
traffic is unaffected. Forward-only (rollback unsafe with GQ1| in flight);
clearing the existing orphans is an operational follow-up.

perf(clickhouse): thread occurredAtMs hint through the trace peek preview (#4785)

* perf(clickhouse): thread occurredAtMs hint through the trace peek preview

The trace peek preview (`TraceIdPeek` / `TracePreviewHoverCard`) fetches a
trace summary by id only, with no `occurredAtMs` partition hint. `trace_summaries`
is partitioned on `OccurredAt`, so a `traceId`-only read cannot prune partitions
and walks every weekly partition including the cold S3 tier, turning a ~100ms
lookup into ~1s.

This adds an optional `occurredAtMs` prop to the peek components, forwards it to
the `tracesV2.header` summary query, and passes it as the drawer's `t` partition
hint when the eye icon opens the drawer. Call sites that already have the row's
timestamp (conversation turns, annotations table) now thread it; sites without a
timestamp fall back to the unconstrained by-id fetch unchanged.

EXPLAIN INDEXES on a known-large tenant: the by-id read walks 303/303 parts
(10,063 granules) at the MinMax/Partition stage; the hinted read prunes to
12/305 parts (144 granules).

perf(clickhouse): backfill drawer occurredAtMs hint from the resolved header (#4786)

* perf(clickhouse): backfill drawer occurredAtMs hint from the resolved header

When the trace drawer opens from a deep link or a refresh whose URL carries no
`t` timestamp, its `occurredAtMs` partition hint is null. Every per-trace read it
fires then runs unconstrained: the summary header by-id scans all `trace_summaries`
partitions, and the span tree / events / signals reads cold-scan every
`stored_spans` weekly partition including the S3 tier.

The header response already carries the trace's real `occurredAt`. This feeds it
back into the drawer store via a new idempotent `backfillOccurredAtMs` action
(sets only when the hint is currently null, never overwriting an opener-supplied
value). Once set, the drawer's other per-trace reads and any header refetch prune
to the trace's weekly partitions. A cold deep-link still pays one unconstrained
header fetch; everything after it for that open drawer is bounded.

* fix(review): SpanTimestamps fields documented as optional with fallback, named params in test helper

* fix(ci): give the dedup-squash dispatch test BRPOP-net headroom

The pre-dispatch squash test is the only one whose stage signals all
fire before dispatchAfter, so its dispatch rides the 5s BRPOP
idle-rescan instead of a signal. On loaded CI runners that net plus
worker overhead exceeded the 10s assertion ceiling twice in a row.
Same ceiling class as the TOCTOU dispatch-gap flake; 30s gives the
net 3x headroom.

* fix(cost): trust explicit/provider-reported cost over the registry estimate

computeSpanCost ranked the static model-registry computation (priority 2)
ahead of the explicit langwatch.span.cost (priority 3), so for a known
model with token counts the registry estimate silently overrode an
authoritative cost. Two real consequences:

- the SDK metrics.cost override (documented for negotiated/custom
  pricing) only took effect for unknown models or missing tokens
- Claude Code turns, which carry Anthropic's own billed cost_usd, were
  re-estimated from the registry for every on-table claude model
  instead of using Anthropic's authoritative figure

Move the explicit/provider cost ahead of the registry (still behind the
per-token enrichment-rate policy, which is the deliberate 'price my way'
override). A zero or absent explicit cost still falls through to the
registry, so spans that never reported a cost are unaffected. Audited
every langwatch.span.cost writer first: the only two are the explicit
SDK metrics blob and Anthropic's cost_usd, both authoritative; no
auto-estimate path exists, so the reorder cannot regress a computed
cost into a stale one.

Regression tests: known model + tokens + explicit cost, on-table claude
+ cost_usd, zero-cost fallthrough, and enrichment-rate precedence.
Updates the claude-code mapper comment and the cost docs to match.

* style: biome format the cost-precedence changes

* fix(licensing): make license generation round-trip test time-independent

The test issued a license at a fixed 2025-06-15 with the standard
one-year validity (expires 2026-06-15), then round-trip validated it
against the real wall clock. From 2026-06-16 on, the 4 validation
assertions failed with EXPIRED — a latent time bomb unrelated to any
code change, tripping purely on the calendar.

validateLicense now threads an optional injectable `now` (defaulting
to the real clock, mirroring the isExpired signature it already calls),
and the round-trip tests validate at the license's own issue time, so
they stay green regardless of when the suite runs. Production callers
are unaffected: the new parameter defaults to new Date().

* feat(nlpgo): if/else conditional branch node

New if_else component: evaluates a Liquid boolean expression (the
language users already know from prompt templates) over its inputs and
emits {true, false} branch outputs. The engine gates downstream nodes
on the emitted booleans:

- Edges from an if/else branch handle act as gates, grouped per gate
  node: at least one taken branch per gate or the target is skipped
  (status "skipped", zero cost, never dispatched); connecting both
  handles of one gate makes a merge point that runs either way
- Skips cascade: a node whose inbound edges all come from skipped or
  errored sources is skipped too; merge-at-end nodes with one live
  branch still run and simply miss the dead inputs
- EvaluateCondition fails loudly on conditions referencing inputs the
  node doesn't have — Liquid's nil semantics would silently flip
  comparisons like context != "" to true — and on parse errors
  (invalid_condition node error)
- Streamed runs emit component_state_change{status:"skipped"} so the
  studio can paint not-taken branches

* fix(event-sourcing): wake the dispatcher when the earliest ready group is due

Delayed groups had no wake at their due time: the send-time signals
fire while the job is still inside its dispatch delay (and the
post-dispatch drain eats any that land mid-cycle), so dispatch waited
out the full fixed BRPOP poll. The TOCTOU squash test rode that 5s
fallback, passing at 5.6s locally and starving past its 10s budget on
slower CI runners, which is what has kept main red since #4726 landed.

The dispatcher now peeks the earliest ready score and clamps the BRPOP
timeout to it, so a due group dispatches on time and a past-due score
(e.g. a signal lost to the drain) self-heals at the floor instead of
the full interval. When the processing queue is saturated the fixed
interval applies as before, so a backed-up worker does not hot-poll.

* fix(studio): make the agent node's DSL snapshot the source of truth

A library agent dragged into a workflow lives in three places: the
agent record, the node's DSL parameters (what the engine executes),
and the drawer editor. The drawer derived everything from the record
fetch: Save cleared the draft, which re-armed a reset effect against
the stale query cache and visibly reverted the edit; a slow or failed
fetch mounted the editor on the starter template over the user's real
code; and Save never wrote the node's parameters, so the workflow kept
executing the old code until the agent was re-dragged.

The node snapshot is now canonical in-workflow state: the editor
derives from it synchronously (draft, then snapshot, then record),
Save writes the submitted values through to the record, the node, and
the query cache in one motion (nothing on screen can revert, the next
run executes the save, no refetch race), and the record only overlays
the node when its content genuinely changed elsewhere and no draft is
in the way. Agent drafts also merge into studio dispatches now, like
prompt drafts always did. The record-to-node builders live in one
shared module used by the picker and the panel.

* feat(studio): allow mutually exclusive branches to converge on one input

An If/Else fork was a dead end: the canvas blocked any second edge into
an input (Cannot connect two values to the same input), so two branches
could never rejoin a single end output.

The Go engine already executes convergent DAGs correctly (shouldSkip
skips the not-taken branch, resolveInputs ignores sources that produced
nothing), so only the frontend gate needed to change. onConnect now
allows a second source on an input when it is mutually exclusive with
the existing source(s), decided by a guards analysis that mirrors the
engine: two sources may share an input only when they sit on opposite
sides of the same If/Else gate. Sources that can run together (two
independent nodes, or two outputs of one node) stay blocked with a clear
message.

Tests: guards/mutual-exclusivity unit tests, store onConnect integration
tests, and Go execution tests proving a converged input deterministically
carries the taken branch value in both directions.

* fix(engine): autoparse string inputs to declared types for code and if/else

A dataset cell or form field arrives as a string, so a python if/else
condition like `amount > 5` over an input declared `float` raised
"'>' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int'". The Go engine
passed inputs to the code sandbox untouched, dropping the input type
coercion langwatch_nlp's field_parser.autoparse_field_value used to do.

Both python execution paths (code block and if/else python condition)
now coerce each string input to its declared input type (float, int,
bool, list, dict) before running, leaving already-typed and unparseable
values alone. Covered by helper unit tests and a real-sandbox execution
test.

* fix(nlpgo): autoparse liquid if/else inputs so numeric comparisons work

The default Liquid if/else condition evaluated a numeric comparison like "question > 5" as false for every value, including 6. The input arrived as the string "6" (datasets and form fields carry strings), and Liquid treats a string-vs-number comparison as a type mismatch that yields false. The python condition and code paths already coerce inputs to their declared types via autoparseInputs; the liquid path did not. Apply the same coercion before EvaluateCondition so "6" reaches Liquid as 6 and "6 > 5" routes true. Proven by a real-engine integration test (6 > 5 true, 4 > 5 false).

fix(experiments-v3): multimodal image split and abort for interactive workbench runs (#4756)

* fix(nlpgo): split image data URLs into multimodal content parts

Vision workflows interpolated dataset image data URLs into message TEXT,
so the model received base64 bytes as literal text (inside the system
message in the reported case) and could only guess. The Python engine
split text-with-image into OpenAI content parts via DSPy; the Go engine
never did. buildMessages output now passes through
splitMessagesWithImages: every inline data:image URL becomes an
image_url part with surrounding text as text parts, and a system
message containing an image keeps only its leading text while the image
and what follows move to a user message, since providers reject image
parts in system role. Downstream (executor filtering, gateway, Bifrost)
already forwards part arrays untouched.

* fix(experiments-v3): authorize abort for interactive workbench runs

Interactive workbench runs stream over SSE and never create a polling
run-state record, so the abort endpoint's ownership check (which only
read runStateManager) 404'd every run and the Stop button reported
"Abort Failed". The orchestrator now records the run owner via
abortManager.setRunning, and the abort route authorizes against that
running-owner, falling back to run-state for the CI/CD polling path.
The cross-tenant guard is preserved.

* fix(experiments-v3): interrupt in-flight stream read on abort

After the abort flag is honored, a cell already blocked waiting on a slow
LLM response kept running until that response arrived, because the abort
was only checked between chunks. The stream read now races the abort flag,
so an abort interrupts the pending read and cancels the reader. Cancelling
the reader disconnects nlpgo, whose request context then cancels the
in-flight execution (the Go engine treats client disconnect as the cancel
signal, so no Go change is needed).

* test(nlpgo): live vision e2e proving dataset images reach the model as image parts

The test pins LANGWATCH_NLP_SERVICE at the subprocess it spawns:
nlpgoFetch only consults the mocked lambda ARN when
LANGWATCH_NLP_LAMBDA_CONFIG is set, so with a dev .env loaded it was
silently routing to whatever long-running nlpgo sat on the ambient URL,
testing a stale build instead of this worktree's engine.

* fix(experiments-v3): make abort scenarios user-observable

CodeRabbit flagged the two abort scenarios in execution-backend.feature
for asserting internals (reader cancelled, run-state record, registered
owner, abort flag) instead of externally observable behavior. Rewrite both
to describe what the user sees (the run stops, no further results) and
update the @scenario bindings to match.

* fix(nlpgo): match uppercase BASE64 data URLs in the multimodal split

RFC 2397 allows uppercase in the media type and the ;base64 token, so
the split regex is now case-insensitive. Also rewords the feature-file
binding note: runSignature applies the split to buildMessages output.

* test(nlpgo): bind the uppercase BASE64 split to its own scenario

* feat(dev): auto-start nlpgo from pnpm dev alongside the gateway

pnpm dev already boots the Go aigateway so the CLI wrappers reach a live
gateway without a second terminal, but nlpgo had no equivalent, so the
experiments workbench, playground and scenarios needed a separate
`make service svc=nlpgo` to work locally. start.sh now schedules nlpgo the
same way: it binds the port the app calls (LANGWATCH_NLP_SERVICE, default
:5561 = PORT+1), points the engine callbacks back at the local app, reuses an
already-listening nlpgo, and skips when the Go toolchain is absent or
LANGWATCH_NLP_SERVICE points at a remote host. Opt out with
LANGWATCH_SKIP_NLPGO=1.

The start-or-skip decision and the nlpgo bind-port resolution move into a
sourced helper (go-service-autostart.sh) so the gateway and nlpgo share one
contract and the logic is unit-testable with bats. `make start` collapses to a
thin `pnpm dev` alias now that bundling nlpgo into it makes the old
concurrently wrapper redundant, and `make test-scripts` runs the langwatch
bats directory too.

Tested: dev-autostart.unit.bats (decision + port resolution, mocked go/lsof),
feature-parity binding for specs/setup/pnpm-dev-process-autostart.feature, and
a live boot of nlpgo via the exact emitted command (GET /healthz -> 200).

* fix(nlpgo): give LWA-reconstructed requests 8MB of header room

net/http's 1MB MaxHeaderBytes default rejects oversized header sections
with a pre-handler 431 that never reaches handler logging, leaving no
trace in any log group.

OpenAI's edge intermittently rejects ordinary requests with the bare
body "Request headers are too large." (reproduced on a direct
litellm-to-OpenAI CI run with no LangWatch in the path). Surfaced
verbatim it reads as a LangWatch infrastructure failure, so upstream
rejections now carry the provider name: "openai: Request headers are
too large.". The reason itself stays verbatim.

* fix(experiments-v3): keep the workbench grid beside the nav menu, not under it

The experiments workbench rendered inside DashboardLayout with
compactMenu={true}. The compact menu is a 56px rail whose inner box is
position:absolute, zIndex 100, and expands to a 200px overlay on hover (see
MainMenu), covering the grid's leftmost columns: the row-select checkbox and
the first dataset cell (the image thumbnails in a vision experiment). The grid
already scrolls horizontally, so the compact rail bought little real estate
while hiding interactive columns. Dropping compactMenu lays the grid beside the
full in-flow navigation menu, which reserves its own width and never overlaps

the compact overlay menu) and specs/experiments-v3/workbench-layout.feature.

A configured-but-portless LANGWATCH_NLP_SERVICE (http://localhost) made

export guard now rewrites empty AND portless local URLs; explicit
host:port stays untouched. Autostart scenarios reworded to behavior
terms per the feature-file convention, bats bindings swept to match.

* fix(nlpgo): let uppercase data URL schemes reach the multimodal split

The pass-through gate was a case-sensitive Contains while the split
regex is case-insensitive, so DATA:IMAGE/... content skipped the split
entirely. One regex scan now decides pass-through; plain text content

* test(event-sourcing): give delayed-dispatch TOCTOU assertions a 3x ceiling

A delayed job produces no dispatcher signal when it becomes ready, so
its dispatch waits for the next BRPOP timeout cycle, and container
clock skew on CI runners widens that window further. The 10s assertion
ceiling sat right on that boundary and flaked three times on this PR

* fix(experiments-v3): keep the image type on dataset columns in mapping dropdowns

Dataset columns typed image (URL) were collapsed to str by the

test(AICreateModal): add per-test cleanup to fix CI-only close-button flake (#4468)

* test(AICreateModal): add per-test cleanup to fix CI-only close-button flake

AICreateModal.test.tsx failed CI-only on `getByRole("button", { name: /close/i })`
("Unable to find role=button and name /close/i"). Root cause is test isolation, not
the component: vitest runs without `globals: true`, so @testing-library/react's
automatic per-test cleanup never registers. Without it, every render() leaks its
portaled Chakra Dialog into document.body; as dialogs accumulate across the file's
cases, focus management marks them aria-hidden, and role-based queries (getByRole)
exclude aria-hidden elements — so the close button intermittently can't be found.
Local single-file runs don't accumulate enough to trip it; CI does (vmThreads pool +
sharding + coverage timing).

Fix: add `afterEach(() => cleanup())` so each test unmounts its dialog and the next
renders against a clean DOM with exactly one live, non-aria-hidden dialog.

- AC1/AC4: verified 30/30 across 10 repeated local runs.
- AC2: cleanup now runs after every test (no dialog accumulation / aria-hidden).
- AC3: test-only — AICreateModal/Dialog/CloseButton unchanged.

#4137 is a red herring (it changed zero frontend files). The flake is CI-timing
dependent, so there is no deterministic local red; the documented failure is
test-unit (4) on c8c6495 (run 26750014253). A repo-wide variant of this gap exists in
test-setup.ts (no global RTL cleanup) — candidate follow-up, out of scope here.

Closes #4467

feat(nlpgo): fetch remote attachment URLs and deliver them to the model as content (#4910)

* feat(nlpgo): fetch remote attachment URLs and deliver them to the model as content

Today a prompt image only reaches the model when its value is an inline
data:image base64 URL; a plain http(s) URL is interpolated as text and the
model never opens it. This adds a fetch pass after the data-URL image split:
any http(s) URL referenced in a message is fetched under the HTTP block's SSRF
policy, a timeout, and a size cap, its type is detected from the response
rather than the file extension (so extension-less S3/CDN URLs work), and it is
re-homed into a multimodal content part. Images inline as base64 data-URL image
parts so they work across every provider; audio and PDFs get their own part
shapes. A reachable response that is not an attachment (an HTML page) is left as
text. A URL that cannot be fetched aborts the run with a clear
attachment_fetch_error naming the URL.

* feat(nlpgo): re-home a system-prompt attachment URL into a user message

Providers reject non-text parts in system-role messages. When an http(s)
attachment URL lands in the system prompt, split the text-before into the
retained system prompt and re-home the attachment (and following text) into a
user message, mirroring what splitMessagesWithImages already does for inline
data-URL images.

* test(nlpgo): live known-answer vision probe for remote image URLs

A live_openai e2e test that serves a solid-color PNG from an opaque local URL,
runs a vision prompt through the in-process gateway to a real model, and asserts
the model reports the color it could only have seen. Proves the fetch -> inline
-> gateway -> vision path end to end and guards against hallucination (the URL
gives nothing away). Gated behind the live_openai build tag + OPENAI_API_KEY.

* fix(nlpgo): split attachment fetch by intent + correct audio format mapping

Review feedback from #4910:
- Breadth: a bare http URL in prose is now best-effort (a reachable non-attachment
  or a failed fetch leaves it as text), so an incidental link can no longer fail
  the whole run. Only an explicit image_url part hard-fails on a bad fetch.
- Audio: map audio/mpeg to the mp3 format token (and audio/wav to wav) that
  providers expect, instead of the raw subtype.
- SSRF: add a redirect-to-metadata test that locks in the SafeDialer dial-time
  re-check.
- Derive a PDF attachment's filename from the URL; drop the raw network error
  from the user-facing message; fix a misleading test comment.

* test(nlpgo): use assert.Empty for empty-string checks (testifylint)

* fix(nlpgo): hard-fail on unfetchable image-typed input URLs instead of passing them as text

An image-typed signature input is an explicit attachment: the studio lets the
author declare an input as an Image, which is a clear statement that the value
is a picture, not prose that happens to carry a link. Before this change such an
input was templated into the message as its raw URL string and only the
best-effort prose path saw it, so an unfetchable image URL silently degraded to
the model guessing from the URL text (a bad cat.png URL made the model answer
"cat" from the filename) instead of failing with a clear error.

Resolve image-typed inputs before message templating: fetch the URL under the
same SSRF + size + timeout guards, inline it as a base64 data URL for the
existing image splitter to deliver, and abort the run with a clear
attachment_fetch_error when the URL cannot be reached or is not an image. A
str-typed URL stays best-effort; an inline data URL passes through untouched.

Dogfooded in the studio: an Image-typed field with an unreachable URL now shows
"Could not load the attachment ...: it could not be reached." in 45ms with no
model call, where it previously guessed a wrong answer.

* refactor(nlpgo): address CodeRabbit review on attachment fetch

- Require an http(s) scheme separator (isHTTPURL helper) instead of a bare
  "http" prefix, so look-alikes like "httpfoo://" are not treated as
  fetchable; applied to both the image_url-part path and image-typed inputs.
- Assert the retained system-prompt text value in the re-home test, not just
  its type.
- Rephrase the system-prompt scenario in user-facing terms (the model still
  receives the image) rather than message-role mechanics.

* docs(specs): phrase attachment-url scenarios in user-facing terms

Rewrite the scenario steps from engine internals ("the engine builds the LLM
messages", "the message content becomes a parts list") to observable
behavior ("I run the workflow", "the model receives the image"), per the
feature-file convention that scenarios describe behavior from the user's
perspective. Scenario titles are unchanged, so the Go test bindings stay intact.

* docs(specs): point the binding comment at the real integration test file

* test(nlpgo): live audio + PDF attachment-URL probes through the real gateway

Two gated (live_openai) known-answer probes that prove non-image attachments
ride the same fetch-and-structure path end to end, complementing the existing
vision probe:

- Audio: a wav whose spoken question is 'Do I have a male voice or a female
  voice?' (Whisper-confirmed) is served from an opaque URL; nlpgo fetches it,
  structures an input_audio part, and openai/gpt-audio echoes the spoken
  question, which is only possible by hearing the fetched clip.
- PDF: a document containing 'order number 4729' and 'customer city Lisbon' is
  served; nlpgo structures a file part, and openai/gpt-5-mini answers with both
  facts, which live only inside the fetched PDF.

Both reach the model through the in-process gateway, confirming it forwards
input_audio and file content parts. Fixtures are supplied via AUDIO_FIXTURE_PATH
and PDF_FIXTURE_PATH, so no binaries are committed and the tests skip when the
fixture or key is absent.

* docs: explain how attachment URLs reach the model from datasets and prompts

Document that an image URL feeding a vision workflow is fetched server-side and
delivered as actual image content (cross-provider, type detected from the
response), that audio and PDF URLs are delivered the same way, and that an
image-typed field with an unloadable URL fails the run with a clear error while
a plain prose link is left as text.

* fix(nlpgo): address security/privacy review on attachment fetch

Four review findings on the attachment-URL path:

- Redact the query string and fragment from the URL in attachment_fetch_error
  (and thus the node/trace): presigned S3/CDN URLs carry X-Amz-Signature and
  security tokens in the query, which a fetch failure would otherwise leak.
- Keep the fetched attachment bytes out of the trace: the messages sent to the
  model carry the full base64, but startLLMSpan now receives a redacted copy
  where inline image/audio/file bytes are summarised as "[media-type, N bytes]",
  so a 20 MB attachment no longer becomes a ~27 MB langwatch.input span attribute
  storing the private payload.
- An explicit image_url part that resolves to a non-image now fails with a clear
  attachment_fetch_error instead of falling through and sending the raw URL to
  the provider, matching the strict intent for explicit attachments.
- Clone http.DefaultTransport before installing SafeDialer so attachment fetches
  inherit Proxy: http.ProxyFromEnvironment, matching the HTTP block, so they work
  in restricted-egress deployments that require an outbound proxy.

Adds regression tests: signed-URL query redaction, trace bytes stripped while the
model copy keeps them, and an explicit image_url pointing at a web page failing.

* fix(nlpgo): also strip userinfo credentials from redacted attachment URLs

redactURLForError stripped the query string and fragment but url.String kept the
userinfo component, so a URL like https://user:token@host/file.png would still
surface the embedded credentials in a fetch-failure error. Clear u.User (with a
matching cut in the non-parsing fallback) and add a regression asserting the
user and password do not leak.

fix(studio): stop prompt editor render loop crashing the playground (#4896)

* fix(studio): stop prompt editor render loop crashing the playground

The undefined-variables banner in PromptTextAreaWithVariables re-measured on
every render: its useLayoutEffect depended on the invalidVariables array
identity, and the prompt editor rebuilds that array on every render, so the
effect ran each render and called setState unconditionally. During the prompt
tab's mount and settle re-renders this churned the commit phase into React's
nested-update limit ("Maximum update depth exceeded"), throwing the whole page
to the top-level error boundary.

Key the layout effect on a stable primitive signature of the invalid variable
names and guard the height setState so it only updates on a real change. The
banner now re-measures only when the set of undefined variables changes.

Adds a BDD spec and an RTL regression test that drives the editor through
repeated re-renders and asserts the banner does not re-measure on every render
(the per-render setState that fed the crash).

* fix(studio): address review on the prompt render-loop fix

perf(clickhouse): cap topic-clustering page-fetch read streams (#4571)

The topic-clustering page fetch reads ComputedInput (a potentially large
payload) for the page of up to 2000 traces. #4496 removed the outer
sort/LIMIT so rows stream, but peak memory still scales with the number
of read streams each holding a ComputedInput block, and for tenants with
large inputs that peak crossed max_memory_usage_per_query
(MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, ~3.5 GiB reading ComputedInput).

This is a background clustering batch, not a latency-critical path, so cap
the read to max_threads=2. Lower parallelism keeps the streaming
ComputedInput buffers well under the per-query limit; the returned rows
are unchanged. Correctness under the cap is covered by the existing
fetchTracesFromClickHouse integration test (2000-trace page); a structural
guard keeps the setting from being dropped.

perf(clickhouse): add time predicate to claude-code log re-fold (stop stored_log_records cold scan) (#4688)

* perf(clickhouse): add time predicate to claude-code log re-fold read

The claudeCodeSpanSync reactor re-reads a turn's marked logs from
stored_log_records on every claude-code log batch, filtering only on
TenantId + TraceId. The table is PARTITION BY toYearWeek(TimeUnixMs) and
tiered to S3, so each read cold-scans every weekly partition (a burst of
S3 GETs). Thread the triggering event's occurredAt as a +/-2-day TimeUnixMs
window so the scan prunes to the turn's partitions; falls back to the
unbounded scan when no time is known.

The window bound is qualified as stored_log_records.TimeUnixMs because the
outer SELECT aliases toUnixTimestamp64Milli(TimeUnixMs) AS TimeUnixMs, which
would otherwise shadow the column and make the bound compare a ms-integer
against a DateTime64 (returning nothing). Covered by a new integration test.

* feat(data-privacy): add scoped DataPrivacyPolicy schema, specs, and tenancy guards

  policy resolution errors, so a resolver/db blip cannot expose restricted

The trace-view notice fired on any [REDACTED] content but described it as PII

copy now names PII or secrets redaction and links to settings generally.

* fix(data-privacy): make contentDropService optional so 3-dep test commands skip the prisma default path

Integration tests construct RecordSpanCommand with the three enrichment
services cast 'as never' specifically to bypass createDefaultDependencies()
(whose require(server/db) cannot resolve under vitest). Requiring
contentDropService in the completeness check pushed those tests back onto the
default path, surfacing as 'Could not find table: test_event_handler_log' in

* test(data-privacy): mock the policy resolver in the protections RoleBinding unit test

The fail-closed change in getUserProtectionsForProject hides content when the

unmocked, so the resolver threw and the new fail-closed path returned
not-visible, breaking the legacy-enum visibility assertions. Mock the resolver
to the platform default so the test exercises the legacy-enum + RoleBinding

* fix(data-privacy): keep contentDropService required, stub it explicitly in tests

Per review, an optional drop service would let a caller silently skip drop

* feat(data-privacy): trace-view markers for dropped and restricted content

Adds mapper and component tests, plus a content-drop view scenario.

Restricting output nulls trace.output upstream, so TraceMessages fell

Retire the legacy privacy controls now that the scoped DataPrivacyPolicy is

The new traces view returned trace and span input/output to the client with no

The cascade resolver supports a narrower scope setting capture over a

an override produced an empty config with Save disabled or a rule that
kept inheriting the parent restriction.

The drawer now tracks which controls the user touched and persists those

becomes a real override. Add mode prefills from the inherited effective

* feat(data-privacy): custom attribute rules and richer restrict audiences

Custom attribute rules replace the exact-key customDropKeys: a rule names a
span-attribute path (exact key or * wildcard, e.g. gen_ai.prompt.*) and either
drops the matching attributes at ingestion or restricts them to an audience at
read time. Distinct patterns union down the cascade and the most-specific
scope wins per pattern. Dropping stamps a second marker listing the dropped
key names (never the values) so the trace view can explain the absence, and a
pattern of only wildcards is rejected at write time so the metadata-survival
guarantee cannot be configured away.

The restrict audience gains the built-in Viewers role group and the project
owner: a rule on personal projects can make traces visible only to the person
themselves, optionally widened with a chosen group. The protections read path
evaluates the new audiences from facts it already holds, resolves every

attribute patterns for the read mappers.

Dogfooding the custom attribute rules surfaced two read-side gaps in the

All span-returning procedures (spansPaginated, spansDelta, spansFull,

perf(clickhouse): guard empty aggregateId from event_log reads (#4943)

* perf(clickhouse): guard empty aggregateId from event_log reads

An event store read with an empty aggregateId issues
`... WHERE AggregateId = ''` against event_log, whose sort key is
(TenantId, AggregateType, AggregateId, IdempotencyKey). The empty-id
key range collects every event written without an aggregate id, and the
read materialises all their EventPayload blobs, exceeding
max_memory_usage_per_query (Code 241) and degrading the instance for
every tenant.

No aggregate type uses an empty string as its id, so an empty/whitespace
aggregateId is always a caller bug (e.g. a re-fold enqueued without one).
Short-circuit getEvents / getEventsUpTo / countEventsBefore to an empty
result at the store boundary (next to validateTenantId), and log a
warning so the upstream empty-id source stays visible.
