perf(clickhouse): prune event_log blob reads via the EventId KSUID timestamp (#4944)

* perf(clickhouse): prune event_log partitions on offloaded-blob reads

`BlobStore.getFromEventLog` resolves an offloaded span/log body with a
point lookup keyed by EventId, but with no predicate on the partition
column. event_log is `PARTITION BY toYearWeek(EventOccurredAt)`, so the
read opens every weekly partition — including the cold ones tiered to S3
— turning each blob resolution into a burst of S3 GETs. In the last 24h
this was one of the highest-volume cold scans on event_log.

Thread the referencing span's start time (`NormalizedSpan.startTimeUnixMs`,
already in hand on the read path) as an optional `occurredAtMs` hint. When
present, getFromEventLog adds a bounded `EventOccurredAt` window (+/-2 days,
keeping `EventOccurredAt = 0` so rows with an unknown occurred time are
never dropped) so the read prunes to the one or two weekly partitions
around the span. The lookup stays uniquely keyed by EventId, so the window
only affects cost, never which row is returned.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor: derive event_log prune window from the EventId KSUID

EventIds are KSUIDs (generateEventId -> generate("event")), so the id we
already look up by carries its own creation timestamp, and EventOccurredAt
is stamped from the same ingestion clock (Date.now() at collection). So
derive the EventOccurredAt partition window from the EventId itself rather
than from a caller-supplied time.

This is both simpler and more correct than the previous span-start-time
hint: every getFromEventLog caller now prunes with nothing to thread, and
we no longer anchor on a span's start time, which can sit days before the
event's ingestion for late-arriving or replayed spans and would then prune
away the very partition holding the row (silently degrading the blob read
to its preview). Non-KSUID/unparseable ids fall back to an unpruned read.

fix(traces): resolve >64KB offloaded IO past mixed-type OTLP attributes (#4888) (#4975)

* fix(traces): resolve >64KB offloaded IO past mixed-type OTLP attributes (#4888)

#4890 wired full=true resolution through every customer-facing trace
detail surface, but >64KB IO still degraded to the 64KB preview in prod.

Root cause (NOT a deploy gap — the #4890 wiring is deployed and the
resolver runs on every detail read): BlobStore.getFromEventLog parsed the
event_log EventPayload with a spanAttributeSchema that REQUIRED
value.stringValue on EVERY span attribute. Real OTLP spans carry
non-string AnyValue siblings (gen_ai.usage.* intValue, temperature
doubleValue, streaming boolValue, tools arrayValue, ...). A single
non-string sibling failed z.array(spanAttributeSchema), failed
eventPayloadSchema.safeParse, and threw BlobFieldNotFoundError — the
resolver then warned and kept the preview. That is the exact prod warn
Drew captured: 'Field "langwatch.input" not found in event payload'.
CI stayed green because every prior test used string-only attributes or
mocked getFromEventLog itself.

Fix: model span.attributes as z.array(z.unknown()) and parse each
attribute defensively (key + optional stringValue), so a single
non-string / malformed sibling can never fail the whole-array parse and
mask the offloaded IO field. The fix is the single chokepoint for all 4
detail surfaces (traces.getById, traces/spans.getTracesWithSpans, REST
GET /:traceId).

Falsifiability: new tests in blob-store.event-log.unit.test.ts drive the
REAL getFromEventLog and the REAL resolveOffloadedTraces orchestrator
over a genuine eventToRecord payload carrying mixed-type siblings + a
>64KB IO field. Pre-fix: 3 fail with the exact prod BlobFieldNotFoundError;
post-fix: 17 pass. Hardened the real-ClickHouse readpath integration
fixture with mixed-type siblings so the un-skipped lane would catch this.

perf(clickhouse): prune event_log partitions on time-local aggregate rehydration (#4521)

The fold-projection re-fold path rehydrates an aggregate's full event history
via getEventRecords, which filters only TenantId + AggregateType + AggregateId
and so cold-scans every weekly partition of event_log on S3. This is by far the
largest cold-scan shape in prod (~20k/day, the dominant driver of the persistent
S3 GET burst).

For time-local aggregate types (trace, evaluation, experiment_run,
simulation_run, suite_run) every event of an aggregate occurs within the
aggregate's own short lifetime, so the scan can be safely lower-bounded to a
window around the triggering event's occurredAt. Thread that occurredAt from the
re-fold executor through the eventLoader and getEvents into getEventRecords, and
add an `EventOccurredAt >= bound` predicate (keeping EventOccurredAt = 0
unknown-time rows) so ClickHouse prunes the older weekly partitions. The
partition expression is monotonic in EventOccurredAt, so the predicate prunes.

Long-lived aggregate types (global, billing_report, simulation_set) and any
read without a usable anchor stay unbounded — the classification in
rehydrationWindow.ts is the correctness contract. The window (45 days, must
exceed any time-local aggregate's lifetime and stay under event_log retention)
errs large so a re-fold can never drop an event.

EXPLAIN INDEXES on a real tenant: parts read drop from 286/286 to 48/288 (~83%
fewer partitions opened) for a trace rehydration.

* perf(clickhouse): add time predicate to trace-peek span tree read

The table-row peek expansion calls the spanTree tRPC query via useTraceSpanTree
without the occurredAtMs partition hint, so getSpanSummaryByTraceId falls back to
an unconstrained stored_spans scan. stored_spans is partitioned on StartTime and
tiered to S3, so each hintless read walks every weekly partition (incl. cold
ones), bursting S3 GETs. In the last 24h this peek shape (paramKeys
[tenantId, traceId]) is one of the top stored_spans cold scans.

The trace-list row already carries its timestamp, so forward it as the
occurredAtMs hint; the server already widens it to a +/-2-day StartTime window
(spanReadHintShape / withPartitionHint). Omitted hints keep the current
unconstrained fallback, so the change is backward-compatible.

perf(clickhouse): prune trace-event reads by resolving the trace time

getEventsByTraceId, getSpanEvents) walked every weekly stored_spans
partition, including the cold S3 tier, whenever the caller did not thread
an occurredAtMs hint or when the trace simply had no matching events.

Two causes, one fix:
- Drawer entry points that drop the occurredAtMs URL hint (back-stack,
  conversation jumps, deep links) and worker callers that never had one
  reached the reads with no hint, so the partition window was empty and
  the scan was unbounded.

  read an empty result is the common, legitimate 'this trace has no
  events' case, so every event-less trace triggered a full-table walk.

(TenantId, TraceId) sort-key seek) when no hint is supplied, build the
same +/-2 day StartTime window, and treat an empty result as
authoritative instead of rescanning unbounded. Traces genuinely absent

perf(clickhouse): bound and harden storage-metering _size_bytes reads (#4855)

* perf(clickhouse): bound and harden storage-metering _size_bytes reads

Storage metering sums `_size_bytes`, a MATERIALIZED byteSize(...) column. On
parts written before the column existed ClickHouse recomputes it on read by
scanning the heavy payload columns, so for the largest tenants a single
`sum(_size_bytes)` read reaches tens of GB and 24-60s, and sometimes trips the
per-query memory limit (Code 241). The existing max_threads cap bounds peak
memory but not the read itself.

Two safe guards:
- Add a coarse `max_execution_time` (45s) to the metering settings. A
  materialized read finishes in a few seconds even for the largest tenants, so
  this only trips the runaway recompute path, stopping a single tenant's
  metering from grinding for a minute and burning tens of GB of reads every
  cache cycle.
- Make the combined total query fall back to the resilient per-table breakdown
  on any failure, so one heavy table tripping the limit degrades only that
  table to zero instead of failing the whole storage-usage metric.

The durable fix is documented inline: backfill the column with
`ALTER TABLE <table> MATERIALIZE COLUMN _size_bytes` (out of band, low-traffic
window) so the recompute never happens and every read hits the stored UInt32.

* perf(span-storage): lock LazilyRead on the single-span fetch paths

Investigation against local CH 25.10.1.3832 (same version line as prod) on a
realistic fat span (19 attrs / 127 events / ~88KB Events.Attributes):

  getSpanByIds   Form A (ORDER BY UpdatedAt DESC LIMIT 1)
    read_bytes = 14,933       (~15KB)        LazilyRead engaged
  getSpanByIds   Form B (scalar-subquery dedup, doc Anti-Pattern 1 form)
    read_bytes = 9,706,538    (~9.7MB)       650x heavier
  getSpanByIds   Form A, optimizer flipped off
    read_bytes = 9,692,701    (~9.7MB)       same as Form B - hence the lock

  getSpanEvents  Form A (inner ORDER BY DESC LIMIT 1, ARRAY JOIN outside)
    read_bytes = 14,933       (~15KB)        LazilyRead survives the subquery
  getSpanEvents  Form B (scalar-subquery dedup inside the subquery)
    read_bytes = 4,570,069    (~4.6MB)       306x heavier

The LazilyRead optimiser (CH 25.4+) defers heavy column reads (Maps + Arrays
including SpanAttributes / Events.* / Links.*) past LIMIT N when
N <= query_plan_max_limit_for_lazy_materialization (default 10 on 25.10).
LIMIT 1 is well inside the threshold. EXPLAIN confirms LazilyRead appears in
both query plans, including through the subquery + ARRAY JOIN composition that
getSpanEvents uses.

This PR adds the per-query SETTINGS lock `query_plan_optimize_lazy_materialization=1`
on both methods so a future cluster / profile override can't silently drop the
optimisation. The failure mode without it (optimizer off) is "degrades to
Form B equivalent" - not catastrophic, but not what the code claims.

Comments at both call sites point at the central SINGLE_SPAN_FETCH_SETTINGS
block which documents the investigation numbers, the threshold, and the
minimum CH version (25.4).

perf(clickhouse): add conversation-id skip-index for thread->traces lookups (#4854)

* perf(clickhouse): add conversation-id skip-index for thread->traces lookups

Resolving a conversation thread to its traces (getTracesByThreadId /
getTracesWithSpansByThreadIds) filters trace_summaries on the conversation id
held in the Attributes map, with no time bound (a conversation can span any
period):

  SELECT DISTINCT TraceId FROM trace_summaries
  WHERE TenantId = {tenantId}
    AND Attributes['gen_ai.conversation.id'] = {threadId}   -- or IN (...)

TenantId is the primary-key prefix but the conversation id is a map element, so
the read decodes Attributes for every granule of every partition the tenant
occupies. In production this shape read ~0.5-0.7 GB per call at 1-2.5s.

Add a bloom_filter skip-index on the conversation-id map element (matching the
existing idx_models / idx_topic_id granularity) so a thread lookup skips the
granule-blocks that cannot contain the id. ADD INDEX attaches to new parts
only; the migration documents the out-of-band MATERIALIZE INDEX backfill for
existing parts. Integration test applies the migration via goose and pins that
the index attaches and the = / IN thread lookups still return the right traces.

The trace-list filter compiler builds correlated EXISTS subqueries over
stored_spans for span- and event-level filters (spans.type, events.*).

previous behaviour.

perf(clickhouse): prune new-trace-count subquery to the poll window (#5023)

The live "new traces since X" poll (`findCount` -> `newCount`) counts traces
with OccurredAt > since, but when a span-level filter is active its bounded
subquery scans stored_spans over the entire dashboard window (e.g. 30 days)
on every poll, reading multiple GB each time even though only the recent
sliver since the last poll can contain new traces.

Raise the window's lower bound passed to the filter subquery to `since`
(less a 2-day buffer) so the stored_spans scan prunes to the recent
partitions. The outer OccurredAt > since predicate is unchanged, so the
count is identical: a trace with OccurredAt > since has its matching span
StartTime >= OccurredAt > since, and the buffer covers OccurredAt-vs-
StartTime skew (matching the withPartitionHint margin used elsewhere). The
change no-ops when since <= the window start.

EXPLAIN INDEXES on the stored_spans subquery for a real tenant: 40 parts /
3571 granules (30-day window) down to 6 parts / 16 granules (since - 2d).

fix(collector): remove un-awaited module-load tiktoken prewarm fetch in tests (#4476) (#5003)

cost.ts fired prewarmTiktokenModels() as an un-awaited side effect at module
load, gated on isBuildOrNoRedis — which is TRUE under unit tests because
vitest.config.ts sets BUILD_TIME=1. Every test file transitively importing
cost.ts (metrics, span-cost-enrichment, model-cost-matching, the cost test
itself) kicked off a background tiktoken BPE-rank fetch (gpt-4 + gpt-4o) at
import time. The grinder reproduced the fallout locally as
"EnvironmentTeardownError: Cannot load tiktoken.cjs after the environment was
torn down". Under --coverage vitest awaits a graceful worker exit, so an
in-flight fetch can outlive teardown.

The real collector worker already prewarms explicitly via startCollectorWorker()
(collectorWorker.ts), which runs only when redis is connected — exactly the case
the removed block SKIPPED. So the block only ever fired in build/test/no-redis,
where no traces are processed and prewarm is pointless. Remove it (and its now
unused isBuildOrNoRedis import); production prewarm is unchanged. Relocate the
removed block's error-logging .catch onto that surviving worker call site so a
prewarm fetch failure is logged rather than left as an unhandled rejection.

Guard: cost.module-load.unit.test.ts asserts importing cost.ts does not
auto-prewarm tiktoken (red->green verified).

Scope note: this removes a real latent leak the issue forensics flagged, but it
is NOT the cause of the test-unit (2) timing. This PR's CI shows shard 2 still at
6m48s with the worker open-handles diagnostic clean (only a MessagePort) — the
residual wedge is the vitest main-process finalize path masked by the
test-unit-global-setup hard floor (#4481/#4713), not an application handle.

* fix(datasets): CSV normalize no longer corrupts rows with two equal cells

Root cause (reproduced): the streaming CSV parse used papaparse `header:true`.
Under our pause/resume backpressure, papaparse re-runs its duplicate-HEADER dedup
against the CURRENT DATA ROW on every resume — so any row holding two equal cells
(an input that equals its expected output, or two blank cells) had the second
value silently suffixed with `_1`, and a "Duplicate headers found and renamed"
warning was logged PER ROW (594k for a 100MB upload). Triggered by any
multi-chunk streamed CSV; a single-string parse doesn't hit it.

Fix: parse with `header:false` (rows as arrays) and map to objects by index,
deduping the real header row exactly once (papaparse's `_1`/`_2` scheme for
genuinely repeated column names is preserved). Row values are never run through
header machinery, so equal cells stay verbatim. Backpressure (pause/resume) and
the per-row size cap are unchanged.

Regression test: a CSV with answer==expected_answer delivered in many small
stream pieces (so it actually streams) normalizes with no `_1` corruption and no
phantom column. typecheck + 147 dataset unit tests green. ADR-032 v14 note (e).

* perf(datasets): scan-before-lock for s3_jsonl edit/delete (stacked on #4908) (#5067)

* perf(datasets): scan-before-lock for s3_jsonl edit/delete

The id-locate scan for edit/delete ran inside the per-dataset advisory lock, so
lock-hold scaled O(chunkCount) S3 reads (~2.5s at 500 chunks). Move the locate
OFF the lock (locateIdsBeforeLock); under the lock the fast path re-reads only
the affected chunk(s) and takes every unaffected chunk's (rowCount, byteSize)
from the authoritative offset index — shrinking lock-held reads to O(affected).

Correctness is preserved by re-validation under the lock: the fast path commits
only when the pre-scan located every target id and the offset index covers every
chunk, and bails to the proven full in-lock scan if any located id isn't where
the hint said (a concurrent move/delete since the scan). So even a future
compaction that moves rows between chunks can't cause a silently-missed delete.
The pre-scan is skipped for a not-ready dataset (no I/O ahead of the readiness
gate). Implements the optimization deferred in ADR-032 v12; recorded as v16.

Trade-off: trusting the offset index for unaffected chunks means a delete no
longer incidentally self-heals counter drift there; recomputeDatasetCounts
remains the explicit I-COUNT repair (the full-scan fallback still self-heals).

Tests: fast-path read-reduction (later chunks never read), hint-bail fallback
for a moved row (edit + delete), legacy no-offsets → full scan. 23 unit tests
green; full dataset + datasetRecord router suites green.

withDatasetLock — contradicting the file header, which documents the write as
recoverable and outside the lock. Holding the per-dataset advisory lock and its
120s transaction budget across S3 round-trips amplifies lock hold for no
correctness gain.

any S3 work), read PG rows + write chunks + orphan-cleanup OUTSIDE the lock
(idempotent by deterministic key → a concurrent/re-run write is harmless), then a
short PG-only critical section under the lock that re-reads to win the race and

re-open it). Add an explicit cross-site check on the session-cookie branch of
authorizeDirectUpload (the API-key path isn't exposed): reject when
Sec-Fetch-Site is cross-site (proxy-independent, all modern browsers), falling
back to Origin-vs-forwarded-Host for older clients. Tests pin both the reject and

- Over-cap finalize now nulls `stagingKey` in the same update that flips the
  dataset to `failed`. The staged object was just deleted, so leaving the key
  set let `retryNormalize` re-drive a missing object and fail with the
  misleading "Uploaded object not found" instead of the real over-cap cause.

  (`deleteChunksFrom` fromIndex 0). `parseInto` flushes chunks to S3 mid-stream,

  staging keys, have no lifecycle TTL, so a permanently-failed dataset leaked
  them forever. Staging is still preserved for a manual retry.

* fix(datasets): observable direct-upload PUT failures + stop ghost rows (#5088)

When the browser→S3 presigned PUT fails (typically a missing bucket CORS
rule), the upload drawer silently fell back to the legacy in-browser-parse
path with three bad consequences:

- the failure was indistinguishable from a no-storage install (no log/
  telemetry), so a fully-broken direct-upload path looked healthy;
- a file over the 25 MB fallback cap got the misleading "requires object
  storage" error even though storage WAS configured;
- each failed attempt archived its content-less `uploading` placeholder and
  the fallback created a second dataset → duplicate ("ghost") rows in PG,
  accumulating unbounded during a CORS outage.

Changes:
- log PresignedUploadFailedError loudly with an operator-facing CORS/
  connectivity hint, distinct from DirectUploadUnavailableError;
- show an accurate, non-misleading error for over-cap files when storage is
  configured (UI stays jargon-free per copywriting.md; CORS detail → log);
- hard-delete the content-less pending placeholder instead of archiving it
  (new status-guarded DatasetRepository.deletePendingUpload), so a finalize
  racing the abort is never destroyed and no ghost row is left behind.

Does not replace applying the bucket CORS rule, which is the actual unblock.

Root cause of the failed prod direct uploads was NOT bucket CORS (that is live
and correct) — it was the app's own Content-Security-Policy. `connect-src`
never listed the S3 origin, so in production the browser refused the presigned
PUT before it left the page. The opaque fetch TypeError then drove the silent
fallback + the misleading "requires object storage" error on large files.

CSP is production-only (start.ts), which is why local dev uploads succeeded and
masked this.

Derive the allowed storage origin(s) from the same env the S3 client uses
(buildStorageConnectSrc) so the CSP tracks the configured bucket/region/
endpoint: explicit S3_ENDPOINT → its origin; plain AWS → region-scoped
path-style + virtual-hosted forms; Azure endpoint too. Unit-tested.

CI: tsgo (tsconfig.tsgo.json) flagged TS2559 — process.env (ProcessEnv) shares

connect-src change. Net start.ts diff: ~28 lines. My hunks are biome-clean;
the remaining pre-existing format debt is out-of-hunk (not reviewdog-flagged).

* fix(datasets): address review — CSP header injection + edge cases (Aryan)

Blockers:
- Validate S3_REGION with /^[a-z0-9-]+$/ before interpolating into the CSP
  header; a value with ';' or whitespace would inject extra CSP directives /
  source tokens. Falls back to the AWS wildcard on a non-region value.
- safeOrigin: reject the string "null" that `new URL("file:///x").origin`
  returns for opaque-origin schemes — it would emit an unquoted `null` source
  that matches null-origin documents and weakens the policy.

Non-blockers:
- Gate the AWS `*.amazonaws.com` fallback on an AWS signal (S3_ENDPOINT/
  S3_REGION/S3_BUCKET_NAME/AWS_REGION) so a pure-Azure or local-FS deployment

- runFallbackParseAndDrawer: replace the reason ternary with an exhaustive

  default.

fix(datasets): legacy column-type migration timeout + upload/create dropdown consolidation (#5115)

* fix(datasets): widen txn budget for legacy postgres column-type migration

Changing a column type on a legacy postgres-layout dataset runs
migrateDatasetRecordColumns (one UPDATE per row) inside the interactive
transaction at dataset.service.ts, which was opened with no timeout
option -> Prisma's 5s default. On any dataset large enough for those
per-row UPDATEs to exceed 5s, the final dataset.update() throws P2028
'Transaction already closed'.

The s3_jsonl chunk-rewrite path already runs under a 120s budget via
withDatasetLock; the legacy path was missed. Share the same budget by
exporting the timeout constants (renamed DATASET_MUTATION_TXN_*) and
passing { timeout, maxWait } to the legacy $transaction.

Adds a regression test that drives a legacy-layout column-type change
through upsertDataset and asserts the transaction is opened with the
wide budget, not the 5s default.

* fix(datasets): skip per-row migration for type-only column changes

The real cost wasn't the transaction timeout — it was doing O(rowCount)
no-op UPDATEs. In the legacy postgres layout the stored entry JSON is
untyped (column types are metadata), and the record migrator only remaps
keys, never values. A type-only change (string->image) therefore rewrote
every row with byte-identical JSON.

Gate migrateDatasetRecordColumns on whether the column KEY structure
changed (columnKeysChanged: ordered names differ). Type-only changes now
do a single dataset.update — O(1), no long transaction. The widened txn
budget stays as a safety net for genuine rename/add/remove migrations
that still touch every row.

Tests: type-only change does no findDatasetRecords/per-row UPDATE; a
rename still migrates under the wide budget.

* test(datasets): assert maxWait + tighten column-migration gate

CodeRabbit: the budget test pinned timeout but not maxWait, so a
regression nulling maxWait would slip through — now asserts both.

Review follow-ups (P3):
- Gate the key-diff on `columnsChanged` so the unconditional `.map`
  over stored columnTypes stays off the common name-only edit path.
- Rename test now seeds real rows and asserts values move old_name ->
  new_name (data survives the rename), instead of an empty-records test
  titled 'large'.

- replace the two header buttons (Bulk upload / Upload or Create Dataset)

  supersedes it here; component still used by studio + add-rows)

  (onCreateFromScratch), matching the old single-upload escape hatch

- Menu positioning sameWidth so the dropdown matches the button width

* fix(datasets): skip per-row migration on pure column reorder too

Address @Aryansharma28 review: columnKeysChanged compared ordered name
arrays, so a pure reorder ([a,b]->[b,a]) ran migrateDatasetRecordColumns
and rewrote every row byte-identically — the O(rowCount) no-op the PR set
out to avoid. The migrator matches by name first, so equal name SETS are
always identity; compare sorted names instead. Column order is
dataset.columnTypes metadata, persisted by dataset.update regardless.

Legacy datasets can carry entry keys outside columnTypes. Migration policy

* fix(dev): self-heal the mcp-server build after an interrupted install

mcp-server is a cross-directory workspace member that links last, so an
interrupted prep run (Ctrl-C, OOM, the compose crash) leaves
mcp-server/node_modules half-written: the .bin/tsup symlink exists while the
tsup package never finished linking. The next pnpm install reports "Lockfile
is up to date" and skips repair, so the build died with
`Cannot find module '.../tsup/dist/cli-default.js'`.

Re-link @langwatch/mcp-server when tsup's entrypoint is absent. Fail fast and
surface the repair output if the relink itself fails, instead of falling
through to a misleading build error.

fix(compose): isolate mcp-server node_modules in a named volume (#5144) (#5145)

The compose `init` service runs `pnpm install` + `pnpm run build` for
mcp-server inside the container against the `./mcp-server` host bind mount.
With no isolation, the container install writes container-shaped pnpm
symlinks (e.g. `node_modules/tsup -> ../../app/node_modules/.pnpm/...`)
straight into the host tree. Those paths dangle on the host, so a
host-side mcp-server build fails with `Cannot find module
'.../mcp-server/node_modules/tsup/dist/cli-default.js'`.

mcp-server was the only bind-mounted workspace whose node_modules was not
isolated in a named volume. Mount `mcp_server_modules` at
`/mcp-server/node_modules` on every service that bind-mounts `./mcp-server`
(init, app, workers, ai-server), mirroring `app_modules` / `bullboard_modules`.
The container install now writes into the named volume and the host tree is
left untouched.

  saved edits), classic footer pager (prev / Page N of M / next).
- Editing still works per page: record mutations target each record by its id.

  page's records, which would strand an unsaved edit), and selection clears per
  page. The trailing add-row appears only on the last page.

(first-page + pager, navigation, per-record edit on a later page, add-row gated

effect to setPage(0); the next listPaginated read failed the page positive()
guard -> broken editor. Root cause was a clamp target that could fall below 1.

  currentPage = min(page, pageCount), used for the query display + pager + nav.
  The snap-back effect now floors at pageCount, so an out-of-range page can only
  be pulled down to the real last page, never to 0. Empty / single-page /
  shrunk-under-you are all valid by construction.

  getDatasetPage no longer returns truncated and the editor always shows the

  truncatedReadTooltip usage.

0 records) replaces the truncated-read test; multi-page count assertion kept.
Validated in jsdom out-of-band (Docker-gated suite): EMPTY_PAGES=[1]. typecheck
+ biome + feature-parity green.

* fix(datasets): address review — page-switch bounce, ctx.prisma, loading test

CodeRabbit review on #5156:

- listPaginated: build DatasetService from ctx.prisma (request-scoped), not the
  module singleton — matches the rest of the router and preserves test isolation.
- Page-switch bounce (functional bug the sync-returning test mock hid):
  navigating to a not-yet-loaded page briefly cleared databaseDataset.data, so
  totalPages fell back to 1 and the clamp snapped the page back to 1. Fix:
  keepPreviousData holds the prior page's result (no blank grid, count stays
  stable) AND the snap effect now acts only on an authoritative totalPages,
  never on absent data. Reproduced (LAST_REQUESTED_PAGE=1) then confirmed fixed

  editor stays on the requested page instead of bouncing to page 1.

typecheck + biome green.

* refactor(datasets): extract reusable Pagination, align editor pager with traces-v2

Pull the editor's inline page N of M pager into a prop-driven
~/components/ui/Pagination, modeled on the traces-v2 table pager so the
two surfaces behave the same: a rows-per-page selector, a loading
skeleton, and a pager that shows even on a single page (only hidden when
the count is known to be zero). Unlike the traces-v2 one it takes its
state as props instead of reading a feature store, so any surface owns
its own page state and data source.

Derive the page count from count / pageSize — the single source of
truth — instead of the server's totalPages, so it stays correct the
instant rows-per-page changes, before any refetch. Changing the size
resets to page 1; navigation stays gated on pending writes.

CodeRabbit round 2:

  change, so the hydration effect could populate the grid (and dbDatasetId)
  with the OLD dataset's records under the NEW id. Skip hydrating while
  react-query serves previous-key data (isPreviousData). Regression test
  asserts a write during the held window never targets the newly-selected
  dataset.
- Rows-per-page buttons bypassed the save gate: a size change clears
  selection, resets to page 1, and refetches, which could strand a pending
  edit. They now honor navDisabled, and the active size is a no-op.
- Split the Pagination export into PageSizeSelector + PageNav children.

* fix(datasets): refresh paginated total after a delete so the pager can't dead-end

Deleting rows shrinks the dataset, but the paginated editor only holds the
current page in its store, so it can't recompute the whole-dataset count on
its own. The cached server count went stale: the count chip kept the old
total, and deleting every row on the last page stranded the user on an empty
'Page N of N' with no recovery (the clamp effect can't fire without a fresh
count).

useDatasetRecordSync now fires an onRecordsDeleted callback once a batch that
deleted records fully settles (after all writes, never mid-batch); the editor
refetches listPaginated, which heals the total and lets the clamp snap off a

(callback is optional).

A mixed sync batch could delete rows and then finish with an update error:
pendingOps reaches zero via the error path, batchHadDeleteRef stays set, and
the count refresh never ran — so a committed delete left the pager total
stale. Extract flushDeletedBatch and call it from both the success and error
paths so a committed delete always refreshes once the batch fully settles.
Regression test drives the delete-commits / update-fails-last interleave.

* test(datasets): fix @scenario bindings + faithful keepPreviousData sim

feat(data-retention): edit policies + safer remove with fallback preview (#5123)

* feat(data-retention): edit policies + safer remove with fallback preview

Customer reported the retention settings table felt scary: the only row
action was a one-click trash button (no confirm, no explanation), and there
was no way to edit a rule's value without deleting and re-creating it. The
fear was "if I exclude this 91-day rule, will all my traces be deleted?".

This addresses both:

- Row actions now live in the standard "⋮" overflow menu
  (row-actions-overflow-menu.md) with Edit and Remove, replacing the bare
  trash button.
- Edit reuses AddOverrideDrawer in an edit mode: scope is locked and shown
  read-only, the current value is prefilled, and it saves through the
  existing setForScope upsert.
- Remove now routes through a confirmation dialog that states plainly that
  no data is deleted (existing rows keep their stamped retention; only new
  ingestion uses the fallback) and shows the REAL post-removal value.

The fallback number is resolved server-side via a new previewScopeRemoval
query that reuses resolveRetention over the org's rows minus the scope's
own rows — so the dialog can never show a value that diverges from what an
actual removal produces, and it returns only day counts (never a sibling
scope's rule identity, preserving the read-scope gating).

* fix(data-retention): init drawer only on open/editTarget, not scope-ref churn

A background snapshot refetch could change available.projects' reference and
re-run the init effect mid-edit, wiping in-progress scope/preset/custom input.
Depend only on open + editTarget; read the latest scope inputs inside so the
next open re-reads them. Addresses CodeRabbit review.

* style(data-retention): biome organizeImports on changed files

CI lint (biome check) flagged import ordering in RemoveScopeConfirmDialog and
the data-retention page. Auto-fixed; no logic change.

* style(data-retention): apply biome formatting to changed files

CI lint (reviewdog biome ci) checks formatting on diff lines; my service
import, a .filter, and test object literals didn't match biome's canonical
format. Ran biome --write. No logic change; tests + typecheck green.

* feat(data-retention): scope-aware Data Storage total + calmer card headings

Two customer reports on the Data Retention settings page:

1. Data Storage always showed only the current project's storage, even with
   "Organization" / "Everything you can see" selected on the scope filter — so
   an org with a 0 B project and a multi-GB project showed whichever project
   was active, never the org total.
2. The "Data Retention" / "Data Storage" headings were oversized ("feels like
   screaming").

Storage now tracks the scope selector. A new `getScopeStorageUsage` query
resolves the in-scope projects FROM the caller's organization, RBAC-filters
them to `traces:view`, and sums each tenant's storage — so a wider scope can
never surface storage for a project the caller couldn't already see. The card
shows "· N projects" when more than one contributes and the description matches
the scope (project / team / organization / everything you can see).

Aggregation reuses the existing per-tenant `getTotalStorageBytes` rather than a
new `TenantId IN (...)` sum: each per-tenant read keeps the hardened ClickHouse
settings (capped threads + execution time + per-table fallback) and its own
5-minute cache, so an org-wide total is mostly cache hits and one heavy tenant
can't blow the memory ceiling — avoiding the OOM hazard `_size_bytes`'s lazy
recompute caused in production. Reads run with bounded concurrency and a failed
tenant degrades to 0 (acceptable for a display, not billing).

Headings dropped from lg to sm/semibold with xs muted descriptions. Removed the
now-unused `getStorageUsage` / `getStorageBreakdown` tRPC procedures (the
scope query with a PROJECT scope covers the single-project case); the service
methods stay (the total-bytes fallback still uses the breakdown).

* refactor(data-retention): named onSave params, deterministic edit prefill, BDD test nesting

Address review feedback:
- onSave takes a named-params object instead of positional args
- openEditForGroup prefills from an explicit category priority (traces →
  scenarios → experiments) so divergent legacy groups are order-independent
- RemoveScopeConfirmDialog test nests when-blocks under given-contexts

* style(data-retention): apply biome formatting to PR files

* style(data-retention): sort imports in dataRetention router

* refactor(data-retention): resolve scope filter once and derive from it

Compute resolveScopeFilter a single time (memoized) and derive storageScope,
storageDescription, and the row filter from it so they can't drift.

* feat(data-retention): stale-while-revalidate storage cache

The per-tenant byte total now serves stale-while-revalidate: a cached value
returns immediately, and once it ages past the 5-min freshness window the read
still returns instantly while a background recompute runs. Only the first read
for a tenant blocks on the heavy _size_bytes query.

Background refreshes are single-flighted via a Redis SET-NX lock, so when many
pods/tabs see the same entry go stale they don't stampede ClickHouse. A failed
refresh keeps the last good value; a failed cold read caches a degraded 0 marked
already-stale so the scope total backs off yet self-heals on the next read.

Injectable clock makes the timing deterministic in tests.

* refactor(data-retention): named StorageMeterService ctor params + boolean naming

- Constructor takes a single named-params object { resolveClickHouseClient, now }
- Rename boolean won -> hasRefreshLock (is/has prefix convention)

fix(model-providers): pin modern Azure api-version + honour deploymentMapping inline (#5134)

* fix(model-providers): pin modern Azure api-version + honour deploymentMapping inline

Azure prompt-playground runs failed with 'azure: Resource not found' (HTTP
404) for newer (gpt-5-class) deployments. Two independent causes:

1. Stale, un-overridable api-version. In direct (non-gateway) mode the TS
   layer set no api_version, so the downstream gateway (Bifrost) fell back
   to its GA default 2024-10-21 — too old to resolve gpt-5-class Azure
   deployments, which 404 even when the deployment name is correct. The
   customer had no way to override it without enabling the API Gateway.

2. No model->deployment mapping inline. The model id was sent verbatim as
   the Azure deployment name; the existing deploymentMapping field (already
   honoured by the gateway/control-plane path in config.materialiser) was
   ignored by the in-process Studio/playground path.

Fix:
- prepareLitellmParams now always sets api_version for Azure, defaulting to
  a modern DEFAULT_AZURE_API_VERSION (2025-04-01-preview) in direct mode,
  overridable per provider via a new optional AZURE_OPENAI_API_VERSION key
  (surfaced in the direct-mode provider settings form).
- prepareLitellmParams resolves the model's deployment from deploymentMapping
  and forwards it as params.deployment; the nlpgo translator + dispatcher
  honour it (withDeploymentMap maps model id -> real deployment), falling
  back to the prior self-map when absent.

Both playground paths benefit from the api-version fix (the foundry proxy
path already forwards x-litellm-api_version). Deployment mapping is wired on
the verified Studio/dispatcher path.

Customer report.

* fix(model-providers): address review — normalize Azure deployment full-key lookup + mark gateway version optional

- deploymentMap full-key fallback now keys off the normalized params.model
  (was raw `model`, which can be the mp_.../... wire format and miss
  "azure/<model>" mappings). Adds a regression test for the mp-id case.
- AZURE_API_GATEWAY_VERSION added to optionalKeys: prepareLitellmParams
  defaults it when blank, so the form must not mark it required.

* fix(ci): use American spelling (honor) to satisfy go misspell linter

fix(studio): load the saved library prompt when reopening a workflow node (#4993)

* fix(studio): load the saved library prompt when reopening a workflow node

Saving a workflow LLM node's prompt to the library sets promptId and
clears localPromptConfig but leaves the node's stale inline parameters.
On reopen the bridge passed those inline params as initialLocalConfig,
which the prompt editor merged over the prompt it had just fetched from
the library, so a just-saved prompt showed stale content. The prompt was
present in the library and the playground but not in the workflow node.

The bridge now passes only genuine unpublished edits as initialLocalConfig
and the inline mirror as a separate inlineConfigFallback that the editor
uses only when the referenced prompt is not found (e.g. an imported
workflow). A saved prompt now loads its own library content on reopen.

* test(studio): use gpt-5-mini in prompt round-trip test fixtures

* fix(studio): propagate edits to inline fallback prompt (P1 from langwatch-agent)

The missing-prompt init branch in PromptEditorDrawer never seeded
savedFormValuesRef.current with the fallback baseline. In the form-watch
subscription, the !promptId branch is skipped (promptId IS set) and the
savedFormValuesRef.current branch is also skipped (ref is undefined), so
isUnsaved stays false and onLocalConfigChange(undefined) fires on every
edit — silently dropping the user's changes to imported workflows whose
referenced prompts are missing.

Seed savedFormValuesRef.current with the fallback-merged form values in
the missing-prompt branch, mirroring the found-prompt branch's pattern.
Edits now diff against the fallback baseline, isUnsaved flips true, and
the extracted LocalPromptConfig propagates to the bridge.

Adds a regression test that drives a real form edit in the missing-prompt
scenario and asserts onLocalConfigChange receives the edited config.

fix(translate): surface typed model errors instead of generic masking (#5198)

* fix(translate): surface typed model errors instead of generic masking

Inline translation rewrapped every failure in a generic
INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR and the frontend bare-catch showed a hardcoded
toast, so the platform's typed model-error toasts (missing model /
provider disabled / AI call failed) never fired — users only ever saw
"please try again" with no actionable detail.

Route translate through the existing wrapAiCall + featureByKey typed-error
infra (mirrors workflows.commit_message): resolve the model outside
wrapAiCall so ModelNotConfiguredError / ModelProviderDisabledError
propagate untouched, and wrap only the generateText call so provider
failures surface as a typed AiCallFailedError carrying the real
(truncated) provider message. Drop the frontend bare-catch toast so the
global tRPC error handler raises the actionable one.

Visibility fix: makes the real provider failure diagnosable in the UI;
does not itself cure the underlying provider error.

Closes #5197

* test(translate): assert serialised wire cause; tighten provider-disabled comment

CodeRabbit review:
- Assert the formatter-facing error contract (error.data.cause.errorMessage
  via errorFormatterForTesting) that the UI extractor actually reads, instead
  of the raw AiCallFailedError class property — so the test fails if the
  serializer drops the field the toast consumes.
- Make the model-resolution comment precise: the typed
  ModelProviderDisabledError is thrown by the cascade resolver for a
  configured-but-disabled FAST model, not by getVercelAIModel's own guard.

Also fix Biome import ordering.

* fix(translate): restore fallback toast for non-typed failures + log full provider error

Addresses ruthless-review findings:

- P2: the frontend catch only relied on the global typed-error toasts
  (missing model / provider disabled / AI call failed). Non-typed failures
  — "Project not found", DB/resolver errors that surface as a plain
  INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR with no typed cause — left the user with NO
  feedback at all (silent failure). Restore a generic fallback toast,
  gated by shouldShowGenericTranslateError() so it only fires when none of
  the typed extractors matched (no double-toast on the typed cases).

- P3: wrapAiCall truncates the provider error to the first line for the
  client. Log the FULL underlying error server-side before it's truncated,
  so prod triage keeps the later lines (provider bodies, gateway 404
  detail) — the whole point of the visibility work.

- P3 (tests): add backend MODEL_PROVIDER_DISABLED case proving the typed
  cause reaches domainErrorMiddleware untouched (the claim the comment
  makes); add translationError.unit.test.ts covering the fallback gating.

* test(evaluations): BDD specs for unified workflow + evaluations-v3 execution

Specs-first for merging the workflow evaluate path onto the evaluations-v3
orchestrator: workflow-as-target, inline data / dataset id / parameters
inputs, the reworked workflow evaluate endpoint, the nlpgo
execute_evaluation removal, and the Run via API dialog + snippet generator.
Repo-root specs are tagged @unimplemented until each phase binds its tests.

* feat(studio): remove the Optimizations tab from the results panel

Optimizations were DSPy-only and are gone (the server 410s execute_optimization
and the Optimize button is hidden on the Go engine), so the results panel's
Optimizations tab only ever showed 'No optimizations started yet'. Drop the tab
and the now-dead OptimizationResults / LoadedOptimizationResults rendering,
leaving a single Evaluations view, and repoint OptimizationStudio so an
optimizations open-request no longer targets a missing tab.

Adds a regression scenario and integration test asserting the panel shows only
the Evaluations tab.

* feat(experiments-v3): add a workflow target type

Introduce a top-level "workflow" target type (with workflowId /
workflowVersionId) so a whole studio workflow can be evaluated through the
evaluations-v3 pipeline. It is distinct from an "agent" target whose
agentType is "workflow" (a saved agent built as a single code node). This is
the schema and persistence-type foundation; the orchestrator execution
handler (executeWorkflowCell) follows.

* feat(experiments-v3): execute a workflow target through the orchestrator

A workflow target runs the committed studio workflow DSL once per dataset row
via execute_flow, then surfaces the End-node result as the target output and
each of the workflow's own evaluator nodes as an evaluator result (stringy
score/passed coerced). dataLoader loads the workflow DSL (loadedWorkflows), the
orchestrator dispatches workflow targets to the new executeWorkflowCell and
threads the map through getLoadedDataForTarget and targetMetadata, and the run
routes pass it on.

Binds three workflow-target scenarios via a mocked-boundary integration test;
multi-row continuation and cross-row trace linkage stay @unimplemented for the
end-to-end dogfood.

Address the review round on the workflow-as-target work:

- require workflowId when a target's type is workflow (zod refinement), so an

- scope the workflow version lookup to its own workflow, and key the workflow

runWithResults returned summary.runUrl ?? runUrl, and summary.runUrl is the

* fix(sdk): retry results readback through the post-completion materialization lag

Right after a run completes, the results endpoint can briefly 404 (not yet
available) or return 200 with an empty dataset before ClickHouse materializes
the rows. The python SDK cached the empty frame; the typescript SDK threw on
the 404. Both now retry the results fetch when the run reported rows, returning

* docs(experiments): document run-with-results, data-source overrides, and Run Options menu

Update the CI/CD experiments doc for the unified run path: the toolbar entry is
now the Run Options menu (Run in CI/CD), document reading per-row results back

Sweep of the experiment-path fixes onto workflows.run, which had the same two
bugs: it returned the platform (cloud) runUrl instead of the configured
endpoint, and fetched results once with no retry through the post-completion
materialization lag. Extract rebaseUrlToEndpoint and fetchResultsWithRetry into

* fix(python-sdk): defer pandas import, preserve falsy outputs, mark unit tests

- import pandas lazily inside build_results_df so importing langwatch.experiment

- map predicted to output with an is-not-None check so a falsy model output

* refactor(run-via-api): named params, BDD test structure, and review nits

Address CodeRabbit review on the run-via-api surface:
- buildRunSnippet and the useRunViaApiTabs callback take a single named-param
  object (folding lang into the input), per the repo named-parameter rule; all

- drop the unused IMAGE_EXAMPLE import and correct the projectSlug doc comment
- restructure the TableSettingsMenu dialog tests into given/when blocks and
  rename a studio describe to when-form
- delete a restating test comment
- index rows by dataset index in mapResults so the evaluation join is no longer
  O(evaluations x rows) on large result sets

* fix(evaluations): scope workflow evaluate to results-read perm and keep undeclared parameters

Three review fixes on the unified workflow evaluate path:

- The endpoint requires workflows:manage, but the caller then polls the run and reads results on /api/experiments/runs/:runId(/results), which require evaluations:view. A workflows-only scoped key would start a run it could not read. Chain requireApiKeyPermission(evaluations:view) so the ceiling is consistent across start and read. Legacy project keys bypass the ceiling, so existing callers are unaffected.

- A parameter the workflow does not declare as an entry field was added as a dataset column but had no target input or mapping, so buildTargetInputs never read it. Extend the workflow target inputs+mappings with any undeclared parameter keys.

* fix(evaluations): surface workflow evaluator node names in results

Workflow evaluator nodes have no DB evaluator record, so recordEvaluatorResult stored evaluatorName=null and the results table showed the raw node id. The orchestrator now keeps each evaluator node's DSL display name, threads it onto the evaluator_result event, and falls back to it at storage time when there is no DB evaluator. * docs(experiments): document the row_indices override option

* fix(typescript-sdk): only retry results reads through the lag window when rows are expected

fetchResultsWithRetry retried every thrown read error, even when the run reported no rows, turning a permanent failure (e.g. 401) into maxAttempts of avoidable delay and contradicting the documented contract that a no-rows read returns its first result. Gate the error retry on expectsRows so the post-completion projection lag is only waited out when there is something to wait for.

* fix(evaluations): price per-cell LLM cost in evaluations-v3 runs

Evaluations-v3 cells showed no cost for prompt/workflow targets even though the trace showed cost. The cell cost comes from the engine's execution_state.cost, but the Go nlpgo engine never set it for LLM nodes: the gateway returns no cost on this path and the engine has no price table, so only the trace-ingest collector priced the call (from token usage x llmModels.json). That is why the trace had cost and the cell did not.

nlpgo now surfaces the exact token usage + resolved provider/model on the node state (NodeMetrics in execution_state.metrics). The orchestrator prices each cell from those counts via getMatchingLLMModelCost + estimateCost, the same canonical path the collector uses, so the cell cost matches the trace cost. Applied to both the prompt-target (executeCell) and workflow-target (executeWorkflowCell) paths.

* feat(langy): per-session OpenCode workers + per-request creds

The Fix 2 architecture: the pod's server.js becomes a process pool
manager that spawns one opencode subprocess per Langy conversation,
with that session's credentials injected as env vars at spawn time.
The pod itself holds NO user credentials — they arrive in each /chat
request body and die with the worker subprocess. OS process boundaries
make per-session isolation real, not aspirational.

## Control plane (langwatch/src/server/)

- New service: services/langy/LangyCredentialService.ts. Method
  getOrProvision({ projectId, actorUserId }) returns the four creds
  a Langy worker needs:
    * langwatchApiKey  — project.apiKey (sk-lw-*) for MCP tool calls
    * llmVirtualKey    — auto-provisioned VK secret for the AI gateway
    * langwatchEndpoint — process.env.LANGWATCH_API_URL
    * gatewayBaseUrl   — process.env.LW_GATEWAY_BASE_URL
  Per-project Langy VK is provisioned on first use via
  VirtualKeyService.create (picks the first GatewayProviderCredential
  by fallbackPriorityGlobal, throws actionable error if none exists).
  Plaintext is stored encrypted in ProjectSecret under 'langy_vk_secret'.
  Subsequent calls decrypt + return.
  Race-safe: P2002 on ProjectSecret.create triggers re-read of winner's
  secret (the losing-race VK is orphaned, acceptable v1 cost).

- routes/langy.ts /chat handler now:
    * Requires LANGY_INTERNAL_SECRET env (503 if missing)
    * Calls LangyCredentialService.getOrProvision per request
    * Returns 409 with actionable message on LangyCredentialResolutionError
    * POSTs to ${OPENCODE_AGENT_URL}/chat (was /run) with body
      { conversationId, prompt, system, credentials } and header
      Authorization: Bearer ${LANGY_INTERNAL_SECRET}
    * Sends langyOverride as `system` instead of concatenating into
      `prompt` (cleaner separation, lower jailbreak risk)

- 6 unit tests for LangyCredentialService covering: existing secret
  (no re-provision), provision + store path, missing provider credential,
  missing project, missing env config, race on ProjectSecret.create.

## Pod (langwatch/src/tests/langy/k8s/)

- server.js: complete rewrite. Map<conversationId, {child, port,
  openCodeSessionId, lastSeen}>. /chat endpoint validates
  Authorization header against LANGY_INTERNAL_SECRET. On first
  message for a conversation, manager:
    1. Creates /workspace/sessions/{convId} as worker HOME
    2. Writes per-worker .config/opencode/config.json with MCP creds
    3. Reads /workspace/AGENTS.md, substitutes ${LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT},
       writes per-worker AGENTS.md
    4. Symlinks skills/ to /workspace/skills (shared, read-only)
    5. Picks free port via net.createServer().listen(0)
    6. Spawns opencode subprocess with credentials in env, cwd+HOME
       both pointing at workerHome
    7. Polls readiness, creates one opencode session, stores its id
  Subsequent turns reuse the worker, update lastSeen. Reaper kills
  workers idle > LANGY_WORKER_IDLE_MS (default 10 min). MAX_WORKERS
  cap (default 20) returns 'at-capacity' event when reached. SIGTERM
  kills all workers before exit.

- entrypoint.sh: removed the global ~/.config/opencode/config.json
  write (manager does per-worker now), removed the AGENTS.md
  ${LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT} sed substitution (manager does per-worker now),
  removed the `opencode serve --port 4096 &` autostart (manager spawns
  per session). Keeps the skills/ + AGENTS.md template writes.

- pod.yaml: adds env LANGY_INTERNAL_SECRET via secretKeyRef. This is
  the ONLY env var at pod level — it's service-to-service auth, not
  user credential.

- secrets.example.yaml: replaces obsolete GATEWAY_API_KEY +
  LANGWATCH_API_KEY (per-session injection now) with
  LANGY_INTERNAL_SECRET. Documents `openssl rand -hex 32` for generation.

- .env.example: adds LANGY_INTERNAL_SECRET on the control plane side.

## Architecture summary

  [Browser] -> /api/langy/chat (with session cookie)
       |
  [Control plane]
       |  resolves: project.apiKey, per-project VK (auto-provisioned)
       |  POSTs to manager with Bearer LANGY_INTERNAL_SECRET +
       |    { conversationId, prompt, system, credentials }
       v
  [Pod: manager (server.js)]
       |  per-conversation routing:
       |    new      -> spawn opencode subprocess with creds in env
       |    existing -> forward to that subprocess
       |  streams NDJSON events back to control plane
       v
  [Per-session opencode subprocess]
       |  reads per-worker config.json (MCP gets LANGWATCH_API_KEY)
       |  reads per-worker AGENTS.md (URL placeholders resolved)
       |  calls AI gateway as OPENAI_BASE_URL with OPENAI_API_KEY (VK)
       v
  [AI gateway + MCP server + LangWatch API]

Per-session isolation comes from the OS process boundary — Worker A
cannot read Worker B's env even though both live in the same pod.

* fix(langy): wire in-product Langy chat to the OpenCode K8s pod end-to-end

Three independent bugs blocked the UI sidebar from getting a real
response from the agent:

1. **Middleware scoped accidentally to all /api/* requests.**
   `app.use(async (c, next) => {...})` on the langy Hono sub-app
   (`basePath("/api")`) gated every `/api/*` call with the staff-only
   + feature-flag check, returning 403 "Langy is not available for
   your account" on unrelated endpoints (e.g. tRPC `publicEnv`), which
   broke even the sign-in page render. Scoped the middleware to
   `app.use("/langy/*", ...)` so it only guards the Langy endpoints.

2. **Stream parser mismatched the pod's event shape.**
   The /langy/chat handler proxies to the OpenCode pod's /run endpoint
   and re-streams text deltas to the UI. The parser only handled the
   legacy `{type:"text", part:{text:"..."}}` shape, but the pod emits
   `{type:"message.part.delta", properties:{field:"text", delta:"..."}}`.
   Result: 200 OK with text-start → text-end and zero text-delta in
   between — sidebar showed an empty assistant message. Added the
   OpenCode shape to the parser (legacy shape kept for backward compat).

3. **Legacy LANGY_SYSTEM_PROMPT confused the OpenCode agent.**
   The handler used to prepend LANGY_SYSTEM_PROMPT (which describes
   Vercel-AI-SDK `propose_*` tools that don't exist in the pod) into
   the prompt sent to /run. The agent would either parrot the prompt
   back ("I will read your project evaluators, prompts, and datasets...")
   or, with no override, fall through to OpenCode's default "what
   should I do in this repository?" coding-assistant persona. Replaced
   the prepended LANGY_SYSTEM_PROMPT with a tight Langy-specific
   system block phrased around the MCP tool catalog the pod actually
   has (search_traces, get_analytics, list_evaluators, ...).

Verified via Playwright in the browser: sidebar message round-trips
through /api/langy/chat -> pod /run -> OpenCode -> MCP -> AI gateway
and streams a real assistant reply back as text-delta events.

* fix(langy/scenarios): adapter doubled output; judge passed contradictory verdicts; pod over-applied '24h' window

Three issues surfaced auditing the 45-scenario transcripts:

1) langy-agent.ts (test adapter, NOT the in-product backend) was doing a
   cascading `??` lookup that pulled "text" from every event shape it saw.
   That made it (a) concatenate the user's own prompt — which arrives as a
   `message.part.updated` event with the same shape as assistant parts —
   into the captured assistantText, and (b) double-count every assistant
   chunk by reading both the streaming `message.part.delta` AND the final
   accumulated text from `message.part.updated`. Probed the pod directly
   with a "reply PING" prompt: the SSE stream contains exactly one delta;
   doubling was 100% adapter-side. Fix mirrors langy.ts:316-327 — only
   message.part.delta with field==="text". The in-product Langy was
   always clean; the duplication was a test-only artifact.

2) Two scenarios had judge criteria phrased loose enough that an LLM
   judge could mark them PASS while its own reasoning text contradicted
   the verdict:
   - "declines an out-of-scope request": judge wrote "It did not decline
     or redirect to LangWatch capabilities" then marked the "declined"
     criterion as ✓. Rewrite as a hard content check (no haiku/poem/story
     in the reply body) so there's nothing left to wave through.
   - "explains trace failures in plain English": three criteria where one
     was always inconclusive on a project with zero failures; judge would
     pass the scenario overall while leaving the "explains" criterion
     unmet. Collapse to a single criterion that covers both "explained a
     real failure" and "clearly said no failures found".

3) k8s/entrypoint.sh rule 7 + the Response format template told Langy to
   default to "last 24h" and emit "No X in last 24h." on empty results —

The Fix 2 architecture: the pod's server.js becomes a process pool
manager that spawns one opencode subprocess per Langy conversation,
with that session's credentials injected as env vars at spawn time.
The pod itself holds NO user credentials — they arrive in each /chat
request body and die with the worker subprocess. OS process boundaries
make per-session isolation real, not aspirational.

  getOrProvision({ projectId, actorUserId }) returns the four creds
  a Langy worker needs:
    * langwatchApiKey  — project.apiKey (sk-lw-*) for MCP tool calls
    * llmVirtualKey    — auto-provisioned VK secret for the AI gateway
    * langwatchEndpoint — process.env.LANGWATCH_API_URL
    * gatewayBaseUrl   — process.env.LW_GATEWAY_BASE_URL
  Per-project Langy VK is provisioned on first use via
  VirtualKeyService.create (picks the first GatewayProviderCredential
  by fallbackPriorityGlobal, throws actionable error if none exists).
  Plaintext is stored encrypted in ProjectSecret under 'langy_vk_secret'.
  Subsequent calls decrypt + return.

  secret (the losing-race VK is orphaned, acceptable v1 cost).

      { conversationId, prompt, system, credentials } and header

    2. Writes per-worker .config/opencode/config.json with MCP creds
    3. Reads /workspace/AGENTS.md, substitutes ${LANGWATCH_ENDPOINT},

fix(experiments-v3): stop body rows bleeding through sticky header gap on vertical scroll (#5250)

When scrolling the workbench table, body row content was visible above
the column headers — appearing as faint text between the "Prompts or
Agents" super header and the "category_classifier / Score" column
header row.

The column header row's sticky `top` offset was a hardcoded
`SUPER_HEADER_HEIGHT = 51`, but the super header row's actual rendered
height depends on the browser's box-model interpretation of `<th>`

rows became visible.

useLayoutEffect that measures the row via getBoundingClientRect and
tracks changes via ResizeObserver, so the column header sticks flush
against the super header regardless of future style/padding changes.

test(infra): register global afterEach(cleanup) so portaled dialogs stop leaking (#4469) (#5256)

vitest.config.ts runs without `globals: true`, so React Testing Library's
automatic per-test cleanup never registers. Component tests that render
portaled Chakra dialogs/modals and do not call cleanup() themselves leak every
render into document.body; accumulated dialogs get marked aria-hidden by focus
management, and getByRole/getAllByRole then intermittently fail with a CI-only
"Unable to find role" error (root cause of #4467).

Register afterEach(cleanup) once in the shared setupFile (test-setup.ts) so the
whole class of current and future dialog/modal tests is fixed at the root
rather than adding a per-file afterEach(cleanup) to each. cleanup() no-ops when
a test rendered nothing, so node-environment (non-jsdom) tests are unaffected.

Add a regression guard that renders a portaled dialog across two consecutive
tests with no local cleanup: it can see exactly one dialog on the second render
only if the global hook ran between them.

* fix(experiments-v3): 500 on repeated workflow evaluate calls

ExperimentService.findOrCreateForWorkflow's "existing" branch called
the generic ExperimentRepository.upsert with only { workbenchState }.
That method builds Prisma's create: object from the same partial data
via an unsafe type cast, so create: ends up missing required fields

evaluate call after the first for a given workflow threw

The row is confirmed to exist at that point, so this should always
have been an update, not an upsert. Swapped to updateById, which
removed the last caller of the generic upsert — deleted it too since
its unsafe cast was a footgun waiting to bite the next caller.

the URL but the drawer stayed open.

Root cause: every drawer is React.lazy() (perf: lazy-load drawer
registry, #3243) rendered inside a single Suspense boundary in
CurrentDrawer. React Router v7's RouterProvider wraps every navigation
state update in React.startTransition by default. Under React 18
semantics, when a transition-wrapped update causes a Suspense boundary
to suspend for the first time, React keeps showing the previously
committed UI instead of the fallback — so a first-time-this-session
drawer mount (or unmount) silently does nothing until an unrelated
re-render happens to resolve it. A hard refresh bypasses transitions
entirely (fresh initial render), which is why it "fixed" the drawer.

Fixed by threading flushSync through drawer navigations (open, close,
and the two URL-cleanup paths in CurrentDrawer), which forces
ReactDOM.flushSync instead of startTransition. That requires
RouterProvider from "react-router/dom" (flushSync is a no-op without
it, per react-router's own runtime warning) — swapped in main.tsx.

* fix(drawers): close remaining flushSync gaps from ruthless-review

Three follow-ups from review of the flushSync fix:

- navigateToDrawer (module-level open path, used by
  OnlineEvaluationDrawer for flow callbacks) went through
  RouterSingleton.push, which never forwarded flushSync to the
  underlying router at all — same first-time-lazy-Suspense bug,
  unpatched in a live code path. Widened the imperative router type to
  carry {replace, flushSync} and threaded it through push/replace.
  Fixed replace() not passing {replace: true} to navigate() while
  touching this — it was always pushing.
- useUpdateDrawerParams had the same bare push/replace pattern; added
  flushSync for consistency even though it doesn't usually mount a new
  drawer (only drawer.<key> sub-params change, not drawer.open).
- Added regression tests asserting flushSync: true reaches
  router.push/replace on open and close, so a future accidental
  removal fails CI instead of silently reintroducing the bug.

fix(langy): stop proposal-handler registration from looping the workbench (#5280)

The experiments workbench recreates its Langy proposalHandlers object on
most renders (several tRPC mutation/utils objects in its useMemo deps
don't have stable identity across renders). useRegisterLangyHandlers had
`handlers` in its effect's dependency array, so every recreation fired
registerHandlers -> setProposalHandlers (React state) in LangyProvider,
which re-rendered the whole subtree under the provider -- including the
workbench itself -- producing a new handlers object again. Infinite loop,
manifesting as a repeating "Maximum update depth exceeded" console error
on any workbench page (LangyProvider always wraps page content, so this
fired regardless of whether that user has Langy access).

Root fix: proposalHandlers never needed to be React state. Every consumer
(LangySidebar's applyProposal) only reads it at click-time, never during
render. Store it in a ref instead -- registering a new handlers object no
longer triggers a re-render, so the loop can't start. experimentSlug stays
as state since it IS rendered (the "On: <slug>" panel subtitle).

fix(ui): stop Tooltip from clobbering the anchor id of nested asChild triggers (#5351)

* fix(ui): stop Tooltip from clobbering the anchor id of nested asChild triggers

Any place that wraps a Menu/Popover/Clipboard `*.Trigger asChild` directly
inside `<Tooltip>` has both components' asChild clones fighting over the
same DOM node's `id`. Tooltip's id wins, so Zag's own machine (Menu,
Popover, Clipboard, MenuContextTrigger) can no longer find its trigger by
id — its floating-ui position update never runs, and the menu/popover
content renders pinned at the page's raw top-left origin instead of
anchored under the button that opened it.

Fix: insert a plain `<Box as="span" display="inline-flex">` between
Tooltip and the inner Trigger so each asChild clone lands on a different
DOM node. Verified live (before/after screenshots) that Group By now
opens anchored to its toolbar button, and that clicking an option still
works.

Applied to every confirmed instance of the pattern: GroupingSelector,
ColumnsDropdown, AutomateButton, TimeRangePicker, RecentChatsMenu,
LangyGitHubMenu, model-providers (both occurrences), AnnotationPopover,
DrawerHeader, and SyntaxHelpDrawer's copy button.

fix(monitors): stop per-trace evaluations running twice (survivesDispatch dedup) (#5163)

* fix(monitors): stop per-trace evaluations running twice (survivesDispatch dedup)

Per-trace online evaluations ran twice: the groupQueue dedup only prevents
duplicate STAGING — once a job is dispatched (gone from the staging sorted set)
the dedup key is treated as stale (DEL + restage), so a late span arriving after
the evaluationTrigger reactor fires re-stages -> re-dispatches -> duplicate
evaluation runs (6 evaluators x 2 = 12).

Adds an opt-in survivesDispatch flag to the dedup config. When set, STAGE_LUA
honors a dispatched-but-TTL-alive dedup key (squashes the new job) instead of
DEL+restage, in BOTH the single and batch stage paths. Append-only ARGV:
single ARGV[11]; batch per-job stride 8->9 (new arg at offset+9); trailing
nowMs/globalBudget stay end-relative. Default-off = byte-identical existing
behavior. The evaluationTrigger reactor opts in.

Closes #3912

perf(analytics): defer PostHog session recording, keep core capture eager (#5349)

* perf(analytics): defer PostHog session recording, keep core capture eager

posthog.init() set session_recording directly, so the recorder chunk
(rrweb + replay extensions, 50KB+) fetched on the critical path for
every session. Init now starts with disable_session_recording: true;
posthog.startSessionRecording() fires from a requestIdleCallback (with
a window-load/timeout fallback) once first paint is done.

Core capture (autocapture/pageview/identify) is untouched — init still
runs the moment publicEnv resolves, so no event-capture timing changes
and nothing risks being dropped.

Part of #5330 (Tier 1) · parent #5329 · closes #5347

* test(hooks): expand usePostHog coverage to 100%

Adds coverage for: no publicEnv yet, missing POSTHOG_KEY, POSTHOG_HOST
present vs. defaulted, window.posthog exposure, debug-logging gated on
NODE_ENV, the requestIdleCallback timeout arg, and the
already-complete-document fallback branch for the Safari idle-defer
path. Marks the SSR-safety `typeof window` guard as intentionally
unreachable in this browser-only Vite SPA rather than faking a test
for it.

* fix(hooks): cancel pending session-recording start on unmount, address review

- usePostHog.ts: startSessionRecordingWhenIdle() now returns a cancel
  function, tracked in a ref and invoked from the effect's cleanup.
  Without this, a stale idle/timeout/load callback scheduled by a
  previous render (or a component that unmounted before it fired)
  could still call posthog.startSessionRecording() later, re-enabling
  recording out from under state the component no longer reflects.
  (CodeRabbit review, P2)
- Test teardown now also calls vi.restoreAllMocks(), not just
  vi.unstubAllGlobals() — the Safari-fallback tests spy on
  document.readyState via vi.spyOn, which unstubAllGlobals doesn't
  revert, so it could leak a fake readyState into later tests.
  (CodeRabbit + review, P3)
- Added regression coverage for the new cancellation behavior across
  all three defer paths, including the cancelIdleCallback-unavailable
  case. 100% statement/branch/function/line coverage maintained on
  usePostHog.ts.

fix(experiments-v3): resolve pairwise comparator UX bugs from dogfooding (#5367)

* fix(experiments-v3): resolve pairwise comparator UX bugs from dogfooding

Fixes a batch of issues surfaced while dogfooding the pairwise compare
feature (#5142, #5195): mislabeled buttons, dark-mode contrast failures,
inconsistent drawer styling, a raw 400 error leaking to users, and two
state-management bugs where the config drawer silently dropped user
input (Variant A/B/Golden field, and Include cost/duration) on re-render.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(experiments-v3): forward topLevel through ZodDefault unwrap in DynamicZodForm

The prior fix for duplicated Swap And Confirm / Allow Tie labels only
suppressed the inline label when topLevel=true, but the ZodDefault
unwrap branch recursed without forwarding it — every settings field
with .default() (which includes both of these) silently fell back to
topLevel=false, so the duplicate label bug was still live for the one
evaluator it was meant to fix. Verified live: reopening the Pairwise
Compare drawer now shows each label once, and Include cost/duration
toggles persist correctly across save + reopen.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(experiments-v3): add regression test for missing-mapping alert click

Closes the one verification gap noted in the bug-fix batch: the alert
icon's onClick previously fell through to the chip's own uncontrolled
Menu.Trigger before stopPropagation could run. Asserts the click calls
onEdit exactly once and never renders the chip's own dropdown items.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(lint): satisfy biome formatting in pairwise bugfix files

CI's langwatch-app-ci lint job failed on line-wrapping in
ModelSelector.tsx, iconsMap.tsx, and evaluations-legacy.ts.
Applied via `biome check --write`, no logic changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(experiments-v3): apply CodeRabbit review suggestions

- Rename EvaluatorChip's menuOpen/setMenuOpen to isMenuOpen/setIsMenuOpen
  to satisfy the repo's boolean-naming convention (is/has/should prefix).
- Drop the redundant createEvaluator() call in the new alert-click test,
  reusing the already-constructed evaluator instance instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* refactor(ui): reuse providerKey instead of re-deriving in ModelSelector

CodeRabbit: selectedItem.value.split("/")[0] duplicated the already-
computed providerKey (selectedItem.value === model by construction of
the find() above), so just reuse it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(experiments-v3): apply remaining CodeRabbit outside-diff findings

- Rename DynamicZodForm's topLevel param to isTopLevel (boolean naming
  convention), same as the earlier menuOpen -> isMenuOpen rename.
- Fix a real, pre-existing bug in totalColumnPercentage: the dataset/
  target summation loops reconstructed column IDs as `dataset_${id}`
  and bare `target.id`, but resize actually stores under the header's
  real ID (`dataset.${id}` / `target.${targetId}`, per the
  columnHelper.accessor calls above). The mismatch meant a resized
  dataset/target column's width never factored into the table's total,
  silently falling back to the default percentage. Same root cause as
  the pairwise-column width bug this PR already fixes, just for the
  other two column types — verified by tracing the actual header IDs
  written by the resize handler and columnHelper definitions.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
