feat(groupqueue): content-addressed tiered blob offload (ADR-029/030) (#4999)

* docs(groupQueue): ADR-029 content-addressed blob store + ADR-030 hardening + Gherkin specs

Two ADRs and three spec files describe what GQ2 builds:

- ADR-029 — content-addressed, tenant-namespaced, tiered blob store that
  collapses identical fan-out payloads to one stored blob, refcounted by a
  per-blob holder set (the reclaim eval).
- ADR-030 — hardening notes for the store path: payload-size cap, gunzip
  decompression cap, transient-vs-missing error classification, holder TTL
  coordination, atomic hold transfer on retry/squash, server-trusted re-mint
  of read locations, branded TenantId, cluster-slot guard.
- payload-store-content-addressed.feature + payload-store-blob-hardening.feature
  — behavioural contract behind both ADRs (encode/decode shape, holder
  lifecycle, all failure-mode scenarios).
- payload-envelope.feature — note pointing the GQ1 blob-lifecycle scenarios at
  the GQ2 superseded mechanism.

* feat(groupQueue): content-addressed tiered blob store + holder refcount (GQ2)

The on-the-wire and storage machinery behind ADR-029 + ADR-030; dormant until
GROUP_QUEUE_ENVELOPE_WRITES_ENABLED is set.

- jobEnvelope: GQ2 envelope encoding (header + body, version 2) with a payload-
  size cap and decompression cap (zip-bomb guard).
- tieredBlobStore: content-addressed, tenant-namespaced two-tier store (Redis
  4-256 KiB; reused stored-objects bucket above) with server-trusted re-mint
  of read locations and transient-vs-missing error classification.
- blobHolders: per-blob Redis SET with atomic acquire/release/transfer Lua
  scripts; reclaim happens in the eval that drops the last holder (no
  acquire-then-release gap). Self-transfer + already-released become explicit
  no-ops; the release/transfer evals carry only the keys that exist so an
  s3-tier eval can't CROSSSLOT in cluster mode.
- blobKeys: single source of truth for the Redis blob/holder key layout
  (branded TenantId-typed) so the store and the holder Lua can't drift.
- redisJobBlobStore: routed through the shared key builder.
- stored-objects: redactStorageUri family covers s3/gs/azure-blob/file
  case-insensitively, with a free-text variant for SDK error messages; the
  factory exports createStorageRegistry so the GroupQueue can wire the s3 tier.

Unit tests cover envelope encode/decode + size cap + zip-bomb guard; tier
selection + namespacing + re-mint + transient classification; hash-tag guard;
URI redaction. Integration tests prove holder reclaim sequences
(release-without-acquire, self-transfer, s3 reclaim) and TTL refresh.

* feat(groupQueue): wire content-addressed offload through GroupQueue

The collaborator + composition-root wiring that turns the GQ2 machinery into
end-to-end behaviour: large staged values offload to a content-addressed blob;
the holder is acquired at stage and released on completion, dropped via atomic
transfer on retry/squash; a missing blob fail-safes (recover via event replay);
a transient store failure re-stages. Cleanup is tenant-guarded so a mis-routed
ref never reads or releases another tenant's holder (ADR-030 §5).

- envelopeBlobLifecycle: encode/decode/acquire/release/transfer; resolves the
  storage destination per-project; cross-checks ref.projectId against the
  group's tenant on decode AND release AND transfer; redacts storage URIs out
  of error logs.
- groupQueue: wired to the lifecycle on send (orphaned dedup → transfer), batch
  send (per-item orphan), dispatch (decode), success (release), retry
  (atomic transfer to the re-encoded value), terminal failure (release).
- eventSourcing: composition root supplies createStorageRegistry +
  resolveProjectStorageDestination.

Integration tests prove the end-to-end path: payload offloads, dispatch
resolves it, holder + blob reclaim on success. Tenant-mismatch tests prove
decode refuses the cross-tenant read and release/transfer skip the foreign
holder.

* feat(groupQueue): exclude queue machinery from the content-addressed body

Without this, the same event fanned out to N reactors hashes N times because
each reactor's __jobName / __jobType / __pipelineName perturbs the body bytes
— content-addressed dedup never fires for the fan-out it was built for.

This change moves the queue's machinery fields (every `__*` key in jobData:
routing names, __attempt, __context, __groupId, __stagedJobId, __dispatchScore)
into the GQ2 envelope header. The body is now pure user payload, hashed alone.
On decode the machinery is re-merged onto the parsed body so downstream code
sees the same shape as before.

Net effect: 30 reactors fanning out one event share one stored blob (held by
30 distinct slots in the holder set); a retry re-encode produces the SAME
content hash so the atomic transfer is a same-set SADD+SREM rather than a
cross-set reclaim.

Wire format:
- header.p/t/n keep the routing trio (the read-fast-path for the Lua
  dispatcher and readJobRoutingMeta — read without parsing the body).
- header.m carries the rest of the machinery (__attempt, __context,
  __groupId, __stagedJobId, __dispatchScore).
- The routing trio is NOT duplicated in header.m, keeping the wire format
  tight and removing a second source of truth that could drift.
- The strip is allowlist-free — any future `__*` field is automatically
  lifted to the header — so a maintainer can't accidentally regress dedup
  by adding a new machinery field to the body.

Public API contract:
- `GroupQueueProcessor.send` / `sendBatch` reject any user payload that
  contains a top-level `__*` key. The `__*` namespace is reserved for queue
  machinery (always was — INTERNAL_FIELDS); now that violating it would
  silently dedup-collide on the content hash and clobber on decode, the
  contract is enforced at the public send-boundary rather than left implicit.

Tests:
- Unit: two GQ2 envelopes with identical user payloads but different
  machinery produce ONE stored blob (the fan-out invariant). Inline-tier
  GQ2 round-trips machinery via header.m + header.p/t/n so downstream code
  sees the original jobData.
- Integration: a same-content retry with a different __attempt hashes
  identically so the atomic transfer is a same-set SADD+SREM (the queue
  retry-cheapness guarantee). send/sendBatch reject a payload with a
  __custom / __sneaky key so the namespace contract is loud rather than
  silent.

* docs(groupQueue): GroupQueue ARCHITECTURE + README; refresh event-sourcing docs

- queues/groupQueue/ARCHITECTURE.md (new): the technical deep-dive — staging
  Lua, dispatcher loop, tiered envelope (inline ≤ 1 KiB raw / ≤ 4 KiB gzip /
  ≤ 256 KiB Redis-blob / ≤ 50 MiB s3-blob), content-addressed sharing,
  routing-exclusion, holder-set refcount + atomic reclaim, retries, dedup,
  coalescing, pause/resume, tenant isolation, failure handling, observability.
- queues/groupQueue/README.md (new): the usage guide — when to use it,
  configuration knobs, process roles, dedup modes, coalescing, tiered storage
  in usage terms, caveats, testing, observability, common pitfalls.
- event-sourcing/ARCHITECTURE.md: rewrote the Queue System section so it no
  longer claims GroupQueue uses BullMQ (it uses Redis + Lua + fastq); rewrote
  Process Roles, No Checkpoints, Failure Handling to match. Added a pointer
  to the new GroupQueue docs in the Key Implementation Files table.
- event-sourcing/README.md: fixed the "Registration connects to ClickHouse,
  Redis, and BullMQ" line and the BullMQ-retries pitfall; linked the GroupQueue
  README from the queues row in the Navigating-the-Codebase table.

* fix(groupQueue): address 2026-06-24 review + one audit follow-up

BLOCKERS closed:
- blobConstants: restore GQ1's 7-day backstop TTL (new
  GQ1_BLOB_BACKSTOP_TTL_SECONDS); GQ2's 3-day derived TTL stays for
  refcounted/access-refreshed blobs. Staged-but-not-yet-dispatched GQ1 jobs
  see no intervening read between put and TTL, so the cut from 7 → 3 days
  was silently dangerous under the write flag (2026-06-24 review).
- groupQueue.parseDrainedPayload + caller: TransientBlobStoreError is now
  routed through the SAME handleTransientDecode as the dispatched-job path
  (siblings re-staged, dispatched job re-staged with backoff), instead of
  silently dropping every sibling to replay on a brief S3 blip (ADR-030 §2).

NON-BLOCKERS closed:
- envelopeBlobLifecycle.transfer fallback: ordered acquire-then-release
  (awaited on the acquire side, release only if acquire succeeded), so a
  release-before-acquire race can't drop the old blob. Comment tracks
  extending TRANSFER_LUA for the mixed-format case as follow-up.
- envelopeBlobLifecycle: s3 reclaim failures now increment
  gqBlobReclaimS3FailuresTotal on top of the warn (release AND transfer
  paths), so a bucket-lifecycle-only backstop can't silently degrade.
- tieredBlobStore: BlobTooLargeError coerced to null now also warns +
  increments gqBlobDecodeCapExceededTotal — oncall sees possible tamper /
  zip-bomb events distinct from "TTL reclaimed the blob".
- jobEnvelope: assertPayloadWithinCap now accepts a ctx { projectId, queueName,
  logger } and emits a tenant-attributed warn + gqPayloadTooLargeTotal at the
  cap boundary. GQ2 → GQ1 downgrade now emits gqEnvelopeGQ2DowngradeTotal +
  a loud warn identifying which side is missing.
- redisJobBlobStore: split get (worker hot path, refreshes TTL) from peek
  (ops-dashboard inspection, no GETEX). decodeJobEnvelope gains a readMode
  arg threaded from the ops repo so a repeatedly-viewed blocked group can't
  keep its orphan blobs alive indefinitely.
- tieredBlobStore: S3_TIER_THRESHOLD_BYTES = COMMAND_INLINE_THRESHOLD (was
  a re-typed 256*1024 literal — now derived so an ADR-022 retune moves both
  sides in lockstep).
- envelopeBlobLifecycle.decode + release: single splitEnvelope per value
  via new readEnvelopeHoldFromHeader / readEnvelopeRetirement helpers.
  Removes the ~2× Buffer.from + JSON.parse per successful completion on the
  worker hot path.
- jobEnvelope.encode: writesEnabled threaded through as an explicit param
  (env var read stays as fallback for tests). Composition roots can now
  make the rollout contract explicit rather than depending on per-call
  process.env reads.
- tieredBlobStore.contentHash: accepts string | Buffer; hashSource on
  encodeJobEnvelope now passes payloadJson directly. Saves a full-payload
  Buffer.from on the encode hot path (~4 MiB per producer call at fan-out
  size for a 4 MiB payload).

Audit follow-up (from my /review-pr on this branch):
- groupQueue retry path: the re-encode is wrapped in its own try; on failure
  the OLD hold is explicitly released and the slot completes via the
  fail-safe. Prevents a 3-day phantom hold on encode-time transients.

Test doubles updated (peek added to InMemoryJobBlobStore).

Verified locally: typecheck + biome clean; 52 unit tests green
(jobEnvelope + tieredBlobStore + redisHashTag + redact-storage-uri).
Integration tests deferred to CI (no Docker locally).

* fix(groupQueue): register new blob metrics in hot-reload cleanup + align GQ1 TTL test

- metrics.ts: add the four new counter names (gq_blob_reclaim_s3_failures_total,
  gq_blob_decode_cap_exceeded_total, gq_envelope_gq2_downgrade_total,
  gq_payload_too_large_total) to the metricNames cleanup array. Without this,
  every test process that re-loads the module (unit test workers with vitest's
  hot module cache) throws "A metric with the name ... has already been
  registered" at import time, tripping every downstream test file that
  transitively imports event-sourcing (orgBillableEventsMeter, interposition).
- redisJobBlobStore.integration.test: rename THREE_DAYS_SECONDS →
  GQ1_SEVEN_DAYS_SECONDS and update the assertion, reflecting the intentional
  GQ1 backstop restoration to 7 days from 306fa0b04 (BLOCKER #1 in the
  2026-06-24 review). Doc comment on the constant explains why GQ1 differs
  from GQ2's 3-day derived TTL.

* fix(test): interposition mock exposes COMMAND_INLINE_THRESHOLD

The event-sourcing graph now transitively imports COMMAND_INLINE_THRESHOLD from
lean-for-projection (via tieredBlobStore's S3_TIER_THRESHOLD_BYTES derivation in
306fa0b04). interposition.unit.test mocks the module and needs to re-export the
constant, otherwise the mock throws on import and the whole suite loads with 0
tests.

* fix(groupQueue): address 2026-07-03 self-audit P3s (peek symmetry, ops-dash GQ2, distinct counter, silent-fail warn)

- tieredBlobStore: add peek(ref) via a shared fetch(ref, refresh) helper —
  routes redis-tier through redisBlobs.peek (no GETEX), s3-tier unchanged
  (no TTL). Constructor emits a one-time warn when queueName is unset AND a
  logger is available, so a future caller that forgets the observability
  threading surfaces the omission instead of silently no-op'ing the decode-
  cap counter/log.
- jobEnvelope.decodeJobEnvelope: readMode "peek" now ALSO routes the GQ2
  tiered path (was GQ1-only in 306fa0b0), so an ops-dashboard inspection
  of a GQ2-offloaded blob doesn't extend the redis-tier holder TTL.
- queue.redis.repository (ops dashboard): construct a TieredBlobStore
  alongside the RedisJobBlobStore and pass both to decodeJobEnvelope with
  readMode "peek". Fixes the silent-body-loss regression that would have
  hit the moment GROUP_QUEUE_ENVELOPE_WRITES_ENABLED flips in prod — an
  operator viewing a stuck offloaded job now sees the payload instead of
  a blank card.
- groupQueue: new gqRetryEncodeFailuresTotal counter, used by the retry
  re-encode fail-safe path (was folded into gqJobsNonRetryableTotal in
  306fa0b0, mixing "gave up on a bad payload" with "gave up because encode
  blipped mid-retry"). Distinct label set matches gqJobsRetriedTotal so
  oncall can grep them the same way.
- metrics: register the new counter name in the hot-reload cleanup array so
  test workers don't hit the same double-registration issue e9d80d419 fixed.

Verified locally: typecheck + biome clean, 64 unit tests green
(jobEnvelope + tieredBlobStore + redisHashTag + redact + orgBillableEventsMeter
+ interposition — the last two regression-guard the hot-reload + mock fixes).

perf(ui): actually defer GTM/Pendo/Crisp instead of injecting on mount (#5348)

* perf(ui): actually defer GTM/Pendo/Crisp instead of injecting on mount

next-script.tsx accepted a `strategy` prop but ignored it entirely,
injecting every third-party <script> synchronously the instant its
component mounted. Fix the shim to honor strategy: beforeInteractive
injects immediately, everything else waits for requestIdleCallback
(with a window-load/timeout fallback for Safari).

Part of #5330 (Tier 1) · parent #5329 · closes #5346

* test(compat): expand next-script coverage to 100%

Adds coverage for the src-script path (async, onLoad/onError wiring),
non-string children, missing id, arbitrary attribute pass-through,

from tens-of-ms to up to 4s (or until window.load on Safari), making
the open_dashboard gtag event, Reo.identify, the analytics client's

fix(billing): wire evaluation runs to billable events meter (#5125)

* fix(billing): wire evaluation runs to billable events meter

The billable-events meter subscribed to lw.evaluation.scheduled and
lw.evaluation.started, neither of which is ever emitted in production.
The live evaluation pipeline only emits lw.evaluation.reported (via
reportEvaluation / ReportEvaluationCommand / ExecuteEvaluationCommand),
so evaluation executions contributed zero billable rows.

Subscribe the meter to lw.evaluation.reported instead and drop the two
dead subscriptions. The reported event's idempotencyKey is
${tenantId}:${evaluationId}:reported, so retries and replays collapse
to exactly one billable unit per evaluation.

Regression test drives the real ProjectionRouter eventType filter + map
+ store, asserting a billable record is produced for a reported event
and that scheduled/started are ignored — not a shape assertion.

Also extracts the duplicated createMockQueueManager test factory into
the shared testHelpers.

feat(aigateway): bound cached VK config staleness with a ConfigTTL refresh (#5359)

* feat(aigateway): bound cached VK config staleness with a ConfigTTL refresh

The auth cache tied config freshness to the JWT exp, and the change feed
only evicts on mutations that emit events — config edits that bypass the
control plane (e.g. direct DB writes) served stale credentials, base
URLs, and routing chains until process restart. Add a ConfigTTL (default
60s, env LW_GATEWAY_AUTH_CACHE_CONFIG_TTL) that re-fetches a fresh
entry's config in the background once it crosses the TTL, guarded so at
most one refresh runs per entry and failures wait a full TTL.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(aigateway): don't let a stale ConfigTTL refresh resurrect an evicted VK

The background ConfigTTL refresh snapshotted the entry, fetched config, then
unconditionally re-stored it. If a change-feed eviction, async auth rejection,
or a foreground auth refresh removed or replaced the L1 entry while FetchConfig
was in flight, the stale goroutine wrote the old bundle back, so the gateway
kept serving stale (possibly revoked) config until the next invalidation.

Re-check that the live L1 entry is still the one the goroutine started from
before storing (via Peek, which leaves LRU recency untouched); otherwise drop
the result and skip the L2 write. Adds a race regression test that evicts the
entry mid-fetch and asserts it is not resurrected.

* test(aigateway): lock in that ConfigTTL refresh replaces the whole config

Extend the success-refresh test to fetch a non-Credentials config field
(AllowedModels) and assert it reflects the fresh config after refresh, so the
test covers 'fresh.Config = cfg' replacing the whole Config, not just the
mirrored top-level Credentials slice.

fix(cli): route `langwatch claude` telemetry-persist offer into ~/.claude/settings.json

The Path B (ingestion) persist prompt used to write the OTLP export block
into ~/.zshrc. That leaks LANGWATCH/OTEL vars into every unrelated shell
child (git, ripgrep, background services). Claude Code has a native
per-app `env` block in ~/.claude/settings.json that it loads on every
invocation — writing there scopes the telemetry to `claude` runs only and
leaves the profile root clean. Other wrappers (codex, cursor, gemini,
opencode) keep the shell-rc fallback until they grow their own app-scoped
env target.

* fix(traces): repair silently-broken audio players in trace UIs

The audio render path produced dead <audio> elements (no error badge)
for several content-part shapes. Fixes, each with a unit test:

- AG-UI audio parts with an inline data source and no mimeType built
  data:undefined;base64,... because the media data branch had no
  default. Default the data-source mimeType to audio/wav.

- Raw header-less pcm16 (input_audio format "pcm16", the primary OpenAI
  Realtime format) was emitted as data:audio/wav;base64,<raw-pcm>, which
  no browser can decode. Wrap inline pcm16 in a minimal WAV/RIFF
  container (24 kHz mono 16-bit) via a new pure, isomorphic pcmToWav
  helper. Companded g711 cannot be wrapped inline yet, so it falls back
  to the raw view instead of a dead player (follow-up tracked).

- collectAudioParts ignored a bare input_audio/audio object at the span
  input/output root (it only walked messages/content envelopes). Check
  the root object itself.

- traces-v2 parseContentBlocks dropped AI-SDK file audio parts to raw
  JSON while the legacy renderer showed a player. Route file through the
  same audio decoder so both UIs match; non-audio files stay raw.

- TraceAudioPart passed projectId="" while the project resolved, which
  permanently disabled MediaPart's stored-object existence probe (its
  enabled gate needs a truthy id) so failed URLs stuck as broken players
  instead of the missing badge. Gate rendering on a resolved id.

The proven input_audio wav path is unchanged (wav is never re-wrapped).

feat(pairwise-compare): support comparing A vs B without a golden/reference answer (#5381)

* feat(pairwise-compare): add has_golden_answer opt-out (#5378)

Pairwise Compare's judge prompt was hardcoded "golden-aware" — every
comparison assumed a golden/reference answer. The only way to skip it
was picking `input` as a fake golden field, which still framed the
prompt as golden-aware and could confuse the judge.

Adds `has_golden_answer` (default true, preserving current behavior).
When false and the prompt hasn't been customized, the judge uses a
new golden-free template that compares Candidate A vs Candidate B
directly, with no reference-answer framing at all. A customized
prompt is always respected as an explicit user choice, regardless of
the toggle.

Closes #5378

* chore(codegen): regenerate evaluators.generated.ts for has_golden_answer

Regenerated via langevals/scripts/generate_evaluators_ts.py and
copy:langevals-types. No prettier install (or pinned version) is
available in this environment, so both files were reformatted with
Biome instead — the project's actual formatter/linter for the
langwatch/ TS output. That produces incidental reformatting noise
across unrelated fields (line-wrap/quote-style differences vs
whatever prettier version last generated these files); the only
deliberate change is the new has_golden_answer field.

* feat(experiments-v3): wire has_golden_answer through the pairwise UI

Mirrors the evaluator's settings.has_golden_answer (source of truth
the judge reads) into PairwiseEvaluatorConfig.hasGoldenAnswer — the
same dual-representation pattern already used for includeMetrics —
since the orchestrator's cell-generation guard and the missing-
mappings validator only see target.pairwise, not the Python settings.

- PairwiseConfigForm: new "Has golden answer" toggle gates the Golden
  field picker (hidden entirely when off), wired via useFormContext
  the same way the existing Include metrics switches are.
- EvaluatorEditorShared: skip has_golden_answer from the generic
  DynamicZodForm render (same reason include_metrics is skipped) and
  seed the field on new pairwise configs.
- mappingValidation: Golden field is only flagged missing when
  hasGoldenAnswer isn't explicitly false.
- orchestrator: the column-target cell-generation guard previously
  required goldenField unconditionally, silently blocking pairwise
  columns from ever running once the user opted out.
- EvaluationsV3Table: the "is this pairwise column configured" checks
  (stable-columns filter and the pending-pairwise default) also
  treated goldenField as unconditionally required.

`hasGoldenAnswer !== false` throughout defaults old saved configs
(predating this field) to the current golden-required behavior.

* test(experiments-v3): cover has_golden_answer toggle behavior

- New PairwiseConfigForm integration test: Golden field picker shows/
  hides with the toggle, onChange reports hasGoldenAnswer and clears
  goldenField when turned off.
- mappingValidation: golden field is required only when
  hasGoldenAnswer is true; variantA/variantB stay required either way.
- orchestrator: a pairwise column-target cell is generated with an
  empty goldenField when hasGoldenAnswer is false, and still skipped
  when hasGoldenAnswer is true but goldenField is empty.
- Existing PairwiseEvaluatorConfig fixtures updated with the new
  required hasGoldenAnswer field (defaulted to true, preserving prior
  behavior).

* fix(pairwise): match golden-free judge prompt in the tool-call schema too

The tool-call schema's "reasoning" field description was hardcoded to
tell the judge to reason "against the golden answer" regardless of
has_golden_answer, contradicting the user-facing prompt when the
toggle is off. Make it conditional like the prompt template itself.

* fix(pairwise): default legacy hasGoldenAnswer=undefined to golden-aware

loadState() copies persisted experiment state without schema parsing,
so a pairwise config saved before this field existed reaches the form
with hasGoldenAnswer genuinely undefined at runtime. The `??` fallback
let that flow through as falsy, hiding the Golden field picker for
pre-#5378 configs that were always golden-aware. Treat anything other
than an explicit `false` as golden-aware, matching the same
`!== false` convention mappingValidation.ts already uses.

Addresses CodeRabbit review comment on PR #5381.

* test(pairwise): nest mappingValidation pairwise tests into given/when BDD

Flat describe block with 4 unrelated it() cases -> nested given
hasGoldenAnswer/when field-state groups, per repo BDD conventions.

Addresses CodeRabbit review comment on PR #5381.

* test(pairwise): cover isPairwiseConfigured directly, not just via render

EvaluationsV3Table.tsx's "is this pairwise column configured" predicate
had zero direct test coverage even though its identical twin in
orchestrator.ts (the #5378 cell-generation guard) was covered by 2 new
tests. Export the pure predicate so it can be unit-tested without a
full docker-backed component render.

* test(pairwise): fix preview-harness crashes, add golden-off screenshot

PairwiseConfigForm's variant pickers call useTargetName (needs router
context) and GoldenAnswerSection calls useWatch against useFormContext
(needs a FormProvider ancestor) — neither exists in this router-less,
form-less component-preview harness, so the existing "initial state"
screenshot test was crashing before it ever reached a screenshot.
Mock useTargetName the same way useEvaluatorName already is, and wrap
renders in the same FormProvider real usage always provides
(EvaluatorEditorShared.tsx).

Add a second screenshot case with hasGoldenAnswer: false, asserting
the Golden field picker is actually absent — direct visual + assertion
proof of the toggle's core behavior (#5378).

* refactor(pairwise): extract isGoldenFieldSatisfied, address CodeRabbit review

The "golden field required unless hasGoldenAnswer === false" rule was
independently re-implemented in EvaluationsV3Table.tsx,
mappingValidation.ts, and orchestrator.ts. CodeRabbit correctly flagged
this: identical today, but a future change to one without the others
(e.g. a tri-state golden mode) would silently desync UI gating, client
validation, and server cell-generation — exactly the class of bug this
PR already had to fix once (orchestrator.ts's unconditional goldenField
guard). Centralize it next to pairwiseEvaluatorConfigSchema in types.ts.

* test(pairwise): address CodeRabbit nitpicks on new test coverage

- EvaluationsV3Table.test.ts: add the missing hasGoldenAnswer-omitted
  (legacy config) case, locking in that pre-#5378 saved configs still
  require a golden field.
- pairwise-preview.browser.test.tsx: use jest-dom's
  .not.toBeInTheDocument() instead of a manual if/throw, so a failure
  surfaces as a normal assertion diff.

* style(langevals): clarify reasoning_description ternary readability

Addresses CodeRabbit nitpick on PR #5381 — the else-branch string was
visually merged with the if-branch by implicit concatenation.

* fix(langevals): tie reasoning_description to actual prompt swap, not raw flag

reasoning_description was derived from the raw has_golden_answer flag
independent of whether the prompt was actually swapped. A customized
prompt that keeps golden framing (never swapped, since customization is
always respected as-is) combined with has_golden_answer=False produced
a prompt asking for golden comparison while the tool schema's reasoning
field simultaneously claimed no reference answer was involved —
contradictory instructions in the same LLM call. Found in /review on
PR #5381.

* fix(experiments-v3): log when pairwise input has no source with golden off

The synthetic "input" mapping for column-style pairwise targets falls
back to the golden field for datasets with no literal "input" column
(#5100, predates the golden-answer toggle). Since #5378 lets goldenField
be "" when hasGoldenAnswer is off, that fallback silently no-ops for
such rows and the judge prompt renders an empty task/input line with
no signal that anything went missing.

This doesn't invent a new input-mapping mechanism (that's a real gap,
but a product/design call, not a quick fix) — it makes the failure
observable via the same logger.debug pattern already used for the
skip-reason above it, so it's diagnosable instead of indistinguishable
from "row has no input, by design." Found in /review on PR #5381.

* docs(specs): describe golden-answer scenarios from user perspective

Two new pairwise-compare scenarios wrote "Given has_golden_answer is
false/true", naming the internal settings field directly instead of
the user-facing toggle — the same pattern the project's feature-file
convention explicitly bans (config values/internals vs. behavior).
Reworded to match the "Has Golden Answer is toggled on/off" phrasing
already used two scenarios above in the same file. Found in /review
on PR #5381.

perf(clickhouse): add time predicate to analytics stored_spans JOINs (#5072)

* perf(clickhouse): add time predicate to analytics stored_spans JOINs

The analytics aggregation builder joins stored_spans for span-level groupBys
and metrics (e.g. metadata.span_type, error.has_error, events). buildJoinClause
filtered the join subquery on TenantId only, with no StartTime predicate, so
every such analytics query cold-scanned all weekly partitions of stored_spans
(including S3-tiered ones) for the tenant, instead of pruning to the dashboard
window. The SPAN_TIME_FILTER_BOTH_PERIODS / _START_END envelopes already existed
for the filter-subquery path but were never wired into the JOIN path.

Thread the matching StartTime envelope into buildJoinClause and pass it at every
stored_spans join site (both-periods builders and the start/end filter-value
builders). A span's StartTime falls within its trace's lifetime, and the +/-2
day cushion matches the envelope used elsewhere, so the bound prunes partitions
without changing which spans match. evaluation_runs joins are unchanged.

EXPLAIN INDEXES on the join subquery for a real tenant (16-day window):
stored_spans 113 parts / 7739 granules down to 39 parts / 613 granules.

Note: aggregation-builder.test.ts has one pre-existing failure
(performance.first_token quantile routing) that also fails on clean main and is
unrelated to this change.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor: remove Elasticsearch and the BullMQ legacy stack (#4547)

* refactor: remove Elasticsearch and the BullMQ legacy stack

The TraceService / EvaluationService / ExperimentRunService /
FilterService facades all had two backends — a ClickHouse one and an
Elasticsearch one — but every call was already going through ClickHouse.
The ES backends were constructed and never invoked. The legacy BullMQ
stack under src/server/background/ had been replaced piecewise by the
event-sourcing collector (recordSpan) but the old workers, queues, and
the tasks that wrote to ES were still wired up at boot.

This commit deletes both stacks from the application layer:

ES removal (live read/write paths):
- Drop the ElasticsearchTraceService / ElasticsearchEvaluationService /
  ElasticsearchExperimentRunService / ElasticsearchFilterService /
  ElasticsearchAnalyticsService backends (constructed but never called).
- Drop the evaluationEsSync + experimentRunEsSync reactors and the
  annotationEsSync hook — no more dual-write.
- Drop the ES analytics timeseries + scenario-analytics query builders.
- Drop the ES experiments batch-evaluation repository + the ES
  scenario-event service/repository (the SimulationFacade was already
  routing reads to ClickHouse).
- Strip Elasticsearch URL/API-key fields from the org settings input
  schema, the settings UI, and getApp().organizations.update.
- Drop the per-org ES-driven cron handlers
  (scenario_analytics, trace_analytics msearch, retention_period_cleanup,
  schedule_topic_clustering) and the ES task scripts they invoked
  (elasticMigrate, cold/*, deleteTracesRetentionPolicy, syncAnnotations,
  syncTraceCosts, backfillTraceAnalytics, backfillScenarioAnalytics,
  fixCustomMetadataOutsideCustomField, clearTopics, rerunChecks).
- Collapse env.IS_QUICKWIT branches.
- Replace ES query-builder type imports
  (@elastic/elasticsearch/lib/api/types) with neutral structural types
  in the filter / analytics / common-router files that never actually
  ship queries to ES anymore.
- Move the Protections type out of src/server/elasticsearch/protections
  to src/server/traces/protections.

BullMQ legacy stack removal:
- Delete src/server/background/ entirely (worker entry, the six queue
  files, collectorWorker, evaluationsWorker, topicClusteringWorker,
  usageStatsWorker, anomalyDetectionWorker).
- Move the pure helpers under background/workers/collector/ (cost,
  common, evaluations, evaluationNameAutoslug, metrics, piiCheck, rag)
  into src/server/tracer/collector/ — these are consumed app-wide and
  don't depend on BullMQ.
- Extract runEvaluation / runEvaluationForTrace / customEvaluation /
  DataForEvaluation from the deleted evaluationsWorker into
  src/server/evaluations/runEvaluation.ts, switching from ES
  getTraceById / getTracesGroupedByThreadId to TraceService.getById /
  getTracesByThreadId.
- Rewrite src/workers.ts: drop the 15-minute self-restart timer
  (helm/docker already restart-on-exit), drop the BullMQ Worker
  startups, initialize the worker-role app, and start the EE
  governance ingestion-puller worker via a new
  ee/governance/services/pullers/pullerQueue.ts.
- Migrate src/server/api/routers/httpProxyTracing.ts from
  scheduleTraceCollectionWithFallback to getApp().traces.recordSpan via
  CollectorSpanUtils — the only remaining caller of the old collector
  queue.
- Strip the legacy collector dedup (fetchExistingMD5s + 256-version
  cap) from src/server/routes/collector.ts; event sourcing handles
  dedup downstream.
- Drop /api/start_workers, /api/rerun_checks,
  /api/cron/schedule_topic_clustering,
  /api/cron/scenario_analytics,
  /api/cron/traces_retention_period_cleanup — the routes were
  exclusively legacy stack triggers.
- Delete src/server/topicClustering/ (BullMQ-only scheduler) and the
  /settings/topic-clustering page + command-bar entry + route.
- Rewrite TraceUsageService CH-only (drop the EsClientFactory
  constructor parameter and the splitProjectsByFlag fallback).

Core ES dir + package:
- Delete src/server/elasticsearch.ts + src/server/elasticsearch/
  (traces, transformers, patchOpensearch, patchQuickwit).
- Delete elastic/ (helpers, mappings, schema, all migrations).
- Remove @elastic/elasticsearch from package.json + lockfile.
- src/components/checks/TryItOut.tsx: drop the
  transformElasticSearchSpanToSpan call; CH spans already arrive in the
  domain Span shape.

Facade collapse:

* fix(topic-clustering): break circular import causing worker boot TDZ

Restoring topic-clustering reintroduced a runtime regression: workers
crashed on boot with `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'TOPIC_CLUSTERING_QUEUE'
before initialization`. The cycle is

    topicClusteringWorker.ts
      -> topicClustering.ts (line 15: clusterTopicsForProject)
      -> topicClusteringQueue.ts (line 14: scheduleTopicClusteringNextPage)
      -> topicClusteringWorker.ts

When workers.ts imports the queue first, queue.ts re-enters worker.ts via
topicClustering.ts. queue.ts line 18 then reads `TOPIC_CLUSTERING_QUEUE.NAME`
while worker.ts is still on its imports — the const is in TDZ.

Extract the queue name + job-type tuple to a leaf
`topicClusteringQueue.constants.ts` with no cyclic edges. Both worker.ts
and queue.ts now import the constant from there; the cycle on
`runTopicClusteringJob` survives but that's a hoisted function declaration,
so its binding is available regardless of which side enters first.

Caught by `make quickstart all-local`. With the fix the worker logs
"topic clustering checks worker registered" and "topic clustering worker
active, waiting for jobs!" cleanly.

* fix(prompts): stop polling traces.getById for failed assistant messages

When a prompt submission errors (e.g. NLP unreachable, provider 500,
upstream rate-limited), the chat renders an ErrorMessage instead of an
AssistantMessage — but TraceMessage was still mounted unconditionally
on every non-streaming assistant turn. That meant every failed
submission also mounted a trace polling component looking up a trace
that was never emitted, producing a chain of 404s on
`api.traces.getById` (retry: 10, exp-backoff to 60s) and a "Maximum
update depth exceeded" React warning in posthog session-replay.

Gate the TraceMessage mount on `!isError`. Errored assistant turns have
no backing trace; the only thing left to render is the ErrorMessage,
which is already shown above.

Verified live against `make quickstart all-local` with no NLP container
(repro path for "LangWatch NLP is unreachable"). Before: 15 console
errors per submit; after: 1 unrelated pre-existing SVG warning.

feat(charts): datasets-S3 deploy support — worker PVC + migration Job (ADR-032) (#5083)

* feat(charts): datasets-S3 deploy support — worker stored-objects PVC + migration Job (ADR-032)

Carved out of the datasets→S3 JSONL epic (#4895) so the Helm chart ships as
its own release artifact. The TS feature is born-on-storage + dual-read, so it
merges and runs without these chart changes; self-hosted local-filesystem
deployments require the worker stored-objects PVC mount before normalize works,
so this chart must release with-or-before the app image.

- workers/deployment.yaml: mount the app's stored-objects RWO PVC on the worker
  so the off-request normalize job reads staged uploads / writes chunks to the
  shared volume (local-FS backend only).
- _helpers.tpl: guard workers.replicaCount=1 under local-FS (shared RWO PVC).
- dataset-s3-migration-job.yaml + values datasetS3Migration: the one-time
  backfill Job (post-install/post-upgrade hook). Kept off the critical path of
  the feature; default + race-safety decided in this PR, not the epic.
- values storedObjects + NOTES.txt: storage backend config and operator notes.

* fix(charts): gate worker replica guard on workers.enabled; default co-location affinity for consumers of the RWO stored-objects PVC

Review fixes:
- The local-FS workers.replicaCount=1 validation now only runs when
  workers.enabled=true — a disabled worker pool's leftover replicaCount
  no longer fails the render.
- Workers and the dataset-s3-migration Job mount the app's RWO
  stored-objects PVC; on a multi-node cluster an off-node consumer sits
  Pending on a multi-attach error. When local-FS is active and no
  explicit affinity is set, both now default to a required podAffinity
  co-locating them with the app pod (an operator-set affinity still
  overrides wholesale).

* docs(charts): drop the false 'skips when storage isn't S3-configured' claim

The merged backfill task has no such skip — the resolver always returns a
backend, so a no-S3 install backfills to the local-filesystem stored-objects
volume (which is exactly why the Job mounts the PVC).

* fix(charts): repoint preflight message at renumbered NOTES section; correct the hook rollout-gating claim

- NOTES renumbering (Required Secrets 6 -> 7) left the preflight failure
  message pointing at the dataset-storage section.
- post-upgrade hooks fire after resources are submitted, not after the
  rollout completes, so the 'no old-image pod is present when a dataset
  flips' claim only holds under helm --wait/--atomic (or Argo/Flux).
  Comment now states the real contract and the upgrade guidance for
  crossing the ADR-032 boundary.

* fix(charts): default strategy Recreate for app+workers under local-FS; NOTES ops guidance

The k8s default RollingUpdate surges the replacement pod before the old
one releases the RWO stored-objects PVC — on a multi-node cluster the
new pod can land on another node and wedge Pending on a multi-attach
error (and a surged worker keeps the volume anchored to the old node
even if the app uses Recreate alone). Recreate on BOTH deployments
releases the volume before new pods schedule; the co-location affinity
then reunites them. Renders only when local-FS is the active backend;
an explicit deployment.strategy overrides.

NOTES: default-StorageClass requirement (bare-metal), the Recreate
downtime tradeoff, and ArgoCD/Flux PostSync vs plain-helm --wait.

* fix(charts): review follow-ups — Job SA-token parity, README params regen, DRY affinity coalesce

- dataset-s3-migration Job now sets automountServiceAccountToken from
  global.* like app/workers (task never calls the k8s API; IRSA is
  unaffected — the EKS webhook injects its own projected token).
- Regenerate README parameters via readme-generator-for-helm: adds the
  datasetS3Migration.* and app.storedObjects.* blocks plus accumulated
  drift (preflight section, virtualKeyPepper, ...) — the generator had
  been wedged on a missing @param for langy-agent.secrets.internalSecretKey,
  now annotated.
- Hoist the affinity coalesce into a template variable in the Job and
  workers Deployment (was computed twice per site).

* fix(charts): make the local-FS strategy upgradeable and unbreak the migration Job

Two bugs found by live-upgrading a main-chart install on minikube:

1. Deployment strategy: 'type: Recreate' broke every helm upgrade from a
   pre-existing release ('spec.strategy.rollingUpdate: Forbidden'). Helm's
   3-way merge cannot DELETE the live k8s-defaulted rollingUpdate struct
   when the previous release manifest never had a strategy key. Replaced
   with RollingUpdate + maxSurge=0/maxUnavailable=1 — behaviorally
   identical at replicas=1 (old pod releases the RWO PVC before the new
   one schedules) but only UPDATES fields, which the merge applies
   cleanly. Verified: upgrade from a fresh main-chart install now
   succeeds unattended.

2. dataset-s3-migration Job crash-looped on every run: the task's module
   graph eagerly initializes BetterAuth at import time, which throws
   without NEXTAUTH_SECRET (not part of sharedEnv). Wired the same
   secretKeyRef precedence as the app Deployment. Verified: Job completes
   and re-runs self-skip.

* docs(charts): NOTES.txt reflects the kill-then-start rollout (not Recreate)

* fix(charts): full-stack e2e values render again under the workers local-FS guard

values-e2e-full.yaml runs 2 workers (deliberately — it validates the
multi-replica tier), which the new workers.replicaCount=1 local-FS guard
correctly rejects. Disable local-FS + the backfill hook there, same as
values-e2e.yaml: multi-replica deployments use S3/dataplane, never the
shared RWO PVC.

* fix(charts): move NEXTAUTH_SECRET into sharedEnv so workers get it too

The migration Job's fix (previous commit) only wired NEXTAUTH_SECRET into
that one Job — workers run the same app image and the same BetterAuth
eager-init-at-import crash was still reachable there (dataset-normalize
runs on the worker per this PR's PVC mount change), just not yet
triggered by any exercised code path. Moved the secretKeyRef block into
langwatch.sharedEnv so every app-image consumer (app, workers, the
migration Job) gets it from one place instead of copy-pasted per
consumer. NEXTAUTH_PROVIDER stays app-only (real app config, not needed
to avoid the crash).

Live-verified end-to-end on minikube: upgrade succeeds, worker
Deployment carries NEXTAUTH_SECRET, migration Job completes.

* test(charts): CI upgrade test across the ADR-032 strategy boundary

Neither of the two upgrade-blocking bugs found by manual live-upgrade
testing this session (strategy Forbidden error, migration Job
NEXTAUTH_SECRET crash) was catchable by CI — tests/values-e2e.yaml
disables every new code path this PR introduces. Adds
test_dataset_s3_migration_upgrade, chained right after test_workers so
it inherits a release with no strategy key rendered (the pre-#5083
state, k8s-API-server-defaulted RollingUpdate on the live Deployments —
exactly what every existing self-hosted install has today). It seeds a
legacy contentLayout=postgres dataset via SQL (the app's own UI/API can
no longer produce that layout — read-only migration source since
#4895), then upgrades with local-FS + the migration hook enabled for
the first time, which is exactly when the Deployment strategy renders
for the first time too. Asserts: helm upgrade succeeds, the live
strategy is the kill-then-start maxSurge=0 override, the migration Job
completes, the dataset flips to s3_jsonl with the correct row count,
and the chunk file lands correctly on the shared PVC.

Every assertion in this suite was run against a real minikube cluster
before committing (not just syntax-checked) to confirm it actually
catches what it's meant to catch.

* test(charts): make dataset S3 migration seed idempotent for local reruns

CI always starts from a fresh Kind cluster so this never bit CI, but a
local KEEP_CLUSTER=true dev-loop rerun would hit a duplicate-key error
on the hardcoded seed IDs and abort under set -euo pipefail. Delete
before insert; verified idempotent by running twice against a live
cluster.

* docs(charts): clarify pg_query vs pg_exec and the values-e2e.yaml image-timing comment

Both P3 nits from the ruthless review pass: the values-e2e.yaml comment
read as a blanket 'app image never loaded in this job' claim, which is
only true at helm-install-baseline time — test_app/test_dataset_s3_migration_upgrade
load and run it later in the same job. And pg_query/pg_exec now have a
one-line pointer explaining why two Postgres exec helpers exist instead
of one (pg_query's argv-embedding is unsafe for real SQL).

perf(clickhouse): bound key-discovery facet memory so it spills instead of OOMing (#5086)

* perf(clickhouse): bound key-discovery facet memory so it spills instead of OOMing

The metadata-keys / span-attribute-keys / event-attribute-keys facets each
arrayJoin an attribute map's keys and GROUP BY key over the dashboard time
window. A tenant that stuffs high-cardinality data into key names turns the
GROUP BY into millions of groups; reading the keys subcolumn plus the
count() OVER () buffer then allocates gigabytes (observed at ~12 GiB,
MEMORY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED in prod). The queries already prune partitions, so the
lever is memory, not scan width.

Add a shared KEY_DISCOVERY_SETTINGS guard (external GROUP BY spill +
max_memory_usage ceiling), mirroring the span repo's SINGLE_TRACE_READ_SETTINGS,
and pass it through the facet executor. Pathological tenants now spill to disk
and complete, or fail their own facet, instead of allocating against the
server total where the OvercommitTracker degrades unrelated requests.

* fix(clickhouse): apply StartedAt window on outer read only + unit-test the helper

* fix(mailer): trigger emails route To=hashed no-reply, recipients=BCC

Production trigger emails previously rendered every recipient address in
the To: header, leaking the internal recipient list to every receiver,
inviting reply-all storms, and putting user-controlled multi-recipient
content directly into a header (EMAIL_RX blocks CRLF smuggling but
doesn't undo the enumeration leak).

Now:

  - To:  LangWatch Triggers <no-reply+<HMAC>@<domain>>
  - Bcc: configured recipients

The local-part tag is HMAC-SHA256(triggerId, NEXTAUTH_SECRET) truncated
to 12 hex chars — stable per trigger so future bounce processors can
attribute mail back to a row, unguessable without the secret so the
address can't be reverse-engineered or forged.

    BccAddresses, raw-MIME path uses Destinations envelope (no Bcc:
    header rendered to receivers); SendGrid uses bcc / replyTo keys.
    `computeDefaultFrom()` extracted for callers that need to derive
    the no-reply domain from the From: address.
  - sendTriggerEmail: now takes `triggerId`, builds the no-reply To
    via `buildTriggerNoReplyAddress`, recipients ride in bcc.
  - TriggerNotifier.sendEmail: signature changes to
    `{ to: string, bcc: string[], subject, html }`. Test-fire uses a
    "preview" sentinel id so test bounces don't pollute prod bounce
    streams that may key off the hash.
  - Both production dispatchers (outbox + inline pipeline) thread the
    trigger id through.

* feat(outbox): wire .withOutbox to real trigger-dispatch reactors

PR1's `.withOutbox` builder + OutboxReactorDefinition API has been
exported and tested but never invoked by the runtime — `eventSourcing.ts`
read `foldReactors`/`mapReactors` from each StaticPipelineDefinition and
ignored `foldOutboxReactors`/`mapOutboxReactors`, so even if a pipeline
called `.withOutbox`, the reactor would never fire.

Adds the missing wiring:

- `outboxReactorAdapter.ts` wraps an `OutboxReactorDefinition` into a
  regular `ReactorDefinition` whose `handle` invokes `decide(...)` and
  forwards each emitted `OutboxEnqueueRequest` to
  `outbox.enqueueSettle`. The GroupQueue-routed adapter ignores the
  request's `dedupKey`/`groupKey`/`maxAttempts` (those describe the
  spec's row-leased architecture); `enqueueOptions.ttlMs` IS threaded
  because the settle stage's Debounce Mode TTL is the per-trigger
  `traceDebounceMs` knob. When `OutboxRuntime` isn't wired (web
  process, or worker without outbox), the adapter degrades to a
  no-op `handle` so the pipeline registration is harmless.
- `buildServiceOptions` in `eventSourcing.ts` now walks the static
  definition's outbox-reactor maps, adapts each, and merges them into
  the `reactors`/`mapReactors` arrays the runtime already consumes.
- `OutboxEnqueueRequest` grows an optional `enqueueOptions.ttlMs`
  field. The defaults to `DEFAULT_TRACE_DEBOUNCE_MS` (30s) when absent.
- `defineOriginGuardedTraceOutboxReactor` factored out next to the
  existing `defineOriginGuardedTraceReactor` so both `.withReactor`
  and `.withOutbox` trace-pipeline reactors share the same
  origin/age/event-type guard logic (single `passesTraceOriginGuards`
  helper).

Splits the two trigger reactors into NOTIFY-class and PERSIST-class
responsibilities and registers the NOTIFY half via `.withOutbox`:

- `ee/governance/reactors/alertTriggerNotifyOutbox.reactor.ts` — new
  OutboxReactorDefinition; for every active trace-only trigger whose
  action is SEND_EMAIL / SEND_SLACK_MESSAGE, emits an
  `OutboxEnqueueRequest` carrying the settle payload. Registered on
  the trace pipeline via
  `.withOutbox("traceSummary", "alertTriggerNotifyOutbox", ...)`.
- `evaluationAlertTriggerNotifyOutbox.reactor.ts` — same shape on the
  evaluation pipeline; restricts to triggers with evaluation filters
  whose action is NOTIFY.
- `ee/governance/reactors/alertTrigger.reactor.ts` and
  `evaluationAlertTrigger.reactor.ts` keep handling PERSIST-class
  actions (ADD_TO_DATASET, ADD_TO_ANNOTATION_QUEUE) inline; their
  NOTIFY branch is gone. Tests now exercise the persist path with
  `ADD_TO_ANNOTATION_QUEUE` (single-call dispatch path) rather than
  the deleted email mock.

* fix(outbox): adapter short-circuits on isReplay; spec wording updated

drive-feature surfaced two gaps in the .withOutbox path post-round-2:

1. The framework adapter (`outboxReactorAdapter.ts`) was not honoring
   the spec scenario "Replay short-circuits .withOutbox match after row
   retention has elapsed" — `decide()` would still run on replay, and
   if the audit row had aged out the live dispatch path would re-fire
   customer-visible side effects. The adapter now early-returns when
   `context.isReplay` is true. Test added.

2. The spec scenarios in `reactor-outbox-dispatch.feature` still talked
   about reactors "claiming the match" at enqueue, which round-2
   (ebb48532d) made stale: the actual `TriggerSent` claim is now
   post-dispatch in `handleCadenceBatch`. Re-worded the Rule + scenarios
   to distinguish:
     - the audit-row dedup at enqueue (what the spec used to call "the
       claim"), and
     - the post-dispatch `TriggerSent` at-most-once gate (what actually
       prevents double-send across replays / retries).
   The "racing pipelines" scenario was replaced with the more accurate
   "routing is mutually exclusive" — trace-only and eval-filter
   triggers are partitioned by `classifyTriggerFilters`, so no
   cross-pipeline race exists today.

* feat(automations): drawer fixes — capture-block validation, inline cadence, reuse webhook, taller email body, esc-trap

Six fixes against the live automation drawer:

- **`{{ project.url }}` in Block Kit templates no longer fails.** The
  `substituteLiquidForJsonValidation` pass was treating each `{% ... %}`
  and `{{ ... }}` as an independent span, so an embedded
  `{{ project.url }}` *inside* a `{% capture _url %}` block at top level
  got wrapped in a top-level `"___"` string — which then trips the JSON
  schema validator with a misleading marker. Capture blocks (and
  comments) are now folded into one whitespace-only tag span: the body
  is a Liquid-only declaration, never inlined into the JSON output.
  Three new tests; existing 7 stay green.

- **Slack default template type is now Block Kit.** New automations
  open straight into the Block Kit picker (`Digest — inline rich`
  default) instead of falling back to plain text. Historical rows whose
  `slackTemplateType` is null still read as plain text upstream — no
  retyping of saved configs.

- **Inline cadence selector on the Slack + Email config forms.** The
  cadence drives the available template-variable surface (digest
  exposes `digest.windowStart`/`windowEnd`, immediate hides them);
  forcing the author back to the cadence secondary drawer to switch
  was wasted clicks. `InlineCadenceSelect` lives provider-side and is
  wired through new `notificationCadence` + `setNotificationCadence`
  fields on `ConfigFormCtx` — providers stay portable, the
  AutomationDrawer feature store stays the single source of truth.
  Email's `filterVariablesForCadence("immediate")` hard-code is gone:

- **Reuse a Slack webhook from another automation.** Most teams point
  every Slack trigger at the same channel; copy-pasting the URL
  per-trigger is friction. `ReuseSlackWebhook` queries
  `getTriggers` for the current project and lists existing
  `SEND_SLACK_MESSAGE` URLs as `${trigger.name} — ${hostname}`. The
  picker is hidden when no other Slack automation exists, so it
  doesn't advertise an empty menu.

  handler sees it. Monaco's own Escape behaviour (close suggestion

* dev(vite): poll watcher on Docker bind mounts so host edits HMR

Docker-on-macOS does not surface inotify reliably across the bind mount,
so the previous behaviour was 'edit on host, restart the container
manually to see it.' Vite's polling watcher fires on every interval

opt out via LANGWATCH_VITE_NO_POLLING=1.

perf(clickhouse): bound experiment cost lookup to the run's OccurredAt window (#5327)

perf(clickhouse): bound experiment trace-cost lookup to the run's OccurredAt window

Rebased onto main after the Elasticsearch/BullMQ refactor (#4547) moved
enrichItemsWithTraceCosts into experiment-run.service.ts.

enrichItemsWithTraceCosts backfills experiment target-item costs from
`SELECT TraceId, TotalCost FROM trace_summaries WHERE TraceId IN (...)` with no
OccurredAt bound. trace_summaries is partitioned by toYearWeek(OccurredAt), so a
TraceId-only filter cannot prune and opens every weekly partition (including
cold storage) to read two light columns. A target's trace runs during its run,
so its OccurredAt falls inside the buffered run window getRun already computes
(computeOccurredAtRangeForRuns); thread it in and bound the read.

The bound is applied on the outer read only, not inside the max(UpdatedAt) dedup
subquery: OccurredAt can shift across ReplacingMergeTree versions (a late span
can move a trace's min start time), so filtering versions by OccurredAt before
resolving the latest could pick the wrong version.

perf(clickhouse): resolve trace time for hint-less single-trace span reads (#5085)

* perf(clickhouse): resolve trace time for hint-less single-trace span reads

Single-trace stored_spans readers fell back to an unbounded scan when no
occurredAtMs hint was threaded (back-stack / conversation-jump / deep-link
drawer opens and worker callers), walking every weekly partition incl. the
cold S3 tier. Mirror the existing readTraceEvents fix: when no hint is
present, resolve the trace's occurrence time from trace_summaries (a
sort-key point seek) and bound the read to its same partition window. The
caller-hint path is unchanged; only a trace absent from trace_summaries
still scans unbounded.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(clickhouse): restore unbounded fallback for resolved span reads + un-clamp poll readers

Addresses reviewer findings on the hint-less span read path.

- Resolved-time branch had no safety net: it ran a single ±2-day windowed read
  with no isEmpty fallback. trace_summaries.OccurredAt is the trace *start* and
  never widens, so a long-running trace produces spans past OccurredAt + 2 days
  that were silently and permanently dropped. Route the resolved branch through
  withPartitionHint so it rescans unbounded when the bounded read comes back
  empty, matching the hinted path. Events keep their no-fallback behavior (they
  cluster at the trace start); spans cannot.

- findSpansSince / findSpanSummariesSince were routed through readTraceSpans,
  which added an extra trace_summaries resolve per poll plus a
  StartTime <= OccurredAt + 2d upper bound on top of their existing
  StartTime > sinceStartTimeMs lower bound. For a trace still active more than
  2 days after its OccurredAt that upper bound sits in the past, so the live
  delta view silently stopped showing new spans. These readers already prune via
  the since lower bound; run them directly with no resolve and no upper clamp.

- Add an integration test for a trace whose spans fall outside the resolved
  ±2-day window (returned via the unbounded fallback), and update the empty-trace
  test to assert the fallback rather than the old "empty is authoritative".

fix(outbox): wire the outbox runtime into EventSourcing on workers (#5532)

The composition root constructed the EventSourcing runtime BEFORE the outbox
and passed the outbox only to PipelineRegistry (which never read it), so
`EventSourcing._outbox` stayed undefined on every worker. All four `.withOutbox`
trigger reactors were then adapted onto the silent drop path — logging
"...no outbox runtime is wired..." and dropping every dispatch. In production
this took out all trigger automations the moment the event-sourced build went
live: workers emitted ~9.3k drops/hour and zero notify dispatches succeeded.

Fix:
- presets.ts: build the outbox first, construct EventSourcing AFTER it, and pass
  it into the constructor (the `outbox` option was already supported, just never
  given). Both the reactor adapter and the global queue's settle/cadence routing
  + audit adapter read `this._outbox`, set once at construction.
- pipelineRegistry.ts: remove the dead `outbox` dep — it was the second, unused
  channel that made the wrong wiring look plausible.
- eventSourcing.ts: add `isOutboxWired` as an explicit wiring-health invariant.

Tests:
- eventSourcing.outboxWiring.unit.test.ts: an instance built WITH an outbox
  adapts `.withOutbox` reactors to the live path; WITHOUT one it drops.
- presets.outboxWiring.integration.test.ts: boots the real composition via
  initializeDefaultApp and asserts a worker wires the outbox (no drop-warnings)
  while web does not. Verified fail-before/pass-after.

perf(trace-processing): shard recordSpan commands to parallelize hot-trace ingestion (#5531)

* perf(trace-processing): shard recordSpan commands to parallelize hot-trace ingestion

A trace that accumulates thousands of spans (reused trace_id, runaway agent
loop) queues all its recordSpan commands into one GroupQueue group keyed by the
trace id, so they drain one at a time behind a single worker. Each span's
per-span work — PII redaction, cost enrichment, token estimation, content-drop —
runs serially; observed live at ~6.5k commands pending on one group, oldest 11
minutes, starving every other trace's spans.

The command handler reads no trace-level state: it is a pure per-span transform
that emits one span_received event stamped aggregateId = traceId. So the command
need not serialise on the trace — only the trace-summary fold does, and it runs
on its own aggregate-keyed queue (unaffected by the command key). Split the
command's GroupQueue key into `traceId:<shard>` so a hot trace's spans drain
across up to N groups in parallel while the fold stays ordered per trace and the
summary stays exact.

Gated by TRACE_SPAN_PROCESSING_SHARDS (default 1 = the historic trace-only key,
off). The per-tenant soft-cap still bounds how many of a tenant's groups run at
once, so a fanned-out hot trace cannot starve its neighbours. Bounded (not
per-span) so a single trace never creates thousands of GroupQueue groups.

- spanCommandGroupKey.ts: pure FNV-1a bucket + env resolver (clamped 1..128)
- pipeline.ts: install getGroupKey on recordSpan (both blobStore branches)
- pipelineRegistry.ts: resolve shard count from env at composition
- specs/event-sourcing/span-command-sharding.feature: behaviour contract
- unit + wiring tests, incl. non-OTel-compliant trace/span ids

* test(trace-processing): bind span-sharding scenarios for feature-parity

Add `@scenario` bindings on the unit + wiring tests for the six runnable
scenarios in span-command-sharding.feature, satisfying the feature-parity CI
gate. Mark the end-to-end "trace summary is exact regardless of sharding"
scenario `@unimplemented`: its guarantee is structural (the fold runs on its own
trace-keyed queue, unaffected by the command shard key — verified by the
fold-per-trace wiring scenario) and a live GroupQueue + ClickHouse parallel-drain
test is a tracked gap.

* refactor(trace-processing): address PR review on span-command sharding

- Install getGroupKey only when shardCount > 1; when disabled (the default) the
  command falls back to getAggregateId — byte-identical to the historic key with
  zero extra normalization on the span-ingest hot path (Copilot).
- Clamp deps.spanCommandShardCount in the pipeline via a new clampSpanShardCount,
  so a caller bypassing PipelineRegistry's env resolver can't explode the group
  space (Copilot). resolveSpanCommandShardCount now delegates to it.
- MAX_SPAN_SHARD_COUNT declared `as const` per the internal-constant convention
  (CodeRabbit).
- Unit test extracts the shard suffix from the last colon, robust to
  colon-bearing trace ids (Copilot); add clampSpanShardCount coverage.
- Wiring test now covers the blobStore (withCommandInstance) registration branch
  and the disabled-path getAggregateId fallback (Copilot).

* feat(langy): replace iptables sibling-isolation with per-worker OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD

ADR-033 Fix A': iptables loopback-lockdown doesn't work under gVisor, so
sibling-worker isolation now rests on a per-worker OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD
(env-injected, never on the CLI command line) that opencode itself enforces
via HTTP Basic on its internal port. The authProxy translates the caller's
bearer token into that Basic credential; a sibling connecting straight to
another worker's internal port has no credential and gets 401 from opencode
directly, with no iptables rule involved.

Drops iptables.go, LANGY_LOOPBACK_LOCKDOWN_DISABLED, and getFreePortInRange
along with their call sites, now that the internal port no longer needs to
live in a locked range.

* fix(langy): stop treating authproxy's pre-backend 502 as ready in waitForReadiness

startAuthProxy binds and starts serving :externalPort synchronously in
manager.go's spawn(), but opencode itself is a separate process that takes
real time to start listening on :internalPort. Every poll in that window hit
the proxy, which is up, and got a genuine (err == nil) 502 Bad Gateway from
its own rev.ErrorHandler -- previously treated as "ready" by any non-transport-
error response. That immediately fired the one-shot requireOpenCodeAuthEnforced
probe straight at opencode's internal port before it was listening, which
failed on connection-refused and aborted the spawn. Since the proxy always
wins this race against opencode's startup in production, this failed almost
every real worker spawn.

Now 502 from the proxy is treated the same as a transport error: keep
polling instead of racing the auth-enforcement probe against a backend
that isn't there yet.

Regression test drives waitForReadiness through the real startAuthProxy
reverse-proxy chain against a backend that starts listening only after a
delay -- the existing suite only used two independently already-listening
httptest servers, which never exercises a genuine 502 from the proxy.

* fix(langy-agent): add CAP_FOWNER + copy sdk-go before go mod download

Two fixes required for langy-agent to build and run, found while

  instead of the first defaultValue in the file.

* fix(cli-auth): onboarding never swallows the device-approval page

Three-part fix for the CLI login round-trip:
- /cli/auth joins noOrgBouncerRoutes so the global bouncer (CommandBar's
  hook) can't shove a signed-in user into onboarding mid-approval.
- A brand-new user (signed up mid-CLI-login, no org) is round-tripped
  through /onboarding/welcome with return_to=/cli/auth?user_code=… —
  the approval needs an organization to bind to.
- The welcome screen honors a same-origin return_to on finish (both
  tracks) and on the already-onboarded redirect, so the user lands back
  on the approval page with the code intact and the CLI's poll
  completes. Only relative in-app paths are accepted.

fix(prompts): stop prompt playground tabs from leaking memory (#5456)

* fix(prompts): stop prompt playground tabs from leaking memory

Inactive tabs stayed fully mounted (Ark UI Tabs.Root defaults to
hidden-not-unmounted), keeping every tab's form, editor, chat
provider, and queries alive regardless of visibility. Compounded by
the version-history popover and the sidebar's per-row actions menu
firing their queries eagerly on mount instead of on open, and the
Zustand persist layer re-serializing every open tab's full content to
localStorage on every single tab's edit.

- Add lazyMount/unmountOnExit to the tab containers so only the active
  tab's subtree stays mounted.
- Gate VersionHistoryListPopover's and PublishedPromptActions' queries
  on their own popover/menu open state.
- Split DraggableTabsBrowserStore's localStorage persistence per tab
  key so editing one tab no longer rewrites every other open tab's
  content; make orphaned-key cleanup independent of the index's
  integrity so a corrupted or partially-written index can't strand
  per-tab data.

Fixes #5454

* address CodeRabbit review on #5456

- Reword the DraggableTabsBrowser regression test's docblock to
  describe the pre-fix behavior in past tense; it previously asserted
  the bug as still-current, which this PR's own fix makes false.
- Nest PublishedPromptActions.integration.test.tsx's when-blocks under
  a given() layer to match this codebase's BDD test convention.

* document the Immer reference-equality invariant in setItem

Flagged by a hygiene review pass: the per-tab dedup check relies on
Immer's structural sharing to keep untouched tabs' data references
stable across set() calls. That's non-obvious and silently degrades
to "write everything" if the store is ever mutated outside Immer.

* fix(prompts): consolidate per-tab localStorage cleanup onto one robust path

Principles review caught that reset() and the persist adapter's
removeItem() still used lossy cleanup after the per-tab-key split:
reset() removed only the light index key, and removeItem() only
deleted keys tracked in the in-memory ref map. Both orphan
`${projectId}:tab:*` keys in real cases — most concretely when the
same project is open in a second browser tab, whose store instance's
map never saw this instance's keys. That reintroduces the unbounded
localStorage growth this PR set out to fix.

Both now delegate to clearAllPersistedDataForProject, whose prefix
scan is independent of in-memory state. Extract getStorageKey() so the
index-key literal isn't duplicated across the three cleanup call sites.
Add regression tests covering own-tab and untracked-orphan cleanup.

* fix(prompts): don't unmount chat on sub-tab switch; drop bad tabs on rehydrate

Two review findings:

- The nested sub-tabs (Conversation/Variables/Demonstrations/Parameters)
  had unmountOnExit, so switching away from Conversation unmounted the
  chat — tearing down its CopilotKit provider and aborting any in-flight
  generation. Drop unmountOnExit (keep lazyMount): the chat mounts once
  and stays alive across sub-tab switches. Inactive *prompt* tabs still
  fully unmount via the outer browser, which is where the memory win is;
  jsdom can't reproduce Ark's unmount-on-exit so this isn't unit-testable.

- Rehydration: a missing or corrupt per-tab data key made getItem
  fabricate an invalid tab, which failed whole-state validation and wiped
  *every* tab (or threw and rejected the whole store). Now getItem drops
  just the bad tab and keeps the rest; regression test added.

* fix(prompts): flush pending edits before tab unmount; disable Delete while loading

Two findings from review:

- Unmounting an inactive prompt tab could drop a just-typed edit. The
  form sync (lodash debounce) and variable-value sync (usehooks-ts
  useDebounceCallback, which cancels on unmount) both had pending writes
  that never reached the store if you edited then immediately switched
  tabs. Flush both debounced writers on unmount so the edit is persisted
  before teardown. Regression test types a variable value then unmounts
  and asserts it survives.

- PublishedPromptActions gated checkModifyPermission on the menu being
  open, so permission is undefined on first open — and canDelete
  defaulted undefined to "allowed", briefly enabling the destructive
  Delete before the check resolved. Default to disabled until the query
  resolves as allowed. Tests cover the loading and resolved states.

* fix(prompts): migrate legacy single-key persisted tabs instead of wiping them

Existing users have the pre-split persisted format: full tab data embedded
in the ${projectId}:draggable-tabs-browser-store index, with no per-tab
keys. After the split, getItem looked only at per-tab keys — which don't
exist for those sessions — so every tab rehydrated without data, failed
validation, and onRehydrateStorage cleared the whole playground: all open
prompt tabs lost on the first reload after deploy.

getItem now falls back to the embedded t.data when a per-tab key is
absent, and deliberately does not seed the dedup ref so the next persist
writes the per-tab key, completing the migration. Regression test seeds
the legacy payload and proves tabs survive and migrate.

* test(prompts): reset useTabId mock in afterEach to prevent isolation leak

* test(prompts): assert variable value survives tab switch-away-and-back

Round-trip regression for the flush-on-unmount fix, closing the gap PR
Hound flagged: type a variable value, unmount the tab (switch away), then
remount it (switch back) and assert the value is restored on screen —
proving both halves (flush to store on unmount, restore from store on
remount), not just that the panel unmounts. Fails without the flush.
