fix(sdks/python): migrate haystack examples to the 3.x chat API (#7300)

haystack-ai 3.0 removed the non-chat `OpenAIGenerator`, so both haystack
examples failed at import and took main red:

    ImportError: cannot import name 'OpenAIGenerator'
    from 'haystack.components.generators'

`haystack.components.generators` now exposes only `OpenAIImageGenerator`;
the text path is `OpenAIChatGenerator` in `.generators.chat`, which takes
`messages: list[ChatMessage]` rather than `prompt: str`. That change
reaches further than the import:

- `PromptBuilder` -> `ChatPromptBuilder`, whose `prompt` socket emits
  `list[ChatMessage]`, so the pipeline edge is now
  `prompt_builder.prompt -> llm.messages`.
- A reply is a `ChatMessage`, so the content is `reply.text` and the
  token counts move from `result["meta"][0]["usage"]` to
  `reply.meta["usage"]`.
- Haystack 3 rejects a component whose `run` and `run_async` signatures
  differ, so the tracked subclasses override both in step.

Drops an `AnswerBuilder` import the openinference example never used.

fix(ci): compare changed paths byte-exactly in the deployment-impact guard (#7302)

Follow-up to #7294, from a CodeRabbit finding that landed after it merged.
Two ways an unrecognised file could borrow a lockfile's exemption:

- `classify()` trimmed each path. `charts/x/Chart.lock ` (trailing
  space) is a DIFFERENT file from `charts/x/Chart.lock`, and trimming
  collapsed the two together. Names are now compared byte-exact.
- The file list crossed the workflow/script boundary newline-delimited,
  so a path legally containing a newline split into two records that
  classified independently — the tail alone could look exempt. The list
  now travels as `gh api --paginate --slurp` JSON via a temp file and is
  never line-split.

Parsing fails closed on malformed input rather than waving the pull
request through, matching rule R3 in guard-path-filters.ts: a guard that
cannot read its input has to say so.

fix(sdk-ts): migrate to the OpenTelemetry logs SDK 0.221 API surface (#7274)

* fix(sdk-ts): migrate to the OpenTelemetry logs SDK 0.221 API surface

@opentelemetry/api-logs and sdk-logs 0.221 broke the logs API that
sdks/typescript builds on (dependabot #7260's target versions):

- LoggerProviderOptions dropped forceFlushTimeoutMillis; the timeout
  now goes on the forceFlush() call itself via ForceFlushOptions.
- SimpleLogRecordProcessor / BatchLogRecordProcessor now take a single
  options object ({ exporter, ...}) instead of a positional exporter
  argument.
- NoopLoggerProvider was dropped from the public export surface;
  createNoopLogger (still exported) is its replacement, so
  observability-sdk/logger/index.ts builds an equivalent no-op
  LoggerProvider locally instead of instantiating a removed class.
- The Logger interface gained a required enabled() method.
  LangWatchLoggerInternal now implements it by delegating to the
  wrapped OTel logger, which is what actually knows whether a
  processor is registered.

Bumps @opentelemetry/{api-logs,sdk-logs,sdk-node,exporter-logs-otlp-http,
exporter-trace-otlp-http,instrumentation} in sdks/typescript/package.json
to the versions #7260 targeted. Scoped to sdks/typescript only; #7260 also
bumped platform/app, mcp/typescript and packages/react-rum, which are not
covered here.

* Address review comments

- Reset currentLoggerProvider before the NoOp-logger test so it exercises the default provider instead of state leaked from an earlier test (coderabbitai)
- Add a regression test asserting LangWatchLoggerInternal.enabled() delegates to the wrapped OTel logger (coderabbitai)

* fix(sdk-ts): update config-options integration test for sdk-node 0.221's new TracerProvider internals

@opentelemetry/sdk-node 0.221 replaced its NodeTracerProvider/BasicTracerProvider
construction (which stored resolved config under a private `_config`) with the
new unified @opentelemetry/sdk-trace package's TracerProvider, which stores the
same data under `_tracerOptions` instead. This PR's CI never ran the full
sdk-javascript-ci matrix until the merge-conflict-with-main fix above unblocked
it, so this genuine breakage from the sdk-node bump only surfaced just now.

Add a small local helper that reads whichever private field is present, so the
six assertions reaching into the concrete provider's resolved config keep
working.

feat(authz): per-org cutover - the fork live, engine primary one organization at a time (ADR-092 PR 3) (#7151)

* feat(authz): resource facts get their identity and the share-link compat head

* feat(authz): the cutover gate and the collector's per-org repoint

The per-organization switch a cutover flips, and the read repository that
switch chooses between.

`cutover-gate.ts` reads `AuthzCutoverProjection.onEngine` behind a 60s cache
in both directions, modelled on `legacy-fallback-gate.ts`. Unlike stage B's
finalization, a cutover is reversible by design: the positive bound is what
"back on legacy within the gate's cache window" costs when an operator rolls
an organization back, and the negative bound is what lets a completed cutover
take effect fleet-wide without a deploy. An unreadable projection reads as
"not cut over", which is today's behaviour.

`GrantsAuthzReadRepository` answers the read port over the ledger's own
projection - Grant, Role and GrantUsage - rather than the compat RoleBinding /
CustomRole / ShareLink heads. It keeps every fence the legacy repository
carries: bindings gated on current organization membership (a membership read
here, since Grant holds no relation to User), an API key's private role held
to the key it was minted for, and share reads keyed on the presented tokens.
Facts a cut-over organization stores but does not yet act on - lite-member and
the rest - are skipped rather than translated, so no decision moves.

`CutoverAwareAuthzReadRepository` forks per call: the methods whose answers
differ ask the gate, and membership, key ownership and lineage - the same
query against the same table either way - stay on the legacy repository.
The collector and the shadow both compose it.

* feat(authz): the fork goes live - engine primary per cut-over organization

AuthzForkService is the shadow with primacy swapped: the engine answers, the
legacy resolver runs behind it as the reverse-shadow comparison, and every
comparison logs with primary "engine". The seven decision seams - the four
rbac.ts resolvers, the batch, and the two api-key resolvers - ask the cutover
gate for the organization they are about and compose one path or the other,
so an organization can never be half-switched inside one request. Each seam's
legacy body is factored into one implementation the answering path and the
comparison thunk share; a non-cut-over organization's behaviour is byte for
byte what it was, which is what the untouched suites prove.

Offboarding follows the head: the revoked set is now the union of the compat
binding ids and the Grant-head rows this organization holds for the user, so
the lite-member and zero-binding-admin facts a cutover imports cannot outlive
an offboard, and the proof re-collects through the cutover-aware reader.

* feat(authz): the cutover machine - one organization at a time, proof first

The composite per-org cutover migration imports what the backfill and the
genesis import leave behind - share links as RESOURCE facts adopting their
own ids, EXTERNAL memberships as lite-member grants, project credentials
as project-principal grants, and platform operators on a reserved sentinel
aggregate whose deterministic ids dedupe across every organization's pass.

Two proofs stand between the import and the flip: the RESOURCE rows must
reproduce their ShareLink originals field for field, and every member and
every API key must decide identically over the whole registry at every
scope, collected once through the legacy heads and once through the
ledger's own projection - explicitly, never through the forking decorator,
so the comparison means something before the organization moves.

The operator's rollback grows an effect of its own: after the state pin
lands, the cutover sends its rolled-back fact, flips the projection off
synchronously (the revocation class), and bumps the epoch. The gate's 60s
TTL is what bounds the fleet.

* feat(authz): share links speak ledger for a cut-over organization

The last writer a cut-over organization still ran imperatively was
ShareService. Now a mint is a resource fact, a revocation is a revocation
(enforcement deletes the grant and the compat row together), and the view
a link spends is counted on GrantUsage - the row the fold never rebuilds -
and mirrored onto the compat column, so an organization rolled back keeps
counting from where it got to.

Reads never fork: the compat ShareLink head is complete by construction,
so a cut-over organization resolves its tokens on exactly the row and
exactly the query it always did.

* test(authz): the cutover, the fork and the rollback bound to their scenarios

PR 3 built a machine nothing in specs/ described, and stage C and D left
five @scenario annotations pointing at scenarios that did not exist - which
the parity check reads as typos, not as coverage. So the scenarios are
written down and the annotations are pointed at the ones that were already
there: the api-key ceiling case binds the owner-ceiling scenario it actually
proves, and the offboarding case binds "Offboarding a user removes every
grant, with proof".

unified-authorization-engine.feature gains the per-organization fork block -
engine primary, legacy behind it as the reverse-shadow comparison, an
un-cut-over organization unchanged, the rollback landing inside the gate's
cache window, and a cut-over organization's checks reading the ledger's own
head. Every one of them is bound to a test that was written to make the two
resolvers disagree, so the answer is proof of who decided rather than a
coincidence.

The three cutover scenarios in in-place-authz-migration.feature drop
@unimplemented and gain the datastore-lane suites they were waiting for: a
whole pass to a clean proof with the fork then serving a fact that exists
only on the grant head, an operator rollback applied before the call returns
with the queue severed and Redis disconnected, and the import families -
share link, project credential, platform operator, zero-binding admin -
landing with their source rows' business time. They share one harness that
runs the real command handlers, the real reducer and the real two-headed
store inline, because a datastore lane provisions Postgres and Redis, not a
running worker.

Also fixes the backfill's fake ledger, which stopped satisfying the emitter
port when the cutover added completeCutover to it - green under vitest,
red under typecheck:tests.

* docs(authz): the plan records the cutover machine; pr 3 scenarios bound

The delivery plan carried PR 1 and PR 2 as delivered entries and PR 3 as a
promise. It now carries what was built: the gate and why both directions of
its answer expire, the fork at the ten seams with one legacy body both paths
call, the collector repointed per organization, the composite migration's
four import families and its two proofs, ShareService on the ledger with
GrantUsage owning the view count, and the rollback that holds with the queue
stopped.

AUTHZ_CUTOVER_COHORT is written down as its own knob, separate from
SYSTEM_MIGRATIONS_COHORT because the dark migrations can go wide while the
one that changes who decides advances organization by organization - and
with PR 2's trap carried forward: both are plain process.env reads, and both
have to be set on the web and the worker deployments alike, because the ops
page's "run a pass now" runs the same entry point the worker's boot pass
does.

Next is our own organization first, in production.

The source files here are biome's formatting pass over the tree PR 3
touched, folded in rather than left for a later diff to trip over.

* test(authz): the write-fork stub learns enforcement's project read

* fix(authz): the rollback lever cannot strand an organization, and a proof lands every pass

* refactor(authz): one gate, one vocabulary, and the retry scenario bound

* fix(authz): the cutover meets the ledger's finished shape

PR 2 landed on main with a rebase and a further review round behind it, so
the cutover's own commits replay onto a writer that has moved. The seams
that moved:

- The emitter grew the genesis import's deny direction, so every stub that
  claims to be one implements `revokeGrants` and `deleteRole` - the inline
  cutover harness through the real command handlers, the two package fakes
  by refusing, since the cutover emits neither.
- `LedgerActor` is the package's name for the actor, not the app ledger's
  re-export, so the share repository sources it where its siblings do.
- Resource terms now carry the resource's identity, so the wire suite's
  fixtures say which thing they open and where it lives - otherwise every
  negative case there was refused before it reached the rule it names.
- The operator rollback accepts `migrated`, `finalized` AND `rolled_back`:
  the first two are the eligibility PR 2 widened, the third is this PR's
  retry of an effect that died after its pin landed. A rolled-back record
  is no longer a refusal, so the test that demanded one is gone and the
  effect contract carries `decidedAt`.
- The cache bound PR 2 added to the legacy-fallback gate moves into the
  shared gate the cutover gate now shares, so neither grows unbounded.

`legacyBatch` and the genesis deny-direction pair are lifted out of the
functions that outgrew their line budget - no behaviour moves with them.

* fix(authz): the resource proof looks both ways

The import proof swept the ShareLink table and looked each row up among the
grants, so it could only ever see a link the cutover DROPPED. A resource
grant with no share link behind it - access the cutover would INVENT, a link
nobody minted resolving for whoever holds its token - was invisible to it.

That is the direction the deny-direction genesis reconciliation exists for,
and the one the whole design refuses: a crash or a drift window may leave
less access, never more. So the sweep now reports `resource_extra` as well,
the organization is held on it like any other diff, and the case is bound to
its own scenario rather than left to the round trip.

Also joins a Gherkin step that wrapped onto a second line; every other step
in that file is one line.

* docs(authz): the fork suite's header stops overstating one case

The organization-permission case has both resolvers denying, so its answer
discriminates nothing - what proves the engine ran is that the legacy shadow
was never called. The header claimed every case was a disagreement, which
would have a reader credit that one with power it does not have.

* fix(authz): the resource-facts migration renumbers past main's newest

The rebase left 20260818090000 below main's 20260818120000, so it would run
out of order or not at all. Same content, new position; the schema comment
that names it moves with it.

* feat(authz): enrollment paces the migration from the app, and the review's holes close

Two bodies of work, one set of files.

## The three-lens review's seventeen findings, fixed

Access-direction holes (the two P0s first):
- A revoke during the fold's compat-before-head crash window keyed itself off
  the absent Grant row, fell back to a legacy-only delete, and the fold's
  re-run RESURRECTED the revoked link. Revocation now keys on the ShareLink
  ids themselves (they are the grant ids by construction), unions ids from
  both heads for resource-wide sweeps, fences every id to the project, and
  routes on an UNCACHED projection read that fails toward deleting both heads
  and appending the fact - never toward the silent legacy branch.
- Rolling back the genesis import from under a cut-over organization flipped
  writes to legacy while reads stayed on the engine, so a revoked member kept
  access indefinitely. Rollback now takes per-migration guards: a migration
  the cutover stands on refuses to roll back (migration_rollback_blocked_by_
  dependent) until the cutover itself is rolled back first.

The rest: the runner's outcome write is compare-and-set so an in-flight pass
can never overwrite an operator's rolled_back pin; the per-org import chunks
key their command ids on content, not position, so a held org whose member
set changed re-imports instead of parking forever; the rollback fact stamps
max(decidedAt, completion+1) so cross-pod clock skew cannot silently drop it
at the fold; a cutover that never started refuses to "roll back" instead of
stranding the org; offboarding proves grant rows gone directly rather than
through a membership-gated reader that answers [] vacuously; the view-budget
seed converges upward (never refunds) so one legacy view can no longer wedge
parity permanently; parity identity is order-independent and hashes the full
diff set; the shared per-organization gate invalidates in-flight reads and
bounds its map; the fork comparison rate parses "off" as off (it parsed as
NaN and ran at FULL rate); the wire suite regains the negative tests the
rebase dropped; the resource tier reads through the pass-scoped reader; the
cutover harness validates payloads against the real command schemas; and the
consume+mirror write shares one transaction.

## Enrollment in the app, not the environment

SYSTEM_MIGRATIONS_COHORT and AUTHZ_CUTOVER_COHORT are gone. The ops
migrations page enrolls a cloud organization per stage - "migrations"
(backfill + genesis) and "cutover" pace independently - stored as
SystemMigrationEnrollment rows (new table, migration
20260818120002_system_migration_enrollment), read fresh every pass so web
and worker can never disagree the way a per-deployment env var could. A set
env var is ignored with a loud warn. Enroll/withdraw are audited ops
mutations with handled errors and registry copy; self-hosted refuses
enrollment (rows there could only lie).

Self-hosted pacing becomes a code declaration: every migration carries
runsAutomaticallyOnSelfHosted. Backfill and genesis ship true (that is
today's shipped behaviour); the cutover ships FALSE - flipping it in a
release after our own cloud soak IS the self-hosted release act. A
flag-false migration is filtered from the runner entirely on self-hosted
and reads as "not yet available" on the ops page, never as attention.

  nothing pre-cutover can show: the org-level union quirk's replacement (the
  genesis floor grant) is dormant until contract, so every organization with
  an ordinary member parked forever and the cutover waited on it. The sweep

  legacy one (the dormant-fact principle demands identical inference over

  would have been refused at dispatch. The wire contract now names the one

perf(dev): run whole-repo checks in their smallest shape on a pressured machine (#7268)

* perf(dev): run whole-repo checks in their smallest shape on a pressured machine

An 18 GiB laptop that is already swapping cannot pay for a 6 GiB
typecheck ceiling: the footprint expands toward GOMEMLIMIT, every granted
page evicts someone else's, and the machine seizes. Measured there: an
uncapped cold tsc footprinted 7.26 GB against a 1.9 GB max RSS, with
twice as much system time as user time.

The queue now reads ADR-090's pressure level at spawn. Under amber or
red, GOMEMLIMIT drops to its 3 GiB floor, GOMAXPROCS halves (never below
two), and the machine-derived slot limit narrows to one. Explicit
GOMEMLIMIT, GOMAXPROCS and CHECK_SLOTS still win; CHECK_PRESSURE forces
the level; CI is untouched. Go and JS queues move together.

A check that dies by a signal the wrapper did not forward is also named
now, on stderr, as killed from outside. A bare exit 137 read as "the
queue killed it" and taught agents to bypass with CHECK_SLOTS=0, which
removes the serialization for the whole machine.

* fix(dev): keep CI out of the pressured check shape

CI resolves the pressure level to green by rule, before any measurement,
in both queue implementations through one shared isTruthyCI. The queue
already stands down on a runner, and the same reasoning retires the
pressure policy with it: one job, nobody typing, so halving the cores
buys back an interactive machine that does not exist. A swap figure read
inside a container describes the host, not the job. This makes "CI is
unaffected" true by rule instead of by the runner's kernel. An explicit
CHECK_PRESSURE still wins there. A developer machine that turns the
queue off with CHECK_SLOTS=0 keeps its caps, which is the case the
policy exists for.

The outside-kill report now records which signals the wrapper forwarded,
not whether any was forwarded. A run that is interrupted and then killed
by the OS dies of a signal nobody forwarded, and a boolean suppressed
that report because the earlier interrupt had set it. The Go side also
treats its own context cancellation as its own doing, since
exec.CommandContext kills with SIGKILL that no forwarded record covers.

The Go test now asserts the computed GOMAXPROCS value rather than only
that it is set.

* fix(dev): count a group signal as forwarded, and keep the ADR's evidence in the ADR

A Ctrl-C at a terminal reaches the wrapper and the command together, so
the command can die of the signal while the wrapper's own copy is still
pending. Both queue implementations read the forwarded-signal record at
that moment and could report the operator's own interrupt as a kill from
outside, which is the exact mistake the report exists to prevent. The Go
relay now drains what is still queued before it reports, and the JS
wrapper defers the exit handling by one turn so a pending handler runs
first. The Go path has a regression test that fails without the drain.

The test that waits for a pid file no longer busy-spins: the shell
creates the file by redirection before it writes the pid, so an empty
read is as much "not ready" as a missing file, and the 200 attempts
could burn off in microseconds.

Docs: the exit-137 rule now says to believe the queue's report rather
than the code alone, because a forwarded Ctrl-C ends a run the same way.
The CI rule names its precedence against an explicit CHECK_PRESSURE. The
ADR carries the measured numbers in a table with the command to
reproduce them, instead of pointing at a pull request, and no longer
claims a completed cold run in the pressured shape: that run was stopped
by hand at 15.6 of 16.4 GB of swap, so the wall-clock cost stays
unestablished.

* refactor(dev): name the queue test's run options, and guard the group signal

startRun takes one object rather than a tag and an options bag, which is
the repo's rule for a function with more than one argument, and the new
boolean option is isDetached rather than detached, which is the naming
rule for a new boolean. 34 call sites move with it.

The group-signal test no longer negates a possibly missing pid. A missing
one made -0, which process.kill reads as 0, and 0 means the caller's own
process group: on a POSIX runner that is the test runner itself.

* docs(dev): drop the CLAUDE.md notes from the check queue change

The queue itself tells an agent what it needs at the moment it needs it:
it prints the pressured shape on --explain, and it names an outside kill
on stderr when one happens. The ADR and the spec keep the reasoning.

fix(scenarios): a run that did not pass is a result, not an error — and stop the poll caching itself blind (#7285)

* fix(scenarios): report a run that did not pass as a result, and stop the poll caching itself blind

Two bugs in the same poll, both client-side.

A run that finished without passing was reported as "The scenario
encountered an error during execution". FAILED means the run executed
and did not pass — a judge verdict, or the runner stopping at its turn
budget. The server never writes FAILED for execution problems; those are
ERROR. The old branch bucketed all four terminal statuses together, so
every unsuccessful run told the user to go debug healthy infrastructure.
Split out a run_failed result with its own toast, keeping ERROR,
CANCELLED and STALLED on the error path. Navigation stays opt-in via the
toast action — success auto-navigates, this must not.

The poll also timed out on healthy runs. It calls getBatchRunData up to
60 times over 30s with an identical input; under the app-wide staleTime
of 30_000 every call after the first was answered from the first one's
cached result, so the loop could never see the run start and always fell
through to "Run timed out". staleTime: 0 forces real requests.
retry: false matters just as much — fetchQuery only defaults retry off
when it is undefined, and the app defines it globally (4 retries with
backoff), which would burn the whole budget inside a single attempt.

Fixes #7202
Fixes #7199

* test(scenarios): prove the cache bypass actually defeats staleTime

Review finding: the shipped test asserted only that the hook PASSES
{ staleTime: 0, retry: false } to tRPC's .fetch — it would keep passing if

Drives the real pollForScenarioRun against a real QueryClient carrying the
real app defaults, faking only the network. Executed evidence:

  without the bypass -> 1 network call,  result timeout   (the bug)
  with the bypass    -> 5 network calls, result success

The run existed on the server from t=2s in both cases.

Two review findings in code this branch introduced.

   member is a compile error until classified — the rule scenario-run-category.ts
   already states in its own docstring.

   Verified by temporarily adding an ABANDONED member:
     TS2741: Property 'ABANDONED' is missing in type '{ FAILED: ... }'
     but required in type 'Record<ScenarioRunStatus, ...>'

2. The local result type reused the canonical name BatchRunDataResult while
   dropping lastUpdatedAt, so the two read as the same type. Renamed to
   PolledBatchRunData and documented the narrowing.

* fix(scenarios): drop the dead 'View run' button, hoist the action builder

Two review findings.

1. buildViewRunAction returned an action whenever a scenarioRunId existed,
   calling onRunFailed?.() — so callers that pass no handler rendered a
   button that does nothing. ScenarioFormDrawer.tsx:118 is such a caller,
   and the new 'Scenario did not pass' toast is on a common path. Now
   returns undefined when there is no handler.

   Pre-existing shape (run_error had it too), not a regression from this
   branch — fixed because the helper is new code here.

2. The helper was the only named function defined inside a useCallback body
   in src/hooks/, and took two positional string-ish parameters. Moved to
   module scope with a named-parameter object, matching useRunSuite.ts:48,81.

Also renamed one describe to a 'when' condition to match its siblings.

* refactor(scenarios): take the poll's wire shape from the server contract

Addresses the CodeRabbit review on #7285.

The poll declared its own `PolledBatchRunData` / `ScenarioRun` types. They
were a restatement of the server's schema-derived `BatchRunDataResult`, and
they had already drifted: the local copy said `status?: string` where the
server always sends a required `ScenarioRunStatus`. That lie is what forced
the `as ScenarioRunStatus` cast in the classifier. Importing the canonical
type deletes the cast and turns a future wire change into a compile error.

The test fixtures follow: a run is now built from `ScenarioRunData` through
a `makeRun()` helper, so a fixture carrying only the fields the poll happens
to read can no longer keep passing after the shape moves underneath it.

Also switches `pollForScenarioRun` and the cache test's `createCountingFetcher`
to named parameters per CLAUDE.md, and lifts the outcome toast out of the run
callback into `buildRunOutcomeToast` — the callback had grown past the 60-line
lint gate, which the repo enforces on new code.

No behaviour change: same titles, same toast types, same branch order.

* test(scenarios): nested describes, and pin what an unknown status does

Second CodeRabbit round on #7285.

The poll's unit tests carried BDD structure in `// Given:` comments. They are
nested `describe("given …") / describe("when …")` blocks now, per CLAUDE.md.

The review also asked for a regression test on an unrecognised runtime status,
and proposed classifying it as `run_error`. The test is in; the proposed
classification is not, deliberately. tRPC does not runtime-validate its output,
so a status added to the server after this client shipped arrives here
unclassified — and unknown means unknown: it could be a new active state or a
new failure state. Handing back the run lets the run page report the truth,
where calling it an error would put a red toast on a possibly-healthy run,
which is the bug this PR exists to fix.

Verified the new test is not decorative: applying the proposed
`undefined -> "run_error"` change turns it red.

Also corrects a wrong claim in the classifier's own doc comment. It said an
unclassified status "would burn the whole budget and report a false timeout".
It would not — the loop only keeps polling while no run is visible at all, so
an unclassified status falls through to the "a run exists, hand it back"
branch. The comment now says what the code does and why.

* test(scenarios): object param for the batch helper, drop a restating comment

Third CodeRabbit round on #7285. `batchWith` takes `{ runs }` per CLAUDE.md,
and the comment over `pollOnce` now says why the zero-advance is there — the

fix(ops): the tenancy guard lets the enrollment rollout read itself again (#7311)

Enrollment went per-migration and dropped the `stage` column, but the
organization-tenancy guard still admitted `SystemMigrationEnrollment` reads
only alongside a `stage` string. Every read the feature performs lost its
only admitted shape, so in production the ops migrations page threw on both
its queries and - the part that matters more - each worker's migration pass
died at boot reading the organizations it processes. The rollout was inert,
not slow.

Two things were wrong. The model's bound named a departed column; and the
guard rejects a missing or non-object `where` BEFORE consulting any bound,
so a bare `findMany()` was unreachable from `extraBound` whatever it said.
Reads that legitimately span organizations now say so as `platformScopeActions`,
granted per action and only to reads: enroll still declares its organization,
withdraw still names the compound key, and a migration-wide bulk write has no
admitted shape.

The tests drive the real repository through the real middleware, the way the
API-key reaper's do. Nothing did before, which is exactly why a rename on one
side and a predicate on the other could disagree all the way to production.

fix(scenarios): bind the inlined SDK to the OpenTelemetry the app actually has (#7314)

The scenario child bundle inlines @langwatch/scenario and its whole graph but
keeps @opentelemetry/* external, so the SDK inlined there resolves its OTEL
bindings against the app's version rather than the one it was published
against. api-logs 0.221 dropped `NoopLoggerProvider`; the published SDK still
constructed it, so every simulation died at module scope before reading a byte
of job data and surfaced as scenario_infra_error.

Point the vendored scenario package at the workspace SDK, which already moved
to `createNoopLogger`, so it reads from the same copy the app does instead of a
second, older one resolved from npm. Scoped to the vendored 1.2.0: mcp and
skills are on scenario 0.4.x, which pins the SDK to 0.16.1 exactly, and neither
is built through the bundle that breaks. This also drops the duplicate SDK
subtree from the lockfile.

The existing bundle test could not see this. Nothing was missing a MODULE, only
an export, so it failed as a TypeError rather than MODULE_NOT_FOUND, and the
exit code is 1 whether the child crashed on load or reached main() and rejected
its input. The new test pins the parse failure on stdout, which only a fully
evaluated module graph can produce.
